## Tools and evidence in this directory

Everything is reproducible. Nothing here is hand-waved from a blog post.

**Deterministic, runnable now:**

| tool | does |
|---|---|
| **[`tools/Fingerprint.ps1`](tools/Fingerprint.ps1)** | **the Phase 0 gate, and the first thing to run before any session.** Fifteen static checks — tiered compilation, IL-only status, the assembly's size *and SHA-256*, the `clrjit` vtable's code-slot count, both runtime DLL versions, and **every pinned target's IL hash** — with a non-zero exit on any mismatch. It resolves `getJit` from the export directory itself and re-hashes each target's instruction stream straight out of the assembly, then requires `il_index.py` to regenerate the same table, so it needs no other tooling. Mutation-tested at both levels: a same-size byte flip anywhere in the assembly fails loudly, and a single flipped byte *inside a target's IL* is named as that target. Its expected values live in [`known-build.json`](known-build.json) |
| **[`tools/il_index.py`](tools/il_index.py)** | **builds the target table, and is the authority on it.** A self-contained PE/CLI metadata reader — no `ilspycmd`, no `dotnet`, no network — that resolves the hook's **six** detour targets to `(declaring type, name, arity, metadata token, RVA, IL size, SHA-256 of the exact IL bytes)` and writes them into `known-build.json`. Cross-checks every target against the IL dump on RVA, code size and parameter count; `--check` also compares the record against the table and exits non-zero on a mismatch (a hardcoded key list used to drop a target silently); `--mutation-test` proves a one-byte IL edit moves exactly that target's hash |
| **[`tools/check_opcode_table.py`](tools/check_opcode_table.py)** | **the opcode table's own witness.** Walks every method body the IL dump describes with the `OPCODES_1` that `il_index.py` actually ships and compares the visited offsets against the dump's. It exists because the table was one entry short (`br`, `0x38`) for its whole life — which is what refused the auto-aim target as `TARGET TABLE NOT TRUSTWORTHY` — and because the `MoreSects` offset choice inside `method_body()` reads that table, so a wrong width can move which bytes get hashed. Exits non-zero below either threshold; the numbers are in [`docs/hook/HOOK-BUILD-MATRIX.md`](../docs/hook/HOOK-BUILD-MATRIX.md) |
| **[`tools/il_targets.py`](tools/il_targets.py)** | lists candidate methods on a type so a new target can be pinned **without depending on its name** — declaring type, arity, and the return and parameter types decoded from the signature blob, plus IL size and the IL dump's RVA line. It exists because the client's obfuscator gives the movement integrator a metadata name of private-use code points that **cannot be found by searching for the name the decompiler prints** (zero hits in the 89 MB dump). It never writes the record, so `il_index.py` stays the one authority. `--self-test` checks the reader against the four signatures the documents state independently |
| **[`tools/steering_report.py`](tools/steering_report.py)** | reads a Spike 3.1 steering run and says whether the hook moved the player: the pilot's read-back (did the write land), the realised displacement (did the integrator act), the per-phase commanded-vs-observed headings (was the direction obeyed), the relay log's `GmKicked` (did the server object) and the `GmMove` cadence. It also reads an `--escape-test` run — whether `World.RequestEscape()` was reached, returned or threw, and whether a `GmEscape`/`EscapeAck` left the machine — and it keeps the two experiments apart, so a run that asked for only one is not failed for the other. It fails loudly on a run whose target was never patched, because that otherwise reads exactly like a pilot that chose to do nothing, and its own fixture (`tools/tests/test_steering_report.py`) asserts the good, unpatched, kicked, escape, escape-too-soon and empty cases |
| **[`tools/Test-FingerprintGate.ps1`](tools/Test-FingerprintGate.ps1)** | the gate's own falsification test, at the level that matters: it copies the install to a sandbox, flips one byte **inside a target's IL** with the file length unchanged, and asserts the gate exits non-zero naming *that* target while the other three still pass. A gate that cannot be shown to fail is not a gate |
| [`tools/Test-JitVtable.ps1`](tools/Test-JitVtable.ps1) | locates `clrjit!getJit`, resolves `&g_CILJit`, and dumps the `ICorJitCompiler` vtable. **This is Phase 0's most important instrument** — it proves the four-slot layout and which slot holds `compileMethod` on the exact runtime build |
| [`tools/Test-ReadyToRun.ps1`](tools/Test-ReadyToRun.ps1) | reads the COR20 `ManagedNativeHeader` and reports IL-only vs ReadyToRun. Verified on this install: `DarzasDominion.dll` and `MonoGame.Framework.dll` are **IL-only**; `System.Private.CoreLib.dll` **is R2R** |
| [`tools/Get-PeExports.ps1`](tools/Get-PeExports.ps1) | PE export lister; used to confirm `coreclr.dll` exports `GetCLRRuntimeHost` and `g_dacTable`, i.e. that in-process DAC reads are on the table |
| [`tools/poolresolve.py`](tools/poolresolve.py) | resolves `hehe(N)` constant lookups in the IL to real values, by pairing each index with the return type of the call that consumes it. This is what recovered the movement law and the damage law |
| [`tools/il_constants.py`](tools/il_constants.py) | resolves obfuscated literal *values* straight out of the IL dump |
| [`tools/g.py`](tools/g.py) | bounded grep-with-context, written because `World.cs` is 24,381 lines and cannot be read whole |
| [`pe_probe.py`](work/pe_probe.py) | PE/CLI/R2R probe — proves the assembly is pure IL with no ReadyToRun block |
| [`md_probe.py`](work/md_probe.py) | .NET metadata table census — 23,743 methods, 25,105 fields |
| [`_pooldecode.py`](work/_pooldecode.py) | decrypts the obfuscator's constant pool (1035 ints / 16 longs / 787 floats / 229 doubles), verified against eight independently-known packet ids |
| [`tools/analyze_size_histogram.py`](tools/analyze_size_histogram.py) | decides whether a `hook.log.sizes` "ZERO compiled" verdict is a fact about the game or an artifact of the fixed-size histogram table |
| [`tools/pe_probe.py`](tools/pe_probe.py) | minimal PE inspector: subsystem, COM descriptor, imported DLLs and functions |

```powershell
# the one command to run before any session

# the target table behind it, and the proof that the gate can fail
python .\\tools\il_index.py --check
python .\\tools\il_index.py --mutation-test

## What is deliberately not in this directory

- **The hook is a Phase 1 skeleton plus the Phase 2 sensor.** Phase 0 of the plan said the first
  thing to write was the fingerprint gate, not the hook — and that gate is here. Phase 1's
  `Drelay.Hook.dll`, `Drelay.Bootstrap.dll` and `Drelay.Launcher.exe` (in [`out/`](out)) are built,
  have been run against the live game, and are closed; Phase 2 built the sensor on top of them and
  closed on 2026-10-13 ([`PHASE2-SCOPE.md`](../docs/hook/PHASE2-SCOPE.md)).
- **No changes to the Java relay.** The bridge design in [JAVA-BRIDGE.md](../docs/bridge/JAVA-BRIDGE.md) is
  additive by construction: the relay runs identically with and without the hook.
- **No game files were modified**, and none need to be on the recommended injection path. The gate
  and the indexer are read-only; the one test that writes anything writes to a temporary sandbox copy.
- **No pinned constants file.** The movement law, the damage law and the trajectory model were all
  recovered, but they are **called** rather than frozen — see [IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md](../docs/hook/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md)
  Phase 0 item 3 for why a constants file would be a hazard rather than a convenience.
- **No claims without a `file:line` or a measurement.** Where something is genuinely unknown it is
  marked as such and paired with the experiment that would settle it — [CLIENT-MAP.md](../docs/hook/CLIENT-MAP.md)
  §10 lists them all, and two of the three that were "blocking" have since been resolved by the
  constant-pool decode.

```

`hook/build.ps1`:

```ps1
# ============================================================================
#  build.ps1 -- builds the whole Phase 1 hook: native DLL, bootstrap, launcher.
#
#  WHY A SCRIPT RATHER THAN A .vcxproj OR A .csproj SOLUTION
#  --------------------------------------------------------
#  Two reasons, both practical:
#
#    * the native half must be built by the *same* MSVC toolset that produced
#      the runtime it targets, and a .vcxproj hardcodes one.  This script finds
#      the installed toolset through vswhere and reports which one it used, so
#      "which compiler built this DLL" is in the build log;
#    * the managed half must target net9.0 to match the game's runtime, and the
#      only SDK on this machine is 8.0.x.  A plain `dotnet build` with an
#      explicit TargetFramework works; a project file that a future SDK silently
#      retargets would not.
#
#  Nothing is written into the game directory.  The build output goes to
#  hook\out\.
#
#  Usage:
#    .\build.ps1                 # build everything
#    .\build.ps1 -Native         # native only
#    .\build.ps1 -Managed        # managed only
#    .\build.ps1 -Clean
#
#  Exit codes: 0 = built, 1 = build failed, 2 = usage/toolchain problem.
# ============================================================================

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Native,
    [switch]$Managed,
    [switch]$Clean,
    [switch]$Rebuild
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$outDir = Join-Path $root 'out'
$objDir = Join-Path $root 'obj'

function Write-Step { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Cyan }
function Write-Ok   { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Green }
function Write-Bad  { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Red }
function Write-Note { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor DarkGray }

if ($Clean) {
    foreach ($d in @($outDir, $objDir)) {
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $d) {
            Write-Step "clean: removing $d"
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $d -Recurse -Force
        }
    }
    if (-not ($Native -or $Managed)) { exit 0 }
}

# A guard that costs one pass over the project files and saves a confusing
# failure. MSBuild rejects an XML comment containing `--` (MSB4025, "an XML
# comment cannot contain '--'"), and this repository's prose is full of em-dashes
# written as `--`. The error names a line and column in a file nobody was
# editing, so it reads as a corrupt project rather than as a comment style problem.
$projectFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Recurse -Include '*.csproj', '*.props', '*.targets' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch '\\(bin|obj)\\' }
foreach ($file in $projectFiles) {
    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw
    foreach ($match in [regex]::Matches($text, '(?s)<!--(.*?)-->')) {
        if ($match.Groups[1].Value.Contains('--')) {
            $line = ($text.Substring(0, $match.Index) -split "`n").Count
            Write-Bad ("$($file.FullName):$line  an XML comment contains '--', which MSBuild rejects (MSB4025).")
            Write-Note '  use a comma or a colon instead; the prose in this project is full of em-dashes.'
            exit 2
        }
    }
}

$doNative = $Native -or (-not $Managed)
$doManaged = $Managed -or (-not $Native)

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outDir, $objDir | Out-Null

$failures = @()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generated: the bootstrap's pinned-build table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regenerated from known-build.json on every build, so the hook can never be
# built against a stale copy of the build identity Phase 0 pinned.  If Python is
# not available the committed copy is used and the build says so -- the generated
# file is deterministic, so a missing generator is a warning rather than a
# failure.
if ($doManaged) {
    # Two generators, both reading a file that is already the authority:
    #   gen_target_table.py  -- known-build.json  -> the pinned target table
    #   gen_shared_layout.py -- DrelayHookShared.h -> every FieldOffset in the
    #                          managed view of the shared block
    # Both are deterministic, so a missing generator is a warning (the committed
    # output is used) rather than a failure.
    $generators = @(
        @{ Script = 'tools\gen_target_table.py';  What = 'build table' },
        @{ Script = 'tools\gen_shared_layout.py'; What = 'shared-block layout' }
    )
    foreach ($gen in $generators) {
        $script = Join-Path $root $gen.Script
        if ((Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $script)) {
            $genOut = & python $script 2>&1
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
                Write-Bad ("the $($gen.What) could not be regenerated:")
                $genOut | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
                exit 1
            }
            $genOut | ForEach-Object { Write-Note $_ }
        } else {
            Write-Note "python or $($gen.Script) is unavailable; using the committed $($gen.What)"
        }
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Native: Drelay.Hook.dll
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ($doNative) {
    Write-Step '--- native: Drelay.Hook.dll ---'

    $vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $vswhere)) {
        Write-Bad 'vswhere.exe not found: no Visual Studio installation is discoverable.'
        exit 2
    }
    $vsPath = & $vswhere -latest -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath
    if (-not $vsPath) {
        # Fall back to a plain install and let vcvars decide whether the C++
        # toolset is really there; the error message from cl.exe is better than
        # ours would be.
        $vsPath = & $vswhere -latest -products * -property installationPath
    }
    if (-not $vsPath) {
        Write-Bad 'no Visual Studio installation found.'
        exit 2
    }
    $vcvars = Join-Path $vsPath 'VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $vcvars)) {
        Write-Bad "vcvars64.bat not found under $vsPath -- install the Desktop development with C++ workload."
        exit 2
    }

    $nativeDir = Join-Path $root 'native'
    $minhookDir = Join-Path $root 'thirdparty\MinHook'
    $sources = @(
        'DrelayMain.cpp', 'DrelayInstall.cpp', 'DrelayFrame.cpp',
        'DrelaySelfCheck.cpp', 'DrelayLog.cpp', 'DrelayPe.cpp', 'DrelayEvidence.cpp',
        'DrelayCrash.cpp'
    ) | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $nativeDir $_ }
    $minhookSources = @(
        'src\hook.c', 'src\buffer.c', 'src\trampoline.c', 'src\hde\hde64.c'
    ) | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $minhookDir $_ }

    foreach ($s in ($sources + $minhookSources)) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $s)) { Write-Bad "missing source: $s"; exit 1 }
    }

    $defines = @(
        'WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN', 'NOMINMAX', '_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS',
        'UNICODE', '_UNICODE', 'MH_STATIC'
    ) | ForEach-Object { "/D$_" }

    # /W4 and warnings-as-errors on the hook's own sources: this code runs inside
    # the game's frame and a truncation or an unused-parameter bug is exactly the
    # kind of thing that becomes a crash under a different build.
    # Object layout.  Each pass writes into its own directory, which matters
    # because /Fo names each object after its *source* basename: with both passes
    # sharing one directory, MinHook's single-letter file names are exactly the
    # kind that would eventually collide with a future file of ours and silently
    # link the wrong object.  Two directories removes the possibility rather than
    # documenting it.
    $objOurDir = Join-Path $objDir 'our'
    $objMhDir = Join-Path $objDir 'minhook'
    $objSizeDir = Join-Path $objDir 'size'
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $objOurDir, $objMhDir, $objSizeDir | Out-Null

    $nativeObjects = @()
    foreach ($src in $sources) {
        $nativeObjects += Join-Path $objOurDir ((Split-Path -Leaf $src) -replace '\.cpp$', '.obj')
    }
    $minhookObjects = @()
    foreach ($src in $minhookSources) {
        $minhookObjects += Join-Path $objMhDir ((Split-Path -Leaf $src) -replace '\.c$', '.obj')
    }

    # Two passes, on purpose.
    #
    # Pass 1 compiles the hook's own sources at /W4 /WX: this code runs inside
    # the game's frame, and a truncation or an uninitialised read is exactly the
    # kind of thing that becomes a crash only under a different build.
    #
    # Pass 2 compiles the vendored MinHook at /W3 with warnings *not* errors.
    # Its warnings are real but they are its author's to fix, and a hook that
    # cannot be rebuilt because a third-party file grew a new warning is a worse
    # failure than four C4244s in a disassembler's length arithmetic.  The
    # distinction is recorded here rather than by lowering the bar for our own
    # code.
    # Built as literal strings rather than as arrays joined later, because the
    # quoting is the fiddly part and PowerShell's native-command argument passing
    # does not preserve embedded quotes the way a naive `-join ' '` assumes: an
    # array element that is `"/Fo"` plus a quoted path arrives at link.exe with
    # the quotes stripped and the path broken into two arguments, which surfaces
    # as the unhelpful "no argument specified with option '/Fe'".
    $sourceList = ($sources | ForEach-Object { "`"$_`"" }) -join ' '
    $minhookList = ($minhookSources | ForEach-Object { "`"$_`"" }) -join ' '
    $objectList = (($nativeObjects + $minhookObjects) | ForEach-Object { "`"$_`"" }) -join ' '
    $includeList = @(
        ('/I"' + (Join-Path $minhookDir 'include') + '"'),
        ('/I"' + (Join-Path $minhookDir 'src') + '"'),
        ('/I"' + $nativeDir + '"')
    ) -join ' '
    $defineList = ($defines -join ' ')

    # /MD = the runtime the .NET runtime itself ships against (ucrtbase +
    # vcruntime140), /EHsc = the exception model MinHook and the __try blocks
    # assume, /GS and /guard:cf are the defaults and are kept deliberately.
    # NOTE on the trailing separator: `/Fo"<dir>\\"` looks natural but the pair of
    # backslashes before the closing quote escapes it in the command line, so the
    # path arrives unterminated and cl writes every object into the *current*
    # directory under its own name.  A forward slash ends the directory without
    # ending the quote.
    $ourObjArg = ($objOurDir -replace '\\', '/') + '/'
    $mhObjArg = ($objMhDir -replace '\\', '/') + '/'
    $ourArgs = "$sourceList /Fo`"$ourObjArg`" /Fd`"$objDir\Drelay.Hook.pdb`" $includeList $defineList " +
               '/nologo /c /MD /O2 /GL /EHsc /W4 /WX /std:c++17 /Gy /Gw /guard:cf /GS /Zi'
    $mhArgs = "$minhookList /Fo`"$mhObjArg`" $includeList $defineList " +
              '/nologo /c /MD /O2 /GL /W3 /std:c17 /Zi'
    # link.exe takes /OUT: and /PDB:, where cl.exe's driver takes /Fe and /Fd.
    # The system import libraries are named here explicitly rather than left to
    # the `#pragma comment(lib, ...)` in the sources: a pragma is honoured only
    # when cl drives the link, and this script invokes link.exe directly so that
    # the two warning policies above can differ per pass.
    # `user32.lib` is here for the foreground-window census in DrLogProcessIdentity:
    # GetForegroundWindow/GetWindowThreadProcessId/GetWindowTextW are in user32, and
    # the process census in the same function uses tlhelp32, which lives in kernel32
    # and therefore needs nothing extra.
    $linkArgs = "/nologo /DLL /OUT:`"$outDir\Drelay.Hook.dll`" /PDB:`"$objDir\Drelay.Hook.pdb`" " +
                "/MAP:`"$objDir\Drelay.Hook.map`" /MAPINFO:EXPORTS " +
                "$objectList /LTCG /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF /INCREMENTAL:NO /DEBUG " +
                '/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS version.lib crypt32.lib advapi32.lib user32.lib'

    $bat = Join-Path $objDir 'build_native.bat'
    $logPath = Join-Path $objDir 'native_build.log'
    $sizeLog = Join-Path $objDir 'sizeof.txt'
    # The size probe is compiled first and run, because it is the check that the
    # generator's model of MSVC's packing agrees with MSVC.  Building the hook
    # first and discovering the disagreement from a static_assert would name the
    # total but not which field moved.
    $sizeProbeArgs = "/nologo `"$(Join-Path $nativeDir 'SizeProbe.c')`" " +
                     "/I`"$nativeDir`" /DDRELAY_LAYOUT_PROBE /Fo`"$objSizeDir/`" " +
                     "/Fe`"$(Join-Path $objDir 'SizeProbe.exe')`" /MD /O2 /W3"
    # The compiler's output is redirected to a file by the batch itself rather
    # than captured through the pipeline: MSVC writes its banner to stderr, and
    # PowerShell turns a native command's stderr into an error record, which
    # under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' aborts the build on a *successful*
    # compile.  A file is also the artefact you want when a build fails.
    #
    # Each cl invocation is ONE physical line, with `< nul` on it.  Two reasons,
    # and both cost a debugging session the first time: a batch file does not
    # continue an argument list across a line break without a trailing caret, so
    # a multi-line command silently becomes "cl.exe" plus a stray redirect; and
    # cl with no input file waits on stdin rather than exiting, so a malformed
    # invocation hangs the build instead of failing it.
    $lines = @(
        '@echo off',
        "call `"$vcvars`" >nul",
        'if errorlevel 1 exit /b 2',
        ('cl.exe ' + $sizeProbeArgs + ' < nul > "' + $logPath + '" 2>&1'),
        'if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1',
        ('"' + (Join-Path $objDir 'SizeProbe.exe') + '" > "' + $sizeLog + '"'),
        'if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1',
        ('cl.exe ' + $ourArgs + ' < nul >> "' + $logPath + '" 2>&1'),
        'if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1',
        ('cl.exe ' + $mhArgs + ' < nul >> "' + $logPath + '" 2>&1'),
        'if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1',
        ('link.exe ' + $linkArgs + ' < nul >> "' + $logPath + '" 2>&1'),
        'exit /b %errorlevel%'
    )
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $bat -Value $lines -Encoding ASCII
    Write-Note "compiling $($sources.Count) hook source(s) at /W4 /WX, then $($minhookSources.Count) MinHook source(s) at /W3"

    $prevEap = $ErrorActionPreference
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
    & cmd.exe /c "`"$bat`""
    $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEap
    $clExit = $LASTEXITCODE

    $clOut = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $logPath) { Get-Content -LiteralPath $logPath } else { @() }
    $clOut | Where-Object { $_ -match ': error|: warning|fatal error|error LNK|error C' } | Select-Object -First 60 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }

    # The compiler's own view of the layout, checked against the generator's
    # prediction.  This is the check that caught the two wrong strides, and it is
    # a build step rather than a comment because "the model is right" is exactly
    # the assumption that was wrong twice.
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sizeLog) {
        Write-Note 'compiler-reported layout:'
        Get-Content -LiteralPath $sizeLog | ForEach-Object { Write-Note ("  " + $_) }
        $reported = @{}
        foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $sizeLog)) {
            $parts = $line -split '\s+'
            if ($parts.Count -ge 2) { $reported[$parts[0]] = [int]$parts[1] }
        }
        $declared = 0
        if ($reported.ContainsKey('DRELAY_SHARED_SIZE')) { $declared = $reported['DRELAY_SHARED_SIZE'] }
        if ($reported.ContainsKey('DrelayShared') -and $declared -ne 0 -and $reported['DrelayShared'] -ne $declared) {
            Write-Bad ("the compiler says sizeof(DrelayShared) = $($reported['DrelayShared']) but the header " +
                       "declares DRELAY_SHARED_SIZE = $declared")
            $failures += 'sizeof'
        }
    } elseif ($clExit -eq 0) {
        Write-Bad 'the size probe did not produce sizeof.txt'
        $failures += 'sizeof-probe'
    }

    if ($clExit -ne 0) {
        Write-Bad "native build FAILED (toolchain exit $clExit); full log: $logPath"
        $clOut | Select-Object -Last 40 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
        $failures += 'native'
    } else {
        $dll = Join-Path $outDir 'Drelay.Hook.dll'
        $size = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $dll).Length
        Write-Ok ("native: {0} ({1:N0} bytes)" -f $dll, $size)
        Write-Note ("  compiler: " + (($clOut | Select-String -Pattern 'Microsoft \(R\) C/C\+\+').Line | Select-Object -First 1))
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Managed: Drelay.Bootstrap.dll and Drelay.Launcher.exe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ($doManaged) {
    Write-Step '--- managed: Drelay.Bootstrap.dll + Drelay.Launcher.exe ---'

    if (-not (Get-Command dotnet -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        Write-Bad 'dotnet not on PATH.'
        exit 2
    }

    $managedDir = Join-Path $root 'managed'
    foreach ($proj in @('Drelay.Bootstrap', 'Drelay.Launcher')) {
        $projPath = Join-Path $managedDir "$proj\$proj.csproj"
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $projPath)) { Write-Bad "missing project: $projPath"; exit 1 }
        Write-Note "building $proj"
        $dotnetOut = & dotnet build $projPath -c Release -v minimal --nologo 2>&1
        $dotnetExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        if ($dotnetExit -ne 0) {
            Write-Bad "$proj build FAILED"
            $dotnetOut | Select-Object -Last 40 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
            $failures += $proj
        } else {
            Write-Ok "$proj built"
        }
    }

    # The projects build into `bin\Release` directly (AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath
    # is off precisely so that this path is stable), and the hook needs both DLLs
    # beside the launcher, which is also where the native DLL lands.  Copying
    # explicitly rather than publishing keeps the output a flat directory of
    # exactly the files that must travel together, which is what makes "copy this
    # directory next to the game and run the launcher" true.
    if ($failures.Count -eq 0) {
        foreach ($pair in @(
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Bootstrap\bin\Release\Drelay.Bootstrap.dll'; To = 'Drelay.Bootstrap.dll' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Bootstrap\bin\Release\Drelay.Bootstrap.deps.json'; To = 'Drelay.Bootstrap.deps.json' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Bootstrap\bin\Release\Drelay.Bootstrap.pdb'; To = 'Drelay.Bootstrap.pdb'; Optional = $true },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Launcher\bin\Release\Drelay.Launcher.exe'; To = 'Drelay.Launcher.exe' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Launcher\bin\Release\Drelay.Launcher.dll'; To = 'Drelay.Launcher.dll' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Launcher\bin\Release\Drelay.Launcher.runtimeconfig.json'; To = 'Drelay.Launcher.runtimeconfig.json' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Launcher\bin\Release\Drelay.Launcher.deps.json'; To = 'Drelay.Launcher.deps.json' },
            @{ From = 'Drelay.Launcher\bin\Release\Drelay.Launcher.pdb'; To = 'Drelay.Launcher.pdb'; Optional = $true }
        )) {
            $src = Join-Path $managedDir $pair.From
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $src) {
                Copy-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination (Join-Path $outDir $pair.To) -Force
            } elseif (-not $pair.Optional) {
                Write-Bad "expected build output is missing: $src"
                $failures += $pair.To
            }
        }
    }

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Spike 3.2's offline half: SolverHarness, which is NOT part of the hook.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    #
    # IT IS BUILT HERE ANYWAY, AND NOT COPIED TO `out`.  The harness compiles the same two source
    # files the solver does (`DodgeSnapshot.cs`, `DodgeSolver.cs`) rather than referencing the
    # hook's DLL, so building it is the check that the solver is still a pure function of plain
    # data -- a change that reaches for a game type breaks this build, and that is exactly the
    # moment to find out.  It stays out of `out` because `out` is the directory that gets copied
    # next to the game, and a test program has no business there.
    $harnessProj = Join-Path $root 'tools\SolverHarness\SolverHarness.csproj'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $harnessProj) {
        Write-Note 'building SolverHarness (Spike 3.2 offline)'
        $harnessOut = & dotnet build $harnessProj -c Release -v minimal --nologo 2>&1
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            Write-Bad 'SolverHarness build FAILED -- and because it compiles the solver''s own source,'
            Write-Bad 'that means the pure-data contract is broken, not that the harness is wrong.'
            $harnessOut | Select-Object -Last 30 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
            $failures += 'SolverHarness'
        } else {
            Write-Ok 'SolverHarness built'
        }
    }

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The launcher's configuration, offline: LauncherHarness, also NOT part of the hook.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    #
    # SAME ARGUMENT AS THE HARNESS ABOVE.  It compiles the launcher's own settings, config reader,
    # command-line parser, discovery walk and environment builder, so building it is the check that
    # those files are still a pure function of their inputs -- a change that reaches for the
    # registry, the console or the game breaks this build rather than the live one (the registry
    # itself is behind `DiscoveryWindows.cs`, which this project deliberately does not compile).
    # `Test-HookOffline.ps1` runs its C1..C8 invariants.
    $launcherHarnessProj = Join-Path $root 'tools\LauncherHarness\LauncherHarness.csproj'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcherHarnessProj) {
        Write-Note 'building LauncherHarness (the launcher configuration, offline)'
        $launcherHarnessOut = & dotnet build $launcherHarnessProj -c Release -v minimal --nologo 2>&1
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            Write-Bad 'LauncherHarness build FAILED -- and because it compiles the launcher''s own'
            Write-Bad 'configuration sources, that means their pure-input contract is broken.'
            $launcherHarnessOut | Select-Object -Last 30 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
            $failures += 'LauncherHarness'
        } else {
            Write-Ok 'LauncherHarness built'
        }
    }
}

Write-Host ''
if ($failures.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Bad ("BUILD FAILED: " + ($failures -join ', '))
    exit 1
}

# Stamp the output with what it is. A hook build is only meaningful against one pinned build of one
# game, and the two facts a reader of `out\` needs -- which hook this is, and which game build it was
# compiled against -- are not visible in a directory listing of three DLLs and an exe. Written from
# the same two sources the build itself used, so the stamp cannot disagree with what was built.
$versionPath = Join-Path $root 'version.txt'
$version = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $versionPath) {
    (Get-Content -LiteralPath $versionPath -Raw).Trim()
} else { 'unversioned' }
$gameVersion = 'unknown'
$recordPath = Join-Path $root 'known-build.json'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $recordPath) {
    $gameVersion = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $recordPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).game.version
}
$stamp = @(
    "drelay hook $version",
    "game build: Darza's Dominion $gameVersion",
    "built: $((Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ'))"
) -join "`n"
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $outDir 'VERSION.txt'), $stamp + "`n", [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
Write-Note "  stamped out\VERSION.txt as drelay hook $version (game build $gameVersion)"

Write-Ok "build OK -- output in $outDir"
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $outDir -File |
    Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.dll', '.exe' } |
    Sort-Object Name |
    ForEach-Object { Write-Host ("  {0,-28} {1,10:N0} bytes" -f $_.Name, $_.Length) }
exit 0

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/AutoAim.cs`:

```cs
// AutoAim.cs -- the hook's auto-aim module, and the replacement that decides what the
// player shoots at.
//
// WHAT THE CLIENT ALREADY HAS, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH.
//
// The game ships a complete aimbot.  `AimbotSystem.FindTarget(Player, World)`
// (`Game/AimbotSystem.cs:179`) collects every live, non-NPC enemy inside the equipped
// weapon's own range, keeps the ones within a cone of the local aim direction, and picks
// one according to `Prefs.aimbot_priority_mode`; `AimbotSystem.CalculateAimAngle` then
// leads the target for projectile travel, wands, curves, orbits and homing; and
// `Player.Shoot` (`Objects/Entities/Player.cs:2970`) uses that angle instead of the
// mouse's when the whole path is enabled.  None of that is reproduced here.  This module
// **replaces the selection and nothing else**, so the client's own aiming arithmetic, its
// own projectile model and its own target highlight are all still the ones doing the work
// -- the same "call it, do not reimplement it" rule the dodge's damage and trajectory
// paths follow.
//
// What is missing on a desktop install is not the machinery but the two gates in front
// of it:
//
//   1. THE CONE.  The candidate list is filtered by
//      `abs(angleToEnemy - aimDirection) <= min(player.AimAssist * pi / 20, pi)`
//      (`Game/AimbotSystem.cs:293`).  `player.AimAssist` is rebuilt from the equipped
//      gear (`Player.RecalculateAimAssist`, `Objects/Entities/Player.cs:7113`), so a
//      player with no aim-assist affix has a cone of exactly zero and the shipped aimbot
//      finds nothing at all -- the gear enchantment is what makes it appear to work, and
//      only for the enemies the mouse is already near.  A replacement that returns the
//      target itself answers to no cone, which is the full 360 degrees this module is
//      for.
//
//   2. THE FLAG.  `Prefs.enable_aimbot` gates `AimbotSystem.UpdateTarget` -- which is
//      what calls this method -- and `Player.Shoot`, which is what uses its answer.  The
//      property is backed by `GameSettings`, i.e. the game's own settings store, so
//      arming it is a real settings change and it is treated as one below.
//
// THE THREE DECISIONS THIS MODULE ADDS, AND NOTHING ELSE:
//
//   * target the CLOSEST damageable enemy in range (`--autoaim closest`);
//   * target the enemy with the MOST HEALTH in range (`--autoaim highesthp`);
//   * never target something that cannot be damaged.
//
// THE INVULNERABILITY RULE IS THE CLIENT'S OWN AND NOT A LIST OF MAGIC NUMBERS.
// `Entity.Effects.Unhittable()` (`Objects/Components/StatusEffects.cs:150`) is the
// predicate the client itself uses when it decides a health bar is drawn as
// invulnerable, and it answers true for `Invincible`, `Invulnerable` and `Cutscene`.
// Asking it means the module cannot disagree with the client about what "cannot be
// damaged" means, and it keeps being right if the game ever adds a fourth.
//
// WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO.
//
//   * It does not use the client's enemy-priority table (`GetEnemyPriority`).  That
//     table ranks enemies by their `Exp` string and returns zero for anything it does
//     not recognise, which would silently drop enemies the operator asked to target.
//     The two modes here are the literal rules the operator asked for.
//   * It does not aim through its own geometry or lead its own projectiles -- see above.
//   * It does not run at all unless the launcher passed `--autoaim`.  The replacement is
//     published on every run so the plumbing is exercised, but the native side only aims
//     MinHook's `jmp` at it when the switch is set.
//
// FAILURE IS SILENT TO THE GAME AND LOUD IN THE LOG.  Every path that cannot reach the
// original calls through instead, anything thrown is caught and logged once, and the
// worst case is the client's own cone-limited selection -- never a suppressed call and
// never an exception escaping into a frame.

using System;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using System.Threading;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    public static class AutoAim
    {
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // The two modes, and the spellings the operator may use.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        internal const int ModeOff = 0;
        internal const int ModeClosest = 1;
        internal const int ModeHighestHealth = 2;

        /// <summary>
        /// The target `FindTarget` returns nothing for is chosen with no radius at all: this
        /// is the value `AimbotSystem.CalculateWeaponRange` itself returns for a blank or
        /// unreadable weapon (`Game/AimbotSystem.cs:172`), and the client's own range for
        /// that case is this, scaled and clamped by the same two constants below.
        /// </summary>
        private const float DefaultWeaponRange = 5.0f;

        /// <summary>The two constants in `AimbotSystem`'s own selection range (`:293-294`).</summary>
        private const float RangeScale = 1.15f;
        private const float RangeMin = 1.5f;
        private const float RangeMax = 10.0f;

        private const BindingFlags Any =
            BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Static;

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Configuration and state.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static int _mode = ModeOff;
        private static string _modeText = "";
        private static bool _resolved;
        private static string _unresolvedReason;
        private static string _statusLine = "auto-aim: not resolved";

        private static int _loggedEntry;
        private static int _loggedUnresolvedEntry;
        private static int _loggedTrouble;
        private static int _loggedNoTrampoline;
        private static int _loggedFlagForced;
        private static bool _loggedFlagOriginal;

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // The game's own accessors, resolved once on the resolve callback.
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static IntPtr _getEnemies;        // Enemy[] World.GetEnemies()
        private static Func<object, float> _getX;
        private static Func<object, float> _getY;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getDead;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getNpc;
        private static Func<object, double> _getHealth;
        private static Func<object, double> _getMaxHealth;
        private static Func<object, object> _getEffects;
        private static Func<object, object> _getItems;
        private static IntPtr _unhittable;        // bool StatusEffects.Unhittable()
        private static IntPtr _getItemData;       // ItemData Item.get_Data()
        private static IntPtr _getItemBlank;      // bool Item.get_IsBlank()
        private static IntPtr _weaponRange;       // float AimbotSystem.CalculateWeaponRange(EquipmentData)
        private static Type _equipmentDataType;
        private static IntPtr _getAimbotFlag;     // bool Prefs.get_enable_aimbot()
        private static IntPtr _setAimbotFlag;     // void Prefs.set_enable_aimbot(bool)

        /// <summary>Where the module stands, for the run's own log.</summary>
        public static string Status()
        {
            return _statusLine;
        }

        /// <summary>Why the module is not available; null when it is.</summary>
        public static string UnresolvedReason
        {
            get { return _unresolvedReason; }
        }

        // ==================================================================
        // Resolve
        // ==================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// Parse the mode and find every accessor the selection needs.
        ///
        /// RETURNS FALSE WITH A REASON RATHER THAN THROWING, for the same reason the
        /// steering pilot does: this is one module inside a hook that has other work to do,
        /// and nothing about it is allowed to cost the frame read, the patch or the game.
        /// The replacement is published either way -- a module that resolved nothing calls
        /// through on every frame, which is exactly what not being installed looks like.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool Resolve(Assembly game)
        {
            try
            {
                _modeText = (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DRELAY_AIM_MODE") ?? "").Trim();
                _mode = ParseMode(_modeText);

                if (_mode == ModeOff)
                {
                    _resolved = true;
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: off"
                                  + (_modeText.Length == 0 ? " (DRELAY_AIM_MODE unset)"
                                                           : " ('" + _modeText + "' is not a mode)");
                    return true;
                }

                if (game == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "the game assembly is not loaded";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                Type worldType = game.GetType(ManagedArmingProbe.WorldTypeName);
                Type playerType = game.GetType(ManagedArmingProbe.PlayerTypeName);
                Type aimbotType = game.GetType("DarzasDominion.Darza.Game.AimbotSystem");
                Type prefsType = game.GetType("DarzasDominion.Data.Prefs");
                _equipmentDataType = game.GetType("DarzaCore.Data.Items.EquipmentData");

                if (worldType == null || playerType == null || aimbotType == null
                    || prefsType == null || _equipmentDataType == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "type(s) not found:"
                        + (worldType == null ? " World" : "")
                        + (playerType == null ? " Player" : "")
                        + (aimbotType == null ? " AimbotSystem" : "")
                        + (prefsType == null ? " Prefs" : "")
                        + (_equipmentDataType == null ? " EquipmentData" : "");
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                // `GetEnemies` is the same call the client's own selection makes, so the
                // module sees exactly the set of enemies the client does -- no second
                // notion of "what is in the world" to drift from it.
                MethodInfo getEnemies = worldType.GetMethod(
                    "GetEnemies", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Instance, null, Type.EmptyTypes, null);
                if (getEnemies == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "World.GetEnemies() not found";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }
                Type enemyType = getEnemies.ReturnType.GetElementType();
                _getEnemies = getEnemies.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();

                FieldInfo positionField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "Position");
                FieldInfo positionX = positionField != null ? positionField.FieldType.GetField("X") : null;
                FieldInfo positionY = positionField != null ? positionField.FieldType.GetField("Y") : null;
                FieldInfo deadField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "Dead");
                FieldInfo npcField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "Npc");
                FieldInfo healthField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "Health");
                FieldInfo maxHealthField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "MaxHealth");
                FieldInfo effectsField = FieldLookup.Find(enemyType, out _, "Effects");

                string missing = "";
                if (positionField == null || positionX == null || positionY == null)
                {
                    missing += " Position.X/Y";
                }
                if (deadField == null) { missing += " Dead"; }
                if (npcField == null) { missing += " Npc"; }
                if (healthField == null) { missing += " Health"; }
                // `MaxHealth` is read for the evidence only -- the selection is on current
                // health -- so its absence is a gap in the log line and not a refusal.
                if (effectsField == null) { missing += " Effects"; }
                if (missing.Length != 0)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "field(s) not found on " + enemyType.Name + ":" + missing;
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                MethodInfo unhittable = effectsField.FieldType.GetMethod(
                    "Unhittable", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Instance, null, Type.EmptyTypes, null);
                if (unhittable == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = effectsField.FieldType.Name + ".Unhittable() not found";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                // THE WEAPON, FOR THE ONE THING THE CLIENT'S OWN RANGE DOES THAT A
                // CONSTANT CANNOT: a melee weapon and a long staff have ranges an order of
                // magnitude apart, so aiming at a target the equipped weapon cannot reach
                // would stop the player attacking the one beside them. `Player.Items` is a
                // field on `Character`, and `Item.Data`/`Item.IsBlank` are properties --
                // the same three lookups `AimbotSystem`'s own range helper makes.
                FieldInfo itemsField = FieldLookup.Find(playerType, out _, "Items");
                if (itemsField == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "Player.Items not found";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }
                Type itemType = itemsField.FieldType.GetElementType();
                PropertyInfo itemData = itemType != null ? itemType.GetProperty("Data", Any) : null;
                PropertyInfo itemBlank = itemType != null ? itemType.GetProperty("IsBlank", Any) : null;
                MethodInfo weaponRange = aimbotType.GetMethod(
                    "CalculateWeaponRange", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static, null,
                    new[] { _equipmentDataType }, null);
                if (itemType == null || itemData == null || itemBlank == null || weaponRange == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "the weapon chain is incomplete (Item."
                        + (itemData == null ? "Data" : "")
                        + (itemBlank == null ? (itemData == null ? " and " : "") + "IsBlank" : "")
                        + (weaponRange == null ? (itemData == null || itemBlank == null ? " and " : "")
                                               + "AimbotSystem.CalculateWeaponRange" : "")
                        + " not found)";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                PropertyInfo aimbotFlag = prefsType.GetProperty("enable_aimbot", Any);
                MethodInfo aimbotFlagGet = aimbotFlag != null ? aimbotFlag.GetGetMethod(true) : null;
                MethodInfo aimbotFlagSet = aimbotFlag != null ? aimbotFlag.GetSetMethod(true) : null;
                if (aimbotFlagGet == null || aimbotFlagSet == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "Prefs.enable_aimbot is not a readable/writable property";
                    _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                    return false;
                }

                // THE DELEGATES, NOT `FieldInfo.GetValue`. A reflective read on the frame
                // path boxes, and Phase 2 measured what that costs; `FieldAccessor` emits
                // one `ldfld`-shaped delegate per accessor instead. The method handles below
                // are raw calls because a delegate cannot take an `object` receiver for a
                // method declared on a game type the hook cannot name -- the same reason
                // `CollisionObservation` takes its receiver as `object`.
                _getX = FieldAccessor.NestedFloat(positionField, positionX);
                _getY = FieldAccessor.NestedFloat(positionField, positionY);
                _getDead = FieldAccessor.Bool(deadField);
                _getNpc = FieldAccessor.Bool(npcField);
                _getHealth = FieldAccessor.Double(healthField);
                _getMaxHealth = maxHealthField != null ? FieldAccessor.Double(maxHealthField) : null;
                _getEffects = FieldAccessor.Reference(effectsField);
                _getItems = FieldAccessor.Reference(itemsField);
                _unhittable = unhittable.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
                _getItemData = itemData.GetGetMethod(true).MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
                _getItemBlank = itemBlank.GetGetMethod(true).MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
                _weaponRange = weaponRange.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
                _getAimbotFlag = aimbotFlagGet.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
                _setAimbotFlag = aimbotFlagSet.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();

                _resolved = true;
                _statusLine = "auto-aim: " + ModeName(_mode)
                              + " over every damageable enemy within the equipped weapon's range"
                              + " (Player.AimAssist is not consulted; that is the cone this replaces)";
                return true;
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _unresolvedReason = "resolving the module threw: " + HookEntry.FirstFrames(ex);
                _statusLine = "auto-aim: NOT available -- " + _unresolvedReason;
                return false;
            }
        }

        private static int ParseMode(string text)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(text))
            {
                return ModeOff;
            }
            switch (text.Trim().ToLowerInvariant())
            {
                case "off":
                case "none":
                    return ModeOff;
                case "closest":
                case "close":
                case "nearest":
                    return ModeClosest;
                case "highesthp":
                case "highest-hp":
                case "highest":
                case "maxhp":
                case "max-hp":
                    return ModeHighestHealth;
                default:
                    return ModeOff;
            }
        }

        private static string ModeName(int mode)
        {
            switch (mode)
            {
                case ModeClosest: return "closest";
                case ModeHighestHealth: return "highest-hp";
                default: return "off";
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Log what was resolved, once, on the resolve callback. The mode alone is not
        /// enough: "highest-hp" reads identically whether the range came from the equipped
        /// weapon or from the fallback, and those two aim at different things.
        /// </summary>
        public static void LogPlan()
        {
            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "auto-aim plan: " + _statusLine);
            if (_mode != ModeOff && _resolved)
            {
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "auto-aim: the game's own AimbotSystem.UpdateTarget calls "
                                           + "AimbotSystem.FindTarget once per World.Update; this "
                                           + "replacement answers that call, so the client's own "
                                           + "leading, projectile model and target highlight are "
                                           + "unchanged");
            }
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        // ==================================================================
        // The managed replacement
        // ==================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// `AimbotSystem.FindTarget(Player, World)`, replaced.
        ///
        /// THE SIGNATURE IS THE ABI AND NOT A STYLE CHOICE. The target is `public static` and
        /// takes two managed references and returns one, so on x64 the arguments arrive in
        /// RCX and RDX and the answer leaves in RAX. Taking them as `object` is the same
        /// registers with a cast the JIT would have done anyway, and it is what lets this
        /// method read the player and the enemies through managed accessors instead of
        /// reinterpreting addresses -- the route `CollisionObservation.HitCharacterReplacement`
        /// already takes for its receiver.
        ///
        /// `NoInlining` because the published entry point is this method's own code: a JIT
        /// that inlined it into its caller would leave `GetFunctionPointer` pointing at a
        /// method nobody enters.
        /// </summary>
        [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
        public static object FindTargetReplacement(object player, object world)
        {
            if (_mode == ModeOff)
            {
                return CallOriginal(player, world);
            }

            if (!_resolved)
            {
                // ENTERED AND CANNOT ACT, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM NOT BEING ENTERED.
                // The launcher refuses an unknown mode, so on a real session this means the
                // *build* moved under the hook: a field renamed, a type gone. It is also the
                // line the injection suite's own run 13 asserts on, because the synthetic
                // host is not the game and resolves none of it -- which is what makes
                // "patched and entered" measurable without an AimbotSystem to select from.
                // The reason is named either way, so a session that aims at nothing is not
                // left looking like a module that decided there was no target.
                if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref _loggedUnresolvedEntry, 1) == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "auto-aim: the replacement was entered, but the "
                                                + "module did not resolve (" + (_unresolvedReason
                                                ?? "no reason recorded")
                                                + "); the client's own selection runs instead");
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
                return CallOriginal(player, world);
            }

            try
            {
                // THE FLAG IS RE-ASSERTED HERE AND NOT ONLY AT RESOLVE. It is the game's own
                // setting, and the options menu writes it back from its own control, so a
                // session that opens that menu while the client's stored value was off would
                // clear it -- and with it the only call that ever reaches this method. The
                // check is one call and the write happens only when it is actually off.
                EnsureAimbotFlag();

                object chosen = Choose(player, world);
                if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref _loggedEntry, 1) == 0)
                {
                    // ONE LINE, ONCE, AND IT CARRIES THE FIRST CHOICE RATHER THAN ONLY THE
                    // FACT THAT THE REPLACEMENT RAN. "entered" alone cannot be told apart
                    // from "entered and chose nothing every frame", and the first choice's
                    // health is the number that says the module is reading the enemy it
                    // thinks it is. This is also the only place `MaxHealth` is read: the
                    // selection itself is on current health, so a target line that shows
                    // `143/143` rather than `143/600` is what tells those two apart.
                    string detail;
                    if (chosen == null)
                    {
                        detail = "no damageable enemy was inside the weapon's range on that frame";
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        double health = _getHealth(chosen);
                        string max = _getMaxHealth == null
                            ? "?"
                            : _getMaxHealth(chosen).ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                        detail = "the first target is at " + health.ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)
                                 + "/" + max + " health, "
                                 + _getX(chosen).ToString("0.##", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + ","
                                 + _getY(chosen).ToString("0.##", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                    }
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "auto-aim: the replacement answered its first call "
                                               + "in " + ModeName(_mode) + " mode; " + detail);
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
                return chosen;
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref _loggedTrouble, 1) == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "auto-aim: selecting a target threw; the client's "
                                                + "own selection runs instead from here on -- "
                                                + HookEntry.FirstFrames(ex));
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
                return CallOriginal(player, world);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Continue into the real method, through MinHook's trampoline.
        ///
        /// A ZERO TRAMPOLINE MEANS THE HOOK WAS ENABLED WITHOUT THE BOOTSTRAP'S ADDRESS BEING
        /// PUBLISHED FIRST, which the native side orders explicitly. Returning null rather
        /// than calling nothing is the honest answer: "no target" is a state the game already
        /// handles on every frame with nothing in range.
        /// </summary>
        private static object CallOriginal(object player, object world)
        {
            long trampoline = Marshal.ReadInt64(HookEntry.SharedBlockPointer,
                                                GeneratedLayout.Off_managedAimTrampoline);
            if (trampoline == 0)
            {
                if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref _loggedNoTrampoline, 1) == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "auto-aim: the replacement ran with no trampoline "
                                                + "published; the client's selection cannot run, so "
                                                + "no target is chosen on this frame");
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
                return null;
            }
            unsafe
            {
                return ((delegate* managed<object, object, object>)(IntPtr)trampoline)(player, world);
            }
        }

        // ==================================================================
        // The selection
        // ==================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// The rule, applied to the client's own enemy list.
        ///
        /// NO CONE, NO PRIORITY TABLE, NO SHOT GEOMETRY -- the filters are the four that
        /// follow from "target something that can be damaged and can be reached":
        /// not null, not dead, not an NPC, not un-hittable, and within the equipped weapon's
        /// range. Everything else is the score.
        /// </summary>
        private static object Choose(object player, object world)
        {
            if (player == null || world == null || _getEnemies == IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                return null;
            }

            // `GetEnemies` caches its array on the world and rebuilds it only when the
            // enemy dictionary changes, so this is the same allocation the client's own
            // selection makes once per frame and not a second one.
            object raw;
            unsafe
            {
                raw = ((delegate* managed<object, object>)(IntPtr)_getEnemies)(world);
            }
            object[] enemies = raw as object[];
            if (enemies == null || enemies.Length == 0)
            {
                return null;
            }

            float px = _getX(player);
            float py = _getY(player);
            float range = WeaponRange(player);
            float rangeSq = range * range;

            object best = null;
            float bestDistanceSq = float.MaxValue;
            double bestHealth = double.MinValue;

            for (int i = 0; i < enemies.Length; i++)
            {
                object enemy = enemies[i];
                if (enemy == null) { continue; }
                if (_getDead(enemy)) { continue; }
                if (_getNpc(enemy)) { continue; }
                if (Unhittable(enemy)) { continue; }

                float dx = _getX(enemy) - px;
                float dy = _getY(enemy) - py;
                float d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
                // Written this way so a NaN coordinate -- which no frame has produced yet --
                // fails the test instead of passing it.
                if (!(d2 <= rangeSq)) { continue; }

                if (_mode == ModeClosest)
                {
                    if (d2 < bestDistanceSq)
                    {
                        bestDistanceSq = d2;
                        best = enemy;
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    double hp = _getHealth(enemy);
                    if (hp > bestHealth || (hp == bestHealth && d2 < bestDistanceSq))
                    {
                        bestHealth = hp;
                        bestDistanceSq = d2;
                        best = enemy;
                    }
                }
            }

            return best;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// `Effects.Unhittable()` -- the client's own "this cannot be damaged" predicate.
        ///
        /// A MISSING EFFECTS OBJECT IS TREATED AS HITTABLE. `Entity` creates its
        /// `StatusEffects` in its constructor, so a null one means an object that is being
        /// torn down; refusing to aim at it and refusing to aim at everything would be the
        /// same choice made twice, and the cheap one is to let the other filters decide.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool Unhittable(object enemy)
        {
            object effects = _getEffects(enemy);
            if (effects == null)
            {
                return false;
            }
            unsafe
            {
                return ((delegate* managed<object, bool>)(IntPtr)_unhittable)(effects);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The client's own selection radius: `clamp(CalculateWeaponRange(weapon) * 1.15,
        /// 1.5, 10)` (`Game/AimbotSystem.cs:293-294`, and `:392` for the same three numbers
        /// around the same call).
        ///
        /// THE SAME FUNCTION IS CALLED RATHER THAN ITS RESULT RE-DERIVED. It samples every
        /// projectile's position over its lifetime, so it already knows about wavy, orbiting,
        /// boomerang and accelerating weapons -- and reimplementing that here is exactly how
        /// this module would come to disagree with the client about whether a target is
        /// reachable.
        /// </summary>
        private static float WeaponRange(object player)
        {
            float raw = DefaultWeaponRange;
            try
            {
                object[] items = _getItems(player) as object[];
                object weapon = (items != null && items.Length > 0) ? items[0] : null;
                if (weapon != null)
                {
                    bool blank;
                    unsafe
                    {
                        blank = ((delegate* managed<object, bool>)(IntPtr)_getItemBlank)(weapon);
                    }
                    if (!blank)
                    {
                        object data;
                        unsafe
                        {
                            data = ((delegate* managed<object, object>)(IntPtr)_getItemData)(weapon);
                        }
                        if (data != null && _equipmentDataType.IsInstanceOfType(data))
                        {
                            unsafe
                            {
                                raw = ((delegate* managed<object, float>)(IntPtr)_weaponRange)(data);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            catch
            {
                // A weapon that cannot be read costs the range, not the frame: the fallback
                // is the client's own answer for "no weapon", and the log line below says
                // when it was used.
                raw = DefaultWeaponRange;
            }

            float range = raw * RangeScale;
            if (!(range > RangeMin)) { range = RangeMin; }
            if (range > RangeMax) { range = RangeMax; }
            return range;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Keep `Prefs.enable_aimbot` set while the module is on.
        ///
        /// THIS IS A REAL SETTING CHANGE AND IT IS NOT HIDDEN. The property is
        /// `GameSettings`-backed (`DarzasDominion.Data.Prefs`), so it is what the game's own
        /// options menu shows and what it persists -- a session that runs auto-aim leaves the
        /// in-game toggle on. There is no way around it: `Player.Shoot` checks that property
        /// before it ever asks for a target, so with it clear the module is unreachable by
        /// construction. The original value is read and logged at resolve, and the write
        /// happens only when the value is off, so the setting is not rewritten every frame.
        /// </summary>
        private static void EnsureAimbotFlag()
        {
            bool current;
            unsafe
            {
                current = ((delegate* managed<bool>)(IntPtr)_getAimbotFlag)();
            }
            if (!_loggedFlagOriginal)
            {
                _loggedFlagOriginal = true;
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "auto-aim: the in-game aimbot setting was "
                                           + (current ? "ON" : "OFF")
                                           + " when this module first ran; it is set ON while "
                                           + "auto-aim is enabled, and the game persists that "
                                           + "setting (there is no shutdown callback to restore it)");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
            }
            if (current)
            {
                return;
            }
            unsafe
            {
                ((delegate* managed<bool, void>)(IntPtr)_setAimbotFlag)(true);
            }
            if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref _loggedFlagForced, 1) == 0)
            {
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "auto-aim: re-armed the in-game aimbot setting, which "
                                           + "something in the client had cleared; the module is "
                                           + "unreachable while it is off");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// One frame's worth, called from the managed frame replacement.
        ///
        /// WHY THE MODULE NEEDS A FRAME PATH AT ALL, AND WHY `--autoaim` IMPLIES ONE.
        ///
        /// `EnsureAimbotFlag` runs here because the write it makes at *resolve* time does
        /// not survive, and that is a fact about the client rather than a precaution.
        /// `Prefs.enable_aimbot` is `GameSettings`-backed, and the game loads that store
        /// from disk once, in `DarzaWindow`'s constructor (`Graphics/DarzaWindow.cs:759`,
        /// `GameSettings.Load(FileVersions.SettingsPath)`), loading every key over whatever
        /// was there. The resolve callback runs **500 ms after the startup hook signals**
        /// (`DrelayInstall.cpp:1161`), i.e. before the entry point has even reached that
        /// constructor -- so a write made there is on the right store and is then replaced
        /// by the file's value.
        ///
        /// The consequence of getting this wrong is the quiet kind: with the flag clear,
        /// `AimbotSystem.UpdateTarget` never calls `FindTarget`, so the method is never
        /// compiled, so the detour is never matched, so nothing in the log says anything was
        /// wrong. A module that waits for a call that only happens once the flag is set has
        /// to set the flag from somewhere that does not.
        ///
        /// The frame replacement is that somewhere: it is on the game's own thread, at the
        /// top of every frame, before `World.Update` -- which is where `UpdateTarget` sits --
        /// runs. Writing from there cannot race the game's own reads of the same store, which
        /// is why the watcher thread is not allowed to do it: `GameSettings.setBool` is a
        /// `Dictionary` indexer write, and a concurrent `TryGetValue` on the game thread is
        /// the classic way to hang a process that shares no lock.
        /// </summary>
        internal static void OnFrame()
        {
            if (_mode == ModeOff || !_resolved)
            {
                return;
            }
            try
            {
                EnsureAimbotFlag();
            }
            catch
            {
                // The frame path must not throw for this. `EnsureAimbotFlag` reads and
                // writes two game members; anything it can do wrong is a refused write,
                // never the frame.
            }
        }

        // ==================================================================
        // Publishing
        // ==================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// Publish the replacement's entry point, and warm everything it calls.
        ///
        /// CALLED ON EVERY RUN, WHETHER OR NOT THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR AUTO-AIM -- the same
        /// discipline as the steering pilot's, and for the same reason: what the switch
        /// decides is whether MinHook's `jmp` is aimed here at all, and publishing on every
        /// run means the shared slot, the native dispatch and the trampoline handshake are
        /// exercised by runs that have nothing to lose by it.
        ///
        /// THE WARM-UP IS THE POINT. A method first compiled from inside a patched game
        /// method is a JIT in the middle of a frame, so every method on the selection path
        /// is prepared before the patch can go live.
        /// </summary>
        public static void Publish()
        {
            MethodInfo method = typeof(AutoAim).GetMethod(
                nameof(FindTargetReplacement), BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static);
            if (method == null)
            {
                HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "auto-aim: the replacement was not found by name; "
                                            + "nothing published and the target will not be patched");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
                return;
            }

            PrepareSelectionPath();
            RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod(method.MethodHandle);

            IntPtr entry = method.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
            Marshal.WriteInt64(HookEntry.SharedBlockPointer,
                               GeneratedLayout.Off_managedAimReplacement, entry.ToInt64());
            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "managed auto-aim replacement published at 0x"
                                        + entry.ToInt64().ToString("X")
                                        + "; the native side aims MinHook's jmp at it only when "
                                        + "--autoaim asked for it");
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// `PrepareMethod` on every method the selection path calls.
        ///
        /// MATCHED BY NAME ACROSS ALL OVERLOADS, deliberately: `Type.GetMethod(name, flags)`
        /// throws `AmbiguousMatchException` the moment a second overload appears, and
        /// `SteeringPilot` lost every steering run to exactly that when a `WriteInput`
        /// overload was added. Iterating and comparing names cannot be ambiguous. The
        /// accessor delegates are absent from this list because `FieldAccessor` compiles each
        /// of them with `CreateDelegate` at resolve, where it is already too late to be a
        /// first-time cost inside a frame.
        /// </summary>
        private static void PrepareSelectionPath()
        {
            string[] names =
            {
                "FindTargetReplacement", "CallOriginal", "Choose", "Unhittable", "WeaponRange",
                "EnsureAimbotFlag", "ParseMode", "ModeName", "Status", "Resolve", "Publish",
                "OnFrame",
            };
            MethodInfo[] methods = typeof(AutoAim).GetMethods(
                BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Static);
            for (int i = 0; i < methods.Length; i++)
            {
                bool wanted = false;
                for (int n = 0; n < names.Length; n++)
                {
                    if (names[n] == methods[i].Name)
                    {
                        wanted = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (!wanted)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                try
                {
                    RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod(methods[i].MethodHandle);
                }
                catch
                {
                    // A callee that is generic or otherwise unprepared is skipped; the
                    // publish log that follows is what says the path was warmed at all.
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
