```cs
                _threatStepMs[_threatCount] = step;
                _threatSamples[_threatCount] = t.Count;
                _threatCount++;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>The threat's own speed, from its first two samples; 0 when they coincide.</summary>
        private static float SpeedOf(Trajectory t, float stepMs)
        {
            if (t.Count < 2 || stepMs <= 0.0f)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            float dx = t.Xs[1] - t.Xs[0];
            float dy = t.Ys[1] - t.Ys[0];
            return (float)Math.Sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy)) * 1000.0f / stepMs;
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // The search
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// A* from <paramref name="start"/> to <paramref name="target"/>, 8-connected with the
        /// diagonal rule, cost = distance + spacetime danger.
        ///
        /// THE DIAGONAL RULE MATTERS HERE AND IT IS NOT A DETAIL. A diagonal step is allowed only when
        /// both of its orthogonal neighbours are walkable, because the collision grid's solid cells
        /// are the walls rule 2 already refuses -- and a diagonal that passed between two solid cells
        /// would be a path through a corner the game itself would refuse to walk. That is a path the
        /// solver could follow into a wall.
        /// </summary>
        private bool Search(int start, int target)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < _cells; i++)
            {
                _closed[i] = false;
                _inOpen[i] = false;
                _gScore[i] = float.MaxValue;
                _costScore[i] = float.MaxValue;
                _cameFrom[i] = -1;
            }
            _heapCount = 0;
            _pathCount = 0;
            _nodes = 0;

            _gScore[start] = 0.0f;
            _costScore[start] = 0.0f;
            HeapPush(start, Heuristic(start, target));

            int cap = _config.PathNodeCap < 16 ? 16 : _config.PathNodeCap;
            bool found = false;

            while (_heapCount > 0)
            {
                int current = HeapPop();
                if (_closed[current])
                {
                    continue;
                }
                _closed[current] = true;
                _nodes++;

                if (current == target)
                {
                    found = true;
                    break;
                }

                if (_nodes >= cap)
                {
                    _reason = PathReason.NodeCap;
                    return false;
                }

                float g = _gScore[current];
                int cx = current % _gridW;
                int cy = current / _gridW;
                float arrivalSeconds = g / _speedPerSecond;

                for (int d = 0; d < 8; d++)
                {
                    int nx = cx + DirX[d];
                    int ny = cy + DirY[d];
                    if (nx < 0 || ny < 0 || nx >= _gridW || ny >= _gridH)
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    bool diagonal = d >= 4;
                    int nIndex = (ny * _gridW) + nx;
                    if (_closed[nIndex] || !WalkableIndex(nIndex))
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if (diagonal
                        && (!WalkableIndex((cy * _gridW) + nx) || !WalkableIndex((ny * _gridW) + cx)))
                    {
                        continue;
                    }

                    float stepLength = diagonal ? 1.41421356f : 1.0f;
                    float cellX = _grid.OriginX + nx + 0.5f;
                    float cellY = _grid.OriginY + ny + 0.5f;
                    float arrival = arrivalSeconds + (stepLength / _speedPerSecond);
                    float danger = DangerAt(cellX, cellY, arrival);
                    float cost = g + stepLength + (_config.PathStepCostWeight * danger);

                    if (cost < _costScore[nIndex])
                    {
                        _costScore[nIndex] = cost;
                        _gScore[nIndex] = g + stepLength;
                        _cameFrom[nIndex] = current;
                        HeapPush(nIndex, cost + Heuristic(nIndex, target));
                    }
                }
            }

            if (!found)
            {
                _reason = PathReason.Unreachable;
                return false;
            }

            // --- The path, from the target back to the player. ------------------------------
            //
            // THE CHAIN IS WALKED BACKWARDS AND THE LENGTHS ARE ACCUMULATED AS EUCLIDEAN STEPS, not
            // read off `_costScore`: the cost includes danger and the length is a distance, and quoting
            // a danger-weighted number as "how far the path goes" would be exactly the kind of
            // quantity confusion this project has already paid for once.
            int node = target;
            float length = 0.0f;
            while (node >= 0 && _pathCount < _cells)
            {
                _pathIndex[_pathCount++] = node;
                int parent = _cameFrom[node];
                if (parent >= 0)
                {
                    int px = parent % _gridW;
                    int py = parent / _gridW;
                    int qx = node % _gridW;
                    int qy = node / _gridW;
                    float dx = qx - px;
                    float dy = qy - py;
                    length += (float)Math.Sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy));
                }
                node = parent;
            }

            // `_pathIndex` is target-first; the caller wants it player-first, which is also the order
            // the waypoint search walks it in.
            for (int i = 0, j = _pathCount - 1; i < j; i++, j--)
            {
                int tmp = _pathIndex[i];
                _pathIndex[i] = _pathIndex[j];
                _pathIndex[j] = tmp;
            }

            // THE CORNER-CUT CHECK, ON THE PATH THAT WAS ACTUALLY RETURNED. See `WallCrossings`: the
            // diagonal rule is the only thing in this file that can put a route through a wall, so it
            // is checked on every search rather than trusted. A diagonal step whose two orthogonal
            // neighbours are both solid is the exact shape the rule exists to forbid.
            for (int i = 1; i < _pathCount; i++)
            {
                int a = _pathIndex[i - 1];
                int b = _pathIndex[i];
                int ax = a % _gridW;
                int ay = a / _gridW;
                int bx = b % _gridW;
                int by = b / _gridW;
                if (ax != bx && ay != by
                    && !WalkableIndex((ay * _gridW) + bx) && !WalkableIndex((by * _gridW) + ax))
                {
                    _stats.WallCrossings++;
                }
            }

            _length = length;
            _cost = _costScore[target];
            _reason = PathReason.Found;
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Straight-line distance to the target -- admissible, so A* returns an optimal path.
        ///
        /// THERE IS NO TIE-BREAK TOWARD THE GOAL RAY, AND ITS ABSENCE IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN
        /// OMISSION. `HANDOFF-DIRECTED-DODGE.md` section 4.2 suggests one, to make the path "go around
        /// rather than go wide". A tie-break changes WHICH of several equal-cost paths is returned,
        /// which is a second opinion about the shape of the answer riding on top of the search -- and
        /// the search already has a shape opinion, in `StepCostWeight`. Adding a second before the
        /// first has been measured would leave no way to attribute a change to either. It is the first
        /// thing to try if the measured paths go wider than the operator wants.
        /// </summary>
        private float Heuristic(int index, int target)
        {
            int ax = index % _gridW;
            int ay = index / _gridW;
            int bx = target % _gridW;
            int by = target / _gridW;
            float dx = ax - bx;
            float dy = ay - by;
            return (float)Math.Sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy));
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The danger of being at a world position at a given time, in world units of cost.
        ///
        /// IT INTERPOLATES BETWEEN SAMPLES RATHER THAN SNAPPING TO ONE. A bullet sampled at 30 ms
        /// covers up to 0.72 units between knots at 24 units/s, which is larger than the collision
        /// disc -- so a cell tested against the nearest knot alone can read "clear" for a bullet that
        /// is crossing it. The two knots either side are interpolated by time, which is the same
        /// one-clock model `PlanWalk` walks on.
        /// </summary>
        private float DangerAt(float x, float y, float seconds)
        {
            float worst = 0.0f;
            for (int i = 0; i < _threatCount; i++)
            {
                Trajectory t = _threats[i];
                float near = _threatNear[i];
                float dx0 = t.Xs[0] - x;
                float dy0 = t.Ys[0] - y;
                if ((dx0 * dx0) + (dy0 * dy0) > near * near)
                {
                    // Cheap early-out against the FIRST sample only. It is not the bound test -- the
                    // bound is per-sample and is done inside the loop below -- it is the common case:
                    // most cells are far from most bullets, and one subtraction pair per threat is all
                    // those cells cost.
                    continue;
                }

                float radius = _threatRadius[i];
                float stepMs = _threatStepMs[i];
                int samples = _threatSamples[i];
                if (samples < 1 || t == null)
                {
                    // UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- `BuildDangerEnvelope` only admits a trajectory with
                    // `Count > 0` -- and written anyway because the alternative to a guard here is an
                    // index of -1 on the game's frame path. The cost is one compare per threat per node.
                    continue;
                }
                int idx = (int)((seconds * 1000.0f) / stepMs);
                if (idx < 0)
                {
                    idx = 0;
                }
                if (idx >= samples - 1)
                {
                    // PAST THE END OF THE SAMPLES IS NOT EXTRAPOLATED. The sampler freezes a bullet at
                    // its last sample when its family declares the shot finished, and inventing motion
                    // beyond that is inventing danger -- the same rule `Trajectory.Alive` and the
                    // trust prefix already apply.
                    idx = samples - 1;
                }
                float fx = t.Xs[idx];
                float fy = t.Ys[idx];
                if (idx < samples - 1)
                {
                    float frac = ((seconds * 1000.0f) - (idx * stepMs)) / stepMs;
                    if (frac < 0.0f) { frac = 0.0f; }
                    if (frac > 1.0f) { frac = 1.0f; }
                    fx += (t.Xs[idx + 1] - fx) * frac;
                    fy += (t.Ys[idx + 1] - fy) * frac;
                }

                float dx = fx - x;
                float dy = fy - y;
                float cellDist = (float)Math.Sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy));
                if (cellDist >= near)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                // Linear in the excess, saturating at 1 for a cell the bullet's own body covers.
                float penalty = cellDist <= radius ? 1.0f : (near - cellDist) / (near - radius);
                if (penalty > worst)
                {
                    worst = penalty;
                }
            }
            return worst;
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // Grid addressing, in the game's own convention
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>Cell index of a world position, or -1 outside the window. The truncation is the game's.</summary>
        private int IndexOf(float worldX, float worldY)
        {
            int cx = (int)worldX - _grid.OriginX;
            int cy = (int)worldY - _grid.OriginY;
            if (cx < 0 || cy < 0 || cx >= _gridW || cy >= _gridH)
            {
                return -1;
            }
            return (cy * _gridW) + cx;
        }

        private bool WalkableIndex(int index)
        {
            return _grid.Cells[index] == 0;
        }

        private float WorldX(int index)
        {
            return _grid.OriginX + (index % _gridW) + 0.5f;
        }

        private float WorldY(int index)
        {
            return _grid.OriginY + (index / _gridW) + 0.5f;
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // The open set: a binary heap over (cell, key)
        // ===================================================================================

        private void HeapPush(int cell, float key)
        {
            if (_heapCount >= _heap.Length)
            {
                return;   // the buffer is sized for every cell; this cannot happen, and refusing beats growing
            }
            int i = _heapCount++;
            _heap[i] = cell;
            _heapKey[i] = key;
            while (i > 0)
            {
                int parent = (i - 1) / 2;
                if (_heapKey[parent] <= _heapKey[i])
                {
                    break;
                }
                Swap(i, parent);
                i = parent;
            }
        }

        private int HeapPop()
        {
            int top = _heap[0];
            _heapCount--;
            if (_heapCount > 0)
            {
                _heap[0] = _heap[_heapCount];
                _heapKey[0] = _heapKey[_heapCount];
                int i = 0;
                for (;;)
                {
                    int left = (2 * i) + 1;
                    int right = left + 1;
                    int smallest = i;
                    if (left < _heapCount && _heapKey[left] < _heapKey[smallest])
                    {
                        smallest = left;
                    }
                    if (right < _heapCount && _heapKey[right] < _heapKey[smallest])
                    {
                        smallest = right;
                    }
                    if (smallest == i)
                    {
                        break;
                    }
                    Swap(i, smallest);
                    i = smallest;
                }
            }
            return top;
        }

        private void Swap(int a, int b)
        {
            int c = _heap[a];
            _heap[a] = _heap[b];
            _heap[b] = c;
            float k = _heapKey[a];
            _heapKey[a] = _heapKey[b];
            _heapKey[b] = k;
        }

        private static double Elapsed(long startTicks)
        {
            return (System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp() - startTicks)
                 * (1000000.0 / System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.Frequency);
        }
    }
}


```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/Phase2Report.cs`:

```cs
// Phase2Report.cs -- the four numbers, on one line, and the histogram that makes one of
// them possible.
//
// WHY A HISTOGRAM AND NOT A MAXIMUM.
//
// The phase's exit criterion is a p99 per-frame cost, and a maximum cannot produce one.
// Phase 1 already learned this the hard way: its endurance run kept a cumulative worst
// case, its frame ring overflowed, and the single 323 microsecond sample it recorded could
// not be placed in time or in a distribution afterwards (PHASE1-VERIFICATION.md section
// 11.4).  A histogram is the smallest structure that answers "how often", and it costs a
// bucket increment on the hot path.
//
// THE EDGES ARE MICROSECONDS AND THEY ARE CHOSEN AROUND THE BUDGET.  HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md
// section 7 gives the frame tick 150 us inside a 16.7 ms frame, so the buckets crowd below
// that and stay coarse above it: what matters is knowing whether the sensor is at 10 us or
// 120, and a run that lands in the overflow bucket has already failed.
//
// A BUCKET PERCENTILE IS AN INTERVAL, NOT A POINT, AND IT IS REPORTED AS ONE.  "p99 is at
// most 20 us" is true and useful; "p99 is 17 us" would be a number the histogram cannot
// support.

using System;
using System.Globalization;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    /// <summary>Bucketed per-frame costs, in microseconds.</summary>
    public sealed class CostHistogram
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// Upper edges, in microseconds; the last bucket is everything above.
        ///
        /// THE BUDGET POINTS ARE EDGES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS ARRAY LOOKS THE
        /// WAY IT DOES.  The phase's criterion is that the per-frame cost fits the
        /// frame-tick slice, and HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 puts that slice at 150 us
        /// inside a 16.7 ms frame with a 300 us ceiling overall.  A histogram whose edges
        /// were 100 and 200 could only say "somewhere between", which is not an answer a
        /// criterion can be checked against -- and the first run of the Phase 2 session
        /// analyser produced exactly that: `sampler p99 <= 200 us`, reported as a failure
        /// when the truth was that the instrument could not decide.
        /// </summary>
        public static readonly int[] Edges = { 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 150, 300, 500, 1000, 2000 };

        private readonly long[] _counts = new long[Edges.Length + 1];

        public long Total { get; private set; }

        public void Add(long microseconds)
        {
            Total++;
            for (int i = 0; i < Edges.Length; i++)
            {
                if (microseconds <= Edges[i])
                {
                    _counts[i]++;
                    return;
                }
            }
            _counts[Edges.Length]++;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The smallest edge at or below which <paramref name="percentile"/> of the samples
        /// fall -- i.e. an upper bound on the percentile, never a point estimate.
        /// </summary>
        public int UpperBoundAt(double percentile)
        {
            if (Total == 0)
            {
                return 0;
            }
            long want = (long)Math.Ceiling(Total * percentile);
            long seen = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < _counts.Length; i++)
            {
                seen += _counts[i];
                if (seen >= want)
                {
                    return i < Edges.Length ? Edges[i] : Edges[Edges.Length - 1];
                }
            }
            return Edges[Edges.Length - 1];
        }

        /// <summary>True when the tail ran past the last edge, which is a failure and not a number.</summary>
        public bool Overflowed => _counts[Edges.Length] > 0;

        // `Edges[Edges.Length]` STOOD IN `Describe()` BELOW UNTIL 2026-10-12, AND IT
        // CRASHED THE REPORT EXACTLY WHEN THE REPORT HAD SOMETHING TO SAY.  The edges array
        // has `Edges.Length` entries, the bucket array has one more, and that expression
        // wanted the LAST EDGE while indexing one past it -- so `Describe()` threw
        // `IndexOutOfRangeException` the first time a sample landed above 2000 us, and not
        // before, because the other arm of the ternary never runs.  It was measured twice:
        //
        //   * on the live session of 2026-10-12 the report stopped after three lines
        //     (frames 300, 601 and 901 of 54 600) at the moment the read's maximum jumped
        //     from 459 us to 4 756 us, and the session's verdict then quoted the stale
        //     901-frame histogram as the phase's per-frame cost;
        //   * on the synthetic host it was reproduced in a single run, and the exception's
        //     own stack named this line -- which is why the frame path now logs its
        //     exceptions once instead of swallowing them in silence.
        //
        // An instrument that fails only on the runs that have an outlier to report is this
        // project's recurring shape, and this is its third instance.  `UpperBoundAt` above
        // had it right from the start, which is what made the mistake invisible in review.

        public string Describe()
        {
            if (Total == 0)
            {
                return "no sample";
            }
            return "n=" + Total + " p50<=" + UpperBoundAt(0.50) + "us p99<=" + UpperBoundAt(0.99)
                   + "us" + (Overflowed ? " (OVERFLOW: " + _counts[Edges.Length] + " above "
                                          + Edges[Edges.Length - 1] + "us)" : "");
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The phase's four decision numbers, in one place.
    ///
    /// IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md names them, and each decides something different: the
    /// warning distribution decides whether there is time to move (Phase 3's dodge budget
    /// and escape-floor timing), the false negatives decide whether the model is complete
    /// enough to rely on at all, the false positives decide whether a dodge would be
    /// over-cautious, and the cost decides whether the Phase 3 solver fits the frame at all.
    ///
    /// They are printed together, on one line, on purpose: a reader who has to assemble
    /// the answer from four places in a log will assemble it wrongly, and a number that
    /// cannot be read is worse than no number -- the lesson Phase 1 wrote down after
    /// `logOverflow` and `logAppendFailures` were briefly the same counter.
    /// </summary>
    public static class Phase2Report
    {
        public static void Log()
        {
            double mean = SensorRead.Threats.MeanWarningMs;
            // NO PARENTHETICAL ABOUT WHICH PROCESS THIS IS.  The first version said
            // "(synthetic host; a live game run is what these are for)", which was true
            // while the host was the only thing it had ever run in and became a lie the
            // moment the hook resolved against the real client.  The bootstrap cannot tell
            // the two apart -- it resolves whatever assembly the launcher names -- so the
            // label belongs to whoever reads the evidence, and `Run-Phase2Session.ps1`
            // supplies it.
            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "PHASE 2 NUMBERS"
                                        + " | warnings: " + SensorRead.Threats.PredictedAndHit
                                        + " predicted hit(s), mean "
                                        + mean.ToString("F1", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "ms"
                                        + " | false negatives: " + SensorRead.Threats.HitUnpredicted
                                        + " (hit, not predicted)"
                                        + " | false positives: " + SensorRead.Threats.PredictedButNeverHit
                                        + " (predicted, retired without a hit)"
                                        + " | cost: read " + SensorRead.Cost.Describe()
                                        + ", sampler " + TrajectorySampler.Cost.Describe()
                                        // THE FIFTH NUMBER, AND THE SOURCE SPLIT, ON THE SAME LINE.
                                        // PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 2 names the straight fraction
                                        // separately from the four, and the 2026-10-12 evening session
                                        // is why the split is here too: `warnings: 0` was true and
                                        // useless, and the question it could not answer -- "did the
                                        // sensor see any bullets at all?" -- is answered by
                                        // `projectiles:` below it.  A reader must not have to open a
                                        // second line to find out that the first number had nothing to
                                        // count.
                                        // THE DECISION COUNT AND ITS PROVENANCE.  The first two
                                        // numbers are the threats set's view; this is the collision
                                        // observation's own, so a reader can see how many decisions
                                        // were counted and how many of them were for a bullet the
                                        // sensor had never seen (a coverage hole, which is a
                                        // different finding from a missed prediction).
                                        + " | collisions: " + CollisionObservation.Entered
                                        + " decision(s), " + CollisionObservation.Known
                                        + " known, " + CollisionObservation.Unknown + " unknown"
                                        + " | projectiles: " + SensorRead.LayerLiveTotal
                                        + " observation(s) from the layer's " + SensorRead.LayerNodesTotal
                                        + " node(s), " + SensorRead.ObjectsLiveTotal
                                        + " from World.Objects" + (SensorRead.LayerSourceResolved
                                            ? "" : " (LAYER SOURCE DID NOT RESOLVE)")
                                        + " | linearity: " + TrajectorySampler.StraightCount
                                        + " linear, " + TrajectorySampler.CurvedCount + " not, straight fraction "
                                        + TrajectorySampler.StraightFraction.ToString("F3", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/SensorRead.cs`:

```cs
// SensorRead.cs -- the frame path's view of the world, and Phase 2's first real read.
//
// WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT YET.
//
// This walks the game's own live-object dictionary once per frame, picks out the
// projectiles, and feeds their identities to the ThreatSet.  It is the "threat set"
// half of Deliverable 2.1: the records exist, they are retired by evidence, and the
// pooling hazard is handled.  It deliberately does NOT yet sample trajectories or
// compare against the collision decision -- that is 2.2 and 2.3, and they are built on
// this, so this is the thing that has to be right first.
//
// WHERE THE LIVE PROJECTILES COME FROM, AND THE CORRECTION THIS FILE NOW CARRIES.
//
// There is no `List<Projectile>` and no projectile dictionary on `World`, and that much
// is unchanged: a projectile is an ordinary world node.  WHAT WAS WRONG IS WHERE THE
// NODE LANDS.  This file originally read `World.Objects` (a
// `Dictionary<int, GameObject>`) and filtered it by type, on CLIENT-MAP.md section
// 5.2's claim that `World.AddObject` puts a projectile there.  **It does not, and the
// 2026-10-12 evening session measured the consequence:** fifteen minutes of real play,
// 54 600 frames, a world present on every one of them, and `live=0` throughout --
// while the game's own log recorded beams, projectile lights and
// `Spawned 1 pending projectile(s) for entity 411542 (Rhinoceros)`.
//
// The static reason, from the decompiled build: `Entity.cs:1521,1550,1589` fires a
// projectile with `Projectile.Rent(...)` -> `World.GameObjectLayer.AddChild(projectile)`
// -> `projectile.World = World`, and never calls `World.AddObject`/`AddSortObject`.  Only
// `World.hehe_EB2C_E5A5_EE82_E9C5_EF78` ever writes `Objects[obj.GameId]`, and its five
// call sites are the map loader, the player, the entity spawn packets and the world's own
// spawn path -- no projectile among them.  So `World.Objects` holds the map's static
// objects plus entities, and **the live projectile set is
// `World.GameObjectLayer.Children`** (`Node._children`, which the layer's overridden
// `AddChild` reaches through `base.AddChild`).
//
// BOTH SOURCES ARE READ, AND BOTH ARE COUNTED.  This is not belt and braces: the counts
// are what closed CLIENT-MAP.md section 10.6's open experiment ("which layer live
// projectiles occupy"), and a hook that silently switched sources on the strength of a
// decompile would have replaced one unmeasured assumption with another.  The sensor line
// carries `objects_live=` and `layer_live=` separately, so the next run says which
// collection carried the bullets rather than asserting it.
//
// `Allocations.Projectiles` is still a `Pool<Projectile>` free list of recycled instances
// and must never be enumerated as "the live ones": doing so yields a threat set of dead
// objects, which presents as a dodge that reacts to bullets that are not there.
//
// BOTH SOURCES ARE SHARED WITH OTHER THINGS, so the filter is a real filter: the
// dictionary holds static and 3d objects, and the layer holds everything the world draws
// -- the player, enemies, effects, lasers and sweeps.  The synthetic host now puts
// non-projectiles in both, so a filter that never rejects anything cannot pass.
//
// WHY REFLECTION, FOR NOW, AND WHY THAT IS NOT LAZINESS.
//
// Reading a field of a type the hook cannot reference at compile time has two honest
// implementations: reflect, or resolve the field's offset once and read raw memory.  The
// project's own rule (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.5) is that offsets must be
// *measured*, never derived from declaration order, and the measurement machinery for
// reference fields and inline value types exists in StartupHook.cs already.
//
// This version reflects, and it does so on purpose: Phase 2's job is to produce four
// numbers, one of which is the per-frame cost.  A reflection-based read produces a
// correct warning distribution, correct false-negative and false-positive rates, and an
// honest -- probably bad -- cost number, and it does that without first betting the
// phase on a hand-computed offset for a private nested struct inside
// `Dictionary<int, GameObject>`.  If the cost is the problem, this file's own log says
// so, in microseconds, on every run; that is the evidence that would justify replacing
// it with the raw walk, and not a guess made before the first measurement.

using System;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Reflection;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    public static class SensorRead
    {
        /// <summary>The game's live-object dictionary type is generic; this is the field on `World`.</summary>
        public const string ProjectileTypeName = "DarzasDominion.Darza.Game.Objects.Projectile";

        private static bool _resolved;
        private static string _unresolvedReason = "not attempted";

        private static FieldInfo _sharedField;
        private static FieldInfo _objectsField;
        private static FieldInfo _layerField;
        private static FieldInfo _childrenField;
        private static FieldInfo _gameIdField;
        private static FieldInfo _startTimeField;

        // EMITTED ACCESSORS, NOT GetValue: a GetValue per field per object per frame
        // boxes every value type it returns, and the collections that causes were measured
        // in the sampler's p99 (PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 4.11).  Built once, on resolve.
        private static Func<object> _getShared;
        private static Func<object, object> _getObjects;
        private static Func<object, object> _getLayer;
        private static Func<object, object> _getChildren;
        private static Func<object, int> _getGameId;
        private static Func<object, int> _getStartTime;
        private static Type _projectileType;
        private static Type _layerType;

        internal static readonly ThreatSet Threats = new ThreatSet();

        /// <summary>
        /// The live projectile objects this frame, reused every frame rather than
        /// reallocated, and handed to the sampler.
        ///
        /// IT HOLDS REFERENCES, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.  A strong reference keeps a
        /// projectile alive for the length of the frame in which it was read, which is
        /// the frame the sampler is about to look at it in -- the alternative is a
        /// collection between the read and the sample, which would hand the sampler a
        /// bullet that has already been recycled.
        ///
        /// INTERNAL RATHER THAN PRIVATE, AND THE ONE REASON IS THE TRACE. The Spike 3.2
        /// recorder records "the bullets that could matter" from *this* frame's list, and the
        /// alternative -- walking the game's drawing layer a second time per frame -- would
        /// double the cost of a run whose purpose is to be an ordinary run. A copy would be
        /// worse than either: it would allocate once per frame forever.
        /// </summary>
        internal static readonly List<object> LiveObjects = new List<object>();

        /// <summary>The identity of each live projectile, in lockstep with LiveObjects, so the sampler can mark a prediction on the right record.</summary>
        internal static readonly List<ThreatKey> LiveKeys = new List<ThreatKey>();

        /// <summary>
        /// Which keys have already been taken from a source this frame, so the two sources
        /// cannot count the same bullet twice.  Reused, never reallocated.
        /// </summary>
        private static readonly HashSet<long> SeenKeys = new HashSet<long>();

        private static int _frame;
        private static long _framesRead;
        private static long _framesUnreconciled;

        // PER SOURCE, BECAUSE THE SPLIT IS THE MEASUREMENT.  `objects_live` and
        // `layer_live` on the sensor line are what says which collection carries the
        // bullets on this build; their sum is `live`.
        private static long _objectsLiveTotal;
        private static long _layerLiveTotal;
        private static long _layerNodesTotal;

        /// <summary>Frames whose read threw, kept apart from frames with nothing to read.</summary>
        private static long _readExceptions;
        private static long _retiredByReconcile;
        private static long _lastCostUs;
        private static long _maxCostUs;
        private static long _nextLogFrame = 150;

        /// <summary>Bucketed per-frame read cost, for the p99 the phase has to publish.</summary>
        public static readonly CostHistogram Cost = new CostHistogram();

        public static bool Resolved => _resolved;

        /// <summary>The frame counter the collision observation turns into a warning.</summary>
        public static int Frame => _frame;

        /// <summary>Identities currently believed live. Only meaningful after a frame has run.</summary>
        public static int TrackedCount => Threats.Count;

        /// <summary>
        /// Resolves the four things the read path needs, once, on the resolve callback.
        ///
        /// A FAILURE HERE IS NOT FATAL AND MUST NOT BE.  The sensor is Phase 2's; the
        /// frame read, the patch and the evidence all belong to Phase 1 and keep working
        /// without it.  So this returns false with a reason, the reason is logged, and
        /// the frame path simply does not run the sensor.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool Resolve(Assembly game)
        {
            try
            {
                Type worldType = game.GetType(ManagedArmingProbe.WorldTypeName);
                _projectileType = game.GetType(ProjectileTypeName);
                if (worldType == null || _projectileType == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "types not found: World=" + (worldType != null)
                                        + " Projectile=" + (_projectileType != null);
                    return false;
                }

                // THE NAMES ARE CANDIDATES, AND THE ONE THAT MATCHED IS LOGGED.  `GameId`
                // is declared on the base `GameObject` and `_startTime` privately on
                // `Projectile`, so a lookup that asked only one type would find half of
                // what it needs and report the other half as missing.
                string sharedName;
                string objectsName;
                string gameIdName;
                string startName;
                _sharedField = FieldLookup.Find(worldType, out sharedName, "Shared", "_shared");
                _objectsField = FieldLookup.Find(worldType, out objectsName, "Objects", "_objects");
                _gameIdField = FieldLookup.Find(_projectileType, out gameIdName,
                                                "GameId", "_gameId", "ObjectId");
                _startTimeField = FieldLookup.Find(_projectileType, out startName,
                                                   "_startTime", "StartTime", "startTime");

                if (_sharedField == null || _objectsField == null || _gameIdField == null
                    || _startTimeField == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "fields not found: World.Shared=" + (_sharedField != null)
                                        + " World.Objects=" + (_objectsField != null)
                                        + " Projectile.GameId=" + (_gameIdField != null)
                                        + " Projectile.StartTime=" + (_startTimeField != null);
                    return false;
                }

                // The dictionary must be enumerable as a non-generic IDictionary, which
                // is what lets this file walk a collection whose element type it cannot
                // name.  `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` implements it, so this is a check on
                // the game's shape rather than on ours.
                Type objectsType = _objectsField.FieldType;
                if (!typeof(IDictionary).IsAssignableFrom(objectsType))
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "World.Objects is " + objectsType.FullName
                                        + ", which is not an IDictionary";
                    return false;
                }

                _getShared = FieldAccessor.Static(_sharedField);
                _getObjects = FieldAccessor.Reference(_objectsField);
                _getGameId = FieldAccessor.Int(_gameIdField);
                _getStartTime = FieldAccessor.Int(_startTimeField);

                // THE SECOND SOURCE, AND THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY CARRIES THE BULLETS.
                // `World.GameObjectLayer` is a field whose name equals its type name, and
                // the child list hangs off `Nodes.Node`, so `_children` is found by the
                // same hierarchy walk as everything else -- `Children` is a property, and
                // `GetField` does not see properties.
                //
                // NOT FATAL IF IT DOES NOT RESOLVE, AND DELIBERATELY SO: refusing here
                // would throw away the read, the patch and the whole run over a field
                // name, and the sensor line's `layer_nodes=0 layer_live=0` says exactly
                // what happened.  What it must not do is stay quiet, so a missing layer
                // is a WARN with the reason on it.
                string layerName = "(none)";
                string childrenName = "(none)";
                _layerField = FieldLookup.Find(worldType, out layerName, "GameObjectLayer", "_gameObjectLayer");
                if (_layerField != null)
                {
                    _layerType = _layerField.FieldType;
                    _childrenField = FieldLookup.Find(_layerType, out childrenName,
                                                      "_children", "children", "Children");
                }

                if (_childrenField != null && typeof(IList).IsAssignableFrom(_childrenField.FieldType))
                {
                    _getLayer = FieldAccessor.Reference(_layerField);
                    _getChildren = FieldAccessor.Reference(_childrenField);
                }
                else
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("WARN", "the sensor could not resolve the projectile layer: "
                                                + layerName + " field=" + (_layerField != null)
                                                + ", child list=" + childrenName
                                                + (childrenName != "(none)" && !typeof(IList).IsAssignableFrom(_childrenField.FieldType)
                                                    ? " (" + _childrenField.FieldType.FullName + ", not an IList)" : "")
                                                + "; projectiles will be read from World.Objects only, "
                                                + "which the client does not populate -- expect live=0");
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }

                _resolved = true;
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "sensor read path resolved: " + objectsName
                                            + " is " + objectsType.Name + ", projectiles are "
                                            + _projectileType.FullName + " (" + FieldLookup.Hierarchy(_projectileType)
                                            + "), identity " + gameIdName + " + " + startName
                                            + "; the projectile source is "
                                            + (_getChildren != null
                                                ? layerName + "." + childrenName + " ("
                                                  + FieldLookup.Hierarchy(_layerType) + ", "
                                                  + _childrenField.FieldType.Name + ")"
                                                : "World.Objects ONLY -- the layer did not resolve"));
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
                return true;
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _unresolvedReason = ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message;
                return false;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Why the read path is not available, for the log.</summary>
        public static string UnresolvedReason => _unresolvedReason;

        /// <summary>
        /// One frame's read.  Called from the managed replacement, so its caller is
        /// managed and allocating here is safe -- it is only expensive.
        ///
        /// THE ASYMMETRY IS THE IMPORTANT PART.  If anything goes wrong -- no world, no
        /// dictionary, an exception mid-walk -- the frame is NOT reconciled.  A read that
        /// did not happen is not evidence that a bullet is gone, and reconciling anyway
        /// is how one hiccup retires every live bullet at once.
        /// </summary>
        public static void OnFrame()
        {
            if (!_resolved)
            {
                return;
            }

            _frame++;
            long t0 = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();

            Threats.BeginFrame();
            LiveObjects.Clear();
            LiveKeys.Clear();
            bool enumerationOk = false;
            int objectsLive = 0;
            int others = 0;
            int layerLive = 0;
            int layerNodes = 0;
            int layerOthers = 0;
            SeenKeys.Clear();

            try
            {
                object world = _getShared();
                if (world != null)
                {
                    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
                    // SOURCE 1: `World.Objects`.  KEPT, COUNTED, AND NOT THE PROJECTILE
                    // SET.  It is where the map's static objects and the entities live,
                    // and reading it costs a walk of a few hundred entries per frame;
                    // dropping it would throw away the measurement this correction rests
                    // on.  `objects_live` on the sensor line is what it contributed.
                    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
                    object objects = _getObjects(world);
                    IDictionary dictionary = objects as IDictionary;
                    if (dictionary != null)
                    {
                        foreach (DictionaryEntry entry in dictionary)
                        {
                            object value = entry.Value;
                            if (value == null)
                            {
                                continue;
                            }
                            if (!_projectileType.IsInstanceOfType(value))
                            {
                                others++;
                                continue;
                            }
                            if (Track(value))
                            {
                                objectsLive++;
                            }
                        }
                        enumerationOk = true;
                    }
                    else if (_framesUnreconciled == 0)
                    {
                        // WHY AN UNRECONCILED FRAME NEEDS A REASON.  The first version
                        // reported `unreconciled=N` and nothing else, and when the sensor
                        // came back with every frame unreconciled there was nothing to read:
                        // "no world yet", "a world with no object dictionary" and "the
                        // dictionary is not an IDictionary" are three different problems
                        // with three different owners, and a bare count cannot tell them
                        // apart.  This cost one diagnostic round.
                        HookEntry.AppendLog("WARN", "the sensor cannot enumerate: "
                                                    + "World.Shared is non-null but its Objects field is "
                                                    + (objects == null ? "null" : "not an IDictionary")
                                                    + " (" + (objects == null ? "null"
                                                              : objects.GetType().FullName) + ")");
                        HookEntry.FlushLog();
                    }

                    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
                    // SOURCE 2: `World.GameObjectLayer.Children`, WHICH IS WHERE THE
                    // CLIENT'S PROJECTILES ACTUALLY ARE (see the file header, and the
                    // measurement this correction comes from).
                    //
                    // INDEXED RATHER THAN ENUMERATED, AND THE COUNT IS READ ONCE.  A
                    // `foreach` over a `List<Node>` throws the moment anything is added
                    // to it, and the world is mutated on this very thread every frame --
                    // the layer is the collection the game adds bullets to.  Reading
                    // `Count` once and indexing keeps the walk bounded and cannot throw
                    // mid-enumeration.
                    //
                    // THE WALK IS O(EVERYTHING THE WORLD DRAWS) -- static objects,
                    // entities, effects, lasers and sweeps as well as bullets -- which
                    // CLIENT-MAP.md section 10.6 predicted would be the cost of reading a
                    // layer instead of a list.  The histogram on this file's own report
                    // line is where that prediction gets a number; if the p99 leaves the
                    // 150 us frame-tick slice, the next step is `_dynamicList`, which the
                    // layer keeps for exactly the nodes that move.
                    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
                    if (_getChildren != null)
                    {
                        object layer = _getLayer(world);
                        if (layer != null)
                        {
                            IList children = _getChildren(layer) as IList;
                            if (children != null)
                            {
                                int count = children.Count;
                                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
                                {
                                    object node = children[i];
                                    if (node == null)
                                    {
                                        continue;
                                    }
                                    layerNodes++;
                                    if (!_projectileType.IsInstanceOfType(node))
                                    {
                                        layerOthers++;
                                        continue;
                                    }
                                    if (Track(node))
                                    {
                                        layerLive++;
                                    }
                                }
                                enumerationOk = true;
                            }
                            else if (_framesUnreconciled == 0)
                            {
                                HookEntry.AppendLog("WARN", "the sensor cannot walk the projectile layer: "
                                                            + "its child field is "
                                                            + (_getChildren(layer) == null ? "null" : "not an IList"));
                                HookEntry.FlushLog();
                            }
                        }
                        else if (_framesUnreconciled == 0)
                        {
                            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "the sensor has a world but no GameObjectLayer yet, "
                                                        + "so only World.Objects was read this frame");
                            HookEntry.FlushLog();
                        }
                    }
                }
                else if (_framesUnreconciled == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "the sensor has no world yet: World.Shared is null, so "
                                                + "no frame is reconciled (a read that did not happen is "
                                                + "not an absence)");
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // THE FIRST EXCEPTION IS ALWAYS LOGGED, AND KEYING THAT ON THE UNRECONCILED
                // COUNT WAS A BLIND SPOT.  The frame before the world exists is unreconciled
                // for an ordinary reason -- there is nothing to read yet -- and it sets the
                // count to one; every frame after it that threw was then silent, and the
                // only symptom was `live=0 unreconciled=N` with no reason attached.  It cost
                // a diagnostic round.  Two counters, because "the world is not there yet"
                // and "the read threw" are different problems.
                _readExceptions++;
                if (_readExceptions == 1)
                {
                    // THE STACK, NOT ONLY THE TYPE.  "NullReferenceException" out of a dozen
                    // nested calls says nothing about which one; the first line of the trace
                    // says everything, and this fires once per run so it can afford the
                    // characters.
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "the sensor's frame read threw; no frame is "
                                                 + "reconciled while this lasts: " + ex.GetType().Name
                                                 + ": " + ex.Message + " | " + HookEntry.FirstFrames(ex));
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
            }

            // THE READ'S COST IS MEASURED AROUND THE READ, AND THE SAMPLER'S AROUND THE
            // SAMPLER.  The first version of this timed them as one window, and the
            // number that came out -- 300 to 1200 microseconds, against 7 to 16 for the
            // read alone -- was not the read's cost at all: it was the read plus the
            // sampler plus the gen0 collections the sampler's own boxing triggers, all
            // attributed to the read.  Two costs that are reported separately are
            // measurements; one number that contains both is a number nobody can act on.
            long t1 = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();

            if (enumerationOk)
            {
                _retiredByReconcile += Threats.Reconcile(_frame);
                _framesRead++;
                _objectsLiveTotal += objectsLive;
                _layerLiveTotal += layerLive;
                _layerNodesTotal += layerNodes;

                // Deliverable 2.2, on the set that was just read.  Only when the
                // enumeration succeeded: sampling a partial set would report a straight
                // fraction for a frame the sensor did not really see.
                TrajectorySampler.OnFrame(LiveObjects, LiveKeys, _frame);
            }
            else
            {
                Threats.NoteUnreconciledFrame();
                _framesUnreconciled++;
            }

            long frequency = Stopwatch.Frequency;
            _lastCostUs = frequency > 0 ? ((t1 - t0) * 1000000L) / frequency : 0L;
            Cost.Add(_lastCostUs);
            if (_lastCostUs > _maxCostUs)
            {
                _maxCostUs = _lastCostUs;
            }

            if (_frame >= _nextLogFrame)
            {
                _nextLogFrame += 150;
                // THE SPLIT IS APPENDED, NOT INSERTED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the field
                // order before it is what the injection suite and the session analyser
                // already parse, and a line whose meaning moves cannot be compared with
                // the runs it is being compared against.
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "sensor: frame " + _frame + ": live=" + (objectsLive + layerLive)
                                            + " other=" + others + " tracked=" + Threats.Count
                                            + " retired=" + _retiredByReconcile
                                            + " unreconciled=" + _framesUnreconciled + " threw=" + _readExceptions
                                            + " frames_read=" + _framesRead
                                            + " cost=" + _lastCostUs + "us max=" + _maxCostUs + "us"
                                            + " layer_nodes=" + layerNodes + " layer_live=" + layerLive
                                            + " layer_other=" + layerOthers + " objects_live=" + objectsLive);
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Records one projectile and returns whether it was new this frame.
        ///
        /// THE SEEN-SET IS WHY THIS EXISTS.  Two sources are walked, and a bullet that
        /// appeared in both would otherwise be counted twice, sampled twice, and would
        /// make `sampled` exceed `live` -- a comparison the injection suite uses as its
        /// witness.  `Threats.Observe` is idempotent for the record, but the lists the
        /// sampler reads are not.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool Track(object projectile)
        {
            int gameId = _getGameId(projectile);
            int startTime = _getStartTime(projectile);
            ThreatKey key = new ThreatKey(gameId, startTime);
            if (!SeenKeys.Add(key.Packed))
            {
                return false;
            }
            LiveObjects.Add(projectile);
            LiveKeys.Add(key);
            Threats.Observe(key, _frame);
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>Bullets read from `World.Objects` so far -- the source that carries none on the client.</summary>
        public static long ObjectsLiveTotal => _objectsLiveTotal;

        /// <summary>Bullets read from the world's drawing layer so far -- the source that carries them.</summary>
        public static long LayerLiveTotal => _layerLiveTotal;

        /// <summary>Nodes walked in the layer so far, bullets or not: the cost this correction buys.</summary>
        public static long LayerNodesTotal => _layerNodesTotal;

        /// <summary>True when the layer source resolved. False means `live=` is Objects-only and will read 0 on the client.</summary>
        public static bool LayerSourceResolved => _getChildren != null;
    }
}
```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/SensorSelfTest.cs`:

```cs
// SensorSelfTest.cs -- T3 and T4, run on every launch, in the bootstrap.
//
// WHY A SELF-TEST AND NOT A UNIT TEST PROJECT.
//
// The hook ships as a startup hook and a native DLL; there is no test runner in the
// process and adding one would mean a second build configuration that nobody would run.
// The project already has the pattern that fits: `selfcheck.txt` is the hook's own
// acceptance test, made of checks that run where the hook runs (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md
// section 9).  These are the same kind of check, for the two pieces of Phase 2 that are
// pure functions of plain data.
//
// WHAT THEY CATCH, AND WHY IT IS WORTH THE CODE.
//
// Both failures are invisible in a live run.  A bullet retired while it is still alive
// makes the dodge hesitate; a bullet that never retires makes it move for no reason.
// Neither looks like a defect in a log -- they look like a badly tuned dodge, which is
// the failure mode IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md section 2 says offline tests exist to prevent.
// The rules are four lines each and every one of them has a wrong version that is one
// character away.
//
// The results go into the bootstrap's log, and the injection suite asserts that the run
// reports zero failures.  A self-test that is only run by hand is a self-test that is
// only run once.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    public static class SensorSelfTest
    {
        /// <summary>One assertion's outcome, kept for the summary line.</summary>
        private sealed class Result
        {
            public string Name;
            public bool Ok;
            public string Detail;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// A set built with this run's configured rules.
        ///
        /// THE RULES ARE READ FROM THE ENVIRONMENT SO THE SELF-TEST CAN BE SHOWN TO FAIL.
        /// A self-test whose assertions always pass because the code under test agrees
        /// with itself is worth nothing -- the project already learned that from
        /// `tools/Test-FingerprintGate.ps1`, which exists to prove the fingerprint gate
        /// refuses a mutated build.  Setting `DRELAY_SENSOR_RETIRE_MISSES=1` configures a
        /// rule that is knowingly wrong (one strike retires a live bullet on any
        /// hiccup), and the assertion that catches it -- T4b -- must then fail.  The
        /// injection suite runs exactly that, and would fail if this self-test ever
        /// stopped having teeth.
        /// </summary>
        private static ThreatSet NewSet()
        {
            return new ThreatSet
            {
                MinAgeFrames = Knob("DRELAY_SENSOR_MIN_AGE", 3),
                RetireAfterMisses = Knob("DRELAY_SENSOR_RETIRE_MISSES", 2)
            };
        }

        /// <summary>A positive integer from the environment, or the fallback.  Plain `DRELAY_` names, per PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 4 trap 1.</summary>
        private static int Knob(string name, int fallback)
        {
            string value = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name);
            int parsed;
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(value) && int.TryParse(value, out parsed) && parsed > 0)
            {
                return parsed;
            }
            return fallback;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Runs every assertion and returns the counts.  Never throws: a self-test that
        /// can take the hook down is worse than the bug it is looking for, so each
        /// assertion is run inside its own guard and a throw is counted as a failure.
        /// </summary>
        public static void Run(out int passed, out int failed)
        {
            var results = new List<Result>();

            Check(results, "T4a a bullet is kept while it is seen every frame", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                for (int frame = 0; frame < 10; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), frame);
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                return set.Count == 1;
            });

            Check(results, "T4b one absence does not retire a live bullet", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                for (int frame = 0; frame < 5; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), frame);
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                set.BeginFrame();                       // frame 5: absent once
                set.Reconcile(5);
                bool kept = set.Count == 1;
                set.BeginFrame();                       // frame 6: present again
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), 6);
                set.Reconcile(6);
                return kept && set.Count == 1;
            });

            Check(results, "T4c TWO consecutive absences retire it", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                for (int frame = 0; frame < 5; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), frame);
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Reconcile(5);
                bool afterOne = set.Count == 1;
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Reconcile(6);
                return afterOne && set.Count == 0;
            });

            Check(results, "T4d a returning bullet resets the miss streak", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                for (int frame = 0; frame < 5; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), frame);
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                // Absent, present, absent, absent: the streak must restart at the
                // reappearance, so the second absence is still only the first strike.
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Reconcile(5);
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), 6);
                set.Reconcile(6);
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Reconcile(7);
                bool aliveAfterOneMoreMiss = set.Count == 1;
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Reconcile(8);
                return aliveAfterOneMoreMiss && set.Count == 0;
            });

            Check(results, "T4e a bullet inside its grace is not charged a miss", () =>
            {
                // Seen once, then absent for the whole grace window: it must survive all
                // of it, because being absent while young is "not yet", not "gone".
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), 0);
                set.Reconcile(0);
                for (int frame = 1; frame <= set.MinAgeFrames; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                    if (set.Count != 1)
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                return true;
            });

            Check(results, "T4f a FAILED enumeration accrues no miss (no reconcile, no strike)", () =>
            {
                // The rule with the most expensive wrong version: if the caller
                // reconciles after a read that did not happen, one hiccup retires a live
                // bullet.  Modelled by simply not reconciling, and then reconciling
                // twice more than the retire threshold would allow if the skipped frames
                // had counted.
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                for (int frame = 0; frame < 5; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Observe(new ThreatKey(7, 100), frame);
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                for (int frame = 5; frame < 12; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.NoteUnreconciledFrame();        // enumeration failed; no Reconcile
                }
                return set.Count == 1;
            });

            Check(results, "T4g a new bullet is admitted on its first observation", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(11, 200), 0);
                set.Reconcile(0);
                return set.Count == 1;
            });

            Check(results, "T3a invalidating a key removes its record at once", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(3, 9), 0);
                set.Reconcile(0);
                bool removed = set.Invalidate(new ThreatKey(3, 9));
                return removed && set.Count == 0;
            });

            Check(results, "T3b a RE-RENTED object cannot inherit the old bullet's state", () =>
            {
                // The pooling hazard, as a test.  Same startTime, different GameId -- the
                // shape a re-rent produces -- must not be the same record, so the new
                // bullet is admitted with a fresh age rather than inheriting the old
                // one's history.
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(3, 9), 0);
                set.Reconcile(0);
                for (int frame = 1; frame < 20; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                }
                bool oldGone = set.Count == 0;

                set.BeginFrame();
                set.Observe(new ThreatKey(4, 9), 20);   // re-rented: new GameId, same startTime
                set.Reconcile(20);
                bool fresh = set.Count == 1;

                // And the fresh one is inside its grace, not carrying twenty frames of
                // age: absent for the whole window and still kept.
                for (int frame = 21; frame <= 20 + set.MinAgeFrames; frame++)
                {
                    set.BeginFrame();
                    set.Reconcile(frame);
                    if (set.Count != 1)
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                return oldGone && fresh;
            });

            Check(results, "T3c invalidating an unknown key is a no-op, not an insert", () =>
            {
                ThreatSet set = NewSet();
                set.Invalidate(new ThreatKey(99, 99));
                return set.Count == 0;
            });

            Check(results, "gate: a straight trace may be projected", () =>
            {
                float[] xs = { 0f, 1f, 2f, 3f, 4f };
                float[] ys = { 0f, 2f, 4f, 6f, 8f };
                return LinearityGate.IsLinear(xs, ys, 5, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance);
            });

            Check(results, "gate: a wavy trace may NOT be projected", () =>
            {
                float[] xs = { 0f, 1f, 2f, 3f, 4f };
                float[] ys = { 0f, 3f, -3f, 3f, 0f };
                return !LinearityGate.IsLinear(xs, ys, 5, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance);
            });

            Check(results, "gate: a zero-span trace may NOT be projected", () =>
            {
                float[] xs = { 5f, 5f, 5f, 5f };
                float[] ys = { 5f, 5f, 5f, 5f };
                return !LinearityGate.IsLinear(xs, ys, 4, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance);
            });

            Check(results, "gate: two points are not a trajectory", () =>
            {
                float[] xs = { 0f, 1f };
                float[] ys = { 0f, 1f };
                return !LinearityGate.IsLinear(xs, ys, 2, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance);
            });

            Check(results, "gate: a trace just inside the tolerance passes, just outside fails", () =>
            {
                // One interior sample off the chord by a known distance, measured
                // perpendicular to it.  The chord here is the x axis, so the offset is
                // the y value and the check is exact.
                float[] inside = { 0f, 1f, 2f, 3f, 4f };
                float[] insideYs = { 0f, 0.04f, 0f, 0f, 0f };
                float[] outside = { 0f, 1f, 2f, 3f, 4f };
                float[] outsideYs = { 0f, 0.06f, 0f, 0f, 0f };
                return LinearityGate.IsLinear(inside, insideYs, 5, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance)
                    && !LinearityGate.IsLinear(outside, outsideYs, 5, LinearityGate.DefaultTolerance);
            });

            // THE HISTOGRAM'S OVERFLOW PATH, WHICH IS THE ONLY PATH THAT EVER CRASHED.
            //
            // `Describe()` indexed `Edges[Edges.Length]` -- one past the end -- and the
            // mistake was invisible until a sample landed above the last edge, so every run
            // that had an outlier worth reporting lost its numbers instead of reporting it
            // (PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 4.14, where that cost a live session's cost
            // percentiles).  A self-test that never fills the overflow bucket would have
            // exactly the blind spot of the code it guards, so this one fills it on
            // purpose: if `Describe()` throws, `Check` records the exception by name.
            Check(results, "histogram: an overflowing bucket can still be described", () =>
            {
                CostHistogram histogram = new CostHistogram();
                histogram.Add(3);
                histogram.Add(9000);
                if (!histogram.Overflowed)
                {
                    return false;
                }
                string text = histogram.Describe();
                return text.Contains("OVERFLOW") && text.Contains("above 2000us");
            });

            passed = 0;
            failed = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < results.Count; i++)
            {
                if (results[i].Ok)
                {
                    passed++;
                }
                else
                {
                    failed++;
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "sensor self-test FAILED: " + results[i].Name
                                                 + (string.IsNullOrEmpty(results[i].Detail)
                                                        ? "" : " -- " + results[i].Detail));
                }
            }

            HookEntry.AppendLog(failed == 0 ? "INFO" : "ERROR",
                                "sensor self-test: " + results.Count + " assertion(s), " + passed
                                + " passed, " + failed + " failed (threat set: two-strike retirement "
                                + "with a min-age grace and no strike for a failed read; linearity gate)");
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Runs one assertion so that a throw is a failed check and not a dead hook.
        /// </summary>
        private static void Check(List<Result> results, string name, Func<bool> assertion)
        {
            var result = new Result { Name = name, Ok = false, Detail = "" };
            try
            {
                result.Ok = assertion();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                result.Detail = ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message;
            }
            results.Add(result);
        }
    }
}
```
