```cs
                + "skipped: no-player {2}, dead-or-safe {3} | mode '{4}'",
                _frame, _totalMoved, _skippedNoPlayer, _skippedNotAlive, _mode));
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        private static void LogFrame(object input, float rotation, float x, float y,
                                     float dx, float dy, float commanded)
        {
            if ((_loggedFrames++ % LogEveryFrames) != 0)
            {
                return;
            }
            float readBack = _getMoveAngleRadians(input);
            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", string.Format(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                "steer frame {0} phase {1} cmd {2:0.0}deg wrote {3:0.0000}rad read-back {4:0.0000}rad "
                + "rot {5:0.0}deg pos ({6:0.000},{7:0.000}) d ({8:0.0000},{9:0.0000}) |d| {10:0.0000}",
                _frame, _phase + 1, commanded * 180.0 / Math.PI, commanded, readBack,
                rotation * 180.0 / Math.PI, x, y, dx, dy,
                Math.Sqrt((double)dx * dx + (double)dy * dy)));
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // The managed replacement on the movement integrator
        // ===================================================================================
        //
        // THIS METHOD IS WHAT MINHOOK'S `jmp` LANDS IN, and that is not an implementation
        // detail: it is the reason the actuator is safe.  `World.hehe_EB2C_E5A5_EE82_E9C5_
        // EF68(float, float)` is an ordinary instance method, so on x64 the receiver is in
        // RCX and the two floats are in XMM1 and XMM2; a static method taking those three
        // explicitly has the same ABI, and the game's own `call` becomes a
        // managed-to-managed call with no native frame anywhere in the chain
        // (MANAGED-ENTRY-HANDOFF.md section 3, and PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 4.4 for the
        // measurement that settled it).
        //
        // THE ORIGINAL IS CALLED ON EVERY PATH.  A replacement that steered and returned
        // would stop the player's movement, collision, escape handling and `GmMove`
        // emission in one line -- the most destructive thing this file could do -- so the
        // call-through happens even when the steering path threw.

        /// <summary>
        /// The replacement: steer, then run the game's own movement tick.
        /// </summary>
        [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
        public static void MovementIntegratorReplacement(IntPtr self, float logicDt, float frameDt)
        {
            try
            {
                BeforeOriginal();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // Swallowed for the reason the frame replacement's catch gives: an
                // exception escaping into the game's movement tick is worse than a missed
                // experiment. `BeforeOriginal` already logs and counts its own failures, so
                // this only catches something in the call itself.
                if (System.Threading.Interlocked.Exchange(ref _failureLogged, 1) == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "the movement replacement threw before calling "
                                                 + "through; the game's movement tick still runs: "
                                                 + ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message);
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
            }

            CallOriginal(self, logicDt, frameDt);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Continue into the real method through MinHook's trampoline, as a MANAGED
        /// function pointer -- `delegate* managed`, never `delegate* unmanaged`, because
        /// the unmanaged form is a managed-to-native transition and puts a preemptive
        /// thread state under the original body (PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 4.4).
        /// </summary>
        [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
        private static void CallOriginal(IntPtr self, float logicDt, float frameDt)
        {
            long trampoline = Marshal.ReadInt64(HookEntry.SharedBlockPointer,
                                                GeneratedLayout.Off_managedMovementTrampoline);
            if (trampoline == 0)
            {
                // Must not happen: the native side publishes the trampoline before it
                // enables the hook, because the first call arrives immediately. Returning
                // would freeze the player in place, so this is loud.
                if (System.Threading.Interlocked.Exchange(ref _failureLogged, 2) != 2)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "the movement replacement ran with no trampoline "
                                                 + "published; the game's movement tick cannot run "
                                                 + "and the player will not move");
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
                return;
            }

            unsafe
            {
                ((delegate* managed<IntPtr, float, float, void>)(IntPtr)trampoline)(self, logicDt, frameDt);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Prepare and publish the replacement, and warm everything it calls -- the same
        /// discipline as the frame tick's and the collision hook's, for the same reason: a
        /// method compiled on its first call is compiled from inside a patched game
        /// method, which is a JIT in the middle of the frame.
        ///
        /// CALLED ON EVERY RUN, WHETHER OR NOT THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR STEERING.  Publishing
        /// the address costs one JIT of a method that will never be entered, and it means
        /// the plumbing -- the shared slot, the native dispatch by target name, the
        /// trampoline handshake -- is exercised by every run rather than only by the runs
        /// where a mistake would move the player.  What the switch decides is whether
        /// MinHook's `jmp` is aimed at it at all; the native side reads that.
        /// </summary>
        public static void Publish()
        {
            MethodInfo method = typeof(SteeringPilot).GetMethod(
                nameof(MovementIntegratorReplacement), BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static);
            if (method == null)
            {
                HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "the movement replacement was not found by name; "
                                             + "nothing published and the target will not be patched");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
                return;
            }

            MethodInfo callOriginal = typeof(SteeringPilot).GetMethod(
                "CallOriginal", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Static);
            if (callOriginal != null)
            {
                RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod(callOriginal.MethodHandle);
            }
            RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod(method.MethodHandle);
            PreparePilotPath();

            IntPtr entry = method.MethodHandle.GetFunctionPointer();
            Marshal.WriteInt64(HookEntry.SharedBlockPointer,
                               GeneratedLayout.Off_managedMovementReplacement, entry.ToInt64());
            HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "managed movement replacement published at 0x"
                                        + entry.ToInt64().ToString("X")
                                        + "; the native side jumps straight into it only when "
                                        + "--move-steer asked for it");
            HookEntry.FlushLog();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Prepare the pilot's own static methods before the patch goes live, so the frame path is
        /// not compiled from inside a patched frame.
        ///
        /// THESE ARE ORDINARY METHODS, WHICH IS WHY THIS ONE IS SAFE. The warm-up's removed pass
        /// called `PrepareMethod` on the emitted accessors' `Method` -- a `DynamicMethod`, whose
        /// handle the runtime is not obliged to accept -- and that is what died at startup. Every
        /// name in the list below resolves to a normally declared static method with a real
        /// `RuntimeMethodHandle`, and this has run on every launch since the first build of the
        /// pilot.
        ///
        /// `PrepareMethod` covers the method named and nothing it calls, so the callees on the
        /// frame path are named explicitly. The accessor delegates are not in the list because
        /// `FieldAccessor` compiles each of them at resolve, where `CreateDelegate` is called.
        ///
        /// **IT MATCHES BY NAME ACROSS ALL OVERLOADS, AND THAT IS A FIX RATHER THAN A STYLE.**
        /// This used to call `GetMethod(name, flags)` once per name. `Type.GetMethod` throws
        /// `AmbiguousMatchException` when a name has more than one overload, and the moment
        /// Deliverable 3.3 added `WriteInput(object, float, float)` beside the original
        /// `WriteInput(object, float)`, this method threw -- on the frame-path warm-up, from inside
        /// `Publish`, which took the whole `Publish` call with it:
        ///
        ///     publishing the movement replacement threw; the movement target will not be patched
        ///     ... System.Reflection.AmbiguousMatchException: Ambiguous match found for
        ///     'Drelay.Bootstrap.SteeringPilot Void WriteInput(System.Object, Single)'.
        ///
        /// So an overload silently cost the project its actuator -- every steering run, not just the
        /// dodge's -- and nothing about the build could see it, because it is a runtime lookup. The
        /// synthetic probe (`tools\Probe-DodgeDryRun.ps1`) is what caught it. Iterating the methods
        /// and matching the name cannot be ambiguous, so no future overload can repeat it.
        /// </summary>
        private static void PreparePilotPath()
        {
            string[] names =
            {
                "BeforeOriginal", "WriteInput", "StopInput", "PhaseAngle", "AdvancePhase",
                "ReleaseInput", "Accumulate", "EndCall", "EmitPhaseSummary", "EmitRunSummary",
                "LogFrame", "ParsePlan", "BuildStatus", "Missing", "Resolve", "Warm",
            };
            MethodInfo[] methods = typeof(SteeringPilot).GetMethods(
                BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Static);
            for (int i = 0; i < methods.Length; i++)
            {
                bool wanted = false;
                for (int n = 0; n < names.Length; n++)
                {
                    if (names[n] == methods[i].Name)
                    {
                        wanted = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (!wanted)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                try
                {
                    RuntimeHelpers.PrepareMethod(methods[i].MethodHandle);
                }
                catch
                {
                    // A callee that is generic or otherwise unprepared is skipped; the rest of
                    // the path is still warmed, and the failure is not silent because the publish
                    // log follows.
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/ThreatSet.cs`:

```cs
// ThreatSet.cs -- the Phase 2 sensor's bookkeeping, and the gate that decides whether a
// trajectory may be projected.
//
// WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE, AND WHY IT HAS A SELF-TEST.
//
// DODGE-ALGORITHM.md sections 3 and 4 specify two things that must be right no matter
// where the data comes from: how a bullet is retired when it stops being observed, and
// when a sampled trajectory may be extended past its last trustworthy point.  Both are
// pure functions of plain data -- no game pointers, no offsets, no managed reads -- so
// both can be exercised on their own, and that is what `SensorSelfTest` does on every
// run, in the bootstrap, before the hook patches anything.
//
// That matters more here than usual.  The tests they correspond to, T3 and T4 in
// IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md's list, are about failures that are invisible in a live run:
// a retired-but-live bullet shows up as a dodge that hesitates, and a ghost bullet that
// never dies shows up as a dodge that moves for no reason.  Neither looks like a bug in
// the log.  A self-test is the only place they are cheap to see.
//
// The rules, restated from DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 3.3 so the code can be read
// against them:
//
//     present                        -> missStreak = 0, keep
//     absent and age < minAgeFrames  -> keep, and do NOT accrue a miss
//     absent otherwise               -> ++missStreak; retire once missStreak >= 2
//     a failed enumeration           -> reconcile nothing at all
//
// and the last of those is not a detail: "a failed read is not evidence of absence", so
// the caller that could not enumerate must not call `Reconcile`.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The identity of a live bullet: `(GameId, startTime)`, per DODGE-ALGORITHM.md
    /// section 3.2.
    ///
    /// THE PAIR IS THE POINT, NOT THE POINTER.  `Projectile` is pooled, and a re-rented
    /// instance gets a new `GameId`; state keyed on an object's address would silently
    /// inherit a dead bullet's history, which presents as "the dodge reacts to bullets
    /// that do not exist" (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4).  Keying on the pair makes
    /// that impossible by construction, and `ThreatSet.Invalidate` makes it impossible
    /// again by observation.
    /// </summary>
    public readonly struct ThreatKey : IEquatable<ThreatKey>
    {
        public readonly int GameId;
        public readonly int StartTime;

        public ThreatKey(int gameId, int startTime)
        {
            GameId = gameId;
            StartTime = startTime;
        }

        /// <summary>Packed for a dictionary key; the two are 32 bits each by construction.</summary>
        public long Packed => ((long)GameId << 32) ^ (uint)StartTime;

        public bool Equals(ThreatKey other) => GameId == other.GameId && StartTime == other.StartTime;
        public override bool Equals(object obj) => obj is ThreatKey other && Equals(other);
        public override int GetHashCode() => Packed.GetHashCode();
        public override string ToString() => "(" + GameId + "," + StartTime + ")";
    }

    /// <summary>What is known about one bullet that is believed to be live.</summary>
    public struct ThreatRecord
    {
        public ThreatKey Key;
        public int FirstSeenFrame;
        public int LastSeenFrame;

        /// <summary>
        /// Consecutive frames the bullet was absent.  Only ever advanced by a frame in
        /// which the enumeration SUCCEEDED.
        /// </summary>
        public int MissStreak;

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether the sensor saw this bullet on a collision course with the player
        /// inside its horizon, and when.  This is Deliverable 2.3's prediction half: the
        /// warning a hit gets is the distance between this and the moment the game's own
        /// collision decision fires.
        /// </summary>
        public bool Predicted;
        public int FirstPredictedFrame;
        public long FirstPredictedTick;

        /// <summary>Set when the game's collision decision was observed for this bullet.</summary>
        public bool HitObserved;

        /// <summary>Frames since it was first seen; the age the min-age rule tests.</summary>
        public int Age(int frame) => frame - FirstSeenFrame;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The live-bullet set: one record per key, retired by evidence rather than by
    /// quota.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class ThreatSet
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// A bullet observed at spawn may legitimately not appear in the live view for a
        /// few frames -- the object exists before whatever the frame path enumerates has
        /// caught up -- and charging a miss for that would retire live bullets.  Three
        /// frames is the grace the reference engine's reconcile also carries; it is a
        /// count of frames and not of milliseconds because the sensor works in frames.
        /// </summary>
        public int MinAgeFrames = 3;

        /// <summary>
        /// Two strikes: the smallest value that survives a single incomplete read.  One
        /// would retire a live bullet on any hiccup; three would let a ghost persist for
        /// frames the dodge is spending on it.
        /// </summary>
        public int RetireAfterMisses = 2;

        private readonly Dictionary<long, ThreatRecord> _records = new Dictionary<long, ThreatRecord>();
        private readonly HashSet<long> _seenThisFrame = new HashSet<long>();
        private readonly List<long> _retireNow = new List<long>();

        /// <summary>Records believed live.</summary>
        public int Count => _records.Count;

        /// <summary>Frames in which a reconcile retired at least one bullet.</summary>
        public int RetiredTotal { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>Frames whose enumeration failed and were therefore not reconciled.</summary>
        public int UnreconciledFrames { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>
        /// Bullets the sensor predicted would hit and that were retired without the game
        /// ever deciding they did.  This is the false-positive count, and it is the rate
        /// that decides whether a dodge would be over-cautious.
        /// </summary>
        public long PredictedButNeverHit { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>Bullets the game decided were hitting and the sensor had predicted.</summary>
        public long PredictedAndHit { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>Bullets the game decided were hitting and the sensor had not predicted.  The false negatives.</summary>
        public long HitUnpredicted { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>Warning, in milliseconds, accumulated over the predicted hits.</summary>
        public double WarningTotalMs { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>The single record for a key, if it is tracked.</summary>
        public bool TryGet(ThreatKey key, out ThreatRecord record)
        {
            return _records.TryGetValue(key.Packed, out record);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Marks that the sensor saw this bullet on a collision course inside its horizon.
        /// Only the FIRST such frame is kept, because the warning a hit is credited with
        /// is the warning the sensor actually had -- not the most recent glance at it.
        /// </summary>
        public bool MarkPredicted(ThreatKey key, int frame, long tick)
        {
            ThreatRecord record;
            if (!_records.TryGetValue(key.Packed, out record) || record.Predicted)
            {
                return false;
            }
            record.Predicted = true;
            record.FirstPredictedFrame = frame;
            record.FirstPredictedTick = tick;
            _records[key.Packed] = record;
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The game's collision decision, for a bullet the threat set knows about.
        ///
        /// RETURNS TRUE THE FIRST TIME ONLY, so the caller counts each hit once, and
        /// reports the warning the sensor actually had: the distance between the frame it
        /// first saw this bullet on a collision course and this instant.  A hit the sensor
        /// never predicted is a false negative and is counted as one -- that number is
        /// half of what decides whether the model is complete enough to rely on.
        /// </summary>
        public bool MarkHit(ThreatKey key, long tickNow, out double warningMs)
        {
            warningMs = 0.0;
            ThreatRecord record;
            if (!_records.TryGetValue(key.Packed, out record) || record.HitObserved)
            {
                return false;
            }
            record.HitObserved = true;
            _records[key.Packed] = record;

            if (record.Predicted)
            {
                PredictedAndHit++;
                warningMs = TicksToMs(tickNow - record.FirstPredictedTick);
                if (warningMs >= 0.0)
                {
                    WarningTotalMs += warningMs;
                }
                else
                {
                    warningMs = 0.0;
                }
            }
            else
            {
                HitUnpredicted++;
            }
            return true;
        }

        private static double TicksToMs(long ticks)
        {
            return ticks * 1000.0 / System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.Frequency;
        }

        /// <summary>Mean warning over the predicted hits, in milliseconds.</summary>
        public double MeanWarningMs => PredictedAndHit == 0 ? 0.0 : WarningTotalMs / PredictedAndHit;

        /// <summary>Starts a frame.  The seen-set is per frame, so a missed reconcile cannot leak into the next one.</summary>
        public void BeginFrame()
        {
            _seenThisFrame.Clear();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Records that a bullet was observed this frame.  Called once per live bullet
        /// the frame path could identify, and only with arguments -- see
        /// HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.3: the spawn hook reads no managed field at
        /// all.
        /// </summary>
        public void Observe(ThreatKey key, int frame)
        {
            long packed = key.Packed;
            _seenThisFrame.Add(packed);

            ThreatRecord record;
            if (_records.TryGetValue(packed, out record))
            {
                record.MissStreak = 0;
                record.LastSeenFrame = frame;
                _records[packed] = record;
                return;
            }

            record = new ThreatRecord
            {
                Key = key,
                FirstSeenFrame = frame,
                LastSeenFrame = frame,
                MissStreak = 0
            };
            _records[packed] = record;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Ends a frame in which the enumeration SUCCEEDED.  Anything not seen accrues a
        /// miss, unless it is still inside its grace, and anything at two strikes is
        /// retired.
        ///
        /// A FAILED ENUMERATION MUST NOT CALL THIS.  Skipping it charges no miss, which
        /// is exactly the intended asymmetry: a read that did not happen is not evidence
        /// that a bullet is gone, and treating it as such is how a live bullet gets
        /// retired by a hiccup.
        /// </summary>
        public int Reconcile(int frame)
        {
            _retireNow.Clear();
            foreach (KeyValuePair<long, ThreatRecord> entry in _records)
            {
                if (_seenThisFrame.Contains(entry.Key))
                {
                    continue;
                }

                ThreatRecord record = entry.Value;
                if (record.Age(frame) < MinAgeFrames)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                record.MissStreak = record.MissStreak + 1;
                if (record.MissStreak >= RetireAfterMisses)
                {
                    _retireNow.Add(entry.Key);
                }                else
                {
                    _records[entry.Key] = record;
                }
            }

            for (int i = 0; i < _retireNow.Count; i++)
            {
                // A PREDICTED BULLET THAT NEVER HIT IS THE FALSE-POSITIVE COUNT, and it is
                // only knowable here: retirement is the moment the evidence says the
                // bullet is gone, and if the game's collision decision never fired for it
                // then the sensor's prediction was one the player was never going to be
                // hit by.  That rate is what decides whether a dodge would be
                // over-cautious.
                ThreatRecord record;
                if (_records.TryGetValue(_retireNow[i], out record) && record.Predicted
                    && !record.HitObserved)
                {
                    PredictedButNeverHit++;
                }
                _records.Remove(_retireNow[i]);
            }
            RetiredTotal += _retireNow.Count;
            return _retireNow.Count;
        }

        /// <summary>Records that this frame's enumeration failed, for the evidence and for the self-test.</summary>
        public void NoteUnreconciledFrame()
        {
            UnreconciledFrames++;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Drops a record outright, because the instance behind the key was observed
        /// being re-rented or reset.  Belt and braces next to the keyed identity: the
        /// pair already makes inheritance impossible, and this makes it explicit the
        /// moment the pool hands the object out again.
        /// </summary>
        public bool Invalidate(ThreatKey key)
        {
            return _records.Remove(key.Packed);
        }

        /// <summary>Everything goes -- a zone change, or `World.ClearWorld`.</summary>
        public void InvalidateAll()
        {
            _records.Clear();
            _seenThisFrame.Clear();
        }

        /// <summary>Read-only view, for the sensor's own decision pass.</summary>
        public void CopyRecords(List<ThreatRecord> into)
        {
            into.Clear();
            foreach (KeyValuePair<long, ThreatRecord> entry in _records)
            {
                into.Add(entry.Value);
            }
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The linearity gate: may a sampled trajectory be projected past its trace?
    ///
    /// DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 4.4 rule 3.  A bullet whose samples all lie close to
    /// the straight line through its endpoints is one the sensor may extend with
    /// confidence; a wavy, orbiting or bouncing one is not, and extending it would
    /// paint danger where the bullet is not and safety where it is.  The gate is the
    /// only place a lane is ever extended, which is why it is a function with a
    /// self-test rather than three lines inside the sampler.
    /// </summary>
    public static class LinearityGate
    {
        /// <summary>How far an interior sample may sit off the endpoint chord.</summary>
        public const float DefaultTolerance = 0.05f;

        /// <summary>
        /// <paramref name="xs"/>/<paramref name="ys"/> hold <paramref name="count"/>
        /// points, oldest first, on a fixed time grid.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool IsLinear(float[] xs, float[] ys, int count, float tolerance)
        {
            // Fewer than three points is not a trajectory -- there is no interior sample
            // to contradict the chord, so the honest answer is "not established", which
            // is what a false return means here.  The first version of this returned
            // true for two points, which would have let a single frame of motion be
            // extrapolated to the horizon.
            if (count < 3)
            {
                return false;
            }

            float ax = xs[0];
            float ay = ys[0];
            float bx = xs[count - 1];
            float by = ys[count - 1];

            float dx = bx - ax;
            float dy = by - ay;
            float span = (float)Math.Sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy));

            // A stationary trace has no direction to project along.  "Zero span" is the
            // reference engine's own condition and it is the one that matters most: a
            // bullet whose samples all coincide is exactly the case where extrapolating
            // would invent a lane out of nothing.
            if (span <= 0.0f)
            {
                return false;
            }

            for (int i = 1; i < count - 1; i++)
            {
                // Perpendicular distance from the interior point to the chord, which is
                // the quantity the tolerance is about.  Computed as the cross product
                // over the span so it is a distance and not an area.
                float cross = ((xs[i] - ax) * dy) - ((ys[i] - ay) * dx);
                float distance = (float)Math.Abs(cross) / span;
                if (distance > tolerance)
                {
                    return false;
                }
            }
            return true;
        }
    }
}
```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/TraceRecorder.cs`:

```cs
// TraceRecorder.cs -- the live half of Spike 3.2: record what the solver would decide against.
//
// =====================================================================================
// WHY A RECORDER AT ALL, WHEN THE SENSOR ALREADY EXISTS
// =====================================================================================
//
// The Phase 2 sensor observes the world and keeps counts. It does not keep *traces*: the
// per-bullet sample set it builds every frame is handed to the linearity gate, folded into a
// fraction, and dropped. So the four numbers Phase 2 produces describe the sensor, and none of
// them can be replayed -- there is no file that says "at frame 412 the player was here and these
// two bullets were on these paths".
//
// That is exactly what Spike 3.2 needs, because its first and most important invariant is T7:
//
//     "PREDICTED AND ACTUAL COLLISION AGREE. ... log every predicted first-impact time and every
//      `HitCharacter` call that returned `true` ... and assert the model predicted the ones that
//      happened. This is the hook's ground truth ... It is the one to build first. It is the only
//      test that can tell us whether the trajectory model is right."
//
// "The ones that happened" already exist: `CollisionObservation` writes one `collision:` line per
// resolved hit, with the bullet's key and the warning the sensor had. What does not exist is the
// other half -- what the model said, frame by frame, about every bullet it was tracking. This
// file writes it.
//
// =====================================================================================
// WHAT IT WRITES, AND WHY EACH FIELD IS THERE
// =====================================================================================
//
//   H  a header: the run, the grid window, the configuration the solver would have used
//   G  the collision grid window, once per change, run-length encoded
//   F  one frame: the clock, the player, and every live bullet's sampled path
//
// ONE FILE, THREE RECORD KINDS, JSON LINES. The format is deliberately boring: an offline
// harness has to read it, a human has to be able to look at it when the harness disagrees, and
// a format that needs its own parser is a format that will be read only by the code that wrote
// it -- which is how a fixture stops being evidence.
//
// THE PLAYER IS RECORDED EVEN WITH NO BULLETS ANYWHERE. A trace of a peaceful walk is the
// control case for T7: zero predicted impacts against zero resolved hits is the only way to show
// that the recorder is not inventing danger.
//
// =====================================================================================
// THE COST, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS OFF BY DEFAULT
// =====================================================================================
//
// Recording every frame at 60 Hz costs one file append and one string build per frame, plus
// about a kilobyte per bullet per frame. That is far too much to leave on for a normal session
// and it is why the switch is `DRELAY_TRACE` and not a default. The mitigations are the ones
// section 8 names for the sampler: cull bullets that cannot reach the player inside the horizon
// before recording them, and cap the number recorded per frame. What is recorded is therefore
// "the bullets that could matter", which is also the set the solver would have evaluated.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.IO;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Text;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The one place in the hook that writes a replayable trace of the decision's own input.
    /// </summary>
    public static class TraceRecorder
    {
        private const string EnvTrace = "DRELAY_TRACE";
        private const string FileName = "trace.jsonl";

        /// <summary>Bullets recorded per frame, at most. The rest are counted, not written.</summary>
        private const int MaxThreatsPerFrame = 48;

        /// <summary>
        /// Half-width of the grid window, in tiles, centred on the player.
        ///
        /// 64 RATHER THAN THE 24 IT WAS, AND THE PATHFINDER IS THE REASON. 24 was exactly the region
        /// the 600 ms admission horizon could touch -- the comment here used to say so -- and a
        /// decision that never looks further than one step does not need more. A path does: it is a
        /// route around a corridor of fire toward a point on the player's own line, and with a 24-cell
        /// radius the search would be aiming at a target it cannot see the far side of.
        ///
        /// At one world unit per cell this is 128 units across, and the recorder copies it only when
        /// the player's tile changes -- so the wider window also changes LESS OFTEN, which is why the
        /// trace does not grow by the 7x the cell count does. It is written run-length encoded (see
        /// `WriteGridWindow`), and a window is mostly one value.
        ///
        /// IT MUST STAY EQUAL TO `DodgeAdapter`'s OWN, because the harness reproduces the live
        /// decision from this recording: a trace recorded with a smaller window than the live solver
        /// reads is an offline result for a different world.
        /// </summary>
        private const int GridRadius = 64;

        private static bool _enabled;
        private static bool _resolved;
        private static string _unresolvedReason = "not attempted";
        private static string _path;
        private static StreamWriter _writer;

        private static readonly StringBuilder Line = new StringBuilder(4096);
        private static readonly CultureInfo Inv = CultureInfo.InvariantCulture;

        // The grid window, reused between frames. The layout is row-major over [x, y] so that a
        // reader can index it the way `World` indexes its own `byte[x, y]`.
        private static byte[] _gridCells = new byte[(2 * GridRadius) * (2 * GridRadius)];
        private static int _gridWidth;
        private static int _gridHeight;
        private static int _gridOriginX;
        private static int _gridOriginY;
        private static bool _gridResolved;
        private static bool _gridWindowValid;
        private static bool _gridDirty;
        private static long _gridGeneration;

        // Accessors, resolved once. All optional: a missing one degrades the trace, never the run.
        private static Func<object> _getWorld;
        private static Func<object, object> _getPlayer;
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerX;
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerY;
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerRadius;
        private static Func<object, double> _getPlayerHealth;
        private static Func<object, object> _getGameScene;
        private static Func<object, object> _getInput;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getMoving;
        private static Func<object, float> _getMoveAngleRadians;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getPlayerDead;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getSafeWorld;
        private static Func<float> _getWorldRotation;
        private static Func<object, float> _getLogicTotal;
        private static Func<object> _getClock;
        private static Func<object, object> _getGridArray;
        private static Func<object, int, int, byte> _gridAt;

        private static long _framesRecorded;
        private static long _threatsRecorded;
        private static long _threatsSkipped;
        private static int _failureLogged;
        private static int _framesUntilLog = 600;

        /// <summary>Whether the recorder is switched on and has a file.</summary>
        public static bool Enabled => _resolved && _enabled;

        /// <summary>Why not, when not.</summary>
        public static string UnresolvedReason => _unresolvedReason;

        // ===================================================================================
        // Resolution
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// Reads the switch, opens the file, and resolves every accessor the trace needs.
        ///
        /// EVERY ACCESSOR IS OPTIONAL AND A MISSING ONE IS NOT FATAL. The trace's job is to make
        /// the offline harness possible; a trace with no health reading is still a trace that can
        /// test T7, and refusing to record because one field moved would turn "the model cannot be
        /// checked" into "the model cannot be checked and the reason was a rename".
        /// </summary>
        public static bool Resolve(Assembly game, string runDir)
        {
            string switchValue = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(EnvTrace);
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(switchValue) || switchValue == "0")
            {
                _unresolvedReason = "DRELAY_TRACE is not set";
                return false;
            }

            try
            {
                const BindingFlags Any = BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic
                                       | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Static;

                Type worldType = game.GetType(ManagedArmingProbe.WorldTypeName);
                Type playerType = game.GetType(ManagedArmingProbe.PlayerTypeName);
                if (worldType == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = ManagedArmingProbe.WorldTypeName + " not found";
                    return false;
                }

                FieldInfo sharedField = worldType.GetField("Shared", Any);
                FieldInfo playerField = worldType.GetField("Player", Any);
                FieldInfo playerPositionField = playerType?.GetField("Position", Any);
                FieldInfo positionXField = playerPositionField?.FieldType.GetField("X");
                FieldInfo positionYField = playerPositionField?.FieldType.GetField("Y");
                FieldInfo radiusField = FindRadius(playerType);
                FieldInfo healthField = playerType?.GetField("Health", Any);
                FieldInfo deadField = worldType.GetField("PlayerDead", Any);
                FieldInfo safeField = worldType.GetField("SafeWorld", Any);
                FieldInfo sceneField = worldType.GetField("GameScene", Any);
                FieldInfo inputField = sceneField?.FieldType.GetField("GameInput", Any);
                FieldInfo movingField = inputField?.FieldType.GetField("Moving", Any);
                FieldInfo moveAngleField = inputField?.FieldType.GetField("MoveAngle", Any);
                FieldInfo angleRadiansField = moveAngleField?.FieldType.GetField("Radians", Any);
                FieldInfo rotationField = worldType.GetField("WorldRotation",
                    BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Static);

                if (sharedField == null || playerField == null || positionXField == null
                    || positionYField == null)
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "the player path did not resolve: World.Shared="
                                        + (sharedField != null) + " World.Player=" + (playerField != null)
                                        + " Player.Position.XY="
                                        + (positionXField != null && positionYField != null);
                    return false;
                }

                _getWorld = FieldAccessor.Static(sharedField);
                _getPlayer = FieldAccessor.Reference(playerField);
                _getPlayerX = FieldAccessor.NestedFloat(playerPositionField, positionXField);
                _getPlayerY = FieldAccessor.NestedFloat(playerPositionField, positionYField);
                if (radiusField != null)
                {
                    _getPlayerRadius = FieldAccessor.Float(radiusField);
                }
                if (healthField != null)
                {
                    _getPlayerHealth = FieldAccessor.Double(healthField);
                }
                if (deadField != null)
                {
                    _getPlayerDead = FieldAccessor.Bool(deadField);
                }
                if (safeField != null)
                {
                    _getSafeWorld = FieldAccessor.Bool(safeField);
                }
                if (sceneField != null && inputField != null)
                {
                    _getGameScene = FieldAccessor.Reference(sceneField);
                    _getInput = FieldAccessor.Reference(inputField);
                    if (movingField != null)
                    {
                        _getMoving = FieldAccessor.Bool(movingField);
                    }
                    if (moveAngleField != null && angleRadiansField != null)
                    {
                        _getMoveAngleRadians = FieldAccessor.NestedFloat(moveAngleField, angleRadiansField);
                    }
                }
                if (rotationField != null)
                {
                    _getWorldRotation = FieldAccessor.StaticFloat(rotationField);
                }

                // The game's own clock, for the `LogicTotal` the sampler already depends on.
                Type clockType = game.GetType("DarzasDominion.Graphics.ClientTime");
                FieldInfo staticClock = game.GetType("DarzasDominion.Graphics.DarzaWindow")?
                    .GetField("Time", Any);
                FieldInfo logicTotal = clockType?.GetField("LogicTotal", Any);
                if (staticClock != null && logicTotal != null)
                {
                    _getClock = FieldAccessor.Static(staticClock);
                    _getLogicTotal = FieldAccessor.Float(logicTotal);
                }

                ResolveGrid(worldType, Any);

                string dir = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(runDir)
                    ? runDir
                    : Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DRELAY_HOOK_RUNDIR");
                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(dir))
                {
                    _unresolvedReason = "no run directory (DRELAY_HOOK_RUNDIR is unset)";
                    return false;
                }
                Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
                _path = Path.Combine(dir, FileName);
                _writer = new StreamWriter(new FileStream(_path, FileMode.Create, FileAccess.Write,
                                                          FileShare.Read, 1 << 16));
                _writer.AutoFlush = false;
                _enabled = true;
                _resolved = true;

                WriteHeader();
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "trace recorder ARMED: writing " + _path
                                            + " -- player, grid and every culled threat's sampled path, "
                                            + "JSON lines, one frame per line. The cost is real; this "
                                            + "switch is off by default for that reason.");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
                return true;
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _unresolvedReason = ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message;
                _enabled = false;
                return false;
            }
        }

        private static FieldInfo FindRadius(Type playerType)
        {
            if (playerType == null)
            {
                return null;
            }
            FieldInfo f = playerType.GetField("Radius",
                BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance);
            if (f != null)
            {
                return f;
            }
            // `GameObject.Radius` is on the base, not on `Player`.
            Type t = playerType.BaseType;
            while (t != null && t != typeof(object))
            {
                f = t.GetField("Radius", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance);
                if (f != null)
                {
                    return f;
                }
                t = t.BaseType;
            }
            return null;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The client's collision grid: `private byte[,] World.&lt;grid&gt;`, the one `World` itself
        /// indexes with a truncated float position.
        ///
        /// THE NAMES ARE PRIVATE-USE CODE POINTS AND THAT IS NOT A PROBLEM HERE. The field is
        /// obfuscated, so it cannot be found by name -- it is found as *the only `byte[,]` on
        /// `World`*, which is a structural property rather than a spelling, and this project has
        /// been bitten twice by trusts placed in spellings (PHASE3-SCOPE.md section 4.3).
        /// </summary>
        private static void ResolveGrid(Type worldType, BindingFlags any)
        {
            FieldInfo candidate = null;
            int count = 0;
            FieldInfo[] fields = worldType.GetFields(any);
            for (int i = 0; i < fields.Length; i++)
            {
                if (fields[i].FieldType == typeof(byte[,]))
                {
                    candidate = fields[i];
                    count++;
                }
            }
            if (candidate == null || count != 1)
            {
                _gridResolved = false;
                return;
            }
            try
            {
                _getGridArray = FieldAccessor.Reference(candidate);
                _gridAt = FieldAccessor.ByteArray2D(candidate.FieldType);
                _gridResolved = true;
            }
            catch (Exception)
            {
                _gridResolved = false;
            }
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // The per-frame entry
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// One frame. Called from the frame replacement, after the sensor, on a frame the sensor
        /// says it read successfully.
        ///
        /// THE ORDER MATTERS AND IS NOT ARBITRARY. It runs after `SensorRead.OnFrame` because it
        /// borrows that frame's projectile list rather than walking the layer a second time --
        /// the walk is the expensive part and doing it twice would double the frame cost of a
        /// run whose whole purpose is to be a normal run.
        /// </summary>
        public static void OnFrame(List<object> liveProjectiles, List<ThreatKey> liveKeys,
                                   int frame, float frameSeconds)
        {
            if (!_enabled || _writer == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                object world = _getWorld();
                object player = world == null ? null : _getPlayer(world);
                if (player == null)
                {
                    return;   // no character yet: nothing to record and nothing to decide on
                }

                float px = _getPlayerX(player);
                float py = _getPlayerY(player);

                WriteFrame(frame, frameSeconds, world, player, px, py, liveProjectiles, liveKeys);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // ONCE PER RUN, for the reason the frame path's own catch is written that way: an
                // exception thrown every frame would fill the log ring and hide everything else.
                if (System.Threading.Interlocked.Exchange(ref _failureLogged, 1) == 0)
                {
                    HookEntry.AppendLog("ERROR", "the trace recorder threw; the trace is truncated "
                                                 + "from this frame and the game is unaffected: "
                                                 + ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message + " | "
                                                 + HookEntry.FirstFrames(ex));
                    HookEntry.FlushLog();
                }
            }
        }

        private static void WriteFrame(int frame, float frameSeconds, object world, object player,
                                       float px, float py, List<object> projectiles, List<ThreatKey> keys)
        {
            float radius = _getPlayerRadius != null ? _getPlayerRadius(player) : 0.25f;
            double health = _getPlayerHealth != null ? _getPlayerHealth(player) : 0.0;
            bool dead = _getPlayerDead != null && _getPlayerDead(world);
            bool safe = _getSafeWorld != null && _getSafeWorld(world);
            float rotation = _getWorldRotation != null ? _getWorldRotation() : 0.0f;
            float clock = 0.0f;
            if (_getClock != null && _getLogicTotal != null)
            {
                object c = _getClock();
                if (c != null)
                {
                    clock = _getLogicTotal(c);
                }
            }

            float intent = 0.0f;
            bool moving = false;
            if (_getInput != null && _getGameScene != null)
            {
                object scene = _getGameScene(world);
                object input = scene == null ? null : _getInput(scene);
                if (input != null)
                {
                    if (_getMoving != null)
                    {
                        moving = _getMoving(input);
                    }
                    if (_getMoveAngleRadians != null)
                    {
                        intent = _getMoveAngleRadians(input);
                    }
                }
            }

            // THE GRID RECORD IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE FRAME THAT REFERENCES IT, AND ONLY WHEN THE
            // WINDOW HAS MOVED. The window is a property of the map and of which tile the player
            // is standing on; writing it every frame would multiply the file for no information,
            // and writing it *after* the frame would mean the reader sees a dangling id.
            RefreshGrid(world, px, py);

            Line.Length = 0;
            Line.Append("{\"t\":\"F\",\"f\":").Append(frame);
            Line.Append(",\"dt\":").Append(Num(frameSeconds));
            Line.Append(",\"clock\":").Append(Num(clock));
            Line.Append(",\"px\":").Append(Num(px));
            Line.Append(",\"py\":").Append(Num(py));
            Line.Append(",\"r\":").Append(Num(radius));
            Line.Append(",\"hp\":").Append(Num(health));
            Line.Append(",\"moving\":").Append(moving ? "true" : "false");
            Line.Append(",\"intent\":").Append(Num(intent));
            Line.Append(",\"dead\":").Append(dead ? "true" : "false");
            Line.Append(",\"safe\":").Append(safe ? "true" : "false");
            Line.Append(",\"rot\":").Append(Num(rotation));
            Line.Append(",\"grid\":").Append(_gridWindowValid ? _gridGeneration : 0).Append(',');

            // Cull first, record second (section 8's mitigation 1). A bullet that cannot reach
            // the player inside the horizon has no bearing on the decision the trace exists to
            // check, and recording it would make the file mostly noise.
            Line.Append("\"threats\":[");
            int written = 0;
            int skipped = 0;
            long declinedBefore = TrajectorySampler.Declined;
            if (projectiles != null && keys != null)
            {
                for (int i = 0; i < projectiles.Count && i < keys.Count; i++)
                {
                    if (written >= MaxThreatsPerFrame)
                    {
                        skipped++;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if (!TrajectorySampler.FillTrajectory(projectiles[i], out Trajectory t))
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    t.Key = keys[i].Packed;
                    if (!CouldReach(t, px, py, radius))
                    {
                        skipped++;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if (written > 0)
                    {
                        Line.Append(',');
                    }
                    AppendThreat(t, keys[i]);
                    written++;
                }
            }
            Line.Append(']');
            Line.Append(",\"skipped\":").Append(skipped);

            // AND THE ONES THE CLIENT SAYS CANNOT HIT THE PLAYER, COUNTED RATHER THAN MERELY DROPPED.
            //
            // THIS NUMBER IS THE INSTRUMENT FOR THE FIX, NOT DECORATION. `FillTrajectory` declines
            // a projectile whose `HitsPlayer` is false or whose `LocalSeedDerived` is true
            // (SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md section 12), which on the run that produced this line was
            // **51.8 % of every threat record** -- a player's own shots, born inside their collision
            // disc. A frame line with `nohit=0` on a session where the player was shooting means the
            // exclusion is not in force, and `bootstrap.log`'s resolution line says why. A count is
            // the only way to tell "there were none" from "the filter did nothing", and the two look
            // identical in the threat array.
            Line.Append(",\"nohit\":").Append(TrajectorySampler.Declined - declinedBefore);
            Line.Append('}');
            Line.Append('\n');

            _writer.Write(Line.ToString());
            _framesRecorded++;
            _threatsRecorded += written;
            _threatsSkipped += skipped;

            // Flushed periodically rather than per frame: the operator closes the game by hand and
            // a buffer that dies with the process takes the trace with it. Every 30 frames is half
            // a second of exposure, which is the same trade `HookEntry.FlushLog` makes.
            if ((frame % 30) == 0)
            {
                _writer.Flush();
            }

            if (--_framesUntilLog <= 0)
            {
                _framesUntilLog = 600;
                HookEntry.AppendLog("INFO", "trace: " + _framesRecorded + " frame(s), "
                                            + _threatsRecorded + " threat record(s), "
                                            + _threatsSkipped + " culled, "
                                            + (_writer.BaseStream.Length / 1024) + " KB");
                HookEntry.FlushLog();
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether a bullet could reach the player's disc inside the trust prefix.
        ///
        /// A CULL, AND THE DIRECTION OF ITS ERROR MATTERS. It may drop a bullet that would have
        /// mattered only if the sampled path is a bad model of the true one -- and if the model is
        /// that bad, the trace is not evidence about the model anyway. What it must never do is
        /// drop a bullet whose own sampled path crosses the player, which it cannot: this is a
        /// bounding-box test against the very samples the solver would have used.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool CouldReach(Trajectory t, float px, float py, float playerRadius)
        {
            float r = playerRadius + t.Radius;
            float r2 = r * r;
            for (int s = 0; s < t.Count; s++)
            {
                float dx = t.Xs[s] - px;
                float dy = t.Ys[s] - py;
                if ((dx * dx) + (dy * dy) <= r2)
                {
                    return true;
                }
            }
            // Also keep a bullet whose *current* disc is within a few radii, which is the case
            // where the model is least certain and the evidence most valuable.
            float cx = t.Xs[0] - px;
            float cy = t.Ys[0] - py;
            float near = r + 2.0f;
            return (cx * cx) + (cy * cy) <= (near * near);
        }

        private static void AppendThreat(Trajectory t, ThreatKey key)
        {
            // THE IDENTITY IS THE SENSOR'S, NOT THE SAMPLER'S, AND GETTING THAT WRONG MADE THE
            // WHOLE TRACE USELESS FOR T7. `Trajectory` carries a `GameId` field and
            // `TrajectorySampler.FillTrajectory` leaves it at zero on purpose -- identity is not
            // that file's to read (see its comment) and the sensor is the one that resolves it, as
            // `(GameId, startTime)`. The first version of this method wrote `t.GameId` instead of
            // the key it was handed, so **every bullet in the trace was recorded as
            // `GameId = 0`** -- and `(0, startTime)` collides across bullets and matches nothing
            // the game ever resolved. The recorded run read as: 11 predictions, all false
            // positives, and two real collisions the model "never predicted".
            Line.Append("{\"id\":").Append(key.GameId);
            Line.Append(",\"st\":").Append(key.StartTime);
            Line.Append(",\"x\":").Append(Num(t.Xs[0]));
            Line.Append(",\"y\":").Append(Num(t.Ys[0]));
            Line.Append(",\"rad\":").Append(Num(t.Radius));
            Line.Append(",\"lin\":").Append(t.Projectable ? "1" : "0");
            Line.Append(",\"dmg\":").Append(Num(t.Damage));
            Line.Append(",\"dmgp\":").Append(Num(t.DamagePercent));
            Line.Append(",\"mdmg\":").Append(t.ManaDamage);
            Line.Append(",\"n\":").Append(t.Count);
            Line.Append(",\"xs\":[");
            for (int s = 0; s < t.Count; s++)
            {
                if (s > 0)
                {
                    Line.Append(',');
                }
                Line.Append(Num(t.Xs[s]));
            }
            Line.Append("],\"ys\":[");
            for (int s = 0; s < t.Count; s++)
            {
                if (s > 0)
                {
                    Line.Append(',');
                }
                Line.Append(Num(t.Ys[s]));
            }
            Line.Append("],\"alive\":[");
            for (int s = 0; s < t.Count; s++)
            {
                if (s > 0)
                {
                    Line.Append(',');
                }
                Line.Append(t.Alive[s] ? '1' : '0');
            }
            Line.Append("]}");
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // The collision grid
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// Re-reads the window when the player's tile has moved, and writes the `G` record.
        ///
        /// THE WINDOW'S ORIGIN IS THE PLAYER'S TILE MINUS THE RADIUS, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE
        /// GAME'S. `World` indexes its grid with a C cast of the float position (`conv.i4`,
        /// truncation toward zero), so this does the same and the offline harness can therefore
        /// reproduce the game's own walkability answer exactly -- which is the whole point of
        /// recording the grid rather than recording a boolean.
        /// </summary>
        private static void RefreshGrid(object world, float px, float py)
        {
            if (!_gridResolved || _getGridArray == null || _gridAt == null || world == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            int originX = (int)px - GridRadius;
            int originY = (int)py - GridRadius;
            if (!_gridWindowValid || originX != _gridOriginX || originY != _gridOriginY)
            {
                _gridOriginX = originX;
                _gridOriginY = originY;
                _gridDirty = true;
            }

            if (!_gridDirty)
            {
                return;
            }

            object array = _getGridArray(world);
            if (array == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            int w = 2 * GridRadius;
            int h = 2 * GridRadius;
            if (_gridCells.Length < w * h)
            {
                _gridCells = new byte[w * h];
            }

            for (int gy = 0; gy < h; gy++)
            {
                for (int gx = 0; gx < w; gx++)
                {
                    byte c = 0;
                    try
                    {
                        c = _gridAt(array, originX + gx, originY + gy);
                    }
                    catch (Exception)
                    {
                        // Out of the map's bounds. The game's own query bounds-checks and answers
                        // "not solid"; here the reader is told the same thing, and the solver's
                        // own `InWindow` test is what refuses to rely on it for a candidate it
                        // cannot see.
                        c = 0;
                    }
                    _gridCells[(gy * w) + gx] = c;
                }
            }

            _gridWidth = w;
            _gridHeight = h;
            _gridWindowValid = true;
            _gridDirty = false;
            _gridGeneration++;

            // RLE over the linear cell order, which is the encoding the game's own `GmTiles`
            // uses for the same field: (value, runLength) pairs. A window is mostly one value, so
            // this is a few hundred bytes instead of two thousand.
            Line.Length = 0;
            Line.Append("{\"t\":\"G\",\"g\":").Append(_gridGeneration);
            Line.Append(",\"ox\":").Append(originX);
            Line.Append(",\"oy\":").Append(originY);
            Line.Append(",\"w\":").Append(w);
            Line.Append(",\"h\":").Append(h);
            Line.Append(",\"rle\":[");
            int i = 0;
            bool first = true;
            while (i < _gridCells.Length)
            {
                byte value = _gridCells[i];
                int run = 1;
                while (i + run < _gridCells.Length && _gridCells[i + run] == value)
                {
                    run++;
                }
                if (!first)
                {
                    Line.Append(',');
                }
                first = false;
                Line.Append(value).Append(',').Append(run);
                i += run;
            }
            Line.Append("]}\n");
            _writer.Write(Line.ToString());
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // Header, close, and the frame-seconds source
        // ===================================================================================

        private static void WriteHeader()
        {
            Line.Length = 0;
            Line.Append("{\"t\":\"H\",\"v\":1");
            Line.Append(",\"dodge\":\"").Append(EscapeJson(ConfigLine())).Append('"');
            Line.Append(",\"player\":\"").Append(EscapeJson(ManagedArmingProbe.PlayerTypeName)).Append('"');
            Line.Append(",\"projectile\":\"").Append(EscapeJson(SensorRead.ProjectileTypeName)).Append('"');
            Line.Append(",\"samples\":").Append(Trajectory.MaxSamples);
            Line.Append(",\"gridSource\":\"").Append(_gridResolved ? "World.byte[,]" : "none").Append('"');
            Line.Append('}');
            Line.Append('\n');
            _writer.Write(Line.ToString());
            _writer.Flush();
        }

        /// <summary>The configuration the solver would run with, recorded so a trace explains itself.</summary>
        private static string ConfigLine()
        {
            try
            {
                return DodgeConfig.FromEnvironment().Describe();
            }
            catch (Exception)
            {
                return "unavailable";
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Flushes and closes. Safe to call more than once; the process may die without it.</summary>
        public static void Close()
        {
            if (_writer == null)
            {
                return;
            }
            try
            {
                _writer.Flush();
                _writer.Dispose();
            }
            catch (Exception)
            {
                // Nothing useful can be done here, and throwing from a shutdown path is worse.
            }
            _writer = null;
            _enabled = false;
        }

        /// <summary>The counters, for the run summary.</summary>
        public static string Summary()
        {
            if (_path == null)
            {
                return "trace: not enabled (" + _unresolvedReason + ")";
            }
            return "trace: " + _framesRecorded + " frame(s), " + _threatsRecorded
                   + " threat record(s), " + _threatsSkipped + " culled, path " + _path;
        }

        // ===================================================================================
        // Formatting
        // ===================================================================================

        /// <summary>
        /// A float, invariantly formatted and short.
        ///
        /// `R`-style round-tripping is not used: the trace's job is to be read by a float parser,
        /// and four decimals is well inside the tolerance of every quantity here (world units are
        /// metres-of-a-tile and milliseconds are integers). It halves the file, which for a
        /// 30-second recording of 40 bullets is the difference between 7 MB and 14.
        /// </summary>
        private static string Num(float value)
        {
            if (float.IsNaN(value) || float.IsInfinity(value))
            {
                return "0";
            }
            return value.ToString("0.####", Inv);
        }

        private static string Num(double value)
        {
            if (double.IsNaN(value) || double.IsInfinity(value))
            {
                return "0";
            }
            return value.ToString("0.####", Inv);
        }

        private static string EscapeJson(string text)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(text))
            {
                return "";
            }
            // THE CONTROL CHARACTERS ARE ESCAPED, AND FOR A WHILE THEY WERE NOT. This handled the
            // backslash and the quote and nothing else, on the reasoning that a settings string has no
            // exotica in it -- and then `DodgeConfig.Describe` grew a multi-line form, and an
            // UNESCAPED NEWLINE went into a JSON string. The result was not a bad value but a BROKEN
            // FILE: line 3 of `trace.jsonl` read `path enable=True target=1.5s ...`, which every
            // line-by-line reader reports as a corrupt recording, and the blame lands on the trace
            // rather than on the writer. A JSON writer that does not escape control characters is a
            // writer that is one string away from this, so it escapes them.
            return text.Replace("\\", "\\\\")
                       .Replace("\"", "\\\"")
                       .Replace("\r", "\\r")
                       .Replace("\n", "\\n")
                       .Replace("\t", "\\t");
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Bootstrap/TrajectorySampler.cs`:

```cs
// TrajectorySampler.cs -- Deliverable 2.2: call the game's own trajectory, do not
// reimplement it.
//
// THE ONE IDEA THIS FILE IS BUILT AROUND.
//
// `ProjDesc.GetPosition(int time, float sin, float cos, out float x, out float y,
// int gameId)` is virtual, with one override per trajectory family -- straight, wavy,
// parametric, boomerang, orbiting, curving, accelerating, wall-bouncing, homing.  The
// hook CALLS it (DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 4.1) and the decisive reason is the third
// one that section gives: calling it makes the dangerous-position model and the game's
// own collision test exactly consistent by construction, so a dodge cannot disagree
// with the engine about where a bullet will be.  That is the failure mode that makes
// dodges feel haunted, and reimplementing the families is the research project that
// section rules out.
//
// HOW A HOOK WITH NO COMPILE-TIME REFERENCE TO THE GAME CALLS IT ANYWAY.
//
// Reflection's `MethodInfo.Invoke` would work and is unusable: it boxes the two `out`
// floats, allocates an argument array and re-validates the signature on every one of
// twenty-one samples per bullet per frame.  So the call is emitted ONCE, as a
// `DynamicMethod` that does a single `callvirt` and stores the two results into a
// caller-owned `float[2]`.  That is the same technique StartupHook.cs already uses for
// `ldsflda` and `ldflda`, for the same reason: the runtime can answer a question about a
// type the hook cannot name, but only if it is asked once.
//
// `callvirt`, not `call`.  The method looked up is the base `ProjDesc`'s, and virtual
// dispatch is what reaches the concrete family -- a `call` would run the abstract
// declaration's body, which does not exist, or the base's, which would predict every
// bullet as straight.  That failure is silent and is exactly the one the linearity gate
// exists to catch, so this file reports the fraction of straight bullets it sees rather
// than assuming the dispatch worked.
//
// SAMPLING, AND WHY THE STEP MATTERS MORE THAN THE MODEL.
//
// DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 4.2: sampling a path at fractions of its lifetime silently
// aliases anything periodic, so the grid is fixed at 30 ms and bounded at a 600 ms
// horizon -- twenty-one points, one of them at the live anchor.  The step is a sampling
// rate and not a game constant, which is why it needs no adaptation.
//
// AND EVERY SAMPLE SET IS ANCHORED ON THE LIVE POSITION.  The predicted polyline is
// translated by `live - predicted(now)` before anything looks at it (section 4.4 rule 1),
// which makes model error relative rather than cumulative: the point at delta zero is
// exact by construction and the error at the end of the horizon is only however wrong
// the model is over 600 ms.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Reflection.Emit;

namespace Drelay.Bootstrap
{
    public static class TrajectorySampler
    {
        /// <summary>The game's trajectory descriptor base, by the name DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 4.1 cites.</summary>
        public const string DescTypeName = "DarzaCore.Data.ProjDesc";

        /// <summary>Sampling step, in milliseconds.  Section 4.2's fixed grid.</summary>
        public const int StepMs = 30;

        /// <summary>Horizon, in milliseconds.  Section 4.3's derived working value.</summary>
        public const int HorizonMs = 600;

        /// <summary>Thirty-millisecond steps to a 600 ms horizon, plus the anchor.</summary>
        public const int SampleCount = (HorizonMs / StepMs) + 1;

        private delegate void SampleFn(object desc, int time, float sin, float cos,
                                       float[] outPair, int gameId);

        private static bool _resolved;
        private static string _unresolvedReason = "not attempted";

        private static SampleFn _sample;

        // Emitted accessors.  This is the file whose p99 the boxing showed up in: 21 samples
        // per bullet per frame is where a GetValue per field stops being free.
        private static Func<object, object> _getDesc;
        private static Func<object, float> _getSin;
        private static Func<object, float> _getCos;
        private static Func<object, int> _getAge;
        private static Func<object, int> _getStartTime;
        private static Func<object, float> _getProjectileX;
        private static Func<object, float> _getProjectileY;
        private static Func<object, float> _getRadius;
        private static Func<object> _getWorld;
        private static Func<object, object> _getPlayer;
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerX;
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerY;
        private static Func<object> _getClock;
        private static Func<object, float> _getLogicTotal;
        private static FieldInfo _descField;
        private static FieldInfo _sinField;
        private static FieldInfo _cosField;
        private static FieldInfo _ageField;
        private static FieldInfo _positionField;
        private static FieldInfo _pointX;
        private static FieldInfo _pointY;
        private static FieldInfo _radiusField;

        // THE TWO FLAGS THAT DECIDE WHETHER A PROJECTILE IS A THREAT TO THE PLAYER AT ALL.
        // `Projectile.HitsPlayer` is the client's own dispatch condition -- `Hit()` sends a
        // `HitsPlayer == false` projectile to `HitEnemy()` and never to `HitCharacter()` -- and the
        // client's spawn path sets it to `this is Enemy` (`Entity.cs:1600`). So a projectile the
        // local player fired can never reach the player, and neither can an ally's. Both are
        // otherwise indistinguishable from an enemy bullet here: same type, same radius, same
        // position, and they are born at the muzzle, which is inside the player's collision disc.
        //
        // THE MEASUREMENT THAT PUT THEM HERE. On `20261015-151232-p5424`, 932 of 1210 tracked
        // bullets first appear within 0.3 units of the player and fly away -- a three-shot spread
        // every 8 frames -- and they were **51.8 % of every threat record in the session**, 959 of
        // its 971 "already touching" verdicts, and the cause of 255 of its 1140 moves. A player who
        // was merely shooting had the dodge taking the wheel around its own muzzle.
        private static FieldInfo _hitsPlayerField;
        private static FieldInfo _localSeedField;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getHitsPlayer;
        private static Func<object, bool> _getLocalSeed;

        /// <summary>What the resolution log calls the two exclusion flags, found or MISSING.</summary>
        private static string _cannotHitNames = "not attempted";

        /// <summary>
        /// Projectiles the sampler declined because the client says they cannot hit a player.
        ///
        /// IT COUNTS OBSERVATIONS, NOT PROJECTILES, AND EVERY CONSUMER TAKES A DELTA. Three callers
        /// walk the same frame's projectile list -- the sensor's own predictor, the adapter and the
        /// recorder -- so one own shot is declined three times here and this number is roughly three
        /// times the number of own shots fired. That is harmless and intended, because no consumer
        /// reads it as a total: each wraps its own loop and reports the difference, which is that
        /// caller's own count for that frame.
        /// </summary>
        public static long Declined;

        /// <summary>
        /// True when the exclusion is actually in force. False means `HitsPlayer` did not resolve and
        /// the threat set still contains the player's own shots -- a degraded run, and one the
        /// reports say so on rather than leaving to be inferred from a count.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool CannotHitFilterResolved => _getHitsPlayer != null || _getLocalSeed != null;

        // THE TIME BASE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THE CLIENT DOES NOT STORE.  The host carries
        // an AgeMs per projectile; the client does not, and computes the age itself as
        // 	ime.LogicTotal - _startTime (CLIENT-FINDINGS.md section 4, Projectile.cs:670).
        // So when there is no age field, the age is DERIVED from the game's own clock:
        // DarzasDominion.Graphics.DarzaWindow.Time is a public static ClientTime, and
        // ClientTime.LogicTotal is a public float in milliseconds.
        private static FieldInfo _startTimeField;
        private static FieldInfo _clientTimeField;
        private static FieldInfo _logicTotalField;
        private static bool _deriveAgeFromClock;

        // The player, for the intersection test that turns a sampled polyline into a
        // prediction Deliverable 2.3 can compare against.
        private static FieldInfo _worldSharedField;
        private static FieldInfo _worldPlayerField;
        private static FieldInfo _playerPositionField;
        private static FieldInfo _playerX;
        private static FieldInfo _playerY;
        private static FieldInfo _playerRadiusField;

        /// <summary>Reads `World.Player.Radius`. Null when the field was not found.</summary>
        private static Func<object, float> _getPlayerRadius;

        private static readonly float[] Xs = new float[SampleCount];
        private static readonly float[] Ys = new float[SampleCount];
        private static readonly float[] Pair = new float[2];

        private static long _framesSampled;
        private static long _bulletsSampled;
        private static long _straight;
        private static long _curved;
        private static long _lastCostUs;
        private static long _maxCostUs;
        private static long _nextLogFrame = 150;

        /// <summary>Bucketed per-frame sampler cost, kept apart from the read's.</summary>
        public static readonly CostHistogram Cost = new CostHistogram();

        public static bool Resolved => _resolved;
        public static string UnresolvedReason => _unresolvedReason;

        /// <summary>Fraction of sampled bullets whose trajectory may be projected. Zero when nothing has been sampled.</summary>
        public static double StraightFraction
        {
            get
            {
                long total = _straight + _curved;
                return total == 0 ? 0.0 : (double)_straight / total;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The linearity counts, published so the phase's fifth number can ride on the
        /// same line as the other four.
        ///
        /// WHY THEY MOVED.  `LogSummary` held these and was never called -- the sensor has
        /// no orderly shutdown to call it from, because the operator kills the game rather
        /// than letting it exit -- so the straight fraction, which is one of the numbers
        /// Phase 2 exists to produce, was reachable only by finding the sampler's own
        /// periodic line.  A number that lives in a different place than the numbers it is
        /// read with gets read wrongly; that is the same lesson PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 4.9
        /// records for the four.
        /// </summary>
        public static long StraightCount => _straight;

        /// <summary>Bullets the gate refused to project; see <see cref="StraightCount"/>.</summary>
        public static long CurvedCount => _curved;

        /// <summary>Bullet sample sets taken so far.</summary>
        public static long BulletsSampled => _bulletsSampled;

        /// <summary>
        /// Resolves the fields and emits the call.  Failure is not fatal: the frame read,
        /// the patch and the threat set all keep working, and the reason is logged.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool Resolve(Assembly game)
        {
            const BindingFlags Any = BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic
                                   | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Static;
            try
            {
                Type projectileType = game.GetType(SensorRead.ProjectileTypeName);
                Type descType = game.GetType(DescTypeName);
                if (projectileType == null || descType == null)
                {
```
