`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/ConfigFile.cs`:

```cs
// ConfigFile.cs -- the user-facing configuration file.
//
// HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 5 is the specification: the file lives at
// %LOCALAPPDATA%\drelay\hook\drelay.config.json, and it is read with System.Text.Json
// (already in the shared framework -- no new dependency) into a `Settings`, the same type
// the command line fills, so that the merge in `Options.Apply` is the only place
// precedence exists.
//
// THREE RULES FROM SECTION 5, AND EACH ONE IS A DESIGN DECISION RATHER THAN A STYLE:
//
//   1. A MISSING FILE IS NOT AN ERROR.  It means "defaults", and the first-run path
//      (section 6) is the only thing that creates one.
//   2. AN UNPARSEABLE *FIELD* IS A REFUSAL WITH A NAMED FIELD, NOT A SILENT DEFAULT.  A
//      typo in `"AutoAim": "closests"` must fail the way `--autoaim closests` already
//      does.  A typo that silently resolves to "off" costs a session spent watching the
//      game not aim.
//   3. TEST-HARNESS FLAGS ARE NOT IN THE SCHEMA.  `--test-target`, `--frame-helper`,
//      `--frame-replacement`, `--assembly`, `--exe`, `--off`, `--full-trace`, `--trace`,
//      `--move-steer` and `--escape-test` stay command-line-only: a user-facing config
//      that offers `FrameHelper` is offering a switch that allocates 64 KB per frame on
//      purpose.  A config file that mentions one of them is refusing nothing -- the key is
//      simply unknown, and unknown keys are ignored.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One row of the schema: the JSON key as a user writes it, and the flag it lands on.
    ///
    /// THE TABLE IS THE ANSWER TO SECTION 13 C7 ("every field of the config has a
    /// corresponding flag, and every user-facing flag a field").  It is data rather than
    /// prose so the test can assert it in both directions instead of trusting a table in a
    /// document: `LauncherHarness --check c7` walks this array, and separately compares it
    /// against the keys the reader actually recognised on a document that contains exactly
    /// these keys.
    /// </summary>
    internal sealed class ConfigField
    {
        public readonly string Key;
        public readonly string Flag;

        public ConfigField(string key, string flag)
        {
            Key = key;
            Flag = flag;
        }
    }

    internal static class ConfigFile
    {
        public const string FileName = "drelay.config.json";

        /// <summary>The field table of section 5.1, as data.</summary>
        public static readonly ConfigField[] Schema = new ConfigField[]
        {
            new ConfigField("GamePath", "--game"),
            new ConfigField("AutoAim", "--autoaim"),
            new ConfigField("Dodge.Enabled", "--dodge"),
            new ConfigField("Dodge.Act", "--dodge-act"),
            new ConfigField("Dodge.DecisionDisc", "--dodge-disc"),
            new ConfigField("Dodge.WindowSeconds", "--dodge-window"),
            new ConfigField("CollectDelayMs", "--collect-delay"),
            new ConfigField("DiscoveryWindowMs", "--discovery-ms"),
            new ConfigField("ResolveDelayMs", "--resolve-delay"),
            new ConfigField("LiveSeconds", "--live-seconds"),
            new ConfigField("PauseAfterRun", "--pause-after-run"),
            new ConfigField("RunRoot", "--runroot"),
            new ConfigField("DbgDump", "--dbg-dump"),
            new ConfigField("Verbose", "--verbose"),
            new ConfigField("NoWait", "--no-wait"),
            new ConfigField("TimeoutMs", "--timeout"),
            new ConfigField("Hook", "--hook"),
            new ConfigField("Bootstrap", "--bootstrap"),
        };

        /// <summary>
        /// The default location: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\drelay\hook\drelay.config.json`, which is the
        /// same root the run directories are already created under.
        ///
        /// NOT BESIDE THE EXECUTABLE, because the zip may be unpacked somewhere read-only
        /// (Program Files, a network share), and a first-run experience that cannot write its
        /// own config is not a first-run experience.
        /// </summary>
        public static string Directory(string localAppData)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(localAppData))
            {
                localAppData = Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData);
            }
            return Path.Combine(localAppData, "drelay", "hook");
        }

        public static string DefaultPath(string localAppData)
        {
            return Path.Combine(Directory(localAppData), FileName);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Read the file into a `Settings` in which only the keys actually present are set.
        ///
        /// <paramref name="recognised"/> is how many keys of the schema were seen, and it is an
        /// output rather than a hidden counter for the C7 test: fed a document containing every
        /// key in <see cref="Schema"/>, the reader must recognise exactly those keys, so a key
        /// added to this method without being added to the table is a test failure rather than a
        /// silent extra setting.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool TryRead(string path, out Settings settings, out List<string> recognised,
                                   out string error)
        {
            settings = new Settings();
            recognised = new List<string>();
            error = null;

            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(path) || !File.Exists(path))
            {
                // Rule 1: a missing file is not an error.
                return true;
            }

            string text;
            try
            {
                text = File.ReadAllText(path);
            }
            catch (IOException ex)
            {
                error = path + ": cannot be read: " + ex.Message;
                return false;
            }
            catch (UnauthorizedAccessException ex)
            {
                error = path + ": cannot be read: " + ex.Message;
                return false;
            }

            if (text.Trim().Length == 0)
            {
                // An empty file is a file with nothing in it, which is what a user who opened the
                // template and deleted the contents has.  It means "defaults", like a missing file.
                return true;
            }

            JsonDocument document;
            try
            {
                document = JsonDocument.Parse(text, new JsonDocumentOptions
                {
                    // `CommentHandling = Skip` and `AllowTrailingCommas` so a user's stray comment
                    // or trailing comma is not a startup failure.  The template itself is written
                    // with comments, so this is not a convenience: it is required by the file the
                    // launcher writes.
                    CommentHandling = JsonCommentHandling.Skip,
                    AllowTrailingCommas = true,
                });
            }
            catch (JsonException ex)
            {
                error = path + ": is not valid JSON: " + ex.Message;
                return false;
            }

            using (document)
            {
                JsonElement root = document.RootElement;
                if (root.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object)
                {
                    error = path + ": the top level must be a JSON object, not " + Describe(root);
                    return false;
                }

                foreach (JsonProperty property in root.EnumerateObject())
                {
                    if (!ApplyProperty(path, property, settings, recognised, ref error))
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
            }

            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// One top-level key.  Unknown keys are ignored (section 11 step 2); a known key with the
        /// wrong type or a bad value refuses and names the key.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool ApplyProperty(string file, JsonProperty property, Settings settings,
                                          List<string> recognised, ref string error)
        {
            switch (property.Name.ToLowerInvariant())
            {
                case "gamepath":
                    recognised.Add("GamePath");
                    return ReadString(file, property, ref settings.GamePath, ref error);

                case "autoaim":
                    recognised.Add("AutoAim");
                    if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
                    {
                        // Null is "off", which is the same statement as the key's absence: the
                        // written template leaves it null rather than "closest", because aiming
                        // is an action with a real side effect (`Prefs.enable_aimbot` is set and
                        // persisted).  Section 9.3.
                        settings.AutoAim = null;
                        return true;
                    }
                    if (property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String)
                    {
                        error = Field(file, "AutoAim", "must be a mode name or null, got " + Describe(property.Value));
                        return false;
                    }
                    if (!Options.TryParseAutoAim(property.Value.GetString(), out string mode, out string why))
                    {
                        error = file + ": AutoAim " + why;
                        return false;
                    }
                    settings.AutoAim = mode;
                    return true;

                case "dodge":
                    return ReadDodge(file, property, settings, recognised, ref error);

                case "collectdelayms":
                    recognised.Add("CollectDelayMs");
                    return ReadInt(file, property, "CollectDelayMs", ref settings.CollectDelayMs, ref error);

                case "discoverywindowms":
                    recognised.Add("DiscoveryWindowMs");
                    return ReadInt(file, property, "DiscoveryWindowMs", ref settings.DiscoveryWindowMs, ref error);

                case "resolvedelayms":
                    recognised.Add("ResolveDelayMs");
                    return ReadInt(file, property, "ResolveDelayMs", ref settings.ResolveDelayMs, ref error);

                case "liveseconds":
                    recognised.Add("LiveSeconds");
                    return ReadInt(file, property, "LiveSeconds", ref settings.LiveSeconds, ref error);

                case "pauseafterrun":
                    recognised.Add("PauseAfterRun");
                    return ReadBool(file, property, "PauseAfterRun", ref settings.PauseAfterRun, ref error);

                case "runroot":
                    recognised.Add("RunRoot");
                    return ReadString(file, property, ref settings.RunRoot, ref error);

                case "dbgdump":
                    recognised.Add("DbgDump");
                    return ReadBool(file, property, "DbgDump", ref settings.DbgDump, ref error);

                case "verbose":
                    recognised.Add("Verbose");
                    return ReadBool(file, property, "Verbose", ref settings.Verbose, ref error);

                case "nowait":
                    recognised.Add("NoWait");
                    return ReadBool(file, property, "NoWait", ref settings.NoWait, ref error);

                case "timeoutms":
                    recognised.Add("TimeoutMs");
                    return ReadInt(file, property, "TimeoutMs", ref settings.TimeoutMs, ref error);

                case "hook":
                    recognised.Add("Hook");
                    return ReadString(file, property, ref settings.HookDll, ref error);

                case "bootstrap":
                    recognised.Add("Bootstrap");
                    return ReadString(file, property, ref settings.BootstrapDll, ref error);

                default:
                    // Unknown keys are ignored, on purpose: a config that carries a key from a
                    // later version must not stop this one from starting.
                    return true;
            }
        }

        private static bool ReadDodge(string file, JsonProperty property, Settings settings,
                                      List<string> recognised, ref string error)
        {
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
            {
                return true;
            }
            if (property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object)
            {
                error = Field(file, "Dodge", "must be an object, got " + Describe(property.Value));
                return false;
            }
            recognised.Add("Dodge");
            foreach (JsonProperty child in property.Value.EnumerateObject())
            {
                switch (child.Name.ToLowerInvariant())
                {
                    case "enabled":
                        recognised.Add("Dodge.Enabled");
                        if (!ReadBool(file, child, "Dodge.Enabled", ref settings.Dodge, ref error)) { return false; }
                        break;
                    case "act":
                        recognised.Add("Dodge.Act");
                        if (!ReadBool(file, child, "Dodge.Act", ref settings.DodgeAct, ref error)) { return false; }
                        // `Act` implies `Enabled`, exactly as `--dodge-act` does.  The implication
                        // itself is applied once, in `Options.ApplyImplications`.
                        break;
                    case "decisiondisc":
                        recognised.Add("Dodge.DecisionDisc");
                        if (!ReadDouble(file, child, "Dodge.DecisionDisc", ref settings.DodgeDisc, ref error))
                        {
                            return false;
                        }
                        break;
                    case "windowseconds":
                        recognised.Add("Dodge.WindowSeconds");
                        if (!ReadDouble(file, child, "Dodge.WindowSeconds", ref settings.DodgeWindowSeconds, ref error))
                        {
                            return false;
                        }
                        break;
                    default:
                        break;
                }
            }
            return true;
        }

        private static bool ReadBool(string file, JsonProperty property, string key,
                                     ref bool? value, ref string error)
        {
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
            {
                // Null means "not set" everywhere in this schema, which is what keeps the
                // compiled default in charge (section 10.5).
                return true;
            }
            if (property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.True && property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.False)
            {
                error = Field(file, key, "must be true or false, got " + Describe(property.Value));
                return false;
            }
            value = property.Value.GetBoolean();
            return true;
        }

        private static bool ReadInt(string file, JsonProperty property, string key,
                                    ref int? value, ref string error)
        {
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
            {
                return true;
            }
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Number && property.Value.TryGetInt32(out int parsed))
            {
                if (parsed < 0)
                {
                    error = Field(file, key, "must be a non-negative whole number, got " + parsed);
                    return false;
                }
                value = parsed;
                return true;
            }
            error = Field(file, key, "must be a non-negative whole number, got " + Describe(property.Value));
            return false;
        }

        private static bool ReadDouble(string file, JsonProperty property, string key,
                                       ref double? value, ref string error)
        {
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
            {
                // `null` here is the same statement as `-1.0` on the command line: "not set", so
                // the solver's own default applies.
                return true;
            }
            if (property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number
                || !property.Value.TryGetDouble(out double parsed)
                || parsed < 0.0
                || double.IsNaN(parsed)
                || double.IsInfinity(parsed))
            {
                error = Field(file, key, "must be a non-negative number or null, got " + Describe(property.Value));
                return false;
            }
            value = parsed;
            return true;
        }

        private static bool ReadString(string file, JsonProperty property, ref string value, ref string error)
        {
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null)
            {
                return true;
            }
            if (property.Value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String)
            {
                error = Field(file, property.Name, "must be a string or null, got " + Describe(property.Value));
                return false;
            }
            string text = property.Value.GetString();
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(text))
            {
                value = text;
            }
            return true;
        }

        private static string Field(string file, string key, string what)
        {
            return file + ": " + key + " " + what;
        }

        private static string Describe(JsonElement element)
        {
            switch (element.ValueKind)
            {
                case JsonValueKind.String: return "a string";
                case JsonValueKind.Number: return "a number";
                case JsonValueKind.True:
                case JsonValueKind.False: return "a boolean";
                case JsonValueKind.Array: return "an array";
                case JsonValueKind.Object: return "an object";
                case JsonValueKind.Null: return "null";
                default: return element.ValueKind.ToString().ToLowerInvariant();
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The template a first run writes, and -- because it is written before the configuration
        /// is resolved -- the settings that first run actually uses.
        ///
        /// IT IS NOT THE COMPILED DEFAULTS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT.  `Options`' defaults
        /// are all-off so that nothing acts unless it was asked; this file is the asking.  It turns
        /// on the two things a drelay session is for -- auto-aim at the closest damageable enemy,
        /// and the live dodge -- and it says so in the comments, in the same file, so that turning
        /// either off is an edit rather than a search.
        ///
        /// THIS DEVIATES FROM SECTION 9.3, WHICH SAID THE TEMPLATE LEAVES `AutoAim` NULL, AND THE
        /// DEVIATION IS THE OPERATOR'S DECISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.  The argument against it
        /// stands and is worth remembering: aiming arms and persists the game's own
        /// `Prefs.enable_aimbot`, and the dodge moves the player.  The argument for it is that the
        /// alternative shipped a launcher whose headline feature -- "double-click it" -- attached a
        /// hook that did nothing, which is what the first no-argument run of 2026-10-16 reported.
        /// §15 records the decision and the state the file is in now.
        ///
        /// `DecisionDisc` AND `WindowSeconds` STAY NULL because their defaults belong to
        /// `DodgeConfig.Default()` and are not written down twice (section 10.5).  `ResolveDelayMs`,
        /// `RunRoot`, `DbgDump`, `Verbose`, `NoWait`, `TimeoutMs`, `Hook` and `Bootstrap` are in the
        /// schema and deliberately NOT in the template.
        /// </summary>
        public static string Template()
        {
            var text = new StringBuilder();
            text.Append("{\n");
            text.Append("  // drelay hook configuration. Written by a first run, and used by it.\n");
            text.Append("  //\n");
            text.Append("  // This is what a launch with no arguments does: auto-aim at the closest\n");
            text.Append("  // damageable enemy, and the live dodge (the solver decides every frame and\n");
            text.Append("  // steers the player when it has a move). Turn either off by setting\n");
            text.Append("  // \"AutoAim\" to null or \"Dodge\".\"Act\" to false.\n");
            text.Append("  //\n");
            text.Append("  // Every key is optional; a key that is absent or null means \"the launcher's\n");
            text.Append("  // default\". The command line always wins over this file: `--autoaim highesthp`\n");
            text.Append("  // beside \"AutoAim\": \"closest\" runs highesthp.\n");
            text.Append("\n");
            text.Append("  // Required unless the game is discovered or --game is given.\n");
            text.Append("  \"GamePath\": \"\",\n");
            text.Append("\n");
            text.Append("  // What the hook does. These are the release-relevant ones.\n");
            text.Append("  \"AutoAim\": \"closest\",     // \"closest\" | \"highesthp\" | null (off)\n");
            text.Append("  \"Dodge\": {\n");
            text.Append("    \"Enabled\": true,        // run the solver every frame and log decisions\n");
            text.Append("    \"Act\": true,            // ...and let the decision steer the player.\n");
            text.Append("                            // false still solves and logs; it just never moves you\n");
            text.Append("    \"DecisionDisc\": null,   // --dodge-disc, multiples of the disc-crossing time\n");
            text.Append("    \"WindowSeconds\": null   // --dodge-window, absolute floor in seconds\n");
            text.Append("  },\n");
            text.Append("\n");
            text.Append("  // Timing. The first two are reporting bounds: the patch no longer waits for\n");
            text.Append("  // the discovery window, so these only decide when the per-target verdicts are\n");
            text.Append("  // measured and how long the evidence recording runs.\n");
            text.Append("  \"CollectDelayMs\": 0,\n");
            text.Append("  \"DiscoveryWindowMs\": 10000,\n");
            text.Append("  \"LiveSeconds\": 5,\n");
            text.Append("  \"PauseAfterRun\": false    // true restores the pre-0.2 behaviour: stop reading\n");
            text.Append("                            // the world when the evidence window closes\n");
            text.Append("}\n");
            return text.ToString();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Write the template, creating the directory if it is not there yet.
        ///
        /// IT NEVER OVERWRITES: it is called only when the file does not exist, and it checks once
        /// more here so a future caller cannot delete a user's settings by accident.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool WriteTemplate(string path, out string error)
        {
            error = null;
            try
            {
                if (File.Exists(path))
                {
                    return true;
                }
                string dir = Path.GetDirectoryName(path);
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(dir))
                {
                    System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
                }
                File.WriteAllText(path, Template(), new UTF8Encoding(false));
                return true;
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException || ex is UnauthorizedAccessException
                                       || ex is NotSupportedException || ex is ArgumentException)
            {
                error = path + ": cannot be written: " + ex.Message;
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/Configuration.cs`:

```cs
// Configuration.cs -- the one place the four sources are merged.
//
// HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 4:
//
//   1. command line             --game, --autoaim, ...        (highest)
//   2. config file              drelay.config.json
//   3. auto-discovery           Steam / recordedFrom / cwd
//   4. compiled defaults        the numbers in Options        (lowest)
//
// FIELD BY FIELD, NOT SOURCE BY SOURCE (section 4.1).  `--autoaim highesthp` on the command
// line must not discard a `GamePath` that only the config file knows, and a config file that
// sets two fields must not discard the compiled defaults for the rest.
//
// WHY THIS IS ITS OWN FILE.  The merge is the single most error-prone part of the feature --
// its failure mode is a setting that silently does not apply -- and section 13 C1 is a named
// invariant about it.  Keeping it out of `Program.Main` is what lets the offline harness run
// the *shipped* merge rather than a copy of it, with a fake discovery environment standing in
// for the registry.

using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    internal enum ResolveOutcome
    {
        /// <summary>Every source was merged and every path resolved; `Options` is usable.</summary>
        Ready,

        /// <summary>No source named the game and discovery did not find it. The caller reports.</summary>
        NoGamePath,

        /// <summary>A source supplied a contradictory or unusable value; `Error` says which.</summary>
        Invalid,
    }

    internal sealed class ResolveResult
    {
        public ResolveOutcome Outcome;
        public Options Options;
        public DiscoveryResult Discovery;
        public string Error;

        /// <summary>
        /// Things the merge decided that the operator did not literally ask for and would not
        /// otherwise see.  Reported by the caller rather than printed here, because the offline
        /// harness runs this same function and a resolve that writes to the console cannot be
        /// checked.
        /// </summary>
        public List<string> Notices = new List<string>();
    }

    internal static class Configuration
    {
        public static ResolveResult Resolve(
            Settings config, Settings cli, List<string> gameArguments,
            IDiscoveryEnv discoveryEnv, PinnedBuild pinned, string launcherDirectory)
        {
            var result = new ResolveResult();

            var options = new Options();

            // 1. the compiled defaults are `Options`' own field initialisers, so the config
            //    file is the first overlay and a field it does not mention is untouched.
            options.Apply(config);

            //    THE FILE'S ACTING REQUEST IS REMEMBERED BEFORE THE COMMAND LINE IS APPLIED,
            //    because the command line can replace the *actuator* without touching the field
            //    that asked for it.  See the note at the resolution below.
            bool actingRequestedByFile = options.DodgeAct;

            // 2. the command line, which wins over the config file for every field it sets.
            options.Apply(cli);

            options.GameArguments = gameArguments ?? new List<string>();

            // 2a. THE COMMAND LINE'S ACTUATOR CHOICE BEATS THE FILE'S, AND ONLY WHEN IT MADE ONE.
            //
            // `Dodge.Act` and `--move-steer` both say "this is what steers the player", so they
            // contradict each other, and per-field precedence cannot express that on its own: the
            // two live in different fields, so the file's `Act` would survive a command line that
            // asked for a different pilot.  Two spells of the same contradiction therefore resolve
            // differently, and the difference is who is doing the deciding:
            //
            //   * `--dodge-act --move-steer X`, both typed by hand, is a mistake and is REFUSED
            //     (`Options.Validate`) -- a run that quietly moved the player the way one of two
            //     contradictory flags asked is the surprise `--move-steer`'s design exists to
            //     prevent;
            //   * `"Act": true` in the file with `--move-steer X` on the command line is a RUN,
            //     because the command line is the more specific statement: it wins, `Act` is
            //     cleared for this run, and the notice below says so.  Without this, the release
            //     default itself would break `Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Sweep/Hold`, which
            //     passes `--move-steer` and cannot turn a config field off.
            //
            // The file's `Dodge.Enabled` is NOT cleared: solving and logging do not contradict
            // "somebody else steers", and a field the operator set is not discarded silently.
            if (actingRequestedByFile && !cli.DodgeAct.HasValue && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(cli.MoveSteer))
            {
                options.DodgeAct = false;
                result.Notices.Add(
                    "--move-steer '" + cli.MoveSteer + "' chose the actuator, so \"Dodge\": "
                    + "{\"Act\": true} from the configuration file is off for this run. The solver "
                    + "still runs and logs; set \"Dodge\": {\"Enabled\": false} as well to stop it.");
            }

            // 3. auto-discovery, and ONLY for a GamePath no other source supplied.
            //
            //    Section 4.1's diagram draws discovery between the config file and the command
            //    line, which would make it beat the config file; section 4's table says the
            //    config file beats auto-discovery, and section 6 says discovery runs "if GamePath
            //    is still unknown".  Those agree on one behaviour and this is it: discovery may
            //    fill a GamePath, never overwrite one.  The order of the two overlays is therefore
            //    unobservable, and the command line is applied first so that a `--game` never even
            //    pays for the probe.
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.GamePath))
            {
                result.Discovery = Discovery.Find(discoveryEnv, pinned);
                if (result.Discovery.Found)
                {
                    options.GamePath = result.Discovery.GameDirectory;
                    options.DiscoveredFrom = result.Discovery.GameDirectory;
                }
            }

            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.GamePath))
            {
                result.Outcome = ResolveOutcome.NoGamePath;
                result.Options = options;
                return result;
            }

            // 4. the contradictions, checked BEFORE the implications, because the implications are
            //    what make `--dodge-act` and `--move-steer` agree and a check that ran after them
            //    could never fire.
            if (!options.Validate(out string error))
            {
                result.Outcome = ResolveOutcome.Invalid;
                result.Error = error;
                result.Options = options;
                return result;
            }

            // 5. the flags that imply other flags, once, for both sources (section 10.6).
            options.ApplyImplications();

            // 6. absolute paths, and the three that default to "beside the launcher".
            options.ResolvePaths(launcherDirectory, out error);
            if (error != null)
            {
                result.Outcome = ResolveOutcome.Invalid;
                result.Error = error;
                result.Options = options;
                return result;
            }

            result.Outcome = ResolveOutcome.Ready;
            result.Options = options;
            return result;
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/Discovery.cs`:

```cs
// Discovery.cs -- finding the game when nobody said where it is.
//
// HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 7 is the specification.  The probe order is fixed and
// first-hit-wins:
//
//   1. HKCU\Software\Valve\Steam -> SteamPath (falling back to
//      HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Valve\Steam -> InstallPath), then
//      <steam>\steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf, then every library in it.  This is the FIRST
//      probe and not the last, because on a Steam machine it is the only one that is right;
//      the pinned record is the fallback, not the other way round.
//   2. The pinned record, `GeneratedBuildTable.RecordedFrom` -- the machine the build was
//      verified on.  Exactly the case where it is right, and one absent path when it is wrong.
//   3. <launcher dir> and its parent -- covers "unpacked into the game folder", which is what
//      the release notes tell the user to do anyway.
//
// DISCOVERY PRODUCES A CANDIDATE; THE GATE DECIDES.  Finding a directory named
// `Darza's Dominion` does not make it the right build, and the two apphosts that ship together
// carry *different* assemblies: the root `DarzasDominion.exe` is the pinned one and the one
// under `OpenGL\` is not.  So a candidate is only accepted when the assembly beside the apphost
// is the pinned size, and the OpenGL variant is named as the problem rather than silently
// skipped -- a user with the OpenGL install needs to know that is what is wrong (section 7).
//
// THE ENVIRONMENT IS AN INTERFACE.  Everything this file needs -- the registry, the
// filesystem, the launcher's own directory -- arrives through `IDiscoveryEnv`, so the Steam
// library walk is testable against a fake tree with no Steam, no game and no registry
// (section 11 step 3).  The Windows implementation is `DiscoveryWindows.cs`, which is the one
// file the offline harness does not compile.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.IO;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    /// <summary>Everything discovery is allowed to look at.</summary>
    internal interface IDiscoveryEnv
    {
        bool TryReadRegistryString(string keyPath, string valueName, out string value);
        string ReadTextOrNull(string path);
        bool DirectoryExists(string path);
        bool FileExists(string path);
        long FileSize(string path);
        string LauncherDirectory { get; }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The pinned build, as discovery needs it.  A parameter rather than a direct read of
    /// <c>GeneratedBuildTable</c> so that this file -- and the test that walks a fake Steam
    /// tree -- compiles without the bootstrap assembly.
    /// </summary>
    internal sealed class PinnedBuild
    {
        public string RecordedFrom;
        public string ExecutableFileName;
        public string AssemblyFileName;
        public long AssemblySize;
        public long AssemblySizeOpenGlVariant;
        public int SteamAppId;

        /// <summary>The directory name the pinned record used, e.g. `Darza's Dominion`.</summary>
        public string RecordedDirectoryName
        {
            get
            {
                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RecordedFrom)) { return null; }
                return Path.GetFileName(RecordedFrom.TrimEnd('\\', '/'));
            }
        }
    }

    internal sealed class DiscoveryResult
    {
        /// <summary>The game directory, or null when discovery failed.</summary>
        public string GameDirectory;

        /// <summary>The human-readable refusal, or null on success.</summary>
        public string Failure;

        /// <summary>
        /// True when the failure is "this is the OpenGL install".  It is a separate flag from
        /// `Failure` because the first-run path treats it differently: it is a refusal the user
        /// cannot fix by editing the config file (section 6's second rule), so it is printed and
        /// not paused on.
        /// </summary>
        public bool OpenGlVariant;

        public bool Found { get { return GameDirectory != null; } }
    }

    internal static class Discovery
    {
        private const string SteamKeyCurrentUser = @"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam";
        private const string SteamKeyMachine = @"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Valve\Steam";
        private const string SteamPathValue = "SteamPath";
        private const string SteamInstallPathValue = "InstallPath";

        public static DiscoveryResult Find(IDiscoveryEnv env, PinnedBuild pinned)
        {
            var result = new DiscoveryResult();
            if (env == null || pinned == null)
            {
                result.Failure = "discovery has no environment to look in";
                return result;
            }

            var candidates = new List<string>();
            var problems = new List<string>();

            foreach (string probe in CandidateDirectories(env, pinned))
            {
                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(probe)) { continue; }
                string directory = Trim(probe);
                if (!env.DirectoryExists(directory)) { continue; }

                string exe = Path.Combine(directory, pinned.ExecutableFileName);
                if (!env.FileExists(exe)) { continue; }

                string assembly = Path.Combine(directory, pinned.AssemblyFileName);
                if (!env.FileExists(assembly))
                {
                    problems.Add(directory + ": has " + pinned.ExecutableFileName
                                 + " but no " + pinned.AssemblyFileName);
                    continue;
                }

                long size = env.FileSize(assembly);
                if (size == pinned.AssemblySize)
                {
                    result.GameDirectory = directory;
                    return result;
                }
                if (size == pinned.AssemblySizeOpenGlVariant)
                {
                    // NAMED, NOT SKIPPED.  Retrying the next candidate would hide the one
                    // explanation the user needs: the hook only knows the root apphost, and this
                    // directory holds the OpenGL build.
                    result.OpenGlVariant = true;
                    result.Failure = directory + " holds the OpenGL build of the game ("
                                     + pinned.AssemblyFileName + " is " + size + " bytes, the pinned "
                                     + "DirectX one is " + pinned.AssemblySize + " bytes), and only the "
                                     + "root " + pinned.ExecutableFileName + " is the build this hook was "
                                     + "compiled against. Point GamePath at the root install.";
                    return result;
                }

                problems.Add(directory + ": " + pinned.AssemblyFileName + " is " + size
                             + " bytes, not the pinned " + pinned.AssemblySize);
            }

            result.Failure = problems.Count > 0
                ? "a directory named like the game was found, but not the pinned build: "
                  + string.Join("; ", problems.ToArray())
                : "no Steam library, no pinned location and no launcher directory held the game";
            return result;
        }

        /// <summary>The probe list, in order, with duplicates removed.</summary>
        private static IEnumerable<string> CandidateDirectories(IDiscoveryEnv env, PinnedBuild pinned)
        {
            var seen = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            var results = new List<string>();

            foreach (string candidate in SteamCandidates(env, pinned))
            {
                if (seen.Add(candidate)) { results.Add(candidate); }
            }

            foreach (string candidate in PinnedAndLocal(env, pinned))
            {
                if (seen.Add(candidate)) { results.Add(candidate); }
            }

            return results;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Probe 1: the Steam registry, the library list, and the app manifest.
        ///
        /// THE APP ID IS USED FOR THE MANIFEST, NOT FOR THE DIRECTORY.  `appmanifest_<id>.acf`
        /// names the install directory the user actually got (`"installdir"`), which is the
        /// authoritative answer and survives a rename; the pinned record's own leaf name is the
        /// fallback for a library whose manifest was not written yet.  Neither is trusted to be
        /// the right *build*: that is what the size check above is for.
        /// </summary>
        private static IEnumerable<string> SteamCandidates(IDiscoveryEnv env, PinnedBuild pinned)
        {
            var results = new List<string>();

            string steam = null;
            if (!env.TryReadRegistryString(SteamKeyCurrentUser, SteamPathValue, out steam)
                || string.IsNullOrEmpty(steam))
            {
                env.TryReadRegistryString(SteamKeyMachine, SteamInstallPathValue, out steam);
            }
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(steam)) { return results; }

            var libraries = new List<string>();
            string libraryFolders = Path.Combine(steam, "steamapps", "libraryfolders.vdf");
            string vdf = env.ReadTextOrNull(libraryFolders);
            if (vdf != null)
            {
                libraries.AddRange(ParseQuotedValue(vdf, "path"));
            }
            if (libraries.Count == 0)
            {
                // The registry path is itself a library, and on a single-drive install the VDF
                // says nothing the registry did not already say.
                libraries.Add(steam);
            }

            foreach (string library in libraries)
            {
                string common = Path.Combine(library, "steamapps", "common");

                string manifest = Path.Combine(library, "steamapps",
                                               "appmanifest_" + pinned.SteamAppId + ".acf");
                string acf = env.ReadTextOrNull(manifest);
                if (acf != null)
                {
                    List<string> installDirs = ParseQuotedValue(acf, "installdir");
                    if (installDirs.Count > 0)
                    {
                        results.Add(Path.Combine(common, installDirs[0]));
                    }
                }

                string recordedName = pinned.RecordedDirectoryName;
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(recordedName))
                {
                    results.Add(Path.Combine(common, recordedName));
                }
            }

            return results;
        }

        /// <summary>Probes 2 and 3: the pinned record, then the launcher's own directory.</summary>
        private static IEnumerable<string> PinnedAndLocal(IDiscoveryEnv env, PinnedBuild pinned)
        {
            var results = new List<string>();
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(pinned.RecordedFrom))
            {
                results.Add(pinned.RecordedFrom);
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(env.LauncherDirectory))
            {
                results.Add(env.LauncherDirectory);
                string parent = Path.GetDirectoryName(env.LauncherDirectory.TrimEnd('\\', '/'));
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(parent)) { results.Add(parent); }
            }
            return results;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Every value written after a `"key"` in a Steam KeyValues file.
        ///
        /// A TOLERANT SCANNER RATHER THAN A PARSER, deliberately.  `libraryfolders.vdf` is a
        /// Valve KeyValues file with two historical shapes (numbered keys holding a plain path,
        /// and numbered blocks holding a `"path"`), and the only thing this launcher wants out of
        /// it is the list of strings that follow a given key.  A full parser would be a second
        /// implementation of Valve's format to keep in step with Steam's; a scanner that skips
        /// everything it does not recognise cannot disagree with Steam about anything that
        /// matters here.
        /// </summary>
        internal static List<string> ParseQuotedValue(string text, string key)
        {
            var values = new List<string>();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(text)) { return values; }

            // ONE TOKEN AT A TIME, AND A MATCH CONSUMES THE TOKEN AFTER IT.
            //
            // The obvious shape -- read a token, read its value, read the next token -- assumes
            // the file is a flat list of pairs.  A KeyValues file is not: a nested block gives a
            // run of quoted tokens with an odd length between two braces, and the pairing then
            // drifts so that every later `"path"` is read as somebody else's *value*.  Consuming
            // only the matched key's own value keeps the scan aligned no matter how the blocks
            // nest, which is the only property this scanner needs.
            int i = 0;
            string token;
            while ((token = NextQuoted(text, ref i)) != null)
            {
                if (!string.Equals(token, key, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { continue; }
                string value = NextQuoted(text, ref i);
                if (value == null) { break; }
                values.Add(Unescape(value));
            }
            return values;
        }

        /// <summary>The next quoted string, or null at the end of the text.</summary>
        private static string NextQuoted(string text, ref int i)
        {
            while (i < text.Length && text[i] != '"') { i++; }
            if (i >= text.Length) { return null; }
            i++; // opening quote
            int start = i;
            while (i < text.Length && text[i] != '"')
            {
                if (text[i] == '\\' && i + 1 < text.Length) { i++; }
                i++;
            }
            string token = text.Substring(start, Math.Min(i, text.Length) - start);
            if (i < text.Length) { i++; } // closing quote
            return token;
        }

        private static string Unescape(string value)
        {
            return value.Replace("\\\\", "\\").Replace("\\\"", "\"");
        }

        private static string Trim(string path)
        {
            string trimmed = path.Trim().Trim('"');
            trimmed = trimmed.Replace('/', '\\');
            return trimmed.TrimEnd('\\');
        }
    }
}
```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/DiscoveryWindows.cs`:

```cs
// DiscoveryWindows.cs -- the real registry and filesystem behind `IDiscoveryEnv`.
//
// THE ONE FILE THE OFFLINE HARNESS DOES NOT COMPILE, and that is the point of the split:
// `Discovery.cs` holds every decision (probe order, the library walk, the build gate) and this
// file holds the four syscalls.  A test of the walk against a fake tree therefore tests the
// shipped logic rather than a second copy of it, and this file is small enough to read in one
// sitting -- which is the only honest way to be sure that the fake and the real environment
// implement the same contract.

using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Runtime.Versioning;
using System.Text;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    // The registry is Windows-only and this class is the only place in the launcher that touches
    // it, so the platform requirement is stated once, here, rather than at every call site.  The
    // caller guards the construction with `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()`, which is what keeps the
    // analyzer's promise honest rather than merely silenced.
    [SupportedOSPlatform("windows")]
    internal sealed class WindowsDiscoveryEnv : IDiscoveryEnv
    {
        private readonly string _launcherDirectory;

        public WindowsDiscoveryEnv(string launcherDirectory)
        {
            _launcherDirectory = launcherDirectory;
        }

        public string LauncherDirectory
        {
            get { return _launcherDirectory; }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// A string value from the registry, with the hive written into the key path.
        ///
        /// The path form is `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\...`, which is how the documents name these keys;
        /// mapping it here rather than at every call site keeps the probe list readable and keeps
        /// the hive choice in one place.
        /// </summary>
        public bool TryReadRegistryString(string keyPath, string valueName, out string value)
        {
            value = null;
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(keyPath)) { return false; }

            Microsoft.Win32.RegistryKey hive;
            string subKey;
            if (keyPath.StartsWith("HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                hive = Microsoft.Win32.Registry.CurrentUser;
                subKey = keyPath.Substring("HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\".Length);
            }
            else if (keyPath.StartsWith("HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                hive = Microsoft.Win32.Registry.LocalMachine;
                subKey = keyPath.Substring("HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\".Length);
            }
            else
            {
                return false;
            }

            try
            {
                using (var key = hive.OpenSubKey(subKey, writable: false))
                {
                    if (key == null) { return false; }
                    value = key.GetValue(valueName) as string;
                    return !string.IsNullOrEmpty(value);
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is System.Security.SecurityException
                                       || ex is UnauthorizedAccessException
                                       || ex is IOException)
            {
                // A registry that cannot be read is a discovery that finds nothing through this
                // probe, not a launcher that fails to start.  The game may be one directory away.
                return false;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// A small text file, or null.  Bounded by size on purpose: `libraryfolders.vdf` is a few
        /// kilobytes and `appmanifest_*.acf` is smaller, so a file claiming to be one of them and
        /// weighing a gigabyte is not one of them, and reading it into memory would be the
        /// launcher's fault rather than the user's.
        /// </summary>
        public string ReadTextOrNull(string path)
        {
            try
            {
                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(path) || !File.Exists(path)) { return null; }
                var info = new FileInfo(path);
                if (info.Length <= 0 || info.Length > 4 * 1024 * 1024) { return null; }
                // Steam writes these in the system code page; ASCII is a subset of both that and
                // UTF-8, and every byte this scanner looks at -- quotes, braces, digits, slashes
                // -- is ASCII.  Reading as UTF-8 with replacement avoids a BOM-at-the-front edge
                // case and cannot shift the bytes that matter.
                using (var reader = new StreamReader(path, new UTF8Encoding(false), detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks: true))
                {
                    return reader.ReadToEnd();
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException || ex is UnauthorizedAccessException
                                       || ex is NotSupportedException || ex is ArgumentException)
            {
                return null;
            }
        }

        public bool DirectoryExists(string path)
        {
            try
            {
                return !string.IsNullOrEmpty(path) && Directory.Exists(path);
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is ArgumentException || ex is NotSupportedException
                                       || ex is PathTooLongException)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        public bool FileExists(string path)
        {
            try
            {
                return !string.IsNullOrEmpty(path) && File.Exists(path);
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is ArgumentException || ex is NotSupportedException
                                       || ex is PathTooLongException)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        public long FileSize(string path)
        {
            try
            {
                return new FileInfo(path).Length;
            }
            catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException || ex is UnauthorizedAccessException
                                       || ex is ArgumentException || ex is NotSupportedException
                                       || ex is PathTooLongException)
            {
                return -1;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```csproj
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <!--
    Drelay.Launcher: starts the game suspended, injects the hook, resumes it.

    A console application rather than a windowed one: it is a diagnostic tool
    first, and its output is the evidence for Spike 1.1. It needs no elevation,
    because CreateProcess plus CreateRemoteThread on a process it created
    requires no privilege at all.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- net8.0 for the same reason as the bootstrap; see Drelay.Bootstrap.csproj. -->
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <AssemblyName>Drelay.Launcher</AssemblyName>
    <RootNamespace>Drelay.Launcher</RootNamespace>
    <UseAppHost>true</UseAppHost>
    <AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>false</AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>
    <PublishSingleFile>false</PublishSingleFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    The launcher references the bootstrap, and that is deliberate rather than
    convenient.

    Both processes have to agree on the shared block's layout and on its total
    size, and the size is a compile-time constant here: the launcher creates the
    mapping at that size, and the native DLL's sizeof(DrelayShared) must be the
    same number. A second copy of that constant in the launcher would be a second
    place for it to be wrong, and the failure it produces (a mapping one size and
    a reader another) is exactly the class of bug this design spends its effort
    turning into a loud refusal.

    So the layout lives once, in Drelay.Bootstrap\DrelayBlock.cs, and the launcher
    links against it. The bootstrap DLL is never loaded by the launcher; this is a
    compile-time dependency on a library of types, which is what it always was.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\Drelay.Bootstrap\Drelay.Bootstrap.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/EnvironmentBlock.cs`:

```cs
// EnvironmentBlock.cs -- the controlled environment the game is started with.
//
// THE CHILD'S ENVIRONMENT IS BUILT, NOT INHERITED, and this file is the whole of that
// decision.  Every `DOTNET_*` and every `DRELAY_HOOK_*` variable the operator has in their own
// shell is deleted before the launcher adds its own, because the hazard is the namespace rather
// than one known variable -- `DOTNET_TieredCompilation` is only the member of it that is known
// to break this design today (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 1, PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 4
// trap 1).
//
// IT IS ALSO WHERE THE CONFIG FILE BECOMES REAL, and where the config file's *absence* has to
// mean something.  HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 13 C2: "an unset field is absent from the
// child's environment, not set to the default".  A field the user never mentioned is a field
// the hook should decide, and the hook's own defaults are the same numbers the launcher would
// have written (`DrelayInstall.cpp`: kDefaultCollectDelayMs 0, kDefaultDiscoveryWindowMs 10000,
// kDefaultResolveDelayMs 100; `DrelayMain.cpp`: 60000 ms) -- so writing only what was supplied
// costs nothing and keeps one authority for each number.
//
// THE NAMES THAT ARE ALWAYS WRITTEN ARE THE LAUNCHER'S OWN, and each one is always written
// because its absence is not a neutral state: the session id, the run directory, the game
// directory, the block file, and `DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN` -- for which an *absent* variable means
// "act" (`StartupHook.cs`: `dryRun = GetEnvironmentVariable(EnvDryRun) == "1"`), which is the
// opposite of the safe default.
//
// `inherited` IS A PARAMETER rather than a call to `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariables()` so
// that the whole block is a pure function of its inputs, which is what makes C2 a check rather
// than an inspection.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    internal static class EnvironmentBlock
    {
        public static List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> Build(
            Options options, string gameDir, string bootstrap, uint session, string runDir,
            IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string>> inherited, Action<string> report)
        {
            var variables = new List<KeyValuePair<string, string>>();
            var removed = new List<string>();

            foreach (var entry in inherited)
            {
                string key = entry.Key;
                if (key.StartsWith("DOTNET_", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                    key.StartsWith("DRELAY_HOOK_", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                {
                    removed.Add(key);
                    continue;
                }
                // A NAME THIS PROCESS IS ABOUT TO SET ITSELF IS DROPPED RATHER THAN
                // INHERITED, so the environment block never carries the same variable twice.
                // `DRELAY_KEEP_READING` is outside the `DRELAY_HOOK_` namespace (it has to
                // be: the operator may set it in their own shell), so the prefix filter
                // above does not catch it, and `--pause-after-run` writes `0`.  Two entries
                // for one name is a block whose meaning depends on how the child's runtime
                // happens to resolve duplicates -- which is not a contract to rely on.
                if (options.PauseAfterRun &&
                    key.Equals("DRELAY_KEEP_READING", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                {
                    removed.Add(key);
                    continue;
                }
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(key, entry.Value));
            }

            // The bootstrap is the only DOTNET_* variable the design needs, and it
            // is what makes the managed half run before the game's Main.
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                "DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS", bootstrap));

            // THE ONE CASE WHERE A `DOTNET_*` VARIABLE IS ADDED BACK DELIBERATELY.
            //
            // The filter above exists so that a stray `DOTNET_TieredCompilation` in the
            // operator's shell cannot silently change the JIT's behaviour underneath the
            // hook.  Crash-dump configuration is the opposite kind of thing: it cannot
            // change how the process runs, it only decides whether a death leaves a body
            // behind, and the launcher is the only place it can be set -- the filter is
            // exactly what stops the operator from setting it themselves.
            if (options.DbgDump)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DOTNET_DbgEnableMiniDump", "1"));
                // 2 = with heap.  A mini dump without the heap has the stacks, which is
                // usually enough; the heap is what makes `clrstack`/SOS usable, and this
                // is the case where the alternative is no evidence at all.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DOTNET_DbgMiniDumpType", "2"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DOTNET_DbgMiniDumpName", System.IO.Path.Combine(runDir, "crashdump.dmp")));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DOTNET_CreateDumpDiagnostics", "1"));
            }

            // THE LAUNCHER'S OWN NAMES, ALWAYS WRITTEN.  See the file header: each of these is a
            // fact about *this* run that no outside source may hold an opinion about.
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_SESSION", session.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_RUNDIR", runDir));
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_GAMEDIR", gameDir));
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.AssemblyPath))
            {
                // Named explicitly so the bootstrap does not have to know what the
                // game's assembly is called. Several files derive that name from
                // the pinned build record instead of hard-coding it, and this is
                // the value that lets the same hook be pointed at a test host.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_ASSEMBLY", options.AssemblyPath));
            }
            // The file backing the shared block. Passed as a path rather than as a
            // kernel object name so that the block has no commit charge at creation
            // and so that a crashed run leaves its block on disk.
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                "DRELAY_HOOK_BLOCK", System.IO.Path.Combine(runDir, "shared.block")));
            variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN", options.DryRun ? "1" : "0"));

            // The native side's watchdog timeout, overridable so the timeout path
            // itself is testable.  A watchdog nobody has ever seen fire is a
            // watchdog that does not work, and this one has to: it is what keeps a
            // bootstrap that never runs from being a game that never starts.
            //
            // WRITTEN ONLY WHEN THE USER ASKED FOR IT, because the launcher's default and the
            // native default are the same 60 s (`DrelayMain.cpp`: `uint32_t timeoutMs = 60000`).
            if (options.SetTimeoutMs)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS", options.TimeoutMs.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }
            if (options.SetCollectDelayMs)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_COLLECT_DELAY_MS",
                    options.CollectDelayMs.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }
            if (options.SetDiscoveryWindowMs)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS",
                    options.DiscoveryWindowMs.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }
            if (options.SetResolveDelayMs)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS",
                    options.ResolveDelayMs.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }

            // THE ONE SWITCH WHOSE ABSENCE IS THE FEATURE, SO IT IS ONLY EVER SET TO TURN
            // SOMETHING OFF.  `DRELAY_KEEP_READING` is a plain `DRELAY_` name (the hook
            // reads it before the launcher's filter is relevant, but the operator may also
            // set it in their own shell), and the hook's default is now "keep reading"; an
            // unset variable and a set-to-0 one must therefore not be the same thing.  They
            // are not: the launcher writes the variable only when asked, and the hook reads
            // an empty value as "not set".
            if (options.PauseAfterRun)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_KEEP_READING", "0"));
            }
            // How long the hook records after the patch.  Clamped here as well as in
            // the hook so that a typo is refused by the launcher's own message rather
            // than silently reduced to the ceiling inside the process.
            if (options.SetLiveSeconds)
            {
                int liveMs = options.LiveSeconds > 6 * 3600 ? 6 * 3600 : options.LiveSeconds;
                if (liveMs < 0)
                {
                    liveMs = 0;
                }
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS",
                    (liveMs * 1000).ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }
            if (options.FullTrace)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FULLTRACE", "1"));
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.TestTargets))
            {
                // Test-only, and loud about it: the bootstrap logs every test target
                // it appends, so a run that used this switch cannot later be mistaken
                // for a run of the pinned game build.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_HOOK_TEST_TARGETS", options.TestTargets));
            }
            if (options.FrameHelper)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_HELPER", "1"));
            }
            if (options.FrameReplacement)
            {
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
            }
            if (options.Trace)
            {
                // THE THREE THAT TOGETHER MAKE A TRACE NON-EMPTY. See `Options.Trace`.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_TRACE", "1"));
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.MoveSteer))
            {
                // BOTH NAMES, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN.
                //
                // The hook is loaded into a process the launcher starts, so the value
                // could just be left in the inherited environment -- but the launcher
                // deletes every inherited `DRELAY_HOOK_*` name precisely so that a
                // stale shell variable cannot change what gets patched, and whether
                // the player may be moved is exactly that kind of decision.  So the
                // native side is told through the namespace it does not inherit
                // (`DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT`, which the managed replacement
                // publishes for), and the *value* is passed under its own name for the
                // managed side to read.  A value with no name would be a setting that
                // silently does nothing; a name with no value would be a patch with no
                // behaviour.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_MOVE_STEER", options.MoveSteer));
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.AutoAim))
            {
                // THE SAME TWO-NAME SPLIT AS `--move-steer`, AND FOR THE SAME REASON.
                // `DRELAY_HOOK_AIM_REPLACEMENT` lives in the namespace the launcher owns and
                // deletes inherited values from, so a stale shell variable cannot decide that
                // a patched game method jumps into managed code; the *mode* travels under its
                // own name (`DRELAY_AIM_MODE`) for the managed side, which is where the
                // selection lives, to read. A value with no flag would patch nothing; a flag
                // with no value would patch a method that then does nothing.
                //
                // AND IT TURNS THE FRAME REPLACEMENT ON, WHICH IS NOT OPTIONAL.  The module
                // has to arm `Prefs.enable_aimbot` before `AimbotSystem.FindTarget` is ever
                // called -- nothing else compiles it, so nothing else patches it -- and the
                // only place it may make that write is the game's own thread. The frame
                // replacement is the one game-thread entry point that exists on every run.
                // `AutoAim.OnFrame` carries the whole argument, including why the write at
                // resolve time is lost to `GameSettings.Load` in `DarzaWindow`'s constructor.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_AIM_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_AIM_MODE", options.AutoAim));
            }
            if (options.Dodge)
            {
                // THE THREE DEPENDENCIES OF A LIVE DECISION, SET TOGETHER. See `Options.Dodge`.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_DODGE", "1"));
                // THE DECISION WINDOW, IF THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR ONE. It travels under its own name
                // for the managed side to read, and it is set even in a plain `--dodge` dry run
                // because the window changes which candidates are admissible -- so a dry run that
                // does not carry it is a dry run of a different dodge from the one that will act.
                if (options.DodgeDisc >= 0.0)
                {
                    variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                        "DRELAY_DODGE_DECISION_DISC",
                        options.DodgeDisc.ToString("0.####", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
                }
                if (options.DodgeWindowSeconds >= 0.0)
                {
                    variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                        "DRELAY_DODGE_WINDOW_S",
                        options.DodgeWindowSeconds.ToString("0.####", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
                }
            }
            if (options.DodgeAct)
            {
                // AND THE ACTUATOR'S OWN TWO, WHICH ONLY THIS SWITCH SETS.
                //
                // `DRELAY_DODGE_ACT` is the adapter's gate; `DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT` plus
                // `DRELAY_MOVE_STEER=dodge` is the pilot's. The same name-with-a-value split as
                // `--move-steer`, for the same reason: the *flag* that decides whether a patched
                // game's frame enters managed code lives in the namespace the launcher owns and
                // deletes inherited values from, and the *value* travels under its own name.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_DODGE_ACT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT", "1"));
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_MOVE_STEER", "dodge"));
            }
            if (options.EscapeTestSeconds >= 0.0)
            {
                // Same two-name split as `--move-steer`, and for the same reason: the
                // *flag* that decides whether managed code is entered lives in the
                // namespace the launcher owns and deletes inherited values from
                // (`--escape-test` sets `--frame-replacement`, so that name is already
                // set above), and the *parameter* travels under its own name for the
                // managed side to read.
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(
                    "DRELAY_ESCAPE_TEST_SEC",
                    options.EscapeTestSeconds.ToString("0.###", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
            }
            if (options.Off)
            {
                // With the off switch set, the startup hook is not installed at
                // all: "off" has to mean the process is untouched, and the
                // strongest form of that is not injecting managed code into it.
                variables.RemoveAll(v => v.Key == "DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS");
                variables.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>("DRELAY_HOOK_OFF", "1"));
            }

            if (report != null && options.Verbose)
            {
                report("environment   : removed " + removed.Count + " variable(s):");
                foreach (string key in removed)
                {
                    report("                  " + key);
                }
            }

            // A Unicode environment block is a NUL-separated, double-NUL-terminated
            // sequence of `name=value` strings, sorted case-insensitively --
            // which is what CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT requires.
            variables.Sort((a, b) => string.Compare(a.Key, b.Key, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

            return variables;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The block as the NUL-separated, double-NUL-terminated string
        /// `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` requires.  Split from <see cref="Build"/> so that the
        /// ordering and the filter can be asserted as data rather than through a pointer.
        /// </summary>
        public static string ToBlockText(List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> variables)
        {
            var builder = new System.Text.StringBuilder();
            foreach (var pair in variables)
            {
                builder.Append(pair.Key).Append('=').Append(pair.Value).Append('\0');
            }
            builder.Append('\0');
            return builder.ToString();
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/FirstRun.cs`:

```cs
// FirstRun.cs -- the two rules that decide whether a refusal is allowed to hold the window open.
//
// HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 6, and both rules are about WHO IS WATCHING:
//
//   * "Pause only when there is nobody to read the output otherwise.  A first run from a script
//     or from the future proxy must not block on a keypress.  Detection: `args.Length == 0` AND
//     `!Console.IsInputRedirected` and the failure is a user-fixable one.  Scripted runs always
//     pass at least one argument, so this only affects the double-click path."
//   * "Never pause on a refusal the user cannot fix by editing the file (missing DLLs beside the
//     launcher, a game build whose fingerprint does not match).  Print and exit."
//
// IT IS A FUNCTION RATHER THAN AN `if` IN `Main` because section 13 C5 is a named invariant
// ("a zero-argument run with redirected input never pauses") and a check that has to start a
// process to see an `if` is a check nobody runs.  `LauncherHarness --check c5` calls this, and
// also asserts -- by reading the source -- that `Main` has exactly one `Console.ReadKey` and
// that it is guarded by this function, so the helper cannot drift away from its only caller.

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    internal static class FirstRun
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// Whether a refusal may wait for a keypress.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="noArguments">
        /// `args.Length == 0`: the double-click path.  A scripted run always passes at least one
        /// argument, and a refusal it cannot read is a refusal it cannot act on.
        /// </param>
        /// <param name="inputRedirected">
        /// `Console.IsInputRedirected`.  A redirected stdin is a machine on the other end of a
        /// pipe; `Console.ReadKey` would either throw or block it forever.
        /// </param>
        /// <param name="userFixable">
        /// Whether editing the configuration file, or starting the launcher differently, could
        /// change the outcome.  An OpenGL install or a game build whose fingerprint does not match
        /// is not something a file this program wrote can fix.
        /// </param>
        public static bool ShouldPause(bool noArguments, bool inputRedirected, bool userFixable)
        {
            return noArguments && !inputRedirected && userFixable;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether this run may create the configuration file.
        ///
        /// §6 HAS THE TEMPLATE WRITTEN ONLY WHEN DISCOVERY FAILS, AND THAT IS TOO NARROW.  On a Steam
        /// machine discovery *succeeds*, which is the common case and the whole point of §7 -- so the
        /// operator whose game was found is the one user who never gets the file, and the only way to
        /// change what the hook does is to know the schema by heart.  The file is written whenever a
        /// no-argument run finds it missing, and never by a scripted run (which must not create files
        /// it did not ask for) and never over a file that exists (which may be the operator's edits).
        ///
        /// IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE CONFIGURATION IS RESOLVED, so that the file describes the run
        /// that is about to happen rather than the one after it -- a written default that the run
        /// then ignores would be a lie about what just ran.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool ShouldWriteTemplate(bool noArguments, bool configExists)
        {
            return noArguments && !configExists;
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/NativeMethods.cs`:

```cs
// NativeMethods.cs -- the Win32 surface the launcher needs, plus the one piece of
// machine code it has to synthesise.
//
// WHY THERE IS MACHINE CODE IN THIS FILE
// --------------------------------------
// The launcher has to make the hook DLL do three things inside a process it just
// created and suspended:
//
//     LoadLibraryW(hookPath)  ->  GetProcAddress(module, "DrelayHook_Init")  ->  call it
//
// None of those can be done from here, and the obvious approach -- inject
// `LoadLibraryW` alone and then resolve `DrelayHook_Init` with a second remote
// call -- does not work, for a reason that is easy to miss:
//
//   * `CreateRemoteThread` gives the remote function exactly ONE pointer-sized
//     argument, and `GetProcAddress(HMODULE, LPCSTR)` needs two.  Passing the
//     first in RCX and hoping the second lands in RDX does not happen: the
//     documented calling convention puts the thread parameter in RCX and leaves
//     RDX undefined.
//   * `GetExitCodeThread` returns a 32-bit value, so a second remote call cannot
//     even hand back the 64-bit function pointer it resolved.
//   * and the launcher cannot call `GetProcAddress` on the DLL locally, because
//     the module is not loaded in the launcher's own address space -- a pointer
//     resolved here would point at nothing in the target.
//
// So the sequence is performed as one self-contained stub written into the
// target.  It is position-independent, has no branches, and its only memory
// operand is a RIP-relative load of an immutable data block placed immediately
// after it -- which means there is nothing in it to relocate, and the two things
// that could go wrong (a wrong encoding, a wrong data offset) are both visible in
// the byte layout below rather than hidden behind a marshaller.
//
// The stub's own encoding is asserted by a round-trip test at build time in
// tools/Test-LauncherStub.ps1, because hand-written machine code that is never
```
