```cs
        // A TARGET FOR A TEST HOST, AND ONLY EVER FOR A TEST HOST.
        //
        // The hook's target table comes from `known-build.json` through
        // `GeneratedBuildTable.cs`, and that is the Phase 0 gate's pinned record of
        // *the game*: `Fingerprint.ps1` checks exactly those four IL hashes, so a
        // fifth entry there would be a lie about the build and `il_index.py` would
        // drop it on the next regeneration anyway.  A test that wants the detour to
        // match a method of `SyntheticHost` therefore cannot use that route at all,
        // and before this option existed no run in `Test-Injection.ps1` could patch a
        // target -- which is why its most ambitious assertion was `GAP 9c the read
        // path is open but no frame has entered the detour yet`.
        //
        // The value is one or more specs separated by `;`, each
        // `name|declaringType|methodName|ilSize|ilHash`.  It travels as
        // `DRELAY_HOOK_TEST_TARGETS`, which the launcher *sets* rather than passes
        // through: the launcher deletes every inherited `DRELAY_HOOK_*` name, so a
        // stray variable in an operator's shell cannot reach the hook, and a normal
        // session -- this is null -- publishes exactly the four game targets.
        //
        // THE CONFIG FILE CANNOT SET IT (HANDOFF section 5 rule 3): a user-facing
        // configuration that offers this switch is offering a way to patch a method that
        // is not in the pinned build.
        public string TestTargets;

        // Phase 2's mechanism test: call a plain managed helper from the frame detour
        // every frame.
        //
        // OFF BY DEFAULT BECAUSE THE HELPER ALLOCATES ON PURPOSE.  The measurement is
        // whether managed code that triggers collections is safe on the game's frame
        // thread -- see PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 3 and native\DrelayFrame.cpp's
        // "THE MANAGED FRAME HELPER" note.  64 KB per frame is the probe, not a
        // feature, so it is opt-in and reaches the hook as
        // `DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_HELPER=1` (a name the launcher *sets*, so it cannot be
        // inherited by accident).
        public bool FrameHelper;

        // Phase 2's other mechanism test: patch the frame tick with a MANAGED method
        // instead of a native detour, so the game's own `call` becomes a
        // managed-to-managed call.
        //
        // IT REPLACES THE DETOUR RATHER THAN ADDING TO IT, so it is opt-in and mutually
        // exclusive with `--frame-helper` in practice: with this on, the native frame
        // read and the ring are not written by this file any more, because this file is
        // not in the path.  See `managedFrameReplacement` in DrelayHookShared.h.
        public bool FrameReplacement;

        // PHASE 3'S ACTUATOR REQUEST, AND IT IS THE ONE SWITCH THAT MOVES THE PLAYER.
        //
        // The value is passed to the hook verbatim as `DRELAY_MOVE_STEER`, and the
        // hook decides what it means (see `SteeringPilot`): a mode name, optionally
        // with parameters.  Three properties matter and each is deliberate:
        //
        //   * EMPTY MEANS NOTHING HAPPENS.  The movement replacement is still
        //     published and still calls through, so the plumbing is exercised by
        //     every run, but the player is only ever moved when an operator asked;
        //   * IT IS A *VALUE*, NOT A FLAG, because the interesting experiments are
        //     "hold this heading", "sweep these headings and calibrate", "walk the
        //     speed boundary" -- and a boolean cannot carry which one;
        //   * IT IS PASSED THROUGH RATHER THAN INVENTED HERE.  The launcher owns the
        //     `DRELAY_HOOK_*` namespace and deletes inherited names from it; this one
        //     is the operator's, so the launcher's job is to place it in the child's
        //     environment unchanged and let the hook read it.
        //
        // IT IS NOT IN THE CONFIG FILE (section 5.1, rule 3): it is an experiment that
        // moves the player, not a setting.
        public string MoveSteer;

        // THE AUTO-AIM REQUEST: `--autoaim closest` or `--autoaim highesthp`.
        //
        // WHY IT IS A VALUE AND NOT A FLAG.  The two modes are the same mechanism with a
        // different score, and a boolean could not say which one was asked for -- the same
        // argument `--move-steer` carries.  The value is passed to the hook verbatim as
        // `DRELAY_AIM_MODE`; the launcher validates that it is one of the two names it
        // knows so a typo is refused at the command line rather than silently selecting
        // nothing once the game is already running.
        //
        // IT IS ALSO A REAL SETTING CHANGE, AND THE HELP TEXT SAYS SO.  The replacement
        // arms the game's own `Prefs.enable_aimbot`, because `Player.Shoot` checks that
        // property before it ever asks for a target -- see `AutoAim` in the bootstrap.
        //
        // AND IT IMPLIES `--frame-replacement`.  That is not a preference: the flag has to be
        // armed from the game's own thread before `AimbotSystem.FindTarget` is ever called,
        // and the frame replacement is the only game-thread entry point every run has.  The
        // reason the write cannot wait for the aim target itself is circular -- the target is
        // compiled only once the flag is set -- and `AutoAim.OnFrame` carries the full account.
        public string AutoAim;

        // SPIKE 3.2'S RECORDING REQUEST.
        //
        // IT SETS THREE THINGS, AND EACH ONE IS A DEPENDENCY THE OPERATOR SHOULD NOT HAVE TO KNOW
        // ABOUT. The trace recorder reads `DRELAY_TRACE`; it is called from the MANAGED frame
        // replacement and not from the native frame detour, so it needs
        // `DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT=1`; and its input is the Phase 2 sensor's threat set, so it
        // needs `DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR=1`. A run that gets any of them wrong writes a valid header and
        // zero frames -- an empty file that looks exactly like a session in which no bullet came
        // near, which is why the offline harness now fails on an empty recording rather than
        // reporting every invariant vacuously held. The run of `20261014-164314-p12060` is that
        // file, and it cost a session.
        public bool Trace;

        // PHASE 3'S ESCALATION TEST: call `World.RequestEscape()` once, under hook control.
        //
        // WHY IT IS A SWITCH AND NOT PART OF THE DODGE.  The escape is Phase 3's floor --
        // reached only when the projected damage is lethal and no admissible move avoids it
        // -- but the *call itself* has never been measured, and the 2026-10-13 run is the
        // receipt: `escape MISSING never compiled`, because nothing ever called it, so the
        // JIT never compiled it and the detour never saw it. A floor nobody has stood on is
        // not a floor. This switch tests the actuator alone, with no threat set and no
        // solver behind it, which is why it can be tested before the dodge exists.
        //
        // SECONDS, NOT FRAMES, AND MEASURED FROM THE FIRST FRAME WITH A WORLD.  Frames are
        // the client's variable-rate loop and would make the delay depend on the frame rate;
        // wall clock from run start would make it depend on how long the operator took to get
        // into a zone. From "the world exists" it is the one origin the operator controls.
        //
        // IT IMPLIES `--frame-replacement`, because that is where the call is made from, and
        // it is a fatal combination to get wrong silently: a run that asked for the escape
        // test and did not install the frame replacement would report "the test never armed"
        // and read as a client refusal. `ApplyImplications` adds the flag and says so.
        public double EscapeTestSeconds = -1.0;

        // DELIVERABLE 3.3: THE DODGE'S OWN TWO SWITCHES, AND THEY ARE TWO ON PURPOSE.
        //
        // `--dodge` runs the solver on live frames and LOGS what it would have done. That is the
        // plan's requirement ("ship it behind its own switch, defaulting to a mode that logs
        // decisions without acting"), and it is also the only shape in which the decision can be
        // compared against a session's health trace before anything moves.
        //
        // `--dodge-act` additionally lets the decision reach the input -- and even then only
        // because it also puts the pilot in `dodge` mode, where the pilot writes nothing at all on
        // any frame the adapter publishes no command. So moving the player takes three separate
        // decisions: the dodge on, the acting on, and the actuator in dodge mode.
        //
        // BOTH IMPLY THE FRAME REPLACEMENT AND THE SENSOR, for the reason `--trace` does: the
        // adapter runs on the sensor's frame path and its input is the sensor's projectile list, so
        // `--dodge` without either is a solver that decides about an empty world on every frame and
        // reports `NoThreat` -- an empty recording's twin, and that one already cost a session.
        public bool Dodge;
        public bool DodgeAct;

        // THE RULE 6 DECISION WINDOW, PASSED AT STARTUP RATHER THAN REBUILT.
        //
        // `--dodge-disc K` sets the window as a MULTIPLE of the time a projectile takes to cross the
        // collision disc (`player.radius + projectile.radius`). It replaced a constant 50 ms, which
        // was a DISTANCE of `0.05 * speed` -- 1.95x the collision disc on a 16 u/s projectile and
        // 0.53x of it on the 6 u/s ones -- so one number could not be right for both ends of the
        // game. `--dodge-window S` is an absolute floor in seconds under it and is 0 by default.
        //
        // THE TWO PASS -1 FOR "NOT SET" rather than carrying a copy of the solver's default, for the
        // same reason `EscapeTestSeconds` does: a default duplicated in two assemblies is a default
        // that will disagree with itself, and this one already exists in `DodgeConfig.Default()`.
        // Only a value the operator actually typed travels.  THE CONFIG FILE USES `null` FOR THE
        // SAME THING (section 5.1) and lands here as -1.0.
        public double DodgeDisc = -1.0;
        public double DodgeWindowSeconds = -1.0;

        // How long the hook keeps recording after it patches the frame tick, in
        // seconds.  Passed to the hook as `DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS`.
        //
        // FIVE SECONDS WAS HARD-CODED AND IS STILL THE DEFAULT.  It is the right
        // length for proving the detour is entered on a title screen; it cannot
        // record the endurance criterion, which asks for an hour of play with no
        // crash and no frame regression, because the hook writes its evidence when
        // this window closes.  `--live-seconds 3600` is that run.
        //
        // The default is deliberately unchanged so that runs before this switch
        // existed remain comparable with runs after it.
        public int LiveSeconds = 5;

        public List<string> GameArguments = new List<string>();

        public string RunDirectory;

        /// <summary>
        /// The directory auto-discovery produced, when nobody said where the game was.  Reported
        /// once in the transcript, because it is the one input the launcher chose for itself.
        /// </summary>
        public string DiscoveredFrom;

        /// <summary>
        /// Normalise and check an `--autoaim` mode.
        ///
        /// REFUSED AT THE COMMAND LINE RATHER THAN AT THE HOOK, because the two failures look
        /// nothing alike from the outside.  A typo that reached the hook would resolve to
        /// "off", the run would start, and the operator would spend a session watching the
        /// game not aim while `bootstrap.log` said the module had never been asked for
        /// anything -- the class of mistake this project has paid for repeatedly (see the
        /// empty-trace note on `Options.Trace`).  Here it costs one line of console text.
        ///
        /// THE REASON IS RETURNED WITHOUT THE FLAG NAME, because two callers report it: the
        /// command-line parser prefixes `--autoaim`, and the configuration reader prefixes
        /// `drelay.config.json -> AutoAim`.  A typo names the field it was typed in either
        /// way (section 13 C3).
        /// </summary>
        public static bool TryParseAutoAim(string raw, out string mode, out string reason)
        {
            mode = null;
            reason = null;
            string value = (raw ?? "").Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
            switch (value)
            {
                case "closest":
                case "close":
                case "nearest":
                    mode = "closest";
                    return true;
                case "highesthp":
                case "highest-hp":
                case "highest":
                case "maxhp":
                case "max-hp":
                    mode = "highesthp";
                    return true;
                default:
                    reason = "needs a mode: 'closest' (the nearest damageable enemy) "
                             + "or 'highesthp' (the damageable enemy with the most health), got '"
                             + raw + "'";
                    return false;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Copy every field <paramref name="from"/> actually supplied over this one.
        ///
        /// THIS IS WHERE PER-FIELD PRECEDENCE LIVES.  Called once for the configuration file
        /// and then once for the command line, in that order, which is section 4's table
        /// read top to bottom.  `Settings` fields that are null are absent, never zero.
        /// </summary>
        public void Apply(Settings from)
        {
            if (from == null) { return; }

            if (from.GamePath != null) { GamePath = from.GamePath; }
            if (from.ExecutablePath != null) { ExecutablePath = from.ExecutablePath; }
            if (from.AssemblyPath != null) { AssemblyPath = from.AssemblyPath; }
            if (from.HookDll != null) { HookDll = from.HookDll; }
            if (from.BootstrapDll != null) { BootstrapDll = from.BootstrapDll; }
            if (from.RunRoot != null) { RunRoot = from.RunRoot; }

            if (from.TimeoutMs.HasValue) { TimeoutMs = from.TimeoutMs.Value; SetTimeoutMs = true; }
            if (from.CollectDelayMs.HasValue) { CollectDelayMs = from.CollectDelayMs.Value; SetCollectDelayMs = true; }
            if (from.DiscoveryWindowMs.HasValue) { DiscoveryWindowMs = from.DiscoveryWindowMs.Value; SetDiscoveryWindowMs = true; }
            if (from.ResolveDelayMs.HasValue) { ResolveDelayMs = from.ResolveDelayMs.Value; SetResolveDelayMs = true; }
            if (from.LiveSeconds.HasValue) { LiveSeconds = from.LiveSeconds.Value; SetLiveSeconds = true; }

            if (from.DodgeDisc.HasValue) { DodgeDisc = from.DodgeDisc.Value; }
            if (from.DodgeWindowSeconds.HasValue) { DodgeWindowSeconds = from.DodgeWindowSeconds.Value; }
            if (from.EscapeTestSeconds.HasValue) { EscapeTestSeconds = from.EscapeTestSeconds.Value; }

            if (from.Off.HasValue) { Off = from.Off.Value; }
            if (from.Act.HasValue) { DryRun = !from.Act.Value; }
            if (from.FullTrace.HasValue) { FullTrace = from.FullTrace.Value; }
            if (from.Verbose.HasValue) { Verbose = from.Verbose.Value; }
            if (from.NoWait.HasValue) { NoWait = from.NoWait.Value; }
            if (from.PauseAfterRun.HasValue) { PauseAfterRun = from.PauseAfterRun.Value; }
            if (from.DbgDump.HasValue) { DbgDump = from.DbgDump.Value; }
            if (from.FrameHelper.HasValue) { FrameHelper = from.FrameHelper.Value; }
            if (from.FrameReplacement.HasValue) { FrameReplacement = from.FrameReplacement.Value; }
            if (from.Trace.HasValue) { Trace = from.Trace.Value; }
            if (from.Dodge.HasValue) { Dodge = from.Dodge.Value; }
            if (from.DodgeAct.HasValue) { DodgeAct = from.DodgeAct.Value; }

            if (from.AutoAim != null) { AutoAim = from.AutoAim; }
            if (from.MoveSteer != null) { MoveSteer = from.MoveSteer; }
            if (from.TestTargets != null) { TestTargets = from.TestTargets; }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The flags that imply other flags, applied ONCE to the merged result.
        ///
        /// THIS IS A SEPARATE PASS ON PURPOSE (section 10.6).  The command line used to apply
        /// these inside the parser, which is the one place a configuration file cannot reach:
        /// a config that sets `AutoAim` without the frame replacement produces a module that is
        /// published, verified and never entered, and nothing in the log says why.  Applying
        /// them here means both sources go through the same code, and neither can re-derive the
        /// dependency differently.
        /// </summary>
        public void ApplyImplications()
        {
            // `--escape-test` calls `World.RequestEscape()` from the frame replacement, so a run
            // without it reports "the test never armed" -- indistinguishable from a client that
            // refused to escape.
            if (EscapeTestSeconds >= 0.0) { FrameReplacement = true; }

            // Auto-aim must arm `Prefs.enable_aimbot` from the game's own thread before the
            // target method is ever compiled, and the frame replacement is that thread.
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(AutoAim)) { FrameReplacement = true; }

            // `--dodge-act` puts the pilot in `dodge` mode, which is a value the actuator reads
            // by name.  Set here rather than in the parser for the same reason as the two above.
            if (DodgeAct)
            {
                Dodge = true;
                MoveSteer = "dodge";
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The one contradiction the launcher refuses rather than resolves, checked after the
        /// merge and BEFORE <see cref="ApplyImplications"/> -- because the implication above is
        /// what makes the two fields agree, and a check that ran after it could never fire.
        /// </summary>
        public bool Validate(out string error)
        {
            error = null;
            // A CONTRADICTION IS REFUSED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. `--dodge-act` puts the pilot in
            // `dodge` mode; an explicit `--move-steer` says something else. Quietly preferring one
            // would be a run that walks where the operator did not ask -- the exact class of
            // surprise `--move-steer`'s own comment says the mode-value design exists to prevent.
            //
            // IT IS NOW REACHABLE FROM THE CONFIG FILE TOO, because the written template ships
            // `"Act": true`, so the message names both spellings and says which edit resolves it.
            // A refusal that only mentions `--dodge-act` would send an operator who passed
            // `--move-steer` looking for a flag they never typed.
            if (DodgeAct && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(MoveSteer))
            {
                error = "--dodge-act (or \"Dodge\": {\"Act\": true} in drelay.config.json) drives the "
                        + "actuator itself and cannot be combined with --move-steer '" + MoveSteer
                        + "'. Set \"Act\": false in the config file, or drop --move-steer.";
                return false;
            }
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Make every relative path absolute and fill in the three paths that default to
        /// "beside the launcher".
        ///
        /// WHY ABSOLUTE: resolving a relative path against the *current* directory is a way to be
        /// surprised when a script runs from elsewhere, so the default is derived from the
        /// launcher's own location and anything else is resolved against the working directory at
        /// startup, once, where the operator can see it.
        /// </summary>
        public void ResolvePaths(string launcherDirectory, out string error)
        {
            error = null;
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(GamePath))
            {
                return;
            }
            GamePath = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(GamePath);
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(ExecutablePath))
            {
                ExecutablePath = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(ExecutablePath);
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(AssemblyPath))
            {
                AssemblyPath = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(AssemblyPath);
                // When an assembly is named explicitly, its own directory is the
                // one the hook should treat as "the game directory": probing a
                // different one would be measuring the wrong tree.  This is what
                // makes the same launcher usable against a test host.
                if (System.IO.File.Exists(AssemblyPath))
                {
                    GamePath = System.IO.Path.GetDirectoryName(AssemblyPath);
                }
            }
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(HookDll))
            {
                HookDll = System.IO.Path.Combine(launcherDirectory, "Drelay.Hook.dll");
            }
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(BootstrapDll))
            {
                BootstrapDll = System.IO.Path.Combine(launcherDirectory, "Drelay.Bootstrap.dll");
            }
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RunRoot))
            {
                RunRoot = System.IO.Path.Combine(
                    Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData),
                    "drelay", "hook");
            }
            else
            {
                // SECTION 5'S NOTE, ENFORCED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED: "if it is ever exposed, it is
                // exposed as an absolute path".  A relative `RunRoot` in the config file would
                // otherwise be resolved against whatever directory the launcher happened to be
                // started from, which is the surprise every other path here is made absolute to
                // avoid.
                RunRoot = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(RunRoot);
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/managed/Drelay.Launcher/SharedBlock.cs`:

```cs
// SharedBlock.cs -- the launcher's side of the handshake.
//
// The launcher creates the mapping and both events *before* the game process
// exists, so neither the hook nor the bootstrap has to race to be the creator.
// That ownership is what makes the ordering deterministic: by the time the first
// remote thread runs, every kernel object it will need is already there and
// already has the right name.

using System;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.IO;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using Drelay.Bootstrap;

namespace Drelay.Launcher
{
    internal sealed class SharedBlock : IDisposable
    {
        private readonly IntPtr _mapping;
        private readonly IntPtr _view;
        private readonly IntPtr _nativeReady;
        private readonly IntPtr _bootReady;
        private readonly uint _session;
        private static IntPtr _backingFile = IntPtr.Zero;

        private SharedBlock(uint session, IntPtr mapping, IntPtr view, IntPtr nativeReady, IntPtr bootReady)
        {
            _session = session;
            _mapping = mapping;
            _view = view;
            _nativeReady = nativeReady;
            _bootReady = bootReady;
        }

        public static SharedBlock Create(uint session, string runDirectory)
        {
            // A layout bug should be caught here, by the process that creates the
            // mapping, rather than by whoever reads it first -- and the launcher is
            // the only participant that can run this check before anything else
            // exists.
            string complaint;
            if (!SharedLayout.VerifyOffsets(out complaint))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    "the C# view of the shared block is internally inconsistent: " + complaint);
            }

            int size = GeneratedLayout.DrelaySharedSize;

            // The block is backed by a FILE in the run directory, not by a named
            // pagefile section, and that is a correction rather than a preference.
            //
            // A named pagefile-backed section is charged against the system commit
            // limit when it is created, and on this machine
            // `CreateFileMapping(INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, ..., "Local\\name")` for
            // 431 KB fails with error 8 (ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY) from inside the
            // launcher while the identical call from another process succeeds --
            // see tests/MapProbe, which is what established that.  Deliberately
            // resisting that diagnosis, a file-backed section has no commit charge
            // at all: it is a window onto a file that already exists, which is the
            // whole of what this block is.
            //
            // It also makes a crashed run's block readable afterwards, because the
            // bytes are in the run directory rather than in a pagefile.
            string path = Path.Combine(runDirectory, "shared.block");

            // Create or truncate, then set the size explicitly.  A file-backed
            // mapping cannot exceed its file, so the size is not optional.
            using (var stream = new FileStream(path, FileMode.Create, FileAccess.ReadWrite,
                                               FileShare.ReadWrite))
            {
                stream.SetLength(size);
            }

            IntPtr file = NativeMethods.CreateFile(
                path, NativeMethods.GenericRead | NativeMethods.GenericWrite,
                NativeMethods.FileShareRead | NativeMethods.FileShareWrite,
                IntPtr.Zero, NativeMethods.OpenExisting, NativeMethods.FileAttributeNormal, IntPtr.Zero);
            if (file == IntPtr.Zero || file == new IntPtr(-1))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    "CreateFile(" + path + "): " + NativeMethods.LastErrorText());
            }

            _backingFile = file;

            IntPtr mapping = NativeMethods.CreateFileMapping(
                file, IntPtr.Zero, NativeMethods.PAGE_READWRITE, 0, (uint)size, null);
            if (mapping == IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                int error = System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.GetLastWin32Error();
                throw new InvalidOperationException(
                    "CreateFileMapping(" + path + ", " + size + " bytes): " + error + " " +
                    new System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception(error).Message);
            }

            IntPtr view = NativeMethods.MapViewOfFile(mapping, NativeMethods.FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS, 0, 0,
                                                      UIntPtr.Zero);
            if (view == IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("MapViewOfFile: " + NativeMethods.LastErrorText());
            }

            IntPtr nativeReady = NativeMethods.CreateEvent(IntPtr.Zero, true, false,
                SharedProtocol.NativeReadyEventName(session));
            IntPtr bootReady = NativeMethods.CreateEvent(IntPtr.Zero, true, false,
                SharedProtocol.BootReadyEventName(session));
            if (nativeReady == IntPtr.Zero || bootReady == IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("CreateEvent: " + NativeMethods.LastErrorText());
            }

            return new SharedBlock(session, mapping, view, nativeReady, bootReady);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Stamps the header.  The magic is `MagicBoot` rather than `MagicConfig`
        /// until the configuration is complete, so a reader that races the
        /// launcher sees an obviously incomplete block instead of a half-written
        /// one that happens to pass its checks.
        /// </summary>
        public unsafe void WriteHeader()
        {
            DrelayShared* block = (DrelayShared*)_view;
            block->version = SharedProtocol.Version;
            block->structSize = (uint)GeneratedLayout.DrelaySharedSize;
            block->magic = SharedProtocol.MagicBoot;
            block->nativeTimeoutMs = 60000;
            // Cheap liveness without a clock call in a hot path: the bootstrap
            // bumps this, and a reader can tell "never ran" from "ran".
            block->bootTick = 1;
        }

        public unsafe void SetConfigReady()
        {
            DrelayShared* block = (DrelayShared*)_view;
            block->magicConfig = SharedProtocol.MagicConfig;
        }

        public bool WaitForNative(int timeoutMs)
        {
            return NativeMethods.WaitForSingleObject(_nativeReady, (uint)timeoutMs) == NativeMethods.WAIT_OBJECT_0;
        }

        public bool WaitForBootstrap(int timeoutMs)
        {
            return NativeMethods.WaitForSingleObject(_bootReady, (uint)timeoutMs) == NativeMethods.WAIT_OBJECT_0;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Prints what the native side published.  This is the launcher's
        /// contribution to the evidence: it is the only participant that sees the
        /// handshake from outside, so it is the only one that can report "the
        /// bootstrap never answered" as distinct from "the hook refused".
        /// </summary>
        public unsafe void Report(Action<string> write, bool verbose)
        {
            DrelayShared* block = (DrelayShared*)_view;
            write("");
            write("---- shared block ----");
            write(string.Format("  magic/version   : 0x{0:X8} / {1}", block->magic, block->version));
            write(string.Format("  native status   : 0x{0:X8}{1}{2}{3}{4}{5}",
                block->nativeStatus,
                (block->nativeStatus & SharedProtocol.StJitDetoured) != 0 ? " jitDetoured" : "",
                (block->nativeStatus & SharedProtocol.StDiscoveryDone) != 0 ? " discoveryDone" : "",
                (block->nativeStatus & SharedProtocol.StPatched) != 0 ? " patched" : "",
                (block->nativeStatus & SharedProtocol.StRefused) != 0 ? " REFUSED" : "",
                (block->nativeStatus & SharedProtocol.StOff) != 0 ? " OFF" : ""));
            write(string.Format("  self-check      : {0} passed / {1} failed / {2} gap(s)",
                block->selfCheckPassed, block->selfCheckFailed, block->selfCheckGaps));
            write(string.Format("  targets         : {0} found, {1} patched, of {2} pinned",
                block->targetsFound, block->targetsPatched, block->targetCount));
            write(string.Format("  methodDef slot  : {0}", block->methodDefSlotUsed == SharedProtocol.SlotNone
                ? "not proven"
                : "0x" + block->methodDefSlotUsed.ToString("X2")));
            write(string.Format("  compile calls   : {0}", block->traceWrite));
            write(string.Format("  frame calls     : {0} (frame reads {1} ok / {2} failed)",
                block->frameCalls, block->managedReadCount, block->managedReadFailures));
            // Printed next to the read counts because it decides how to read them:
            // two zeroes mean "there was no world to read" when the read path was
            // never opened and something else entirely when it was.
            write(string.Format("  frame read path : {0}{1}",
                ArmStateName(block->managedArmState),
                block->managedArmState == SharedProtocol.ArmArmed
                    ? string.Format(" at t+{0} ms", block->managedArmTick) : ""));
            write(string.Format("  clrjit/coreclr  : {0} / {1}",
                ReadFixedBuffer(&block->clrjitVersion[0], 32), ReadFixedBuffer(&block->coreclrVersion[0], 32)));
            write(string.Format("  runtime tiering : {0}",
                block->effectiveTieredCompilation == 0 ? "off"
                : block->effectiveTieredCompilation == 1 ? "ON (should have refused)" : "unknown"));
            write("");

            if (verbose)
            {
                // A stack local, addressed directly rather than through the
                // index accessor.  A fixed-size buffer field cannot be passed to
                // a `byte*` parameter as `local.name` -- the compiler answers
                // "you can only take the address of an unfixed expression inside
                // of a fixed statement initializer", because the local is a copy
                // and the buffer would move with it.  Taking `&local.name[0]`
                // works because the local is a stack value and never moves.
                for (int i = 0; i < block->targetCount && i < SharedProtocol.MaxTargets; i++)
                {
                    DrelayTargetHash target = SharedLayout.Target(ref *block, i);
                    write(string.Format("  target {0,-12} {1}  entry 0x{2:X}  native {3} bytes  token 0x{4:X8}",
                        ReadFixedBuffer(&target.name[0], SharedProtocol.TargetNameLen),
                        target.found != 0 ? "FOUND" : "MISSING",
                        target.nativeEntry, target.nativeSize, target.tokenRead));
                }
                for (int i = 0; i < block->offsetCount && i < SharedProtocol.MaxReads; i++)
                {
                    DrelayFieldOffset offset = SharedLayout.FieldOffset(ref *block, i);
                    // A STATIC FIELD'S VALUE IS AN ADDRESS IN TWO HALVES, and printing
                    // only `managedOffset` prints half a pointer that looks like a
                    // byte offset.  See DrelayFieldOffset in DrelayHookShared.h.
                    string where = offset.isStatic != 0
                        ? string.Format("0x{0:X8}{1:X8}", offset.managedStaticBase, offset.managedOffset)
                        : "+" + offset.managedOffset;
                    write(string.Format("  offset {0,-32} {1}{2}",
                        ReadFixedBuffer(&offset.name[0], SharedProtocol.FieldNameLen),
                        where, offset.agree != 0 ? "  confirmed" : ""));
                }
            }
        }

        private static unsafe string ReadFixedBuffer(byte* source, int count)
        {
            int len = 0;
            while (len < count && source[len] != 0)
            {
                len++;
            }
            return System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetString(source, len);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The arming gate's state, spelled the way the hook's own logs spell it, so
        /// the launcher's summary and <c>summary.txt</c> cannot disagree about what
        /// "0" means.
        /// </summary>
        private static string ArmStateName(uint state)
        {
            switch (state)
            {
                case SharedProtocol.ArmWaiting: return "waiting for a world";
                case SharedProtocol.ArmArmed: return "ARMED";
                case SharedProtocol.ArmRefused: return "REFUSED (the cross-check disagreed)";
                case SharedProtocol.ArmUnconfigured: return "UNCONFIGURED (no offsets measured)";
                default: return "unknown (" + state + ")";
            }
        }

        public void Dispose()
        {
            if (_nativeReady != IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                NativeMethods.CloseHandle(_nativeReady);
            }
            if (_bootReady != IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                NativeMethods.CloseHandle(_bootReady);
            }
            if (_view != IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                NativeMethods.UnmapViewOfFile(_view);
            }
            if (_mapping != IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                NativeMethods.CloseHandle(_mapping);
            }
            if (_backingFile != IntPtr.Zero)
            {
                NativeMethods.CloseHandle(_backingFile);
                _backingFile = IntPtr.Zero;
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/native/DrelayCrash.cpp`:

```cpp
// DrelayCrash.cpp -- see DrelayCrash.h for why this exists rather than a
// debugger.

#include "DrelayCrash.h"
#include "DrelayGlobals.h"

#include <windows.h>
#include <tlhelp32.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <string.h>

namespace drelay {
namespace {

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The module list.  Snapshotted from an ordinary thread context, then read from
// the handler; the handler itself calls nothing that could take a lock.

struct ModuleInfo {
    wchar_t   name[48];
    uintptr_t base;
    uintptr_t end;
};

constexpr uint32_t kMaxModules = 320;

ModuleInfo g_modules[kMaxModules] = {};
uint32_t   g_moduleCount = 0;
volatile LONG g_installed = 0;
volatile LONG g_inHandler = 0;
volatile LONG g_inResolve = 0;
volatile LONG g_faults = 0;
PVOID         g_veh = nullptr;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION: THE EXCEPTION THE JIT RAISES WHEN IT GIVES UP ON A METHOD,
// AND THE ONE THIS REPORTER USED TO MISTAKE FOR A CRASH.
//
// `0x02345678` is not a Windows status code and it is not an accident.  It is the
// JIT's own channel for "I cannot compile this method", and it is raised in exactly
// one place -- `fatal(int errCode)` in `src/coreclr/jit/error.cpp`:
//
//     ULONG_PTR exceptArg = errCode;
//     RaiseException(FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION, EXCEPTION_NONCONTINUABLE, 1, &exceptArg);
//
// and caught by the JIT's own filter in the same file:
//
//     LONG __JITfilter(PEXCEPTION_POINTERS p, LPVOID param) {
//         if (p->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionCode == FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION) {
//             pParam->errc = (int)p->ExceptionRecord->ExceptionInformation[0];
//             jitInfo->reportFatalError((CorJitResult)pParam->errc);
//             return EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER;
//         }
//         return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
//     }
//
// So it is a FIRST-CHANCE exception the runtime handles as a matter of routine --
// the EE retries the method with MinOpts -- and `param[0]` is a `CorJitResult`, not
// an address: `0x80000001` badCode, `0x80000003` noWay, `0x80000005`
// CORJIT_RECOVERABLEERROR (a `noway_assert`), `0x80000006` an implementation limit.
//
// WHY IT MATTERED HERE.  A run produced a `crash.txt` containing two records with
// `exception 0x02345678 unclassified` and `param[0] 0x80000005`, and it read as a
// crash in the JIT -- with our `compileMethod` detour one frame below, which made it
// look like the hook corrupting the compiler.  It is neither.  The process that
// produced one of those records went on to write its whole evidence set, and the
// same record appears in runs from before this hook had any of the code under
// suspicion.  Nothing about it is a fault.
//
// THE REAL COST.  A `crash.txt` that says "crash" for a handled JIT retry is the
// same defect as `frames.csv` calling a millisecond total a per-frame second: an
// instrument that is wrong about what it is measuring, and that a reader has no way
// to detect.  It cost an hour of looking for a crash that had not happened, while
// the run's ACTUAL death -- `COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE` (0x80131506) from coreclr, which
// terminates the process through `TerminateProcess` and therefore raises nothing
// this handler can see -- left no report at all.
//
// It is still recorded, because "the JIT gave up on a method" is real evidence about
// a process with a JIT hook in it.  It goes to `jit-internal.txt`, named for what it
// is.
#define FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION 0x02345678u

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The report is built in one static buffer, because allocating inside an
// exception handler is exactly the thing that turns a diagnosed fault into an
// undiagnosed one.

char   g_text[16384];
size_t g_len = 0;

void App(const char* text) {
    const size_t n = strlen(text);
    if (g_len + n + 1 >= sizeof(g_text)) {
        return;
    }
    memcpy(g_text + g_len, text, n);
    g_len += n;
    g_text[g_len] = '\0';
}

void AppF(const char* fmt, ...) {
    char line[512] = {};
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, fmt);
    _vsnprintf_s(line, sizeof(line), _TRUNCATE, fmt, args);
    va_end(args);
    App(line);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

void SnapshotModules() {
    const uint32_t previous = g_moduleCount;
    uint32_t count = 0;

    HANDLE snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(
        TH32CS_SNAPMODULE | TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32, GetCurrentProcessId());
    if (snapshot != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        MODULEENTRY32W entry = {};
        entry.dwSize = sizeof(entry);
        if (Module32FirstW(snapshot, &entry)) {
            do {
                if (count >= kMaxModules) {
                    break;
                }
                ModuleInfo& module = g_modules[count];
                // The name is truncated, not rejected: a diagnostic that fails
                // because a path was long would be a diagnostic that fails
                // exactly when it is needed.
                wcsncpy_s(module.name, entry.szModule, _TRUNCATE);
                module.base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(entry.modBaseAddr);
                module.end = module.base + entry.modBaseSize;
                ++count;
            } while (Module32NextW(snapshot, &entry));
        }
        CloseHandle(snapshot);
    }

    g_moduleCount = (count > 0) ? count : previous;
}

// `out` is written for every address, including one that belongs to no module,
// because "which module" being unknown is itself the finding.
void Describe(const void* address, char* out, size_t cap) {
    const uintptr_t value = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(address);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_moduleCount; ++i) {
        if (value >= g_modules[i].base && value < g_modules[i].end) {
            _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "%ls+0x%llX", g_modules[i].name,
                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(value - g_modules[i].base));
            return;
        }
    }

    // The address may belong to a module loaded after the last snapshot -- a
    // lazily loaded one such as crypt32.dll is exactly the sort of thing that
    // would be missing.  Asking the loader takes the loader lock, so it is a
    // fallback rather than the first move, and `g_inResolve` stops a fault
    // *inside* this fallback from recursing into it again.
    if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&g_inResolve, 1, 0) == 0) {
        HMODULE module = nullptr;
        if (GetModuleHandleExW(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS |
                                   GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                               reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(address), &module) != 0 &&
            module != nullptr) {
            wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
            if (GetModuleFileNameW(module, path, MAX_PATH) != 0) {
                const wchar_t* leaf = wcsrchr(path, L'\\');
                leaf = (leaf != nullptr) ? leaf + 1 : path;
                _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "%ls(unsnapshotted)+0x%llX", leaf,
                            static_cast<unsigned long long>(
                                value - reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(module)));
                InterlockedExchange(&g_inResolve, 0);
                return;
            }
        }
        InterlockedExchange(&g_inResolve, 0);
    }
    _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "(no module)");
}

const char* ExceptionName(DWORD code) {
    switch (code) {
        case EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION:      return "ACCESS_VIOLATION";
        case EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR:         return "IN_PAGE_ERROR";
        case EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION:   return "ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION";
        case EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION:      return "PRIV_INSTRUCTION";
        case EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW:        return "STACK_OVERFLOW";
        case EXCEPTION_INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO:    return "INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO";
        case EXCEPTION_DATATYPE_MISALIGNMENT: return "DATATYPE_MISALIGNMENT";
        case EXCEPTION_ARRAY_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED: return "ARRAY_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED";
        case 0x80131506u:                     return "COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE (the CLR fatal error)";
        case 0xC0000409u:                     return "STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN / fail-fast";
        case 0xE0434352u:                     return "CLR managed exception";
        case FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION:             return "FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION (the JIT's own fatal path, "
                                                     "which the JIT catches itself)";
        default:                              return "unclassified";
    }
}

// A plain walk of the faulting thread's return addresses.  This is the frame
// list a debugger would print, and it is short for the same reason a debugger's
// is: the top frame is often a JIT-compiled or trampoline body with no unwind
// data, and the walk stops there.
void AppendStackWalk(const CONTEXT* context) {
    App("  return addresses (RtlCaptureStackBackTrace):\r\n");

    void* frames[62] = {};
    const USHORT captured = RtlCaptureStackBackTrace(0, 62, frames, nullptr);
    for (USHORT i = 0; i < captured; ++i) {
        char described[256] = {};
        Describe(frames[i], described, sizeof(described));
        AppF("    [%02u] %p  %s\r\n", static_cast<unsigned>(i), frames[i], described);
    }
    if (captured == 0) {
        App("    (the walk captured nothing -- no unwind data above the fault)\r\n");
    }

    // A RAW SCAN, BECAUSE THE WALK ABOVE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL HERE.
    //
    // `RtlCaptureStackBackTrace` needs unwind information for every frame it
    // steps over.  A MinHook trampoline, a hand-written thunk and the
    // `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` transition stub all lack it, so the interesting
    // fault -- one reached through the hook -- produces an empty walk.  Scanning
    // the stack for values that land inside a known module needs no unwind data
    // and no cooperation from the code above the fault.
    App("  raw stack scan (module-shaped values, may include stale frames):\r\n");
    const uintptr_t* stack = reinterpret_cast<const uintptr_t*>(context->Rsp);
    uint32_t shown = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 768 && shown < 60; ++i) {
        uintptr_t value = 0;
        bool unreadable = false;
        __try {
            value = stack[i];
        } __except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) {
            unreadable = true;
        }
        if (unreadable) {
            App("    (the stack itself became unreadable here)\r\n");
            break;
        }
        for (uint32_t m = 0; m < g_moduleCount; ++m) {
            if (value >= g_modules[m].base && value < g_modules[m].end) {
                char described[256] = {};
                Describe(reinterpret_cast<const void*>(value), described, sizeof(described));
                AppF("    [rsp+0x%03X] %p  %s\r\n", i * 8,
                     reinterpret_cast<const void*>(value), described);
                ++shown;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if (shown == 0) {
        App("    (nothing module-shaped within 768 slots of rsp)\r\n");
    }
}

void WriteReport(const wchar_t* fileName) {
    // Written to the run directory AND to the debugger channel.  The file is the
    // one that survives a hard kill; the debugger channel is the one that
    // survives a write failure.
    OutputDebugStringA(g_text);

    if (g_runDir[0] == L'\0') {
        return;
    }
    wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
    _snwprintf_s(path, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s\\%s", g_runDir, fileName);
    HANDLE file = CreateFileW(path, FILE_APPEND_DATA, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE,
                              nullptr, OPEN_ALWAYS, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, nullptr);
    if (file == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        return;
    }
    DWORD written = 0;
    WriteFile(file, g_text, static_cast<DWORD>(g_len), &written, nullptr);
    FlushFileBuffers(file);
    CloseHandle(file);
}

LONG CALLBACK VehHandler(EXCEPTION_POINTERS* pointers) {
    if (pointers == nullptr || pointers->ExceptionRecord == nullptr) {
        return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
    }
    const EXCEPTION_RECORD* record = pointers->ExceptionRecord;
    const DWORD code = record->ExceptionCode;

    // First-chance noise that is not a fault.  A vectored handler sees every
    // exception in the process, including the ones the runtime raises and
    // handles routinely, and treating one of those as the crash would produce a
    // confident wrong answer -- the exact failure mode PHASE1-HANDOFF.md
    // section 8 is about.
    switch (code) {
        case 0x406D1388u:            // SetThreadName, raised by every named thread
        case 0xE06D7363u:            // a C++ exception being thrown
        case 0x40010006u:            // OutputDebugString
        case 0x4001000Au:            // Debugger print
        case 0x4000001Fu:            // WOW64 breakpoint
        case EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT:
        case EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP:
        case 0xE0434352u:            // a managed exception being thrown normally
            return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
        default:
            break;
    }

    if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&g_inHandler, 1, 0) != 0) {
        return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
    }
    if (InterlockedIncrement(&g_faults) > 8) {
        InterlockedExchange(&g_inHandler, 0);
        return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
    }

    g_len = 0;
    g_text[0] = '\0';

    char described[256] = {};
    const bool jitInternal = (code == FATAL_JIT_EXCEPTION);
    Describe(record->ExceptionAddress, described, sizeof(described));
    App(jitInternal
            ? "\r\n=== drelay: the JIT gave up on a method (NOT a crash) ===\r\n"
            : "\r\n=== drelay crash report ===\r\n");
    AppF("  exception   0x%08X  %s\r\n", code, ExceptionName(code));
    if (jitInternal) {
        // Said before the stack, because the stack is the misleading part: it shows
        // clrjit and our own detour, which reads as "the hook broke the compiler".
        App("  what        the JIT raised its own fatal-exception channel and caught it\n"
            "              itself; the runtime retries the method. This is recorded as\n"
            "              evidence about the JIT, not as a process death. A real death\n"
            "              (COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE, 0x80131506) terminates through\n"
            "              TerminateProcess and raises nothing this handler can see.\n");
    }
    AppF("  thread      %lu\r\n", GetCurrentThreadId());
    AppF("  at          %p  %s\r\n", record->ExceptionAddress, described);
    AppF("  parameters  %u\r\n", record->NumberParameters);

    if (code == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION && record->NumberParameters >= 2) {
        const ULONG_PTR operation = record->ExceptionInformation[0];
        const ULONG_PTR target = record->ExceptionInformation[1];
        const char* what = (operation == 0) ? "read" : (operation == 1) ? "write" : "execute";
        char targetDescribed[256] = {};
        Describe(reinterpret_cast<const void*>(target), targetDescribed, sizeof(targetDescribed));
        AppF("  access      %s of %p  %s\r\n", what,
             reinterpret_cast<const void*>(target), targetDescribed);
    } else {
        for (DWORD i = 0; i < record->NumberParameters && i < 4; ++i) {
            AppF("  param[%u]    0x%llX\r\n", i,
                 static_cast<unsigned long long>(record->ExceptionInformation[i]));
        }
    }

    if (pointers->ContextRecord != nullptr) {
        const CONTEXT* context = pointers->ContextRecord;
        AppF("  rip %p  rsp %p  rbp %p\r\n",
             reinterpret_cast<const void*>(context->Rip),
             reinterpret_cast<const void*>(context->Rsp),
             reinterpret_cast<const void*>(context->Rbp));
        AppendStackWalk(context);
    }

    AppF("  modules snapshotted: %u\r\n", g_moduleCount);
    App(jitInternal ? "=== end: the JIT's own retry, not a crash ===\r\n"
                    : "=== end crash report ===\r\n");

    // Last, because it is the only step that can fail without losing the report.
    WriteReport(jitInternal ? L"jit-internal.txt" : L"crash.txt");

    InterlockedExchange(&g_inHandler, 0);
    return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
}

LONG WINAPI UnhandledFilter(EXCEPTION_POINTERS* pointers) {
    // A vectored handler runs before this one, so reaching here means the fault
    // is one the vectored handler filtered as benign, or the filter itself
    // failed.  Reported anyway rather than returning EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
    // silently, because silence here is indistinguishable from "no crash".
    VehHandler(pointers);
    return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
}

} // namespace

void DrelayInstallCrashReporter() {
    if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&g_installed, 1, 0) != 0) {
        return;
    }
    SnapshotModules();
    g_veh = AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, VehHandler);
    SetUnhandledExceptionFilter(UnhandledFilter);
    (void)g_veh;
}

void DrelayArmCrashReporter() {
    SnapshotModules();
    if (g_veh != nullptr) {
        RemoveVectoredExceptionHandler(g_veh);
    }
    g_veh = AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, VehHandler);
}

} // namespace drelay

```

`hook/native/DrelayCrash.h`:

```h
// DrelayCrash.h -- the in-process crash reporter.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS INSTEAD OF A DEBUGGER
// -------------------------------------
// PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 3 says the highest-value thing left in Phase 1 is to
// attach a native debugger and break on the fault.  There is no debugger on the
// machine this is built on: no cdb, no windbg, no Visual Studio debugger -- only
// `dbghelp.dll` next to the Windows Kits headers.  So the hook carries its own.
//
// What a debugger would have answered, and what this answers instead:
//
//   * "where did it fault"           -> the exception address, resolved to
//                                       `module+0xRVA` against a module list
//                                       snapshotted before the fault.
//   * "what did it touch"            -> `ExceptionInformation[1]` for an access
//                                       violation, which says whether the read
//                                       was a null, a wild pointer, or a
//                                       plausible-looking small integer.
//   * "who called it"                -> a real stack walk plus a raw stack scan,
//                                       because the faulting thread may have no
//                                       unwind data at the top frame (a MinHook
//                                       trampoline has none).
//
// It is installed from `DrelayHook_Init`, i.e. while the target process is still
// suspended by `CreateProcess(CREATE_SUSPENDED)`, so it is in place before a
// single managed instruction runs and before the watcher thread exists.
//
// THE ONE THING IT MUST NOT DO IS CHANGE THE OUTCOME.  Every handler returns
// `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH`: the runtime's own handling still runs, the fatal
// error is still printed, and the process still dies.  This observes; it does
// not intervene.  A diagnostic that swallows the fault it is measuring would be
// worth less than no diagnostic at all.

#ifndef DRELAY_CRASH_H
#define DRELAY_CRASH_H

namespace drelay {

// Installs the vectored handler and the last-chance filter, and takes the first
// module-list snapshot.  Idempotent.
void DrelayInstallCrashReporter();

// Re-reads the module list AND moves the handler back to the front of the
// vectored chain.  Called from the watcher thread at each point where the
// process is about to do something new, and both halves are necessary:
//
//   * THE MODULE LIST, because the snapshot taken at injection time cannot
//     contain clrjit.dll, coreclr.dll or anything else the host loads later --
//     which is every module a fault here would be in.  It is refreshed from an
//     ordinary thread context on purpose: the loader lock is taken here, and an
//     exception handler is the wrong place to take a lock on the off chance the
//     fault happened while holding it.
//
//   * THE CHAIN POSITION, because `AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, ...)` inserts
//     at the HEAD, so handlers registered with `First=1` run in reverse order of
//     registration.  This DLL registers before CoreCLR exists; the runtime then
//     registers its own, which therefore runs *first* and consumes a
//     managed-context access violation by redirecting it into a managed
//     exception.  The first version of this reporter wrote no report at all for
//     exactly that reason -- the fault was real, reproducible and completely
//     invisible to a handler that had been silently overtaken.  Removing and
//     re-adding puts this one back in front.
void DrelayArmCrashReporter();

} // namespace drelay

#endif // DRELAY_CRASH_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayEvidence.cpp`:

```cpp
// DrelayEvidence.cpp -- the run's evidence, written once at the end.

#include "DrelayEvidence.h"
#include "DrelayGlobals.h"
#include "DrelayLog.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

namespace drelay {

namespace {

FILE* OpenIn(const wchar_t* runDir, const wchar_t* name) {
    wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
    _snwprintf_s(path, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s\\%s", runDir, name);
    FILE* f = nullptr;
    if (_wfopen_s(&f, path, L"wb") != 0) {
        return nullptr;
    }
    return f;
}

void CopyFixedName(const char* source, size_t cap, char* out, size_t outCap) {
    size_t n = 0;
    while (n + 1 < cap && n + 1 < outCap && source[n] != '\0') {
        out[n] = source[n];
        ++n;
    }
    out[n] = '\0';
}

const char* StatusName(uint32_t status) {
    switch (status) {
        case DRELAY_STATUS_OK:          return "ok";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_GAP:         return "gap";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_REFUSED:     return "refused";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_FAILED:      return "failed";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_TIMEOUT:     return "timeout";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_DISABLED:    return "disabled";
        case DRELAY_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED: return "unsupported";
        default:                        return "unknown";
    }
}

void WriteHex(FILE* f, const uint8_t* bytes, size_t count) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        fprintf(f, "%02X", bytes[i]);
    }
}

// The arming gate's state, in the words `hook.log` and `selfcheck.txt` use.
const char* ArmStateName(uint32_t state) {
    switch (state) {
        case DRELAY_ARM_WAITING:      return "WAITING (no world has existed yet)";
        case DRELAY_ARM_ARMED:        return "ARMED (the cross-check passed)";
        case DRELAY_ARM_REFUSED:      return "REFUSED (the cross-check disagreed)";
        case DRELAY_ARM_UNCONFIGURED: return "UNCONFIGURED (no offsets were measured)";
        default:                      return "unknown";
    }
}

// A coordinate pair, or "(not read)" when the chain was refused before reading.
void FormatPoint(char* out, size_t cap, float x, float y) {
    if (x != x || y != y) {
        _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "(not read)");
    } else {
        _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "(%.4f, %.4f)", x, y);
    }
}

// `summary.txt` is the file a person reads first, so it leads with the answer
// (did it install, what was found) and puts the raw numbers underneath.
void WriteSummary(FILE* f) {
    fprintf(f, "drelay hook -- Phase 1 run summary\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "=================================\r\n\r\n");

    const bool installed = (g_shared->nativeStatus & DRELAY_ST_JIT_DETOURED) != 0;
    const bool refused = (g_shared->nativeStatus & DRELAY_ST_REFUSED) != 0;
    const bool off = (g_shared->nativeStatus & DRELAY_ST_OFF) != 0;

    fprintf(f, "result            : %s\r\n",
            off ? "OFF (the off switch was honoured; nothing was installed)"
                : refused ? "REFUSED (a check failed; the game ran unmodified)"
                          : installed ? "installed" : "not installed (see hook.log)");
    fprintf(f, "native status     : 0x%08X\r\n", g_shared->nativeStatus);
    fprintf(f, "self-check        : %u passed, %u failed, %u gap(s)\r\n",
            g_shared->selfCheckPassed, g_shared->selfCheckFailed, g_shared->selfCheckGaps);
    fprintf(f, "install time      : %u ms\r\n", g_shared->installMs);
    fprintf(f, "methodDef slot    : ");
    if (g_shared->methodDefSlotUsed == DRELAY_SLOT_NONE) {
        fprintf(f, "not proven (no candidate slot returned a matching token)\r\n");
    } else {
        fprintf(f, "0x%02X\r\n", g_shared->methodDefSlotUsed);
    }
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    fprintf(f, "runtime\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "  coreclr.dll     : %s\r\n", g_shared->coreclrVersion);
    fprintf(f, "  clrjit.dll      : %s\r\n", g_shared->clrjitVersion);
    fprintf(f, "  JIT/EE GUID     : ");
    WriteHex(f, g_shared->jitGuid, 16);
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "  vtable in .text : %s\r\n", g_shared->jitVtableInText ? "yes (4/4 slots)" : "NO");
    fprintf(f, "  tiering         : %s\r\n",
            g_shared->effectiveTieredCompilation == 0 ? "off"
            : g_shared->effectiveTieredCompilation == 1 ? "ON -- should have refused" : "unknown");
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    fprintf(f, "assembly\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "  MVID            : ");
    // Printed in the same byte order as MVID.ToString("D") in the bootstrap and
    // known-build.json, so the three can be compared by eye rather than by
    // reversing the first three fields in one's head.
    fprintf(f, "%02X%02X%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X\r\n",
            g_shared->mvid[3], g_shared->mvid[2], g_shared->mvid[1], g_shared->mvid[0],
            g_shared->mvid[5], g_shared->mvid[4], g_shared->mvid[7], g_shared->mvid[6],
            g_shared->mvid[8], g_shared->mvid[9], g_shared->mvid[10], g_shared->mvid[11],
            g_shared->mvid[12], g_shared->mvid[13], g_shared->mvid[14], g_shared->mvid[15]);
    fprintf(f, "  size            : %lld bytes\r\n", static_cast<long long>(g_shared->managedAssemblySize));
    fprintf(f, "  entry point tok : 0x%08X\r\n", g_shared->entryPointToken);
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    // Spike 1.2's headline: which of the four targets the compilation stream
    // produced, and whether the token agrees with what Phase 0 pinned.
    //
    // TWO COUNTS, FOR THE REASON THE CLOSING LOG LINE HAS TWO (DrelayMain.cpp): the
    // discovery window's match count and the run's are different facts, and a line
    // reading "1 found, 2 patched" is read as an inconsistency rather than as a target
    // that arrived late.  Run 12 of the injection suite produces exactly that -- one
    // target inside the window, two matched by the end -- and this line used to report
    // the first number beside the second one's label.
    {
        uint32_t matchedByEnd = 0;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_shared->targetCount && i < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS; ++i) {
            if (g_shared->targets[i].found != 0) {
                matchedByEnd++;
            }
        }
        fprintf(f, "targets (%u pinned, %u matched inside the discovery window, "
                   "%u matched by the end of the run, %u patched)\r\n",
                g_shared->targetCount, g_shared->targetsFound, matchedByEnd,
                g_shared->targetsPatched);
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_shared->targetCount && i < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS; ++i) {
        const DrelayTargetHash& t = g_shared->targets[i];
        char name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN] = {};
        CopyFixedName(t.name, sizeof(t.name), name, sizeof(name));
        fprintf(f, "  %-12s %-8s", name, t.found ? "FOUND" : "MISSING");
        if (t.found) {
            const bool tokenAgrees = (t.tokenRead != 0) && (t.tokenRead == t.metadataToken);
            const bool tokenRead = (t.tokenRead != 0);
            fprintf(f, " native %5u bytes at 0x%llX  token 0x%08X (%s; Phase 0 says 0x%08X)",
                    t.nativeSize, static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.nativeEntry), t.tokenRead,
                    tokenRead ? (tokenAgrees ? "agrees" : "DISAGREES") : "not read",
                    t.metadataToken);
        }
        fprintf(f, "\r\n");
    }
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    fprintf(f, "frame tick (Spike 1.3)\r\n");
    // WHICH READ PATH THIS RUN USED, PRINTED BEFORE ITS COUNTERS BECAUSE IT DECIDES HOW
    // TO READ THEM.  Phase 1's frame read is the native detour; Phase 2's is a MANAGED
    // replacement, and in that mode the native detour is not installed at all -- so
    // `calls: 0` and `frame reads: 0 ok` describe a path that does not exist on this run
    // rather than a read that failed.  The 2026-10-12 20:42 session read 19 349 frames
    // through the managed replacement and printed those zeroes here, and the self-check
    // needed the same rule (DrelaySelfCheck.cpp checks 9 and 9c).  A reader who compares
    // two runs' frame costs needs this line before they compare the counters.
    fprintf(f, "  read path       : %s\r\n",
            (g_shared->managedFrameReplacement != 0)
                ? "the MANAGED REPLACEMENT -- the native detour is not installed, so the "
                  "counters below are 0 by construction; the entries are in the bootstrap "
                  "log ('MANAGED REPLACEMENT entered', and the sensor's frame lines)"
                : "the native frame detour");
    fprintf(f, "  calls           : %u\r\n", g_shared->frameCalls);
    fprintf(f, "  worst call      : %u us\r\n", g_frameMaxUs.load());
    // THE ARMING GATE, PRINTED BEFORE THE READ NUMBERS BECAUSE IT DECIDES HOW TO
    // READ THEM.  `frame reads: 0 ok, 0 failed` means one thing when the read path
    // was never armed -- there was no world to read -- and a different thing when it
    // was armed and the read failed.  Until this line existed the two were the same
    // two zeroes.
    {
        char reflected[64] = {};
        char pointer[64] = {};
        FormatPoint(reflected, sizeof(reflected),
                    g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefX, g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefY);
        FormatPoint(pointer, sizeof(pointer),
                    g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrX, g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrY);
        fprintf(f, "  arm state       : %s\r\n", ArmStateName(g_shared->managedArmState));
        if (g_shared->managedArmState == DRELAY_ARM_ARMED) {
            fprintf(f, "  armed at        : t+%u ms\r\n", g_shared->managedArmTick);
        }
        fprintf(f, "  cross-check     : reflection %s vs pointer chain %s\r\n",
                reflected, pointer);
        fprintf(f, "  waited for player: %u probe(s), %u frame(s) found none\r\n",
                g_shared->managedProbeWaits, g_shared->managedFrameWaits);
    }
    fprintf(f, "  frame reads     : %u ok, %u failed\r\n",
            g_shared->managedReadCount, g_shared->managedReadFailures);
    fprintf(f, "  read value      : %.4f%s\r\n", g_shared->managedReadValue,
            g_shared->managedReadValid ? "" : "  (not currently valid)");
    // WHETHER THE READ IS STILL RUNNING, REPORTED AS THE STATE IT IS IN RATHER THAN
    // AS THE INTENT IT WAS LAUNCHED WITH.  The live window closing no longer implies
    // the read has stopped -- that is the release default now -- and a reader
    // comparing two runs needs to know which one this is before comparing their read
    // counts or their frame costs.
    fprintf(f, "  frame read      : %s\r\n",
            g_framePaused.load() != 0
                ? "PAUSED (DRELAY_KEEP_READING=0 was set, so the read stopped when the live "
                  "window closed)"
                : "open (still reading on every frame)");
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    // THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES HOW EVERY OTHER NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS READ.
    //
    // `targets (4 pinned, 0 found)` above is only a statement about the game while
    // the detour inspected every compilation it was entered for.  When it did not,
    // "0 found" means "the hook was not looking", and the two are indistinguishable
    // in `hook.log` unless this line is printed.  `invocations` is counted before
    // the re-entrancy guard; `compilations seen` is counted after it.
    fprintf(f, "compileMethod detour\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "  invocations     : %u  (every entry, counted before the re-entrancy guard)\r\n",
            g_detourInvocations.load());
    fprintf(f, "  instrumented    : %u  (entries the hook actually inspected)\r\n",
            g_compileCalls.load());
    fprintf(f, "  re-entrant skip : %u\r\n", g_reentrantSkips.load());
    if (g_detourInvocations.load() > g_compileCalls.load()) {
        fprintf(f, "  WARNING         : %u compilation(s) were executed and NOT inspected. A target\r\n",
                g_detourInvocations.load() - g_compileCalls.load());
        fprintf(f, "                    reported MISSING in this run is not proof that the game never\r\n");
        fprintf(f, "                    compiled it. See DrelayGlobals.h.\r\n");
    }
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    fprintf(f, "rings\r\n");
    fprintf(f, "  log lines       : %u written, %u overflowed\r\n",
            g_shared->logWrite, g_shared->logOverflow);    // REPORTED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT FAILURES.  `overflowed` is the
    // ring discarding lines the flusher had not read yet; this is the flusher being
    // unable to OPEN the file, which loses every line behind it no matter how much
    // room the ring has.  A run whose log stops mid-session is explained by the second
    // and not by the first, and until they had separate counters the two produced one
    // uninterpretable number.
    if (g_shared->logAppendFailures != 0) {
        fprintf(f, "  log appends     : %u failed pass(es) -- see hook.log.append-failed\r\n",
                g_shared->logAppendFailures);
    }
    fprintf(f, "  trace rows      : %u written, %u overflowed\r\n",
            g_shared->traceWrite, g_shared->traceOverflow);
    fprintf(f, "  frame rows      : %u written, %u overflowed\r\n",
            g_shared->frameWrite, g_shared->frameOverflow);
    fprintf(f, "\r\n");

    fprintf(f,
        "what this run does and does not prove\r\n"
        "  Proves            : the runtime was validated, the compilation stream was observed,\r\n"
        "                      and the targets it produced were matched by IL hash.\r\n"
        "  Does not prove    : that a prediction agrees with the game's collision decision.\r\n"
        "                      That is Phase 2 (L2), and nothing here is evidence for it.\r\n"
        "  A GAP is a check that was not made. It is never a pass. See selfcheck.txt.\r\n");
}

void WriteOffsetsCsv(FILE* f) {
    fprintf(f, "name,managed_offset,managed_static_base,managed_valid,is_static,"
               "jit_offset,jit_valid,agree\n");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_shared->offsetCount && i < DRELAY_MAX_READS; ++i) {
        const DrelayFieldOffset& o = g_shared->offsets[i];
        char name[DRELAY_FIELD_NAME_LEN] = {};
        CopyFixedName(o.name, sizeof(o.name), name, sizeof(name));
        // A STATIC FIELD'S `managed_offset` COLUMN IS AN ADDRESS, NOT AN OFFSET.
        //
        // It is printed as one, because the two halves of a 64-bit address do not
        // fit in the 32-bit field that holds an instance offset and the previous
        // version printed the low half as if it were a number of bytes.  Read the
        // column together with `is_static`: for a static it is `0x<high><low>`, and
        // `managed_static_base` repeats the high half so a consumer that ignores
        // this convention still sees both halves rather than a plausible wrong one.
        fprintf(f, "\"%s\",", name);
        if (o.isStatic != 0) {
            fprintf(f, "0x%08X%08X", o.managedStaticBase, o.managedOffset);
        } else {
            fprintf(f, "%u", o.managedOffset);
        }
        fprintf(f, ",%u,%u,%u,", o.managedStaticBase, o.managedValid, o.isStatic);
        if (o.jitValid) {
            fprintf(f, "%u,1,%u\n", o.jitOffset, o.agree);
        } else {
            fprintf(f, ",0,%u\n", o.agree);
        }
    }
    // Said in the file rather than only in the docs: a reader who opens
    // offsets.csv alone must not conclude that the empty jit column means
    // "agreed by absence".
    fprintf(f, "# jit_offset is empty until Phase 2 wires ICorJitInfo::getFieldOffset.\n");
    // THE PHASE 1 ORACLE, NAMED, BECAUSE THE COLUMN ALONE DOES NOT SAY WHICH ONE IT IS.
    fprintf(f, "# agree is written by whichever route confirmed the value. In Phase 1 that is the\n");
    fprintf(f, "# pointer chain: the offsets are used to walk World.Shared -> Player -> Position and\n");
    fprintf(f, "# the result is compared with the same state read through reflection. See summary.txt\n");
    fprintf(f, "# for the arm state and the two coordinate pairs that were compared, and selfcheck.txt\n");
    fprintf(f, "# for the verdict as a check.\n");
    // A STATIC FIELD'S COLUMNS, STATED IN THE FILE ITSELF.  The encoding is not
    // guessable from the header line and a wrong reading produces a real-looking
    // number, which is the worst kind of wrong.
    fprintf(f, "# For a row with is_static=1, managed_offset is 0x<managed_static_base><managed_offset>:\n");
    fprintf(f, "# a static field has an address rather than an instance offset, and an x64 address does\n");
    fprintf(f, "# not fit the 32-bit column.\n");
}

void WriteFramesCsv(FILE* f) {
    // THE COLUMNS ARE NAMED FOR WHAT THE VALUES ACTUALLY ARE.
    //
    // This read `arg_total_s`/`implied_hz`, which treated the detour's argument as a
    // frame *delta in seconds* and printed `1/arg` as a frequency.  It is neither.
    // `DarzaWindow.Update`'s one parameter is `GameTime.TotalGameTime.TotalMilliseconds`
    // -- see the call site at IL_00fc of `WindowsGame::Update` in the game's IL dump --
    // so it is a monotonically increasing TOTAL, in milliseconds, since the game
    // started.  Printed as seconds it reads as an absurd 27,824 s frame and `1/arg`
    // as 0.00 Hz, and a reader had no way to tell that the instrument was fine.
    //
    // The frame rate is the *increment* between consecutive rows, which is what a
    // reader actually wants and what makes this file evidence: 16.7 ms per call is
    // 60 Hz and is the proof that the detour is on the real per-frame method.
    fprintf(f, "seq,qpc,arg_total_ms,frame_delta_ms,value,read_ok,read_failures,elapsed_us\n");
    const uint32_t written = g_shared->frameWrite;
    if (written == 0) {
        return;
    }
    // Oldest first.  The ring holds the last N rows; if it wrapped, the oldest
    // surviving row is `written - N + 1`, and starting anywhere else would emit
    // the rows out of order with a silent discontinuity in the middle.
    const uint32_t first = (written > DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS)
        ? written - DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS + 1 : 1;
    // The delta is derived here rather than stored, so the shared layout does not
    // change for a reporting detail -- a struct change costs a version bump and a
    // regenerated managed layout, which is not worth a subtraction.
    bool havePrevious = false;
    float previousTotal = 0.0f;
    for (uint32_t seq = first; seq <= written; ++seq) {
        const DrelayFrameRow& row = g_shared->frames[(seq - 1) % DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS];
        const float delta = havePrevious ? (row.argTotal - previousTotal) : 0.0f;
        previousTotal = row.argTotal;
        havePrevious = true;
        fprintf(f, "%u,%llu,%.6f,%.3f,%.4f,%u,%u,%u\n", seq,
                static_cast<unsigned long long>(row.qpc), row.argTotal, delta,
                row.value, row.readOk, row.readFailures, row.elapsedUs);
    }
}

// One JSON object per line, so the file is appendable, greppable and readable
// without a streaming parser -- the same shape the relay's own event log uses.
void WriteEventsJsonl(FILE* f) {
    if (g_shared->traceOverflow > 0) {
        fprintf(f, "{\"kind\":\"ring-overflow\",\"ring\":\"trace\",\"lost\":%u}\n",
                g_shared->traceOverflow);
    }
    const uint32_t traceWritten = g_shared->traceWrite;
    const uint32_t traceFirst = (traceWritten > DRELAY_TRACE_RING_ROWS)
        ? traceWritten - DRELAY_TRACE_RING_ROWS + 1 : 1;
    for (uint32_t seq = traceFirst; seq <= traceWritten; ++seq) {
        const DrelayTraceRow& row = g_shared->trace[(seq - 1) % DRELAY_TRACE_RING_ROWS];
        fprintf(f, "{\"kind\":\"compile\",\"seq\":%u,\"ilSize\":%u,\"nativeSize\":%u,"
                   "\"nativeEntry\":\"0x%llX\",\"token\":%u,\"matched\":",
                seq, row.ilSize, row.nativeSize,
                static_cast<unsigned long long>(row.nativeEntry), row.tokenRead);
        if (row.matchedTarget == 0xFFu) {
            fprintf(f, "null");
        } else {
            char name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN] = {};
            if (row.matchedTarget < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS) {
                CopyFixedName(g_shared->targets[row.matchedTarget].name,
                              sizeof(g_shared->targets[row.matchedTarget].name),
                              name, sizeof(name));
            }
            fprintf(f, "\"%s\"", name);
        }
        fprintf(f, ",\"sizeMatchedTarget\":%s,\"ilHash\":\"",
                row.isTargetCandidate ? "true" : "false");
        WriteHex(f, row.ilHash, 32);
        fprintf(f, "\"}\n");
    }

    if (g_shared->logOverflow > 0) {
        fprintf(f, "{\"kind\":\"ring-overflow\",\"ring\":\"log\",\"lost\":%u}\n",
                g_shared->logOverflow);
    }
    const uint32_t logWritten = g_shared->logWrite;
    const uint32_t logFirst = (logWritten > DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES)
        ? logWritten - DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES + 1 : 1;
    for (uint32_t seq = logFirst; seq <= logWritten; ++seq) {
        const DrelayLogLine& line = g_shared->log[(seq - 1) % DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES];
        // The text is escaped rather than trusted: a log line can contain a quote
        // (a path, an exception message) and an unescaped one breaks every
        // consumer of the file.
        fprintf(f, "{\"kind\":\"log\",\"seq\":%u,\"level\":%u,\"text\":\"", seq, line.level);
        for (size_t c = 0; c < DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN && line.text[c] != '\0'; ++c) {
            const unsigned char ch = static_cast<unsigned char>(line.text[c]);
            switch (ch) {
                case '"':  fputs("\\\"", f); break;
                case '\\': fputs("\\\\", f); break;
                case '\n': fputs("\\n", f);  break;
                case '\r': break;
                case '\t': fputs("\\t", f);  break;
                default:
                    if (ch < 0x20) {
                        fprintf(f, "\\u%04X", ch);
                    } else {
                        fputc(ch, f);
                    }
                    break;
            }
        }
        fprintf(f, "\"}\n");
    }
}

} // namespace

void DrelayWriteEvidence(const wchar_t* runDir) {
    if (runDir == nullptr || runDir[0] == L'\0' || g_shared == nullptr) {
        return;
    }

    if (FILE* f = OpenIn(runDir, L"summary.txt")) {
        WriteSummary(f);
        fclose(f);
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "wrote summary.txt");
    } else {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "could not write summary.txt");
    }

    if (FILE* f = OpenIn(runDir, L"offsets.csv")) {
        WriteOffsetsCsv(f);
        fclose(f);
    } else {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "could not write offsets.csv");
    }

    if (FILE* f = OpenIn(runDir, L"frames.csv")) {
        WriteFramesCsv(f);
        fclose(f);
    } else {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "could not write frames.csv");
    }

    if (FILE* f = OpenIn(runDir, L"events.jsonl")) {
        WriteEventsJsonl(f);
        fclose(f);
```
