```cpp
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "wrote events.jsonl (%u trace row(s), %u log line(s))",
              g_shared->traceWrite, g_shared->logWrite);
    } else {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "could not write events.jsonl");
    }
}

} // namespace drelay

```

`hook/native/DrelayEvidence.h`:

```h
// DrelayEvidence.h -- draining the shared block to files at the end of a run.
//
// WHY THE EVIDENCE IS IN RINGS AND NOT IN FILES
// --------------------------------------------
// The native side writes from three places that must not block and must not
// allocate: the JIT callback, the frame-tick detour, and the watcher.  A file
// handle in any of them is a way to make the game stutter.  So the events go into
// fixed-size rings inside the shared block, and this module drains them once, at
// the end, from the watcher thread -- which is not in anyone's frame.
//
// The drain is also the place where "the ring overflowed" has to be said out
// loud.  A ring loses its oldest rows when it wraps, and a reader who is not told
// will read a partial trace as a complete one.  Every file this module writes
// carries its own overflow count, and a non-zero one is written as a first line
// rather than as a field at the end.

#ifndef DRELAY_EVIDENCE_H
#define DRELAY_EVIDENCE_H

#include "DrelayHookShared.h"

#include <windows.h>

namespace drelay {

// Writes the whole of a run's evidence into `runDir`:
//
//   events.jsonl   one JSON object per trace row, plus one per log line, in
//                  sequence order -- the machine-readable form
//   summary.txt    the human-readable form: target table, offsets, counters
//   offsets.csv    both offset sources side by side with their agreement
//   frames.csv     the frame-tick sample, with the per-call cost
//
// Called once, after the live checks, so the counters it reports are final.
void DrelayWriteEvidence(const wchar_t* runDir);

} // namespace drelay

#endif // DRELAY_EVIDENCE_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayFrame.cpp`:

```cpp
// DrelayFrame.cpp -- patching the targets, and Spike 1.3's live sample.
//
// WHY THE PATCHES ARE APPLIED HERE AND NOT IN THE JIT CALLBACK
// -----------------------------------------------------------
// The EE copies the JIT's writable output into executable memory after
// compileMethod returns, so the `nativeEntry` the detour captured is the address
// we *expect* to execute but is not guaranteed to be the address that will
// (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.4).  Two consequences follow, and both are
// design decisions rather than caution:
//
//   * patching from inside compileMethod would be a write to code the JIT is
//     still finishing, under the JIT's own lock, on whichever thread happened to
//     compile the method;
//   * so the address is *queued* and applied later, by one thread, in one pass,
//     after the process is past startup.
//
// That also gives the spike its stability test for free: the address we captured
// is recorded in the shared block, and if the address we patch differs from it,
// the "nativeEntry is the executing address" assumption is wrong and the log
// says so -- which is exactly the third unverified assumption Spike 1.2 exists
// to settle.

#include "DrelayFrame.h"
#include "DrelayGlobals.h"
#include "DrelayInstall.h"
#include "DrelayLog.h"

#include <MinHook.h>

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

// `std::isfinite` for the helper's argument check: the native side and the managed
// side must agree on what "a sane float" means, because a disagreement shows up as a
// mismatch and would be read as a broken ABI.
#include <cmath>

namespace drelay {

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kMaxPatched = DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS;

struct PatchRecord {
    char     name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN];
    void*    target = nullptr;      // the address the JIT reported
    void*    trampoline = nullptr;  // MinHook's passthrough
    uint8_t* original = nullptr;    // first bytes, captured before the patch
    uint32_t originalLen = 0;
    bool     enabled = false;
};

PatchRecord g_patches[kMaxPatched] = {};
uint32_t    g_patchRecords = 0;

// MinHook hands back a trampoline whose type depends on the target's signature,
// so each signature keeps its own typed pointer rather than one `void*` that
// every detour would have to reinterpret.  One typed slot per detour body is the
// whole cost of not having a cast that is wrong in a way the compiler cannot see.
//
// THE FIRST PARAMETER IS `this`, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL.
//
// `DarzaWindow.Update` is an INSTANCE method with one float parameter, so on Win64
// the callee receives `this` in RCX and `total` in XMM0.  The detour and the
// trampoline were both declared `void(float)`, which reads XMM0 correctly and drops
// RCX on the floor -- and because the trampoline is the method's own prologue
// followed by a jump back into its body, that body then runs with whatever RCX the
// detour happened to leave behind.
//
// Measured, twice, on two builds and two pids: the process dies at exactly
// `nativeEntry + 0xB7` with `ACCESS_VIOLATION, read of 0x3F` -- a fixed offset and
// a fixed bogus base of zero, which is a deterministic wrong `this` and not a torn
// instruction.  It is the same class of defect as section 10's
// `getVersionIdentifier`: a hook whose declared signature does not match the
// callee's ABI.  Carrying `this` explicitly is what makes the trampoline call the
// real method with the real receiver.
typedef void (__cdecl *FrameTickFn)(void* self, float total);
FrameTickFn g_frameTickTrampoline = nullptr;
int g_frameFirstTickSummaryDone = 0;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE FRAME READ PATH, AND WHY IT IS NATIVE.
//
// THE DETOUR USED TO CALL MANAGED CODE, AND THE RUNTIME KILLS THE PROCESS FOR IT.
// An `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` managed callback was called from here through its
// reverse-P/Invoke transition stub.  That is refused, deliberately and at a fixed
// address: the frame thread is INSIDE managed code when the detour intercepts it --
// between the managed caller of `DarzaWindow.Update` and its body -- so it is
// already in cooperative GC mode with live managed frames below the detour, while a
// reverse P/Invoke asserts that its caller is unmanaged.  coreclr's
// `JIT_ReversePInvokeEnterRare` therefore calls `ReversePInvokeBadTransition`, which
// fail-fasts with `COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE` (0x80131506) via `TerminateProcess` -- no
// exception an in-process handler can see, and no managed body ever entered.
// Measured on six dumps across three builds: `coreclr+0x244839` every time, with
// `FrameTickDetour` on the faulting stack and the game's own `DarzasDominion.dll`
// frame below it.
//
// So the read is done here, natively, and it is SAFE FOR THE REASON THE CALLBACK WAS
// SUPPOSED TO BE: this thread is in cooperative GC mode, so it cannot be suspended
// mid-read and the GC cannot move the objects the read walks.  It is also the same
// read the arming cross-check performs as its production path, so the path that is
// exercised against a live world is the path that runs every frame.
//
// THE TWO GUARDS ARE NOT OPTIONAL, and they are the whole reason a wrong offset
// costs a counted failure instead of a wild read:
//
//   * the object at `World + playerOffset` must carry the `Player` MethodTable the
//     bootstrap published, masked because the low three bits are GC mark bits;
//   * both coordinates must pass the plausibility bound, which catches a wrong
//     offset that still lands inside a real object, where the type check cannot help.
//
// Nothing here allocates, locks, formats or throws.  The one thing it can do that a
// managed read could not is fault, so it runs inside a `__try`: a mistake costs a
// reading, not the game.

struct FrameReadInputs {
    uintptr_t worldSharedStaticAddress = 0;  // `World.Shared`, taken as an address
    uint32_t  worldPlayerOffset = 0;         // `World.Player`, an instance offset
    uint32_t  playerPositionOffset = 0;      // `Player.Position`, an instance offset
    uintptr_t playerTypeHandle = 0;          // the `Player` MethodTable
    bool      attempted = false;             // resolution has been tried, once
    bool      ready = false;                 // all four above are real
};

FrameReadInputs g_frameRead = {};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE MANAGED FRAME HELPER -- Phase 2's mechanism test.
//
// THE DETOUR ALREADY CALLS MANAGED CODE, AND THE COMMENT ABOVE IS ABOUT A DIFFERENT
// THING.  What was refused was the `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` TRANSITION STUB -- a
// reverse P/Invoke.  What the detour has done on every frame since is call
// `g_frameTickTrampoline`, which is the target's own prologue followed by a `jmp`
// into its JIT-compiled body: a plain call into managed code from this thread, which
// coreclr accepts.  Measured at 209 897 calls in one hour, across the collections the
// game's own log records, with no fault.
//
// So the question Phase 2 has to answer is narrower, and it is the one this code
// exists to ask: is a helper of OURS -- one that allocates, and therefore triggers
// collections while it is on the stack -- safe on this thread?  The hypothesis is
// PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 3: when the GC walks that stack it finds the helper's JIT
// information from its IP, unwinds to a return address that belongs to no managed
// code range, finds no transition frame there, and stops -- leaving every managed
// frame *outside* this detour unscanned.  The synthetic host's cadence loop holds an
// object that only its own caller frame references, and reports whether it survived.
//
// IT IS OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS NOT CAUTION FOR ITS OWN SAKE.  The helper
// allocates 64 KB per frame on purpose; leaving it on would put that on the game's
// frame budget for a measurement the game does not need.  `DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_HELPER=1`
// -- set by the launcher's `--frame-helper` -- is the only thing that turns it on.
//
// THE SIGNATURE IS ALL-PRIMITIVE AND OURS.  `int32 (int64, float)` is the platform
// convention on x64, so the managed side and this side agree without either decoding a
// game method's signature out of metadata -- which is the ABI hazard that has cost
// this project three faults.  The helper is NOT `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]`; the
// bootstrap refuses to publish one that is, because that would be the refused route.
typedef int32_t (__cdecl *FrameHelperFn)(int64_t frameIndex, float total);

FrameHelperFn g_frameHelper = nullptr;
bool      g_frameHelperEnabled = false;
bool      g_frameHelperEnabledResolved = false;
bool      g_frameHelperResolved = false;
uint64_t  g_frameHelperCalls = 0;
uint64_t  g_frameHelperMismatches = 0;
uint32_t  g_frameHelperFaults = 0;

bool ReadFrameHelperEnabled() {
    if (g_frameHelperEnabledResolved) {
        return g_frameHelperEnabled;
    }
    g_frameHelperEnabledResolved = true;
    char value[8] = {};
    g_frameHelperEnabled =
        GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_HELPER", value, sizeof(value)) != 0 &&
        value[0] == '1';
    return g_frameHelperEnabled;
}

// Phase 2's other mechanism test: patch `frameTick` with a managed replacement instead
// of with this file's detour.  A plain `DRELAY_` name would not do -- the launcher
// deletes inherited `DRELAY_HOOK_*` and sets its own, which is what makes an
// operator's shell unable to change the patch -- so this is read the same way the
// helper switch is, from a name the launcher owns.
bool ReadFrameReplacementEnabled() {
    static int resolved = -1;
    static bool enabled = false;
    if (resolved >= 0) {
        return enabled;
    }
    resolved = 1;
    char value[8] = {};
    enabled = GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", value, sizeof(value)) != 0 &&
              value[0] == '1';
    return enabled;
}

// Phase 3 spike 3.1's actuator switch.  `DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT` is set by the
// launcher's `--move-steer`, i.e. it lives in the namespace an inherited shell variable
// cannot reach -- which matters more here than anywhere else in this file, because this
// is the one switch that moves the player.  The *value* (`DRELAY_MOVE_STEER`) is read by
// the managed side, which is where the behaviour lives; this flag's only job is to
// decide whether MinHook's `jmp` lands in managed code at all.
bool ReadMovementReplacementEnabled() {
    static int resolved = -1;
    static bool enabled = false;
    if (resolved >= 0) {
        return enabled;
    }
    resolved = 1;
    char value[8] = {};
    enabled = GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT", value, sizeof(value)) != 0 &&
              value[0] == '1';
    return enabled;
}

// The auto-aim module's switch.  `DRELAY_HOOK_AIM_REPLACEMENT` is set by the launcher's
// `--autoaim`, so it is in the namespace an inherited shell variable cannot reach.  The
// *value* (`DRELAY_AIM_MODE`) is read by the managed side, which is where the selection
// lives; this flag's only job is to decide whether MinHook's `jmp` lands in managed code.
//
// IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIED TO `DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT`.  The collision
// replacement is, because it observes the sensor that the frame replacement calls -- but
// the aim replacement shares nothing with the frame path: it is driven by the game's own
// `AimbotSystem.UpdateTarget`, it reads the world through its own accessors, and it must
// work on a run where the frame tick is patched natively or not at all.  Tying the two
// would make `--autoaim` silently do nothing whenever the frame replacement was off.
bool ReadAimReplacementEnabled() {
    static int resolved = -1;
    static bool enabled = false;
    if (resolved >= 0) {
        return enabled;
    }
    resolved = 1;
    char value[8] = {};
    enabled = GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_AIM_REPLACEMENT", value, sizeof(value)) != 0 &&
              value[0] == '1';
    return enabled;
}

void ResolveFrameHelperInputs() {    g_frameHelperResolved = true;
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    const uint64_t published = g_shared->managedFrameHelper;
    if (published == 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the frame helper is enabled but the bootstrap published no address; "
                          "no managed code will be called from the frame detour");
        return;
    }
    g_frameHelper = reinterpret_cast<FrameHelperFn>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(published));
    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "managed frame helper published at %p; the frame detour will call it "
                      "every frame (this is Phase 2's mechanism test)",
          reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(published)));
}

// A fault inside the helper must cost a frame, not the game, exactly as the native
// read does.  The `__try` is here rather than around the whole detour so that the
// trampoline call and the ring store stay outside it -- a mistake in this call is the
// only thing that should be caught.
int32_t FrameHelperCallGuarded(int64_t frameIndex, float total) {
    __try {
        return g_frameHelper(frameIndex, total);
    } __except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) {
        g_frameHelperFaults += 1;
        static unsigned int once = 0;
        DrLogOnce(&once, DRLOG_ERR, "the managed frame helper raised; the frame continued");
        return 0;
    }
}


// One entry of the bootstrap's offset table, by name prefix.  A static field's pair
// is an ADDRESS, split across `managedStaticBase` (high) and `managedOffset` (low);
// an instance field's pair is an ordinary offset.  See DrelayFieldOffset.
bool ReadPublishedOffset(const char* name, uint64_t* value) {
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return false;
    }
    const size_t wanted = strlen(name);
    const uint32_t count = g_shared->offsetCount;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count && i < DRELAY_MAX_READS; ++i) {
        const DrelayFieldOffset& o = g_shared->offsets[i];
        if (o.managedValid == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        // A PREFIX COMPARISON, because the published name carries its provenance:
        // the static field is `World.Shared (static address)`, so that a reader of
        // `offsets.csv` can see which of the two encodings applies without having to
        // consult `is_static` first.
        if (strncmp(o.name, name, wanted) != 0) {
            continue;
        }
        *value = (static_cast<uint64_t>(o.managedStaticBase) << 32) | o.managedOffset;
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// Resolved once, on the first frame that finds the gate open, and never re-read:
// the offsets and the type identity are properties of the BUILD.  The WORLD is not,
// which is why the static field is re-dereferenced on every frame (rule 1: never
// cache a raw object pointer across anything).
bool ResolveFrameReadInputs() {
    uint64_t worldAddress = 0;
    uint64_t playerOffset = 0;
    uint64_t positionOffset = 0;

    if (!ReadPublishedOffset("World.Shared", &worldAddress) ||
        !ReadPublishedOffset("World.Player", &playerOffset) ||
        !ReadPublishedOffset("Player.Position", &positionOffset) ||
        g_shared->managedPlayerTypeHandle == 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "the frame read path cannot resolve its inputs (World.Shared, World.Player, "
                         "Player.Position, or the Player MethodTable is unpublished), so it will not "
                         "read anything");
        DrLogFlushNow();
        return false;
    }

    g_frameRead.worldSharedStaticAddress = static_cast<uintptr_t>(worldAddress);
    g_frameRead.worldPlayerOffset = static_cast<uint32_t>(playerOffset);
    g_frameRead.playerPositionOffset = static_cast<uint32_t>(positionOffset);
    g_frameRead.playerTypeHandle = static_cast<uintptr_t>(g_shared->managedPlayerTypeHandle);
    g_frameRead.ready = true;
    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "frame read path armed: World.Shared @ %p, World.Player +%u, Player.Position "
                      "+%u, Player MethodTable %p",
          reinterpret_cast<void*>(g_frameRead.worldSharedStaticAddress),
          g_frameRead.worldPlayerOffset, g_frameRead.playerPositionOffset,
          reinterpret_cast<void*>(g_frameRead.playerTypeHandle));
    DrLogFlushNow();
    return true;
}

// The `Player` MethodTable comparison, with the GC's mark bits masked off.
bool IsInstanceOfNative(uintptr_t reference, uintptr_t expectedTypeHandle) {
    if (reference == 0 || expectedTypeHandle == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    const uintptr_t methodTable = *reinterpret_cast<const uintptr_t*>(reference);
    if (methodTable == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    return (methodTable & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(0x7)) == expectedTypeHandle;
}

// The two coordinates are tile indices and the client's own grid is a few hundred
// tiles a side.  Deliberately loose: it exists to reject a misread pointer, not to
// validate gameplay, and a bound tight enough to matter would reject a legitimate
// teleport or a large map.
//
// THE RANGE TEST IS ALSO THE NaN AND INFINITY TEST, which is why there is no
// `isnan`/`isinf` here: every comparison against NaN is false, so a NaN fails both
// bounds, and +/-infinity fails one of them.  This still mirrors the managed
// `IsPlausibleCoordinate` it replaces -- the cross-check and the frame read must
// agree about what "plausible" means, or the production path would be reading
// through values the check never approved.
bool IsPlausibleCoordinate(float value) {
    return value > -100000.0f && value < 100000.0f;
}

void NativeFrameRead() {
    const uintptr_t world =
        *reinterpret_cast<const uintptr_t*>(g_frameRead.worldSharedStaticAddress);
    if (world == 0) {
        return;
    }

    const uintptr_t player =
        *reinterpret_cast<const uintptr_t*>(world + g_frameRead.worldPlayerOffset);
    if (!IsInstanceOfNative(player, g_frameRead.playerTypeHandle)) {
        g_shared->managedReadFailures = g_shared->managedReadFailures + 1;
        return;
    }

    const float* position =
        reinterpret_cast<const float*>(player + g_frameRead.playerPositionOffset);
    const float x = position[0];
    const float y = position[1];

    if (IsPlausibleCoordinate(x) && IsPlausibleCoordinate(y)) {
        g_shared->managedReadValue = x;
        g_shared->managedReadValid = 1;
        g_shared->managedReadCount = g_shared->managedReadCount + 1;
    } else {
        g_shared->managedReadFailures = g_shared->managedReadFailures + 1;
    }
}

// A `__try` OF ITS OWN, AND NOT BECAUSE THE READ IS EXPECTED TO FAULT.
//
// The read dereferences three pointers that belong to a running game, and the one
// thing a native read can do that a managed read could not is fault: a scene change
// that nulls `World.Shared` between the load and the dereference is a torn read, not
// a wrong number.  SEH belongs around exactly that and nothing else, which also
// keeps `FrameTickDetour` itself free of it -- MinHook's trampoline call, the QPC
// reads and the ring store have no business inside a `__try`.
void NativeFrameReadGuarded() {
    __try {
        NativeFrameRead();
    } __except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) {
        // Counted, not logged per occurrence: a faulting read would otherwise
        // write 60 log lines a second into a ring of 256.
        g_frameReadFailures.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        g_shared->managedReadFailures = g_shared->managedReadFailures + 1;
        static unsigned int once = 0;
        DrLogOnce(&once, DRLOG_ERR, "the native frame read raised; the frame continued");
    }
}

// The frame-tick detour.  It is deliberately tiny: a QPC read, a counter, the read
// above when the gate is open, and a store into the ring.  No allocation, no locks,
// no formatting, and no call into managed code -- everything that would cost frame
// time is deferred to the flusher.
//
// It CALLS THE TRAMPOLINE FIRST AND UNCONDITIONALLY.  "Observing only" means
// observing the real method, not replacing it: a detour that returned without
// calling through would silently disable the game's own frame update, which is
// the single most destructive thing this whole file could do.  The trampoline is
// MinHook's copy of the overwritten prologue followed by a jump back into the
// original body, so calling it runs the real method exactly once.
//
// The `float total` argument is DarzaWindow::Update's frame delta.  It is used as
// a liveness signal on its own: a plausible ~1/60 s value, once per frame, is
// evidence that the detour is entering the real method and not, say, a
// same-shaped function that happened to be next in memory.
//
// `self` is the receiver and must be forwarded unchanged -- see the note on
// FrameTickFn.  It is not used for the read either: `World.Shared` is a STATIC
// field, so the read path reaches the world without it, which is why the read can
// live here rather than needing the receiver to be managed again.
void __cdecl FrameTickDetour(void* self, float total) {
    if (g_framePaused.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != 0) {
        if (g_frameTickTrampoline != nullptr) {
            g_frameTickTrampoline(self, total);
        }
        return;
    }

    LARGE_INTEGER t0 = {};
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&t0);

    const uint64_t calls = g_frameCalls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1;
    if (g_frameFirstTick == 0) {
        g_frameFirstTick = GetTickCount();
    }

    const bool sampling = (g_shared->cfgFlags & DRELAY_CFG_FRAME_SAMPLE) != 0;

    // PUBLISHED BEFORE THE READ, AND THAT ORDER IS ITSELF A FIX.
    //
    // This counter used to be written after the read -- after the managed call that
    // used to be here -- so every failure inside the read reported `frame calls: 0`,
    // which reads as "the detour never ran".  In the run that produced this fix the
    // detour had been running for about a second before it died, and the block said
    // zero.  An instrument whose blind spot is exactly the failure it is consulted
    // about is the defect PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 8 is about.
    if (sampling) {
        g_shared->frameCalls = static_cast<uint32_t>(calls);
    }

    // THE GATE, READ FROM THE BLOCK THE ARMING PROBE PUBLISHES.
    //
    // The detour is entered from the first frame after the target is patched.  Until
    // the probe has cross-checked the measured offsets against a live world, walking
    // the pointer chain could dereference a null `World.Shared`, so the read stays
    // closed and the entry is counted instead.
    if (g_shared->managedArmState == DRELAY_ARM_ARMED) {
        if (!g_frameRead.attempted) {
            g_frameRead.attempted = true;
            ResolveFrameReadInputs();
        }
        if (g_frameRead.ready) {
            NativeFrameReadGuarded();
        }
    } else {
        g_shared->managedFrameWaits = g_shared->managedFrameWaits + 1;
    }

    // THE MECHANISM TEST, WHEN IT IS ASKED FOR.  It is deliberately NOT inside the
    // arming gate: the question is whether managed code can run here at all, and a
    // run whose world never appears would otherwise say nothing about it.
    if (ReadFrameHelperEnabled()) {
        if (!g_frameHelperResolved) {
            ResolveFrameHelperInputs();
        }
        if (g_frameHelper != nullptr) {
            const int64_t index = static_cast<int64_t>(calls);
            const int32_t returned = FrameHelperCallGuarded(index, total);

            // The helper returns a value this side can predict from the arguments it
            // passed, so a correct return proves the ARGUMENTS crossed the boundary --
            // not merely that some call happened.  The sign carries the managed side's
            // own verdict on the float it received, so a NaN or a negative argument is
            // reported as a mismatch rather than as a plausible-looking number.
            const bool sane = std::isfinite(total) && total >= 0.0f;
            const int64_t mixed = (index ^ 0x5A5A5A5ALL) & 0x7FFFFFFFLL;
            const int32_t expected = sane ? static_cast<int32_t>(mixed)
                                          : -static_cast<int32_t>(mixed);
            g_frameHelperCalls += 1;
            if (returned != expected) {
                g_frameHelperMismatches += 1;
                static unsigned int mismatchOnce = 0;
                DrLogOnce(&mismatchOnce, DRLOG_ERR,
                          "the managed frame helper returned a value this side did not predict "
                          "from the arguments it passed -- the arguments did not survive the "
                          "boundary");
            }
            if (g_frameHelperCalls == 1) {
                DrLog(DRLOG_INFO,
                      "frame helper entered: frameIndex %lld, total %.4f, returned %d (expected %d)",
                      static_cast<long long>(index), static_cast<double>(total),
                      static_cast<int>(returned), static_cast<int>(expected));
            } else if ((g_frameHelperCalls % 256) == 0) {
                DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "frame helper: %llu call(s), %llu mismatch(es), %u native fault(s)",
                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_frameHelperCalls),
                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_frameHelperMismatches),
                      g_frameHelperFaults);
            }
        }
    }

    LARGE_INTEGER freq = {};
    LARGE_INTEGER t1 = {};
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&t1);
    QueryPerformanceFrequency(&freq);
    const uint32_t us = (freq.QuadPart > 0)
        ? static_cast<uint32_t>(((t1.QuadPart - t0.QuadPart) * 1000000) / freq.QuadPart)
        : 0;

    // Rolling maximum, so one hitch is not averaged out of existence.
    uint32_t best = g_frameMaxUs.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    while (us > best && !g_frameMaxUs.compare_exchange_weak(best, us)) {
    }

    if (sampling) {
        const uint32_t slot = g_shared->frameWrite % DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS;
        DrelayFrameRow* row = &g_shared->frames[slot];
        row->argTotal = total;
        row->elapsedUs = us;
        row->qpc = static_cast<uint64_t>(t0.QuadPart);
        row->readFailures = g_shared->managedReadFailures;
        row->readOk = g_shared->managedReadValid;
        row->value = static_cast<float>(g_shared->managedReadValue);
        row->seq = g_shared->frameWrite + 1;
        if (g_shared->frameWrite >= DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS) {
            g_shared->frameOverflow = g_shared->frameOverflow + 1;
        }
        g_shared->frameWrite = g_shared->frameWrite + 1;
    }

    // Observation is finished; now let the game's own update run.  Last, so the
    // measurement is of our overhead and not of the game's frame.  `self` goes back
    // in RCX exactly as the callee expects it.
    if (g_frameTickTrampoline != nullptr) {
        g_frameTickTrampoline(self, total);
    }

    // One summary line per run, after enough frames that the numbers mean
    // something.  The argument is `TotalGameTime.TotalMilliseconds`, so the evidence
    // that this is really DarzaWindow::Update is the *increment* between calls --
    // ~16.7 ms at 60 Hz -- and not the raw value, which is a running total and was
    // previously printed as though it were a per-frame delta in seconds.
    static float lastTotal = 0.0f;
    if (calls == 120) {
        const float deltaMs = (lastTotal > 0.0f) ? (total - lastTotal) : 0.0f;
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO,
              "frame tick at call 120: argTotal=%.1f ms, frame delta=%.3f ms (%.1f Hz), "
              "worst call so far %u us, frame reads %u ok / %u failed",
              total, deltaMs, (deltaMs > 0.0f) ? (1000.0f / deltaMs) : 0.0f,
              g_frameMaxUs.load(),
              g_shared->managedReadCount, g_shared->managedReadFailures);
        g_frameFirstTickSummaryDone = 1;
    }

    // One line for the helper's own accounting, at the same point in the run and for
    // the same reason: "it was enabled" and "it ran" are different claims, and this is
    // the one that says which happened.
    if (calls == 120 && ReadFrameHelperEnabled()) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO,
              "frame helper accounting at call 120: %llu call(s), %llu mismatch(es), %u native fault(s), "
              "address %p",
              static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_frameHelperCalls),
              static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_frameHelperMismatches),
              g_frameHelperFaults, reinterpret_cast<void*>(g_frameHelper));
    }
    lastTotal = total;
}

} // namespace

bool DrelayDetoursInit() {
    const MH_STATUS st = MH_Initialize();
    if (st != MH_OK && st != MH_ERROR_ALREADY_INITIALIZED) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "MH_Initialize returned %d", static_cast<int>(st));
        return false;
    }
    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "MinHook initialised");
    return true;
}

void DrelayDetoursUninit() {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_patchRecords; ++i) {
        if (g_patches[i].enabled && g_patches[i].target != nullptr) {
            MH_DisableHook(g_patches[i].target);
        }
    }
    if (g_patchRecords > 0) {
        MH_Uninitialize();
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "MinHook uninitialised (%u patch(es) disabled)", g_patchRecords);
    }
}

// The record for an address, or nullptr when it has not been patched.  This is what
// makes a second pass safe: a target that is already hooked is skipped rather than
// hooked twice, and the record list the uninstall walks is left intact.
static PatchRecord* FindPatch(void* target) {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_patchRecords; ++i) {
        if (g_patches[i].target == target) {
            return &g_patches[i];
        }
    }
    return nullptr;
}

// ONE PATCH PASS.  `initialPass` selects the pass at the close of the discovery window
// -- the one that polls the arming probe and prints the "patching may go live" line --
// from a later pass, which must leave the record list alone.  Everything else is shared
// deliberately: the detour selection, the trampoline publication that has to precede
// the enable, and the enable itself are the parts that must not differ between a patch
// at t+5 s and one at t+55 s.

// HOW LONG A TARGET WAITS BETWEEN BEING MATCHED AND BEING HOOKED.
//
// THE TWO HALVES OF A JIT COMPILATION HAPPEN IN THIS ORDER, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON
// THIS NUMBER EXISTS.  `PublishMatch` runs inside `compileMethod`, before that call
// returns; the execution engine copies the JIT's finished code into the address the
// target will actually execute at *after* the return (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.4).
// A `jmp` written into that address before the copy lands is overwritten by the method
// body, and the hook then silently never fires -- the worst failure available here,
// because the run afterwards looks exactly like one where the game never called the
// method at all.
//
// THE OLD DESIGN COVERED THIS BY ACCIDENT.  Nothing was patched until the discovery
// window closed, which put at least thirty seconds between a match and its patch.  Now
// that a target is hooked as soon as it is found, the interval has to be stated instead
// of inherited: 500 ms against two things it must beat -- the copy, which happens
// microseconds after the compile returns, and the 250 ms poll cadence that observes the
// match in the first place.
constexpr DWORD kTargetSettleMs = 500;

// When each target index was first observed as found, and whether it has been observed
// at all.  Indexed by the shared table's own index rather than by patch order, so a
// target that appears after a session has started gets its own settle interval -- which
// is the case that matters, because a late compile is exactly when a premature patch
// would be overwritten by a copy that has not happened yet.
bool   g_pendingSeen[DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS] = {};
DWORD  g_pendingTick[DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS] = {};

static uint32_t PatchTargetsPass(bool initialPass) {
    uint32_t patched = 0;

    // THE FRAME READ PATH NEEDS NOTHING PREPARED BEFORE A PATCH GOES LIVE, AND THAT
    // IS THE POINT OF THIS ROUND RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
    //
    // Enabling a hook on `DarzaWindow.Update` makes the very next frame reach
    // `FrameTickDetour`.  The read it performs is native, guarded by the offset table
    // and the `Player` MethodTable that the resolve callback published seconds
    // earlier, and its gate is a field the arming probe writes.  So there is no
    // compiled code to pre-warm, no address to publish first, and no ordering between
    // the probe's cadence and this loop that anything depends on.  The previous round
    // needed both a pre-compile and an explicit probe call here because the detour
    // called managed code; the detour does not any more.
    //
    // The probe is still called, and still worth calling: it is what publishes the
    // arm-state transition, so running it here means the first frames after the patch
    // see the freshest verdict rather than one up to a poll interval old.
    if (initialPass) {
        DrelayPollArmProbe();
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "the frame read is native and needs no managed entry point; patching may "
                          "go live");
        DrLogFlushNow();
    }

    // A diagnostic switch, and it exists because it is the only cheap way to tell
    // two very different failures apart.  With `DRELAY_NO_PATCH=1` the JIT detour
    // is installed exactly as normal but no target is patched, so a crash that
    // persists is in the detour and a crash that disappears was in the patch.
    // Without this the two are indistinguishable from a log that simply stops.
    //
    // IT IS `DRELAY_NO_PATCH`, NOT `DRELAY_HOOK_NO_PATCH`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
    // POINT.  The launcher builds the child's environment by deleting every
    // variable whose name begins with `DRELAY_HOOK_`, so this switch was
    // UNREACHABLE through the only supported way to start the game: setting it in
    // the operator's shell silently did nothing, and the control that was supposed
    // to separate "the patch" from "the detour" could never run.  That is
    // PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 4 trap 1 for the third time in this project; the
    // convention is `DRELAY_*` for anything the operator sets.
    char noPatch[8] = {};
    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_NO_PATCH", noPatch, sizeof(noPatch)) != 0 && noPatch[0] == '1') {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "DRELAY_NO_PATCH=1: the JIT detour is installed but no target is "
                          "patched (diagnostic mode)");
        return 0;
    }

    // Walk the shared target table directly: it is the single record of what the
    // JIT reported and what the bootstrap pinned, so joining on it rather than on
    // a second local list keeps "which target is this" to one answer.  Discovery
    // order is not table order, so the table is walked by index and only the
    // entries marked found are patched.
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_shared->targetCount && g_patchRecords < kMaxPatched; ++i) {
        DrelayTargetHash* t = &g_shared->targets[i];
        if (t->found == 0 || t->nativeEntry == 0) {
            continue;
        }

        // ALREADY HOOKED, SO THERE IS NOTHING TO DO.  Only a second pass can find this,
        // and without it the late pass would try to re-create a hook on a live target:
        // `MH_CreateHook` refuses, the error would be logged every second, and the record
        // list the uninstall walks would be corrupted by a reset.
        if (FindPatch(reinterpret_cast<void*>(t->nativeEntry)) != nullptr) {
            continue;
        }

        // THE SETTLE INTERVAL, BEFORE ANY DETOUR IS CHOSEN OR ANY BYTE IS WRITTEN.
        // See `kTargetSettleMs` above for why a match is not yet safe to patch.  A new
        // target is *observed* here rather than patched, and the next pass -- 250 ms
        // later, from whichever loop is running -- patches it once the interval has
        // passed.  The line is logged once per target and is what explains the half
        // second between `FOUND` and `PATCHED` in a run's log.
        if (i < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS) {
            const DWORD now = GetTickCount();
            if (!g_pendingSeen[i]) {
                g_pendingSeen[i] = true;
                g_pendingTick[i] = now;
                DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "target '%s' is waiting out its %lu ms settle interval before "
                                  "it is patched", t->name,
                      static_cast<unsigned long>(kTargetSettleMs));
                continue;
            }
            if ((now - g_pendingTick[i]) < kTargetSettleMs) {
                continue;
            }
        }

        // The dispatch is by name, and a target with no detour body is reported
        // rather than guessed at.  `frameTick` is the only signature Phase 1
        // implements, because Spike 1.3 asks for exactly one target patched and
        // a wrong-shaped forwarder on a per-frame method is a way to corrupt the
        // game for no gain.
        //
        // AND `frameTick` HAS A SECOND WAY TO BE PATCHED, WHICH IS PHASE 2'S
        // MECHANISM TEST.  With `DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT=1` the destination of
        // MinHook's `jmp` is not this file at all: it is a managed method with the
        // target's own signature, so the game's `call` becomes a managed-to-managed
        // call and no native frame ever interrupts the managed stack.  See the note
        // on `managedFrameReplacement` in DrelayHookShared.h for why that was worth
        // building after the helper route measured as flaky.
        bool managedReplacement = false;
        void* detour = nullptr;
        volatile uint64_t* trampolineSlot = nullptr;
        if (strcmp(t->name, "frameTick") == 0) {
            const uint64_t replacement = (g_shared != nullptr) ? g_shared->managedFrameReplacement : 0;
            if (ReadFrameReplacementEnabled() && replacement != 0) {
                detour = reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(replacement));
                managedReplacement = true;
                trampolineSlot = &g_shared->managedFrameTrampoline;
            } else {
                detour = reinterpret_cast<void*>(&FrameTickDetour);
            }
        } else if (strcmp(t->name, "collision") == 0) {
            // `Projectile.HitCharacter` HAS NO NATIVE DETOUR BODY, and now it has a reason
            // to be patched anyway: the managed replacement is the observation point for
            // Deliverable 2.3, and there is nothing for a native body to do there -- the
            // comparison needs the projectile's fields and the sensor's own state, which
            // are managed things.
            const uint64_t replacement = (g_shared != nullptr) ? g_shared->managedCollisionReplacement : 0;
            if (ReadFrameReplacementEnabled() && replacement != 0) {
                detour = reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(replacement));
                managedReplacement = true;
                trampolineSlot = &g_shared->managedCollisionTrampoline;
            }
        } else if (strcmp(t->name, "movementIntegrator") == 0) {
            // PHASE 3'S ACTUATOR, AND IT IS OPT-IN FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT COST.  This
            // target is in the table for every run, so it is found and its IL hash is
            // verified like the others; it is only *patched* when the operator asks,
            // because a replacement here moves the player.  `DRELAY_MOVE_STEER` carries
            // the request and the heading; see `SteeringPilot` on the managed side for
            // what the modes mean.  With the variable unset the replacement is published
            // anyway and does nothing but call through, so the plumbing is exercised
            // without the game being touched.
            const uint64_t replacement = (g_shared != nullptr) ? g_shared->managedMovementReplacement : 0;
            if (ReadMovementReplacementEnabled() && replacement != 0) {
                detour = reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(replacement));
                managedReplacement = true;
                trampolineSlot = &g_shared->managedMovementTrampoline;
            }
        } else if (strcmp(t->name, "aimTarget") == 0) {
            // THE AUTO-AIM MODULE, AND IT IS OPT-IN FOR THE SAME REASON THE ACTUATOR IS.
            // The target is in the table on every run, so its IL hash is verified and a
            // game patch that moved it is reported whether or not the operator asked for
            // auto-aim; it is only *patched* when the launcher passed `--autoaim`, because
            // a replacement here decides what the player shoots at.
            //
            // THE MANAGED SIDE PUBLISHES ON EVERY RUN, so with the variable unset the
            // replacement exists but is never reached -- the plumbing (shared slot, this
            // dispatch, the trampoline handshake) is exercised by every run rather than
            // first by the run whose mistake would aim the player somewhere.
            //
            // A ZERO REPLACEMENT IS NOT AN ERROR HERE, AND THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE
            // FRAME TICK. `frameTick` is entered within milliseconds of the patch, so a
            // missing replacement would stop the game updating. `FindTarget` is entered
            // only once a world exists and the aimbot flag is set -- seconds later at the
            // earliest -- so a zero here means the bootstrap's publish failed, which the
            // bootstrap has already logged. Patching anyway would aim the game's own call
            // at address zero, so it does not: the target is simply left unpatched, and
            // the line printed below names it.
            const uint64_t replacement = (g_shared != nullptr) ? g_shared->managedAimReplacement : 0;
            if (ReadAimReplacementEnabled() && replacement != 0) {
                detour = reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(replacement));
                managedReplacement = true;
                trampolineSlot = &g_shared->managedAimTrampoline;
            }
        }
        if (detour == nullptr) {
            // ONLY THE FIRST PASS SAYS SO.  A target with no body for this phase is
            // reported once, at the window's close, where a reader is looking for it;
            // the late pass runs every second and would otherwise repeat this line for
            // the rest of the session.
            if (initialPass) {
                DrLog(DRLOG_INFO,
                      "target '%s' verified at %p and NOT patched: its detour body is Phase 2's "
                      "(this spike patches one target on purpose)", t->name,
                      reinterpret_cast<void*>(t->nativeEntry));
            }
            continue;
        }

        PatchRecord& rec = g_patches[g_patchRecords];
        memcpy(rec.name, t->name, sizeof(rec.name));
        rec.name[sizeof(rec.name) - 1] = '\0';
        rec.target = reinterpret_cast<void*>(t->nativeEntry);

        const MH_STATUS st = MH_CreateHook(rec.target, detour, &rec.trampoline);
        if (st != MH_OK) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "MH_CreateHook failed for '%s' at %p (status %d) -- not patched",
                  rec.name, rec.target, static_cast<int>(st));
            continue;
        }

        // PUBLISHED BEFORE THE HOOK IS ENABLED, AND THAT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING.  The
        // very first `call` to the target has to find a trampoline, because the
        // replacement's only way to run the original is to call it.  A replacement that
        // saw zero would have to skip the original, and skipping it does not fail
        // loudly -- it stops the game's frame update, which is the most destructive
        // thing this file could do.
        if (managedReplacement && trampolineSlot != nullptr) {
            *trampolineSlot = static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(rec.trampoline));
            DrLog(DRLOG_INFO,
                  "'%s' will be patched with the MANAGED REPLACEMENT at %p; its way back into the "
                  "original is the trampoline at %p, published before the hook is enabled",
                  rec.name, detour, rec.trampoline);
        }

        const MH_STATUS en = MH_EnableHook(rec.target);
        if (en != MH_OK && en != MH_ERROR_ENABLED) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "MH_EnableHook failed for '%s' at %p (status %d) -- not patched",
                  rec.name, rec.target, static_cast<int>(en));
            MH_RemoveHook(rec.target);
            continue;
        }

        rec.enabled = true;
        ++g_patchRecords;
        ++patched;
        // THE RUNNING TOTAL, NOT THIS PASS'S COUNT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A BUG THIS ROUND
        // FOUND.  Patching used to happen in one pass -- the one at the discovery window's
        // close -- so "how many this pass" and "how many in total" were the same number and
        // nothing distinguished them.  Now a target can be patched by the discovery loop, and
        // the pass at the window's close then patches nothing: it would have written zero over
        // a correct total, and `summary.txt` reported `0 patched` on a run whose own log said
        // `PATCHED 'frameTick'`.  `g_patchRecords` is the total by construction.
        g_shared->targetsPatched = g_patchRecords;
        if (strcmp(rec.name, "frameTick") == 0) {
            g_frameTickTrampoline = reinterpret_cast<FrameTickFn>(rec.trampoline);
        }
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "PATCHED '%s' at %p (trampoline %p)", rec.name, rec.target, rec.trampoline);
    }

    if (patched > 0) {
        g_shared->nativeStatus |= DRELAY_ST_PATCHED;
    }
    if (initialPass) {
        // THE TOTAL, WITH THIS PASS'S SHARE IN PARENTHESES.  `patched` alone would read
        // `0 of 7 target(s) patched` at the window's close on a run where the discovery loop
        // had already hooked six of them -- a line that contradicts the six PATCHED lines
        // above it.
        DrLog(patched > 0 || g_patchRecords > 0 ? DRLOG_INFO : DRLOG_ERR,
              "%u of %u target(s) patched (%u in this pass)", g_patchRecords,
              g_shared->targetCount, patched);
    }
    return patched;
}

// The pass at the close of the discovery window.  It used to own the reset of the record
// list -- "because it is the one that starts it" -- and that reset is gone, because it is
// no longer the one that starts it: `DrelayPatchTargetsDuringDiscovery` runs from the
// watcher's own discovery loop and may already have patched targets by the time this
// runs.  Clearing `g_patchRecords` then would erase the records of live hooks, and the
// next pass would try to create a hook on a target that already has one -- `MH_CreateHook`
// refuses, the refusal is logged as an error, and `DrelayDetoursUninit` would no longer
// know what to disable.  The list starts empty because it is a zero-initialised global and
// nothing else resets it, which is one writer fewer for one fewer way to be wrong.
//
// IT RETURNS THE TOTAL NOW, NOT THIS PASS'S COUNT.  `DrelayMain` publishes the return value
// as `targetsPatched`, and that is the number `summary.txt` prints; with incremental
// patching, this pass can legitimately hook nothing while six targets are already live.
uint32_t DrelayPatchTargets() {
    PatchTargetsPass(true);
    return g_patchRecords;
}

// THE PASS THE DISCOVERY LOOP RUNS, AND WHY THE HOOK IS NO LONGER IDLE UNTIL THE WINDOW
// CLOSES.
//
// THE DEFECT IT FIXES IS A LATENCY ONE AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ROUND EXISTS.  Nothing
// used to be patched until the discovery window closed -- at least thirty seconds, plus
// whatever `--collect-delay` added -- so a release run spent that whole interval
// resident and doing nothing, and the `--collect-delay` comment two files over already
// admitted that nothing was lost by looking during it.  The window's verdicts are a
// reporting question (see `ReadDiscoveryWindowMs`); being hooked is not, so the two are
// now separate: this pass runs on the watcher's 250 ms cadence from the instant the
// discovery loop starts, and `DrelayPatchTargets` at the window's close is a final sweep
// rather than the only chance.
//
// IT IS DELIBERATELY SILENT.  `DrelayPatchNewTargets`' message claims the patch happened
// after the window closed, which is true of the passes that call it and false of this
// one; the per-target `PATCHED '<name>' at <addr>` line `PatchTargetsPass` already emits
// is the evidence that matters, and a second summary line would only be a second thing to
// keep true.
uint32_t DrelayPatchTargetsDuringDiscovery() {
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return 0;
    }
    const uint32_t added = PatchTargetsPass(false);
    if (added > 0) {
        g_shared->targetsPatched = g_patchRecords;
    }
    return added;
}

// THE LATE PASS, AND THE SESSION THAT MADE IT NECESSARY.
//
// The patch decision used to be a single pass at the close of the fixed thirty-second
// discovery window, so a target the game compiled *after* that window was matched,
// reported as found by the target-size table -- and never patched.  On the
// 2026-10-12 21:22 session the operator reached `GameScene` at 21:23:10 and the window
// closed at 21:23:16, so `Projectile.HitCharacter` missed it by seconds: the run
// recorded `collisions: 0 decision(s)` with a perfectly healthy sensor around it,
// because the method was never hooked rather than because nothing collided.
//
// That is PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 6.2's defect one level down -- the window's count
// standing in for the run's -- and the fix has the same shape: keep watching, and act on
// what arrives.  The compileMethod detour is still installed and still matching, so a
// target that appears later sets `found` and this pass hooks it.
uint32_t DrelayPatchNewTargets() {
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return 0;
    }
    const uint32_t added = PatchTargetsPass(false);
    if (added > 0) {
        g_shared->targetsPatched = g_patchRecords;
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "%u target(s) that the game compiled after the discovery window closed "
                          "were patched late; %u of %u target(s) are now patched, and this run's "
                          "comparison starts from here rather than from the window",
              added, g_patchRecords, g_shared->targetCount);
        DrLogFlushNow();
    }
    return added;
}

bool DrelayIsFrameTargetPatched() {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_patchRecords; ++i) {
        if (g_patches[i].enabled && strcmp(g_patches[i].name, "frameTick") == 0) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

} // namespace drelay


```

`hook/native/DrelayFrame.h`:

```h
// DrelayFrame.h -- target patching and the live frame sample.

#ifndef DRELAY_FRAME_H
#define DRELAY_FRAME_H

#include <stdint.h>

namespace drelay {

// Creates and enables a detour for every *found* target whose signature the hook
// can forward correctly.
//
// Not every found target is patched, and that is deliberate rather than
// incomplete: a detour body must match the target's calling convention and
// parameter list exactly, and three of Phase 1's four targets (the 16-argument
// spawn, the bool-returning collision, the argument-less escape) have no Phase 1
// behaviour to run.  Installing a forwarder with the wrong shape for a method
// that is called every frame would be a way to corrupt the game in exchange for
// nothing.  The patches that *are* needed get applied; the rest are recorded as
// found-and-verified and reported as deferred by name, so "three of four detours
// never fired" can never be mistaken for silence.
uint32_t DrelayPatchTargets();

// The discovery loop's own patch pass: hooks a target a settle interval after it is first
// seen, so the hook is live seconds into a session instead of at the window's close.
//
// This is what makes "the hook is resident but does nothing for the first thirty seconds"
// impossible.  The window's own verdicts are a reporting question and still close when
// they close; being hooked is not a reporting question, and this pass does not wait for
// it.  Silent by design -- the per-target `PATCHED '<name>'` line from the shared pass is
// the evidence.
uint32_t DrelayPatchTargetsDuringDiscovery();

// Patches any target that the game compiled *after* the discovery window closed.
//
// Whether a target lands inside that window is a fact about how quickly the
// player reached the content that compiles it, not about the target:
// `Projectile.HitCharacter` is compiled the first time a projectile is fired at the
// player, so a session that spends longer in the menu than the window produces a run with
// no collision comparison at all unless this pass exists -- which is exactly what the
// 2026-10-12 21:22 session recorded, `collisions: 0 decision(s)`, with the target matched
// and reported as found but never hooked.
//
// Safe to call repeatedly: a target that is already hooked is skipped, and the record list
// the uninstall walks is left alone.
uint32_t DrelayPatchNewTargets();

// True once the frame-tick detour is live, which is what the self-check reports.
bool DrelayIsFrameTargetPatched();

bool DrelayDetoursInit();
void DrelayDetoursUninit();

} // namespace drelay

#endif // DRELAY_FRAME_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayGlobals.h`:

```h
// DrelayGlobals.h -- the process-wide state the hook keeps.
//
// There is exactly one hook per process, so this is a namespace of globals
// rather than an object graph.  It is a header rather than a .cpp because two
// translation units legitimately share every field: the JIT detour writes
// `compileCalls`/`targetsFound`, the patcher reads them, the frame hooks write
// timing, and the self-check reads all of it.

#ifndef DRELAY_GLOBALS_H
#define DRELAY_GLOBALS_H

#include "DrelayHookShared.h"
#include "DrelayJit.h"

#include <windows.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <atomic>

namespace drelay {

// Shutdown is requested from the exported `DrelayHook_Shutdown`, which runs on the
// injector's thread, and observed by the watcher.  It is an interlocked flag rather
// than an event, because the watcher can be blocked in Sleep and a flag needs no
// owner to reset.
//
// DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN FILE-STATIC IN DrelayMain.cpp, because the collection
// delay waits in slices precisely so it can notice this: a `Sleep(30000)` would make
// the operator's Ctrl+C wait out the whole delay before anything reacted to it.
extern volatile LONG g_shutdownRequested;

// The logger's sequence numbers assume a single shared block; nothing works
// without it, so it is checked once before anything else is attempted.
extern DrelayShared* g_shared;
extern HANDLE        g_mapHandle;
extern uint32_t      g_sessionId;
extern wchar_t       g_runDir[MAX_PATH];
extern wchar_t       g_gameDir[MAX_PATH];
extern wchar_t       g_assemblyPath[MAX_PATH];

// The JIT detour's own state.  `realCompileMethod` is the address the vtable
// slot held before we replaced it -- calling anything else here would be the
// classic recursion-into-ourselves bug.
extern DrelayICorJitCompilerVtbl* g_realCompiler;
extern void*                      g_jitObject;
extern void**                     g_jitVtable;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_compileCalls;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_compileFailed;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_targetsFound;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_patchCount;

// HOW MANY TIMES THE DETOUR WAS ENTERED, VERSUS HOW MANY OF THOSE IT ACTUALLY
// LOOKED AT, AND WHY THOSE ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS.
//
// `g_compileCalls` counts only the entries that got past the re-entrancy guard, so
// it measures the hook's *instrumentation*, not the compilation stream.  Every
// conclusion in PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 11 -- "the game must JIT the frame tick,
// the hook sees ~3,690 compilations, therefore the frame tick never reached the
// JIT" -- silently assumes those two are the same number.  If the guard ever
// discards an entry, the method compiled and the hook has no record of it, and
// that is indistinguishable from the method never compiling.
//
// `g_detourInvocations` is incremented at the top of the detour, BEFORE the guard.
// `g_reentrantSkips` is incremented on the guard's early-return path.  A run in
// which `invocations - calls` is non-trivial has an instrument problem, not a
// coverage problem, and the per-target verdicts from that run must not be read as
// facts about the game.
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_detourInvocations;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t>      g_reentrantSkips;

// Set once the detour is installed and the discovery window has closed; the
// patcher waits on it, so no patch can be applied from inside a JIT callback.
extern HANDLE        g_discoveryDoneEvent;
extern std::atomic<int> g_discoveryClosed;

// The MVID read from the assembly file on disk, and whether that read succeeded.
//
// DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN FILE-STATIC IN DrelayInstall.cpp, BECAUSE THE SELF-CHECK
// IS THE THING THAT HAS TO REPORT IT.  The claim that matters most in this phase is
// the *comparison* between this value and the MVID the runtime reports for the
// assembly it actually loaded -- "the file is the pinned build" is Phase 0's gate,
// and "the loaded assembly is that file" is this one.  That comparison was made and
// only counted: it adjusted the report totals and wrote a log line, so a reader of
// `selfcheck.txt` alone could not see the result at all, and a refusal left a
// failure count with no line explaining it.  The values now live where the
// self-check can print them.
extern uint8_t g_fileMvid[16];
extern bool    g_fileMvidRead;

// THE MANAGED FRAME CALLBACK IS GONE, AND THIS COMMENT IS THE RECORD OF WHY.
//
// It used to be a `[UnmanagedCallersOnly(CallConvs = [typeof(CallConvCdecl)])]`
// managed method whose transition stub the frame detour called, on the argument
// that entering the stub puts the thread into cooperative GC mode and so makes a
// managed read legal from a native detour.
//
// That argument is backwards and coreclr enforces the opposite.  The detour runs on
// the game's frame thread while that thread is INSIDE managed code, so the thread is
// already in cooperative mode with live managed frames below the detour -- and a
// reverse P/Invoke asserts that its caller is unmanaged.  The runtime refuses it:
// `JIT_ReversePInvokeEnterRare` calls `ReversePInvokeBadTransition`, which fail-fasts
// the process with `COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE` (0x80131506) through `TerminateProcess`,
// raising nothing an in-process handler can see.  Six dumps across three builds put
// the exception at `coreclr+0x244839` every time, with `FrameTickDetour` on the
// faulting stack and the game's own managed frame below it.
//
// The frame read is therefore NATIVE: the detour walks `World.Shared -> +Player ->
// +Position` itself, guarded by the `Player` MethodTable that the bootstrap publishes
// in `managedPlayerTypeHandle`.  See DrelayFrame.cpp for the read and
// HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md for the rule that needs rewriting.

// Spike 1.3 liveness.  `frameCalls` is the count the self-check reports; the
// per-call cost is a rolling maximum so a single hitch is not averaged away.
extern std::atomic<uint64_t> g_frameCalls;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t> g_frameMaxUs;
extern std::atomic<uint32_t> g_frameReadFailures;
extern DWORD                 g_frameFirstTick;
extern std::atomic<int>      g_framePaused;

// State the self-check fills in and `DrelayHook_Init` reports.
struct SelfCheckReport {
    uint32_t passed;
    uint32_t failed;
    uint32_t gaps;
};
extern SelfCheckReport g_selfCheck;

// The field-offset cross-check that Phase 2 will run from inside the JIT detour.
//
// NOT IMPLEMENTED IN PHASE 1, and declared here rather than deleted so the gap is
// visible in the header a reader consults.  Phase 1 publishes offsets measured by
// managed reflection and verifies them by reading the same state through a raw
// pointer chain and requiring the two to agree; the JIT's own `getFieldOffset`
// oracle is the independent second source that Phase 2 adds, and until it exists
// the self-check reports check 7 as a GAP rather than as a pass.  A declared and
// unimplemented function would normally be a smell; here it is the record that a
// planned check has not been made.
void DrelayResolveOffsets(void* jitInfo, void* classHandle);

} // namespace drelay

#endif // DRELAY_GLOBALS_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayHookShared.h`:

```h
// DrelayHookShared.h -- the contract between the native hook and the managed bootstrap.
//
// WHY THIS FILE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE IN PHASE 1
// --------------------------------------------------
// The hook is injected before CoreCLR exists, so at injection time there is no
// managed assembly, no metadata and no way for the native side to discover
// anything.  The bootstrap runs later, from inside the runtime, and is the only
// code in the process that can ask the runtime questions about itself (what is
// my MVID, is tiered compilation on, where does the runtime think this field
// lives).  So the division of labour is:
//
//     bootstrap  answers questions about the runtime, and owns all managed reads
//     hook       owns the JIT detour and the patches, and reads nothing managed
//                that the bootstrap has not described to it
//
// This header is the shared vocabulary.  It is included by three compilers --
// MSVC for the native DLL, the C# compiler for the bootstrap and the launcher --
// so it must stay layout-trivial: fixed-width types, no pointers, no bitfields,
// and explicit padding.  Every field is read by at least one side and written by
// the other; nothing here is decorative.
//
// A layout change MUST bump DRELAY_SHARED_VERSION.  The native side refuses to
// use a block whose version it does not know, because the alternative is
// interpreting a stale layout as if it were current -- which presents as
// garbage offsets and a hook that reads the wrong field, not as a crash.
//
// DRELAY_SHARED_SIZE pins `sizeof(DrelayShared)` so the managed side has a number
// to compare against without anyone counting bytes.  It is the output of
// `tools/gen_shared_layout.py --print`, which models MSVC's packing rules over
// this very file, and the static_assert below makes a drift between the model and
// the compiler a build failure rather than a runtime misread.  Hand-counting this
// was tried first and produced three wrong strides; the generator exists because
// of that, not for tidiness.

#ifndef DRELAY_HOOK_SHARED_H
#define DRELAY_HOOK_SHARED_H

// <stdint.h> comes first and on its own, before anything that might pull in
// <windows.h>.  The shared block is compiled as C++17 by cl.exe as well as by
// the C# compiler's P/Invoke view, and MSVC's <windows.h> does not define the
// fixed-width types: without this include the first `uint32_t` in a struct
// produces C3646 ("unknown override specifier") at the first member and then a
// hundred cascading errors, which reads like a broken struct rather than a
// missing header.
#include <stdint.h>

// The launcher builds these names and the bootstrap is given the run directory
// by the launcher, but the *names* of the kernel objects are fixed because both
// sides must agree on them without a filesystem round trip.
#define DRELAY_SHARED_VERSION   7u
#define DRELAY_MAGIC_CONFIG     0x44485243u  /* 'DHRC' -- section holds a valid config */
#define DRELAY_MAGIC_STATUS     0x44485253u  /* 'DHRS' -- native has written its status */
#define DRELAY_MAGIC_BOOT       0x44485242u  /* 'DHRB' -- bootstrap has started and is alive */

// Kernel object names.  {0} is the numeric session id the launcher picks, so two
// sessions on one machine (the root apphost and the OpenGL one, say) cannot
// collide.  The launcher passes the id to the bootstrap in the environment.
#define DRELAY_MAP_FMT          L"Local\\DrelayHook-%u"
#define DRELAY_EVT_NATIVE_FMT   L"Local\\DrelayHook-NativeReady-%u"
#define DRELAY_EVT_BOOT_FMT     L"Local\\DrelayHook-BootReady-%u"

// Environment variables the launcher sets.  Named rather than positional so a
// run can be reconstructed from `hook.log` alone.
#define DRELAY_ENV_SESSION      "DRELAY_HOOK_SESSION"     // numeric session id
#define DRELAY_ENV_RUNDIR       "DRELAY_HOOK_RUNDIR"      // where the CSVs go
#define DRELAY_ENV_GAMEDIR      "DRELAY_HOOK_GAMEDIR"     // game install directory
#define DRELAY_ENV_ASSEMBLY     "DRELAY_HOOK_ASSEMBLY"    // the assembly to identify
#define DRELAY_ENV_BLOCK        "DRELAY_HOOK_BLOCK"       // file backing the shared block
#define DRELAY_ENV_OFF          "DRELAY_HOOK_OFF"         // "1" = observe nothing, patch nothing
#define DRELAY_ENV_DRYRUN       "DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN"      // "1" = decide, do not act
#define DRELAY_ENV_TIMEOUT_MS   "DRELAY_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS"  // native wait for the bootstrap
#define DRELAY_ENV_STARTUPHOOK  "DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS"

// Maximum sizes, fixed so the block is a fixed-size mapping rather than a
// negotiated one.  Four targets is Phase 1's whole target table; the array is
// oversized relative to four only because Phase 2 adds the spawn and collision
// roles as first-class, separate detours.
#define DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS      8
#define DRELAY_MAX_STEPS        8
#define DRELAY_MAX_READS        8
#define DRELAY_MAX_SLOT_PROBE   12
#define DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN  32
#define DRELAY_TYPE_NAME_LEN    96
#define DRELAY_FIELD_NAME_LEN   64
#define DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN     256
// Ring sizes.
//
// THESE ARE SIZED FOR LAUNCH, NOT FOR A SESSION, AND THE SECURITY-SECTION LIMIT
// IS WHY.  A named pagefile-backed section is charged against the process's
// commit *and* against a per-section security limit, and `CreateFileMapping` with
// a maximum size above roughly 1 MB on this machine fails with error 8
// (ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY) even with 6 GB of RAM free -- the first version asked
// for 1.9 MB of rings and could not be created at all.  That number is not
// guessable, so it is recorded here rather than rediscovered.
//
// What the sizes have to cover is one launch: a bootstrap handshake, the
// compilation of four target methods, and a few thousand frames of Spike 1.3's
// sample.  They are deliberately not sized for a multi-hour session; Phase 2's
// sensor will need its own transport, and growing these is the wrong answer to
// that because the mapping is created before either side can negotiate a size.
#define DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES   256
#define DRELAY_TRACE_RING_ROWS  1024
#define DRELAY_FRAME_RING_ROWS  1024

// The reserved tail's size, and the reason it is a constant rather than
// `sizeof(DrelayShared)` in the two places that need it: the launcher creates the
// section before either side can measure anything, so the size must be known from
// a number both can compute.  Total `sizeof(DrelayShared)` is pinned by
// DRELAY_SHARED_SIZE below and asserted at compile time.
//
// EIGHT BYTES HAVE BEEN TAKEN OUT OF IT FOR `managedFrameHelper`, AND SIXTEEN MORE FOR
// `managedFrameReplacement` AND `managedFrameTrampoline`, WHICH IS WHAT THE RESERVE WAS
// KEPT FOR.  Taking them is what keeps those fields from moving any other offset and
// from changing `sizeof(DrelayShared)`: the whole point of the reserve is that a new
// field is an addition inside an existing mapping, and a field that grew the struct
// would force a `DRELAY_SHARED_VERSION` bump and a new mapping size for no benefit.
#define DRELAY_SHARED_RESERVE   262104u

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Status codes.  Ordered by severity: the hook installs only when every check
 * is DRELAY_STATUS_OK or DRELAY_STATUS_GAP, and DRELAY_STATUS_GAP is the one
 * that is explicitly "not checked", never "checked and fine".                  */

typedef enum DrelayStatus {
    DRELAY_STATUS_OK            = 0,
    DRELAY_STATUS_GAP           = 1,   /* deliberately not checkable here */
    DRELAY_STATUS_REFUSED       = 2,   /* a fingerprint mismatch: never patch */
    DRELAY_STATUS_FAILED        = 3,   /* a check that should pass did not */
    DRELAY_STATUS_TIMEOUT       = 4,
    DRELAY_STATUS_DISABLED      = 5,   /* the off switch: nothing was installed */
    DRELAY_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED   = 6
} DrelayStatus;

/* Config flags the launcher/bootstrap may set. */
#define DRELAY_CFG_DRYRUN        0x00000001u  /* decide, never act (Phase 3 default) */
#define DRELAY_CFG_FRAME_SAMPLE  0x00000002u  /* Spike 1.3: sample the frame tick */
#define DRELAY_CFG_FULL_TRACE    0x00000004u  /* log every compilation, not just hits */
#define DRELAY_CFG_SLOT_PROBE    0x00000008u  /* try candidate getMethodDefFromMethod slots */
// 0x00000010 (DRELAY_CFG_MANAGED_READ, "call back into managed for live state") was
// REMOVED rather than left defined.  There is no callback: entering managed code from
// the frame detour is an illegal reverse P/Invoke and the runtime fail-fasts the
// process for it, so the flag could never have been honoured.  The bit is retired and
// must not be reused without a new name, because a saved `shared.block` or a launcher
// from an older build still means the old thing by it.

/* Native status flags. */
#define DRELAY_ST_JIT_DETOURED   0x00000001u
#define DRELAY_ST_DISCOVERY_DONE 0x00000002u
#define DRELAY_ST_PATCHED        0x00000004u
#define DRELAY_ST_REFUSED        0x00000008u
#define DRELAY_ST_OFF            0x00000010u

/* A slot index that means "not probed / not known". */
#define DRELAY_SLOT_NONE         0xFFFFFFFFu

/* The frame read path's arming gate.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BOOLEAN.  The bootstrap publishes
 * the offsets and the type identity during the startup hook, when the runtime is up
 * but the game has no world yet: `World.Shared` is null until a scene loads, and
 * a callback that read through the pointer chain then would read through a null
 * base.  The first version of this simply refused to arm the callback at all in
 * that situation, which was honest and left Spike 1.3's success test -- read one
 * float from the live world -- never executed.  So arming became a decision made
 * LATER, by the managed side, the first time a world exists, and this field is
 * where that decision is published.
 *
 * `DRELAY_ARM_REFUSED` AND `DRELAY_ARM_UNCONFIGURED` ARE DIFFERENT FAILURES AND
 * MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED.  REFUSED means the pointer chain built from the measured
 * offsets did NOT reproduce what reflection says, i.e. the offsets are wrong for
 * this build and the hook must not read through them.  UNCONFIGURED means there
 * were never any offsets to check -- the assembly did not load, or its type names
 * moved -- so the cross-check could not be attempted at all.  One is a finding
 * about the layout, the other is a missing prerequisite; a single "not armed"
 * bit would make them indistinguishable in `summary.txt`, which is exactly the
 * class of defect PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 8 is about. */
#define DRELAY_ARM_WAITING       0u  /* no world yet; the read path is closed and reads nothing */
#define DRELAY_ARM_ARMED         1u  /* the cross-check passed; the read path reads live state */
#define DRELAY_ARM_REFUSED       2u  /* the cross-check disagreed; the read path stays shut */
#define DRELAY_ARM_UNCONFIGURED  3u  /* no offsets were ever measured; nothing to arm */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Target identity.  The IL hash is the identity; everything else in this
 * struct is either a diagnostic or a cross-check the spike must report on.     */

typedef struct DrelayTargetHash {
    char     name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN];  /* "frameTick", "spawn", ... */
    uint16_t ilSizeLow;                     /* ILCodeSize, low 16 bits -- a cheap pre-filter */
    uint8_t  hash[32];                      /* SHA-256 over ILCode[0..ILCodeSize) */
    uint8_t  found;                         /* native: 1 once seen in the compile stream */
    uint8_t  reserved0[3];
    uint64_t firstSeenQpc;                  /* native: when, in QPC ticks */
    uint64_t nativeEntry;                   /* native: the address the JIT returned */
    uint32_t nativeSize;                    /* native: the size the JIT returned */
    uint32_t tokenRead;                     /* native: what the probed slot said, if anything */
    uint32_t metadataToken;                 /* bootstrap: Phase 0's token, for the cross-check */
    uint32_t reserved1;
} DrelayTargetHash;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Offset resolution.  Two independent sources for the same fact, on purpose:
 * the bootstrap measures with managed reflection, and the hook asks the JIT via
 * ICorJitInfo::getFieldOffset.  Agreement is evidence; disagreement is a finding
 * (see PHASE1-SCOPE.md section 1.3).  Neither value is ever read from the IL.   */

/* HOW A STATIC FIELD'S ADDRESS FITS IN TWO 32-BIT FIELDS.
 *
 * `World.Shared` is static, so it has an ADDRESS rather than an instance offset,
 * and on x64 an address is 64 bits.  The first version wrote it with
 * `(uint)address`, which silently truncated it to its low half, and that
 * half-address was what `offsets.csv` and the launcher's console report printed.
 * Nothing read it, so nothing failed -- a wrong number that no check consumed,
 * which is the quietest kind.
 *
 * So for `isStatic != 0` the pair is the address and NOT an offset: the high 32
 * bits are in `managedStaticBase` and the low 32 in `managedOffset`, printed as
 * `0x%08X%08X`.  For every other field `managedStaticBase` is 0 and
 * `managedOffset` is an ordinary instance offset, which is why that column must
 * be read together with `is_static` in `offsets.csv` rather than on its own. */

typedef struct DrelayFieldOffset {
    char     name[DRELAY_FIELD_NAME_LEN];   /* "World.Shared", "World.Player", ... */
    uint32_t managedOffset;                 /* bootstrap: measured from the runtime */
    uint32_t managedStaticBase;             /* bootstrap: non-zero when it is a static field */
    uint8_t  managedValid;
    uint8_t  isStatic;
    uint8_t  reserved0[2];
    uint32_t jitOffset;                     /* native: ICorJitInfo::getFieldOffset, or DRELAY_SLOT_NONE */
    uint8_t  jitValid;
    uint8_t  agree;                         /* 1 when the value has been confirmed by a second route */
    uint8_t  reserved1[2];
} DrelayFieldOffset;

/* `agree` MEANS "CONFIRMED BY AN INDEPENDENT SECOND ROUTE", AND IT HAS TWO.
 *
 * The plan gives this field one producer -- `ICorJitInfo::getFieldOffset`, the
 * JIT's own answer -- and that is Phase 2's.  In Phase 1 the second route is the
 * pointer chain: the offsets are used to walk `World.Shared -> Player ->
 * Position` and the result is compared against the same state read through
 * reflection.  Agreement is evidence the offsets describe this build's layout;
 * disagreement is a finding, and the reason `agree` is written by the managed
 * side rather than only by the JIT.
 *
 * THE TWO SOURCES ARE KEPT APART BY `jitValid`.  `agree` alone would not say
 * which route agreed, and a reader of `offsets.csv` has to be able to tell "the
 * JIT confirmed this" from "the pointer chain confirmed this" -- they are
 * different claims with different confidence, and Phase 2 replaces the second
 * with the first.  So: `jitValid` names the oracle, `agree` names the verdict. */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* The read plan.  The managed side composes these once; the hook executes them
 * on every frame tick.  This split exists so that the hook's hot path contains
 * no knowledge of the game's layout at all -- it follows a plan it was handed,
 * which is what keeps a game patch from turning a read into a wild pointer.
 *
 * Each step either dereferences a pointer at `offset` from the running base, or
 * adds `offset` to the running base (for a value type such as GamePoint, whose
 * fields are inline rather than behind a reference).  A failed read (null base)
 * aborts the whole plan and the frame is counted as `readFailures`; the hook
 * never guesses.
 */
#define DRELAY_STEP_ADD      0u   /* base += offset (inline value type traversal) */
#define DRELAY_STEP_LOAD_PTR 1u   /* base = *(void**)(base + offset), null-checked */

typedef struct DrelayReadStep {
    uint32_t op;      /* DRELAY_STEP_* */
    uint32_t offset;
} DrelayReadStep;

#define DRELAY_READ_F32      0u  /* read a 4-byte float at base + offset */
#define DRELAY_READ_F64      1u  /* read an 8-byte double at base + offset */

typedef struct DrelayReadSpec {
    char     name[DRELAY_FIELD_NAME_LEN];   /* "Player.Position.X" */
    uint32_t stepFirst;                     /* index into steps[] */
    uint32_t stepCount;
    uint32_t readKind;                      /* DRELAY_READ_* */
    uint32_t offset;                        /* final offset from the resolved base */
    uint8_t  valid;
    uint8_t  reserved0[3];
} DrelayReadSpec;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Rings.  A ring rather than an unbounded file because the native side must
 * never allocate or block inside a JIT callback, and because the interesting
 * events are rare.  Each entry carries a sequence number, so the reader (a
 * script, or Phase 4's bridge) can detect both overflow and gaps -- an
 * overflowed ring reports a gap rather than silently dropping rows.            */

typedef struct DrelayLogLine {
    uint32_t seq;
    uint32_t level;                       /* 0=info 1=warn 2=error */
    uint64_t qpc;
    char     text[DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN];
} DrelayLogLine;

typedef struct DrelayTraceRow {
    uint32_t seq;
    uint32_t ilSize;
    uint32_t tokenRead;
    uint32_t nativeSize;
    uint8_t  ilHash[32];
    uint64_t nativeEntry;
    uint64_t qpc;
    uint8_t  matchedTarget;               /* 0xFF = not a target */
```
