```cpp
        report->failed++;
        return false;
    }

    g_realCompiler = reinterpret_cast<DrelayICorJitCompilerVtbl*>(g_jitVtable);
    g_realCompile = reinterpret_cast<CompileMethodFn>(g_jitVtable[DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD]);

    // PATCH THE CODE, NOT THE VTABLE SLOT.  THIS IS THE RESOLUTION OF PHASE 1'S
    // HARDEST FAILURE, AND THE REASONING IS WORTH MORE THAN THE CODE.
    //
    // HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.1 says to overwrite vtable slot 0.  Doing
    // exactly that killed the process -- `Fatal error. Internal CLR error.
    // (0x80131506)` within a few hundred milliseconds -- and the elimination run
    // that pinned it down is recorded in PHASE1-SCOPE.md.  The decisive observation
    // was this: with the slot overwritten, the detour was **never entered**.  A
    // function that is never called cannot be the cause of a crash, so the write
    // itself was the fault, and the only remaining explanation for a detour that
    // is never entered is that the runtime does not call `compileMethod` through
    // that slot at all -- it resolves the address once and keeps it, which is
    // ordinary for a runtime that wants to avoid an indirect call per method.
    //
    // Patching the resolved address instead has both properties that are needed:
    // every call reaches the detour whether it came through the vtable or through
    // a cached pointer, and the vtable is left byte-identical to what the runtime
    // built, so nothing that inspects it can see a change.
    //
    // `DRELAY_HOOK_VTABLE_PATCH=1` restores the documented strategy so the two can
    // be compared on one build rather than argued about.
    char useVtable[8] = {};
    const bool patchVtable =
        GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_VTABLE_PATCH", useVtable, sizeof(useVtable)) != 0 &&
        useVtable[0] == '1';

    if (patchVtable) {
        DWORD oldProtect = 0;
        if (!VirtualProtect(&g_jitVtable[DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD], sizeof(void*),
                            PAGE_READWRITE, &oldProtect)) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "VirtualProtect on the JIT vtable failed (%lu)", GetLastError());
            report->failed++;
            return false;
        }
        InterlockedExchangePointer(reinterpret_cast<PVOID volatile*>(&g_jitVtable[DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD]),
                                  reinterpret_cast<PVOID>(&HookCompileMethod));
        DWORD ignored = 0;
        VirtualProtect(&g_jitVtable[DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD], sizeof(void*), oldProtect, &ignored);
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the JIT vtable slot was overwritten (DRELAY_HOOK_VTABLE_PATCH=1): this "
                          "is the strategy that crashed the process, and the detour was never "
                          "entered under it");
    } else {
        if (g_realCompile == nullptr) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "vtable slot %u is null; nothing to patch", DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD);
            report->failed++;
            return false;
        }
        void* const target = reinterpret_cast<void*>(g_realCompile);
        void* trampoline = nullptr;

        // Asking Windows which module owns the slot is worth one call: if the
        // address is not inside clrjit.dll, the detour is being placed on
        // indirection rather than on the JIT itself, and every later conclusion
        // would be built on a wrong premise.
        wchar_t owner[MAX_PATH] = {};
        DrPeModuleNameOf(target, owner, MAX_PATH);
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "compileMethod resolves to %p in %ls", target,
              owner[0] != L'\0' ? owner : L"an unknown module");

        const MH_STATUS created = MH_CreateHook(target, reinterpret_cast<void*>(&HookCompileMethod),
                                                &trampoline);
        if (created != MH_OK) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "MH_CreateHook on compileMethod (%p) failed: status %d "
                             "(4=NOT_CREATED 5=ENABLED 7=NOT_EXECUTABLE 8=UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION "
                             "9=MEMORY_ALLOC 10=MEMORY_PROTECT 12=FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND)",
                  target, static_cast<int>(created));
            report->failed++;
            return false;
        }
        // The trampoline is the real entry point now, and it is what the detour
        // calls through -- calling the original address would run the patched
        // bytes and recurse.
        g_realCompile = reinterpret_cast<CompileMethodFn>(trampoline);
        // MH_EnableHook takes the *target*, the address MH_CreateHook was given.
        const MH_STATUS enabled = MH_EnableHook(target);
        if (enabled != MH_OK && enabled != MH_ERROR_ENABLED) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "MH_EnableHook on compileMethod (%p) failed: status %d",
                  target, static_cast<int>(enabled));
            report->failed++;
            return false;
        }
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "compileMethod code patched via MinHook (target %p, trampoline %p)",
              target, trampoline);
    }

    g_shared->nativeStatus |= DRELAY_ST_JIT_DETOURED;
    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "compileMethod detoured: real=%p hook=%p",
          reinterpret_cast<void*>(g_realCompile), reinterpret_cast<void*>(&HookCompileMethod));
    // Written to disk *now*, not on the next flusher pass.
    //
    // Everything after this line happens on a JIT thread and may end in a hard
    // process kill; the 250 ms flusher never gets its turn, and the whole log --
    // including the entry counter that says whether the detour works at all --
    // was being lost.  A diagnostic that only survives success is not a diagnostic.
    DrLogFlushNow();
    report->passed++;
    return true;
}

void DrelayInvokeResolveCallback() {
    // CALLED ONCE, HERE, BECAUSE HERE IS WHERE COMPILATION WORKS AGAIN.
    //
    // PHASE1-SCOPE.md §6.1: a startup hook cannot JIT-compile anything, so the
    // bootstrap cannot load the game assembly, reflect over it, or build dynamic
    // methods.  All of that was moved behind this callback, which the native side
    // invokes from its own thread after the runtime has finished starting.
    //
    // The callback is an `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` transition stub, so entering it
    // puts this thread into cooperative GC mode and the managed side may do
    // ordinary work.  It is called *before* discovery is allowed to close, so the
    // offsets are in place before anything reads them.
    if (g_shared == nullptr || g_shared->managedResolveHook == 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "no resolve callback was published; the hook is installed but the "
                          "the frame read will have no offsets");
        return;
    }

    // THE OTHER HALF OF THE BISECT, AND THE PRIME SUSPECT.
    //
    // The process survives when the watcher does nothing at all, and dies right
    // before this call. Everything else in the watcher has been bracketed and passes
    // individually, so the callback -- the only step that enters managed code from a
    // native thread -- is where the remaining probability sits.
    //
    // The name avoids the `DRELAY_HOOK_` prefix the launcher strips; see the note on
    // the skip switch in DrelayInstallJitDetour.
    char skip[8] = {};
    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_SKIP_RESOLVE_CALLBACK", skip, sizeof(skip)) != 0 &&
        skip[0] == '1') {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "DRELAY_SKIP_RESOLVE_CALLBACK=1: the hook is installed but the managed "
                          "callback is never invoked (diagnostic mode)");
        DrLogFlushNow();
        return;
    }

    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "invoking the managed resolve callback at %p",
          reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(g_shared->managedResolveHook)));
    DrLogFlushNow();

    // RE-ARMED AGAIN IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE CALLBACK, because this is the single
    // most likely place for the process to die and the runtime may have
    // registered further handlers since the last arming.
    DrelayArmCrashReporter();

    // WAIT, BEFORE CALLING BACK, AND THE REASON IS THE SAME ONE THAT MADE EVERYTHING
    // ELSE IN THIS PHASE FAIL.
    //
    // The bootstrap's last act before returning is to signal this side, so the
    // callback used to arrive while the runtime was still finishing the
    // startup-hook phase -- the exact window in which managed work has been fatal
    // all through this investigation. The callback enters managed code through an
    // `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` stub, which needs the runtime to be in a state that
    // the startup-hook window is not.
    //
    // THIS IS STILL A MARGIN RATHER THAN A SIGNAL, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING WHY ONE CANNOT
    // BE HAD.  The only thing that proves "the startup hook has returned" is an
    // observation made *after* the return -- and a startup hook cannot make one: it
    // cannot JIT-compile a method (PHASE1-SCOPE.md section 6.1, where every attempt
    // faulted the process), so a new call, a thread or a callback registered from
    // inside it all die before the return they were meant to announce.  The one
    // observable that does follow the return -- the game's entry point being compiled --
    // is compiled before this detour is even installed, microseconds after the
    // bootstrap signals.  So the margin stays, and what changed is its size and its
    // name: 100 ms rather than a hardcoded 500, and `DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS`
    // ('--resolve-delay' at the launcher) rather than a constant in the middle of a
    // function.  The work being deferred has no deadline: the offsets it computes are
    // needed by the frame read, which cannot happen until the game draws a frame.
    const DWORD resolveDelayMs = ReadResolveDelayMs();
    if (resolveDelayMs > 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "waiting %lu ms for the runtime to finish the startup-hook phase "
                          "before the callback", resolveDelayMs);
        DrLogFlushNow();
        Sleep(resolveDelayMs);
    }

    auto resolve = reinterpret_cast<void (__cdecl *)(void)>(
        static_cast<uintptr_t>(g_shared->managedResolveHook));
    __try {
        resolve();
    } __except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) {
        // A fault in the callback must not take the process with it; the hook is
        // already installed and the game is already running.
        DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "the resolve callback raised a native exception; the hook stays "
                         "installed and the frame read stays closed");
    }

    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "resolve callback returned; %u offset(s) published",
          g_shared->offsetCount);
    DrLogFlushNow();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE ARMING PROBE: the watcher thread's half of Spike 1.3's sensor.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.  Phase 1's blocking gap was that the frame
// callback could never read anything: `World.Shared` is null until the game loads
// a scene, the hook attaches long before that, and so the callback was switched
// off at attach and "read exactly one float from the live world" never ran.  The
// fix is to decide when to arm it *later*, once a world exists -- and this is the
// loop that provides the "later", because the watcher thread is the only thing in
// this DLL that is awake for the whole session.
//
// IT IS CALLED FROM EVERY WAIT THE WATCHER DOES, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER
// THAN AN ACCIDENT OF PLACEMENT.  The collection delay (30 s by default), the
// discovery window, the live-check wait and the final idle loop are four separate
// sleeps, and the moment a world appears is not known in advance: an operator who
// reaches a dungeon in ten seconds and one who takes three minutes must both be
// caught.  Once the decision is made the call is one volatile load and a return,
// so calling it forever costs nothing.
//
// WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not decide anything.  The decision needs
// reflection, which belongs on the managed side and not in a native loop that
// also has to keep the discovery window on time.  This function calls, then reads
// the verdict and reports it -- once, with the transition flushed, so the line is
// in `hook.log` (and on the operator's console) at the moment it happens rather
// than only in the evidence written minutes later.

namespace {

uint32_t g_armStateLogged = 0xFFFFFFFFu;   // impossible state: forces the first read
bool     g_armProbeFaulted = false;

const char* ArmStateName(uint32_t state) {
    switch (state) {
        case DRELAY_ARM_WAITING:      return "WAITING";
        case DRELAY_ARM_ARMED:        return "ARMED";
        case DRELAY_ARM_REFUSED:      return "REFUSED";
        case DRELAY_ARM_UNCONFIGURED: return "UNCONFIGURED";
        default:                      return "unknown";
    }
}

// A coordinate pair, or "(not read)" when the chain never got that far.
//
// TWO USES, AND THE SECOND IS WHY IT DOES NOT SIMPLY PRINT THE NUMBERS.  A refusal
// caused by the MethodTable guard never reads a float, so there is no pair to print
// and a NaN rendered as `-nan(ind)` reads like a wrong number rather than an absent
// one.  A refusal caused by the cross-check *throwing* never publishes a pair either,
// so it falls into the same case.
void FormatCrossCheck(char* out, size_t cap, float x, float y) {
    if (x != x || y != y) {
        _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "(not read)");
    } else {
        _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "(%.4f, %.4f)", x, y);
    }
}

// Whether the confirmation rested on two routes that both reported exactly zero.
//
// A ZERO PAIR AGREES FOR ANY TWO ADDRESSES, INCLUDING A WRONG ONE.  The game creates
// its world while a scene is still loading, long before a character is placed in it,
// so `Player.Position` can legitimately be the default (0, 0) at the moment the
// cross-check runs.  Reporting that as a plain confirmation would take more from the
// comparison than it earned; the MethodTable identity check is what carries the
// verification in that case, and a reader is told so.
bool CrossCheckWasTrivial() {
    return g_shared != nullptr &&
           g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefX == 0.0f && g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefY == 0.0f &&
           g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrX == 0.0f && g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrY == 0.0f;
}

} // namespace

void DrelayPollArmProbe() {
    if (g_shared == nullptr || g_armProbeFaulted) {
        return;
    }
    const uint64_t published = g_shared->managedProbeHook;
    if (published == 0) {
        return;
    }

    auto probe = reinterpret_cast<void (__cdecl *)(void)>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(published));
    __try {
        probe();
    } __except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER) {
        // A faulting probe must not take the watcher with it, and it must not be
        // called again: this is the same discipline the resolve callback's own
        // `__try` applies, and the same reason -- the hook is installed and the
        // game is running, so the only acceptable outcome is a missed reading.
        g_armProbeFaulted = true;
        DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "the managed arming probe raised a native exception; it will not be "
                         "called again and the frame read path stays closed");
        DrLogFlushNow();
        return;
    }

    const uint32_t state = g_shared->managedArmState;
    if (state == g_armStateLogged) {
        return;
    }
    g_armStateLogged = state;

    // `WAITING` is the state the run starts in, so the first observation of it is
    // not a transition and gets no line.  Reporting it would put a line in every
    // log saying that nothing has happened yet.
    if (state == DRELAY_ARM_WAITING) {
        return;
    }

    char reflected[64] = {};
    char pointer[64] = {};
    FormatCrossCheck(reflected, sizeof(reflected),
                     g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefX, g_shared->managedCrossCheckRefY);
    FormatCrossCheck(pointer, sizeof(pointer),
                     g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrX, g_shared->managedCrossCheckPtrY);

    switch (state) {
        case DRELAY_ARM_ARMED:
            // "no live player", not "no world": the counter is incremented for both
            // "the world is null" and "the world exists with no character in it yet",
            // and the second is the commoner of the two on a live run -- the world is
            // created while a scene loads, the player some seconds later.
            DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "frame read path ARMED (t+%u ms, after %u probe(s) found no live "
                              "player): reflection and the pointer chain agree on "
                              "Player.Position = %s%s; live reads begin at the next frame tick",
                  g_shared->managedArmTick, g_shared->managedProbeWaits, reflected,
                  CrossCheckWasTrivial()
                      ? " -- but both routes returned exactly zero, so the MethodTable identity "
                        "check is what carries this verification"
                      : "");
            break;
        case DRELAY_ARM_REFUSED:
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "frame read path REFUSED: reflection says %s and the pointer chain "
                             "built from the measured offsets says %s -- the offsets do not "
                             "describe this build, so the callback will never read through them",
                  reflected, pointer);
            break;
        case DRELAY_ARM_UNCONFIGURED:
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "frame read path can never open: the resolve callback published "
                             "no field offsets, so there is no pointer chain to check against the "
                             "world and none to read through");
            break;
        default:
            DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the managed side published arm state %u (%s), which this build "
                              "does not know", state, ArmStateName(state));
            break;
    }
    DrLogFlushNow();
}

void DrelayBeginDiscovery() {
    // The window is measured from the moment it is *opened*, and closing is what
    // opens it.  It used to be opened by the first compilation the detour saw, which
    // put the measurement at ~1.3 s into the process; see `ReadCollectDelayMs` for why
    // that measured the wrong interval and what replaced it.
    //
    // `DrelayWaitForCollectDelay` calls this after the delay, so a caller that reaches
    // here directly still gets a sane window -- it just starts now.
    if (g_discoveryTimerStarted.exchange(1) == 0) {
        g_discoveryStartTick.store(GetTickCount());
    }
}

bool DrelayWaitForCollectDelay() {
    const DWORD delayMs = ReadCollectDelayMs();
    if (delayMs > 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "waiting %lu ms before collection starts, so the operator can get "
                          "past the menu and into gameplay; nothing compiled in this interval "
                          "is lost, only unwatched", static_cast<unsigned long>(delayMs));
        DrLogFlushNow();

        // Sliced rather than one long Sleep, so `DrelayHook_Shutdown` from the
        // operator's console is honoured during the delay instead of after it.  A
        // single Sleep(30000) would make the launcher's shutdown path wait on a
        // watcher that is not listening.
        const DWORD sliceMs = 250;
        // A HEARTBEAT, BECAUSE "THE LOG STOPS" AND "THE WAIT IS STILL RUNNING" LOOKED
        // IDENTICAL.  One live run with a 30 s delay produced a `hook.log` that ended
        // at the `waiting` line and never grew again, while the process lived on and
        // wrote its other evidence files 65 s later.  Nothing in that run could
        // distinguish a watcher still sleeping from a watcher that had died, and the
        // flusher's own failures were invisible too.
        //
        // One line per ~5 s turns that into a fact: a log that stops mid-delay now has
        // a heartbeat after the last one it printed, or it does not, and the two cases
        // mean different things.  It is logged through the same ring as everything
        // else, so it also exercises the flush path during the wait -- which is the
        // path the missing lines would have taken.
        const DWORD heartbeatEvery = (sliceMs > 0) ? (5000 / sliceMs) : 20;
        DWORD slices = 0;
        DWORD waited = 0;
        while (waited < delayMs) {
            if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&g_shutdownRequested, 0, 0) != 0) {
                // NO EVIDENCE IS WRITTEN HERE, AND THAT IS NOT A LOSS.  The caller
                // treats this return as "leave the discovery loop now" and falls
                // through to the same evidence writer the normal path uses, so
                // `summary.txt`, `events.jsonl`, `selfcheck.txt` and the rest are still
                // produced from whatever was collected during the delay.  Writing them
                // here as well would mean two writers for one run.
                //
                // The window is opened first anyway so that the elapsed-time figures
                // those files report are measured from a real timestamp rather than
                // from zero.
                DrelayBeginDiscovery();
                DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "shutdown requested %lu ms into the collection delay; ending "
                                  "collection now and writing the evidence gathered so far",
                      static_cast<unsigned long>(waited));
                DrLogFlushNow();
                return false;
            }
            const DWORD slice = (delayMs - waited < sliceMs) ? (delayMs - waited) : sliceMs;
            Sleep(slice);
            waited += slice;
            ++slices;
            // THE ARMING PROBE RUNS DURING THE DELAY, AND THIS IS THE MOST
            // IMPORTANT OF ITS FOUR CALL SITES.
            //
            // The delay exists so the operator can clear the menu and get into
            // gameplay, which is exactly when `World.Shared` stops being null -- so
            // a probe that only ran after the delay would miss the one moment it is
            // waiting for and the frame read path would stay closed for as long as
            // it takes the game to load another scene.
            DrelayPollArmProbe();
            if (heartbeatEvery > 0 && (slices % heartbeatEvery) == 0 && waited < delayMs) {
                DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "still waiting: %lu of %lu ms before collection starts",
                      static_cast<unsigned long>(waited), static_cast<unsigned long>(delayMs));
                DrLogFlushNow();
            }
        }
    }

    // Opened here and nowhere else, so "collection starts" is one event with one
    // timestamp rather than a property inferred from whatever compiled first.
    DrelayBeginDiscovery();
    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "collection started: watching the compilation stream for up to %lu ms "
                      "(the window closes early the moment every target is in)",
          static_cast<unsigned long>(ReadDiscoveryWindowMs()));
    DrLogFlushNow();
    return true;
}

DWORD ReadDiscoveryWindowMs() {
    char value[32] = {};
    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS", value, sizeof(value)) == 0 ||
        value[0] == '\0') {
        return kDefaultDiscoveryWindowMs;
    }
    char* end = nullptr;
    const long parsed = strtol(value, &end, 10);
    if (end == value || parsed < 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS='%s' is not a non-negative number of "
                          "milliseconds; using the %lu ms default", value,
              static_cast<unsigned long>(kDefaultDiscoveryWindowMs));
        return kDefaultDiscoveryWindowMs;
    }
    // Bounded by the same ceiling the collection delay uses, and for the same reason:
    // this value becomes the length of the watcher's reporting loop, and a typo that
    // meant minutes would present as a hang rather than as a long window.
    constexpr long kMaxDiscoveryWindowMs = 600000;
    if (parsed > kMaxDiscoveryWindowMs) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS=%ld exceeds the %ld ms maximum; clamping",
              parsed, kMaxDiscoveryWindowMs);
        return static_cast<DWORD>(kMaxDiscoveryWindowMs);
    }
    return static_cast<DWORD>(parsed);
}

bool DrelayDiscoveryWindowClosed() {
    if (g_discoveryTimerStarted.load() == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    return (GetTickCount() - g_discoveryStartTick.load()) >= ReadDiscoveryWindowMs();
}

DWORD DrelayDiscoveryPollMs() {
    return kDiscoveryPollMs;
}

void DrelayCloseDiscovery() {
    if (g_discoveryClosed.exchange(1) == 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "discovery window closed after %lu ms: %u compilation(s) seen, "
                          "%u/%u targets matched",
              GetTickCount() - g_discoveryStartTick.load(),
              g_compileCalls.load(), g_targetsFound.load(), g_targetCount);

        // THE TWO NUMBERS THAT DECIDE HOW TO READ THIS RUN.
        //
        // `instrumented` is what `g_compileCalls` counts and what every per-target
        // verdict is derived from.  `invocations` is how many times the detour was
        // actually reached.  When they differ, some compilations were executed and
        // never examined, and a target reported MISSING may simply be one of them.
        const uint32_t invocations = g_detourInvocations.load();
        const uint32_t instrumented = g_compileCalls.load();
        const uint32_t skipped = g_reentrantSkips.load();
        DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "detour accounting: %u invocation(s), %u instrumented, "
                          "%u skipped as re-entrant",
              invocations, instrumented, skipped);
        if (invocations > instrumented) {
            const uint32_t unaccounted = invocations - instrumented - skipped;
            DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the detour was entered %u more time(s) than it inspected "
                              "(%u skipped by the re-entrancy guard, %u by no accounted path). "
                              "A target reported MISSING in this run is NOT proof that the game "
                              "never compiled it -- see DrelayGlobals.h.",
                  invocations - instrumented, skipped, unaccounted);
        }
        if (g_discoveryDoneEvent != nullptr) {
            SetEvent(g_discoveryDoneEvent);
        }

        // FLUSHED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE FLUSHER'S 250 ms CADENCE, BECAUSE
        // THE THINGS THAT HAPPEN NEXT ARE EXACTLY WHAT KILLS THE PROCESS.  The
        // live run that first found a target was patched and then died on the first
        // frame, and the two lines above -- the target-size verdicts' supporting
        // accounting and the window close -- were still sitting in the ring, so the
        // one run that most needed a record of what the detour had seen left none.
        // A decision point is worth a flush; see PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 4 trap 3.
        DrLogFlushNow();
    }
}

void DrelayLogDiscoveryStatus() {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g_targetCount; ++i) {
        const DrelayTargetHash& t = g_shared->targets[g_targets[i].index];
        if (t.found != 0) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "  %-12s FOUND    IL size key %5u  native %5u  entry %p  "
                              "token 0x%08X  (Phase 0 says 0x%08X)",
                  g_targets[i].name, t.ilSizeLow, t.nativeSize,
                  reinterpret_cast<void*>(t.nativeEntry), t.tokenRead, t.metadataToken);
        } else {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR,
                  "  %-12s MISSING  never compiled in the discovery window. Either it was "
                  "inlined, or the game never reached the code path that calls it. "
                  "This target is NOT patched.", g_targets[i].name);
        }
    }
}

uint32_t DrelayTargetCount() {
    return g_targetCount;
}

void DrelayLoadTargets() {
    LoadTargetsFromShared();
}

bool DrelayVerifyLoadedAssemblyMvid(DrelayInstallReport* report) {
    // THE HALF OF THE IDENTITY CHECK THE NATIVE SIDE COULD NOT MAKE EARLIER.
    //
    // "The file on disk is the pinned build" is Phase 0's fingerprint gate.
    // "The assembly the runtime actually loaded is the file on disk" is this, and
    // it is the only version of the claim that a swap between the two cannot
    // defeat.  It needs the runtime's own answer, which the managed side can only
    // obtain after the startup hook has returned -- so it runs here, after the
    // callback, and before the discovery window can close and patch anything.
    //
    // THE REPORT IS NOT TOUCHED HERE, DELIBERATELY.  This function used to adjust
    // `report->passed`/`failed`/`gaps` directly, which meant the strongest identity
    // check in the phase existed only as a counter and a log line -- invisible in
    // `selfcheck.txt`, and on a refusal the totals moved while no line named the two
    // MVIDs that disagreed.  `DrelayRunSelfChecks` now emits it as check 5a, from
    // exactly the values compared below, and the counts are recomputed from the
    // lines.  `report` is accepted and unused for signature compatibility; keep it
    // that way rather than reintroducing a second accounting path.
    (void)report;
    if (!g_fileMvidRead) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the file's MVID could not be read, so the loaded assembly could not "
                          "be checked against it -- reported as a GAP, not as a pass");
        return true;
    }

    uint8_t loaded[16] = {};
    memcpy(loaded, g_shared->mvid, sizeof(loaded));

    bool published = false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(loaded); ++i) {
        if (loaded[i] != 0) {
            published = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!published) {
        // An all-zero MVID is never a real assembly's, so this is "the bootstrap
        // never published" rather than "the assemblies differ".  Reported as a
        // GAP for the same reason every other unmakeable check is: silence here
        // would read as a pass.
        DrLog(DRLOG_WARN, "the bootstrap published no MVID (the block still holds zeros), so the "
                          "loaded assembly could not be checked against the file -- GAP");
        return true;
    }

    if (memcmp(loaded, g_fileMvid, 16) != 0) {
        DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "loaded assembly MVID mismatch: the runtime loaded "
                         "%02X%02X%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X-... and %ls holds "
                         "%02X%02X%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X-... -- refusing to patch anything",
              loaded[0], loaded[1], loaded[2], loaded[3], loaded[4], loaded[5], loaded[6], loaded[7],
              g_assemblyPath,
              g_fileMvid[0], g_fileMvid[1], g_fileMvid[2], g_fileMvid[3],
              g_fileMvid[4], g_fileMvid[5], g_fileMvid[6], g_fileMvid[7]);
        return false;
    }

    DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "loaded assembly MVID verified against the file: "
                      "%02X%02X%02X%02X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X-...",
          loaded[0], loaded[1], loaded[2], loaded[3], loaded[4], loaded[5], loaded[6], loaded[7]);
    return true;
}

} // namespace drelay

```

`hook/native/DrelayInstall.h`:

```h
// DrelayInstall.h -- the public surface of the JIT half of the hook.

#ifndef DRELAY_INSTALL_H
#define DRELAY_INSTALL_H

#include "DrelayHookShared.h"
#include "DrelayJit.h"

#include <windows.h>
#include <stdint.h>

namespace drelay {

// The tally the self-check accumulates.  `gaps` counts checks that were
// deliberately not made -- they are reported separately from passes so that
// "not checked" can never be read as "checked and fine", which is the
// distinction Phase 0 established for the fingerprint gate.
struct DrelayInstallReport {
    uint32_t passed = 0;
    uint32_t failed = 0;
    uint32_t gaps = 0;
};

// Proves which runtime is loaded and that the assembly is the pinned build.
// Returns false on any refusal; every refusal has already been logged with the
// expected and actual value, because a refusal that does not say why is
// indistinguishable from a crash.
bool DrelayRuntimeValidate(DrelayInstallReport* report);

// Replaces vtable slot 0.  Called only after DrelayRuntimeValidate returned true.
bool DrelayInstallJitDetour(DrelayInstallReport* report);

// Discovery state machine, driven by the watcher thread.
void     DrelayBeginDiscovery();
bool     DrelayDiscoveryWindowClosed();
DWORD    DrelayDiscoveryPollMs();
void     DrelayCloseDiscovery();
void     DrelayLogDiscoveryStatus();

// Waits out the operator's head start and then OPENS the discovery window.
//
// This is the only thing that opens the window, so "collection started" has one
// timestamp.  The head start now defaults to ZERO (`--collect-delay` /
// `DRELAY_HOOK_COLLECT_DELAY_MS` still honour a value), because the patch no longer
// waits for the window: a target is hooked a settle interval after it is first seen,
// from the moment the detour is installed.  See `ReadCollectDelayMs` in
// DrelayInstall.cpp for the full argument, and `DrelayPatchTargetsDuringDiscovery`.
//
// Returns false when a shutdown was requested during the wait, so the caller leaves
// its discovery loop at once and falls through to the evidence writer.  The window is
// opened even in that case, so the elapsed-time figures in the evidence are measured
// from a real timestamp.
bool     DrelayWaitForCollectDelay();

// How long the discovery window stays open -- ten seconds by default, and closed early
// the moment every target is in.  `ReadDiscoveryWindowMs` in DrelayInstall.cpp argues
// why the cap is a reporting bound and not a functional one.
DWORD    ReadDiscoveryWindowMs();

// How long the resolve callback waits for the runtime to leave the startup-hook phase
// before it enters managed code.  `--resolve-delay` / `DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS`,
// 100 ms by default; why it is a margin and not a signal is at the call site.
DWORD    ReadResolveDelayMs();

// How long the harness records the patched frame after the patch goes live, and
// whether the frame read is paused when that window closes.  Both are described at
// their definitions in DrelayInstall.cpp: the window is `DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS` (the
// launcher's `--live-seconds`, default 5000 ms, unchanged) and the pause is now OFF by
// default -- `DRELAY_KEEP_READING=0`, or the launcher's `--pause-after-run`, asks for it.
DWORD    ReadLiveWindowMs();
bool     ReadKeepReadingAfterRun();

// Invokes the managed resolve callback, once, after the detour is installed.
//
// The bootstrap cannot do this work itself: a startup hook cannot JIT-compile
// anything (PHASE1-SCOPE.md §6.1), so loading the assembly, reflecting over it and
// building dynamic methods all have to happen after startup has completed.  This is
// called from the watcher thread at exactly that point.
void DrelayInvokeResolveCallback();

// Calls the managed arming probe, if one was published, and reports a change in
// its verdict once.
//
// Spike 1.3's success test -- read one float from the live world -- cannot run
// until the game has a world, and `World.Shared` is null until a scene loads.  The
// probe is the managed side's answer to "is there a world yet, and do the measured
// offsets describe it"; this function is the watcher thread's, and it is what makes
// the question get asked at all.
//
// IT MUST BE CALLED FROM EVERY WAIT THE WATCHER DOES.  Four call sites -- the
// collection delay, the discovery loop, the live-check wait and the idle loop --
// and the reason is that the moment a world appears is not known in advance:
// catching an operator who reaches gameplay in ten seconds and one who takes three
// minutes are the same requirement.  Once the verdict is in, each call is one
// volatile load and a return.
void DrelayPollArmProbe();

// Count of targets the bootstrap published (not the count found).
uint32_t DrelayTargetCount();

// Reads the target table out of the shared block.  Separate from validation so
// that the target list is loaded only once the block is known to be current.
void DrelayLoadTargets();

// Compares the assembly the runtime actually loaded -- which the bootstrap can
// only publish from the managed resolve callback -- against the MVID of the file
// on disk, which validation read earlier.  Returns false on a mismatch.
//
// IT HAS TO RUN AFTER `DrelayInvokeResolveCallback` AND BEFORE ANY PATCH.  The
// comparison is the one claim the fingerprint gate cannot make for itself: the
// gate proves the file is the pinned build, this proves the process is running
// that file, and only the pair rules out a swap between them.  Neither half has a
// value at the time the other does.
bool DrelayVerifyLoadedAssemblyMvid(DrelayInstallReport* report);
} // namespace drelay

#endif // DRELAY_INSTALL_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayJit.h`:

```h
// DrelayJit.h -- just enough of the JIT/EE interface to detour the JIT safely.
//
// SCOPE, DELIBERATELY SMALL
// -------------------------
// The hook is not a JIT inspector.  It needs exactly three things from this
// interface: the vtable slot that compiles a method, the vtable slot that proves
// which runtime we are in, and one slot that turns a method handle into a
// metadata token for *diagnostic* purposes.  Everything else is here only
// because it is before those three in the vtable, and a vtable index is a count
// of everything that precedes it -- so the declarations below are load-bearing
// even where they are never called, and removing an unused one silently moves
// every index after it.
//
// That is also why the order matters more than the contents.  The canonical
// ordering is `src/coreclr/inc/icorjitinfoimpl_generated.h`, which the runtime's
// own generator emits "in exactly the same order, with exactly the same
// whitespace, as the ICorJitInfo interface declaration".  `tools/jit_slots.py`
// parses that file and prints the indices; the constants below are that tool's
// output for .NET 9, and DrelayInstall records which slot it actually used at
// runtime rather than assuming these are right.
//
// THE ONE THING THAT IS VERIFIED AND MUST NOT BE "SIMPLIFIED"
// ----------------------------------------------------------
// `getMethodDefFromMethod` is at 0x7A, NOT the 0x76 that MonoMod's generated
// header documents, and not the 105 that xoofx/ManagedJit uses.  0x76 is
// `runWithErrorTrap` on .NET 9.  Calling the wrong slot with a method handle
// does not fail -- it calls an unrelated function with an unrelated signature,
// which is exactly the class of mistake the architecture document warns about.
// The runtime proof of the index is the token it returns (see spike 1.2).

#ifndef DRELAY_JIT_H
#define DRELAY_JIT_H

#include <windows.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>   // offsetof, for the static_asserts on the two structs below

// The JIT/EE interface version identifier for .NET 9, from
// src/coreclr/inc/jiteeversionguid.h at release/9.0.  Reading this back through
// vtbl[0x02] is the positive proof that we are holding the JIT object and not
// some other four-slot vtable that happened to be at the same address.
#define DRELAY_JITEE_GUID_DOTNET9 { 0xd6218a78, 0x9a34, 0x4c6f, \
    { 0x8d, 0xb5, 0x07, 0x7a, 0x06, 0x02, 0x2f, 0xae } }

// ICorJitCompiler occupies slots 0..3; compileMethod and getVersionIdentifier
// are the two the hook uses.
#define DRELAY_VTBL_COMPILE_METHOD        0x00u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_VERSION_ID        0x02u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_ICOMPILER_SLOTS       4u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_TOTAL_SLOTS_DOTNET9   178u

// ICorJitInfo slots the hook cares about, as derived by tools/jit_slots.py.
// `icos` = the slot is in ICorStaticInfo's contribution; listed here so a future
// reader can re-derive rather than re-guess.
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_METHOD_DEF        0x7Au  // <-- NOT 0x76
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_FIELD_OFFSET      0x62u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_IS_FIELD_STATIC       0x67u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_STATIC_BASE       0x33u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_CLASS_NUM_FIELDS  0x39u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_FIELD_IN_CLASS    0x3Au

// Community values that are wrong, retained as data so the spike can *test* them
// rather than merely disbelieve them.  Testing a wrong index is how we find out
// what it really points at; 0x76 is expected to behave like `runWithErrorTrap`.
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_METHOD_DEF_MONOMOD  0x76u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_METHOD_DEF_MANAGEDJIT 105u
#define DRELAY_VTBL_GET_FIELD_OFFSET_MONOMOD 0x5Eu

typedef struct DrelayCorJitResult {
    int32_t  value;
} DrelayCorJitResult;

#define DRELAY_CORJIT_OK              0
#define DRELAY_CORJIT_INTERNALERROR   0x80000003

typedef enum DrelayCorInfoType {
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_UNDEF   = 0,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_VOID    = 1,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_BOOL    = 2,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_CHAR    = 3,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_I1      = 4,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_U1      = 5,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_I2      = 6,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_U2      = 7,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_I4      = 8,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_U4      = 9,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_I8      = 10,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_U8      = 11,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_R4      = 12,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_R8      = 13,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_STRING  = 14,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_PTR     = 15,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_BYREF   = 16,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_VALUECLASS = 17,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_CLASS   = 18,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_REFANY  = 20,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_TYPE_VAR     = 24
} DrelayCorInfoType;

typedef enum DrelayCorInfoCallConv {
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_CURRENT      = 0x00,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_STD          = 0x01,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_VARARG       = 0x02,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_UNMANAGED    = 0x03,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_STD_MASK     = 0x03,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_HASTHIS      = 0x20,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_ISVIRTUAL    = 0x40,
    DRELAY_CORINFO_CALL_PRIVATE      = 0x80
} DrelayCorInfoCallConv;

typedef struct DrelayCorInfoSigInst {
    uint32_t classInstCount;
    void*    classInst;
    uint32_t methInstCount;
    void*    methInst;
} DrelayCorInfoSigInst;

// CORINFO_SIG_INFO, COPIED FROM THE RUNTIME'S OWN HEADER RATHER THAN FROM A
// BINDING.
//
// THIS STRUCT WAS WRONG FOR THE WHOLE OF PHASE 1, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE
// COMMENT.  The previous version declared `callConv; retType; retTypeClass;
// retTypeSigClass; args; numArgs; token; sigInst; flags; pSig; sigLen;` -- an
// ordering copied from a community binding, with three aggregate members widened
// to pointers and the bitfields expanded into separate fields.  It computed to
// 96 bytes against the runtime's 112, which moved `ILCode` from offset 16 to
// offset 104 and `ILCodeSize` from 24 to 112 *inside CORINFO_METHOD_INFO*.  The
// detour was therefore reading an `mdToken` where it expected a pointer to IL
// and the low half of an argument-list handle where it expected an IL size.
// Nothing about that fails loudly: the size pre-filter simply never matched a
// target, and the handful of times a garbage size did match, `CryptHashData` was
// handed a wild pointer.
//
// The authority is `src/coreclr/inc/corinfo.h` at `release/9.0`, which is the
// header the runtime is compiled from.  The two `static_assert`s below are the
// part that makes this checkable rather than trusted: if a future runtime moves
// a field, the build fails with the offset rather than the hook reading an
// unrelated number.
typedef struct DrelayCorInfoSigInfo {
    int32_t                 callConv;          // CorInfoCallConv, an enum -> 4 bytes
    void*                   retTypeClass;      // @ 8
    void*                   retTypeSigClass;   // @16
    // `CorInfoType retType : 8; unsigned flags : 8; unsigned numArgs : 16;`
    // Three bitfields share ONE four-byte storage unit.  Declaring them as three
    // separate fields is how the previous version gained a pointer-sized hole.
    uint32_t                retTypeFlagsNumArgs;  // @24
    DrelayCorInfoSigInst    sigInst;           // @32, 32 bytes
    void*                   args;              // @64  CORINFO_ARG_LIST_HANDLE
    void*                   pSig;              // @72  PCCOR_SIGNATURE
    uint32_t                cbSig;             // @80
    uint8_t                 pad0[4];
    void*                   methodSignature;   // @88
    void*                   scope;             // @96  CORINFO_MODULE_HANDLE
    uint32_t                token;             // @104 mdToken
    uint8_t                 pad1[4];           //     to 112, the struct's alignment
} DrelayCorInfoSigInfo;

typedef struct DrelayCorMethodInfo {
    void*                    ftn;          // @  0 CORINFO_METHOD_HANDLE
    void*                    scope;        // @  8 CORINFO_MODULE_HANDLE
    uint8_t*                 ILCode;       // @ 16
    uint32_t                 ILCodeSize;   // @ 24
    uint32_t                 maxStack;     // @ 28
    uint32_t                 EHcount;      // @ 32
    uint32_t                 options;      // @ 36 CorInfoOptions, an enum
    uint32_t                 regionKind;   // @ 40 CorInfoRegionKind, an enum
    uint8_t                  pad0[4];
    DrelayCorInfoSigInfo     args;         // @ 48, 112 bytes
    DrelayCorInfoSigInfo     locals;       // @160, 112 bytes
} DrelayCorMethodInfo;

// The contract, checked by the compiler on every build.  `offsetof` is what
// turns "the layout is right" from an assumption into a build step, which is the
// same move `SizeProbe.c` makes for the shared block.
static_assert(sizeof(DrelayCorInfoSigInfo) == 112, "CORINFO_SIG_INFO is 112 bytes on .NET 9 x64");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorInfoSigInfo, retTypeClass) == 8, "CORINFO_SIG_INFO.retTypeClass");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorInfoSigInfo, sigInst) == 32, "CORINFO_SIG_INFO.sigInst");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorInfoSigInfo, args) == 64, "CORINFO_SIG_INFO.args");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorInfoSigInfo, token) == 104, "CORINFO_SIG_INFO.token");
static_assert(sizeof(DrelayCorMethodInfo) == 272, "CORINFO_METHOD_INFO is 272 bytes on .NET 9 x64");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorMethodInfo, ftn) == 0, "CORINFO_METHOD_INFO.ftn");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorMethodInfo, ILCode) == 16, "CORINFO_METHOD_INFO.ILCode");
static_assert(offsetof(DrelayCorMethodInfo, ILCodeSize) == 24, "CORINFO_METHOD_INFO.ILCodeSize");


// Only the eight leading slots are declared, with filler vtable entries for
// slots 8..177.  Declaring them keeps the arithmetic honest: the filler count is
// a visible constant rather than an unexplained pointer arithmetic expression.
#define DRELAY_VTBL_FILLER_SLOTS \
    ((DRELAY_VTBL_TOTAL_SLOTS_DOTNET9 - DRELAY_VTBL_ICOMPILER_SLOTS - 8u))

// Names for the ICorJitCompiler slots the hook touches, so a reader can see the
// calling convention and the exact signature rather than an offset into an array.
typedef struct DrelayICorJitCompilerVtbl {
    DrelayCorJitResult (__cdecl *compileMethod)(
        void* self, void* info, DrelayCorMethodInfo* methodInfo,
        unsigned flags, uint8_t** nativeEntry, uint32_t* nativeSize);
    void (__cdecl *processShutdownWork)(void* self, void* work);
    int  (__cdecl *getVersionIdentifier)(void* self, void* versionIdentifier, uint32_t* identifierSize);
    void (__cdecl *setTargetOS)(void* self, int os);
} DrelayICorJitCompilerVtbl;

// The three ICorJitInfo slots the hook calls, reached by index so the filler
// above does not need a 178-entry struct:
//   getMethodDefFromMethod(self, CORINFO_METHOD_HANDLE, mdMethodDef*)
//   getFieldOffset(self, CORINFO_FIELD_HANDLE) -> unsigned
//   isFieldStatic(self, CORINFO_FIELD_HANDLE) -> bool
typedef uint32_t (__cdecl *DrelayGetMethodDefFn)(void* self, void* ftn, uint32_t* tokenOut);
typedef uint32_t (__cdecl *DrelayGetFieldOffsetFn)(void* self, void* field);
typedef int      (__cdecl *DrelayIsFieldStaticFn)(void* self, void* field);

static __forceinline void* DrelayVtblSlot(void* self, uint32_t index) {
    void*** vptrAtSelf = static_cast<void***>(self);
    void** vtable = *vptrAtSelf;
    return vtable[index];
}

#endif // DRELAY_JIT_H

```

`hook/native/DrelayLog.cpp`:

```cpp
// DrelayLog.cpp -- ring-buffered logging with an asynchronous flusher.

#include "DrelayLog.h"

#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <string.h>

namespace {

DrelayShared* g_shared = nullptr;
wchar_t       g_runDir[MAX_PATH] = {};
wchar_t       g_logPath[MAX_PATH] = {};
HANDLE        g_flusher = nullptr;
HANDLE        g_stopEvent = nullptr;
SRWLOCK       g_writeLock = SRWLOCK_INIT;

// The reader's cursor.  A ring can lose rows when it wraps; the log records the
// sequence number of every line so a consumer can tell a gap from a quiet
// period, and `logOverflow` counts how many lines went unwritten.
uint32_t g_readSeq = 0;

void FormatLine(char* out, size_t cap, int level, const char* fmt, va_list args) {
    static const char* kLevel[] = { "INFO ", "WARN ", "ERROR" };
    int prefix = _snprintf_s(out, cap, _TRUNCATE, "[%s] ", kLevel[level & 3]);
    if (prefix < 0) {
        return;
    }
    size_t rest = cap - static_cast<size_t>(prefix);
    _vsnprintf_s(out + prefix, rest, _TRUNCATE, fmt, args);
}

void Emit(int level, const char* fmt, va_list args) {
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return;
    }

    char text[DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN];
    FormatLine(text, sizeof(text), level, fmt, args);

    // A single writer would be enough for correctness of the ring index, but
    // three threads can log concurrently, so the index is guarded.  An SRW lock
    // in shared mode is cheap and, critically, is not a heap allocation.
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_writeLock);
    uint32_t slot = g_shared->logWrite % DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES;
    DrelayLogLine* line = &g_shared->log[slot];
    // Publish the payload before the sequence number, so a reader that sees the
    // new sequence is guaranteed to see the text that belongs to it.
    memcpy(line->text, text, sizeof(line->text));
    line->level = static_cast<uint32_t>(level);
    line->qpc = static_cast<uint64_t>(__rdtsc());
    line->seq = g_shared->logWrite + 1;
    g_shared->logWrite = g_shared->logWrite + 1;
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_writeLock);
}

// The flusher exists so that the game's frame never touches a file handle.  It
// rewrites the whole visible window each pass rather than appending, because the
// ring is small, the pass is rare, and an append would need bookkeeping that a
// crash could leave inconsistent.
DWORD WINAPI FlusherThread(LPVOID) {
    for (;;) {
        DWORD wait = WaitForSingleObject(g_stopEvent, 250);
        DrLogFlushTo(g_logPath);
        // The near-miss table rides the flusher rather than the detour, for the reason
        // the whole logger exists: the JIT thread must not touch a file.  This is a
        // no-op unless the detour has recorded something new.
        DrLogFlushObserved();
        if (wait == WAIT_OBJECT_0) {
            break;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

} // namespace

void DrLogInit(DrelayShared* shared, const wchar_t* runDir) {
    g_shared = shared;
    if (runDir != nullptr) {
        wcsncpy_s(g_runDir, runDir, _TRUNCATE);
        // The native side's own file.  It deliberately does NOT share `hook.log`
        // with the bootstrap: two writers on one path, opened by two different
        // runtimes with different sharing modes, produced a file that contained
        // one writer's lines and not the other's, and no amount of reasoning about
        // open modes settled it.  Separate files is the answer that cannot fail
        // that way, and the launcher prints both paths so a reader still has one
        // place to look.
        _snwprintf_s(g_logPath, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s\\hook.log", runDir);
    }
}

void DrLogStartFlusher(void) {
    if (g_flusher != nullptr || g_logPath[0] == L'\0') {
        return;
    }
    g_stopEvent = CreateEventW(nullptr, TRUE, FALSE, nullptr);
    g_flusher = CreateThread(nullptr, 0, FlusherThread, nullptr, 0, nullptr);
    if (g_flusher != nullptr) {
        SetThreadDescription(g_flusher, L"drelay-hook-log");
    }
}

void DrLogStopFlusher(void) {
    if (g_stopEvent != nullptr) {
        SetEvent(g_stopEvent);
    }
    if (g_flusher != nullptr) {
        WaitForSingleObject(g_flusher, 2000);
        CloseHandle(g_flusher);
        g_flusher = nullptr;
    }
    if (g_stopEvent != nullptr) {
        CloseHandle(g_stopEvent);
        g_stopEvent = nullptr;
    }
}

void DrLog(int level, const char* fmt, ...) {
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, fmt);
    Emit(level, fmt, args);
    va_end(args);
}

void DrLogOnce(unsigned int* once, int level, const char* fmt, ...) {
    if (once == nullptr || InterlockedCompareExchange(once, 1, 0) != 0) {
        return;
    }
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, fmt);
    Emit(level, fmt, args);
    va_end(args);
}

void DrLogFlushNow(void) {
    if (g_logPath[0] != L'\0') {
        DrLogFlushTo(g_logPath);
    }
}

void DrLogFlushTo(const wchar_t* path) {
    if (g_shared == nullptr || path == nullptr || path[0] == L'\0') {
        return;
    }

    // Snapshot what is new, then write.  Taking the lock only for the snapshot
    // keeps a slow disk away from the frame thread's log calls.
    char lines[64][DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN];
    uint32_t seqs[64];
    uint32_t count = 0;
    uint32_t skipped = 0;

    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_writeLock);
    uint32_t written = g_shared->logWrite;
    uint32_t oldest = (written > DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES) ? written - DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES + 1 : 1;
    if (g_readSeq + 1 < oldest) {
        skipped = oldest - (g_readSeq + 1);
        g_readSeq = oldest - 1;
    }
    for (uint32_t seq = g_readSeq + 1; seq <= written && count < 64; ++seq, ++count) {
        const DrelayLogLine* line = &g_shared->log[(seq - 1) % DRELAY_LOG_RING_LINES];
        memcpy(lines[count], line->text, DRELAY_LOG_LINE_LEN);
        seqs[count] = seq;
    }
    uint32_t consumed = count;
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_writeLock);

    // ALWAYS APPEND.  The previous version of this decided the open mode from its
    // own reader cursor -- "wb" on the first pass, "ab" afterwards -- and on the
    // first pass it truncated the file, destroying every line the bootstrap had
    // already written into it.  The evidence for that is exactly the symptom it
    // produced: hook.log contained the bootstrap's seven lines and not one of the
    // native side's, because the native flusher opened the same path for "wb"
    // moments after the bootstrap had closed it.
    //
    // The two writers share that file, and no ordering is imposed between them, so
    // truncating is never correct: the file is a transcript in arrival order.
    FILE* f = nullptr;
    // CAPTURED IMMEDIATELY, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE CAN CHANGE IT.
    //
    // The first version read `GetLastError()` *inside* the `fwprintf` argument list,
    // which is after `_vsnprintf_s` and the stream machinery have run -- so it
    // reported 0 for a failure that certainly had an error behind it.  A wrong
    // number in a diagnostic is worse than a missing one: it rules out the real
    // cause.  These three reads are the only ones taken anywhere near the failure.
    const errno_t openError = _wfopen_s(&f, path, L"ab");
    const DWORD openLastError = GetLastError();
    if (openError != 0 || f == nullptr) {
        // A FAILED APPEND IS A LOST LINE, AND IT USED TO BE INVISIBLE.
        //
        // This path was a bare `return`.  Every failure of it -- a sharing violation
        // from a scanner or another handle, a missing directory, a full disk, a
        // revoked ACL mid-run -- produced exactly the same evidence as a run in which
        // the hook had nothing left to say: a log that simply stops.  That ambiguity
        // is why two live runs could not be told apart from "the collection delay
        // never finished", and it is the same failure mode as a log that only survives
        // a clean exit.
        //
        // IT COUNTS IN `logAppendFailures`, NOT IN `logOverflow`, AND SHARING ONE WAS
        // A MISTAKE.  `logOverflow` means "lines the ring discarded before the flusher
        // read them"; this is "flush passes that could not write the file".  The two
        // lose lines at different rates per pass, so a shared counter produced a
        // number that could not be interpreted: a live run reported `748 overflowed`
        // while the file had actually been unopenable, and I spent a round trying to
        // reconcile arithmetic that had no single meaning.  A counter that cannot be
        // read is worse than no counter, because it produces a confident wrong answer.
        //
        // The lines themselves are still in the ring, and `DrLogFlushTo` retries them
        // on the next pass because `g_readSeq` only advances on a successful write --
        // so a transient failure costs nothing, and the count is what makes a
        // persistent one visible.
        //
        // THE FIRST FAILURE ALSO WRITES A SIDE FILE, AND THAT IS NOT REDUNDANT.
        // The counter says how many passes failed; it cannot say why, and the reason
        // is not recoverable after the fact.  A sibling file named
        // `hook.log.append-failed` carries the errno and the path the hook was actually
        // trying to open -- which is the difference between "another process held the
        // file" and "the path was never what we thought".
        if (g_shared != nullptr) {
            g_shared->logAppendFailures = g_shared->logAppendFailures + 1;

            static volatile LONG reported = 0;
            if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&reported, 1, 0) == 0) {
                wchar_t sidePath[MAX_PATH] = {};
                _snwprintf_s(sidePath, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s.append-failed", path);
                FILE* side = nullptr;
                if (_wfopen_s(&side, sidePath, L"wb") == 0 && side != nullptr) {
                    // WRITTEN IN UTF-8, NOT WITH `fwprintf` ON A WIDE STREAM.
                    //
                    // The first version used `_wfopen_s` with `fwprintf` and `%ls`,
                    // which emits UTF-16: every byte was followed by a NUL, so the file
                    // read as `e r r n o : 1 3` in any ordinary viewer.  The content was
                    // right and the presentation made it look corrupt -- the same defect
                    // as a wrong number, in that it costs a reader time to notice it is
                    // not one.
                    fprintf(side,
                            "drelay hook: could not append to the log\n"
                            "  path          : %ls\n"
                            "  errno         : %d\n"
                            "  win32 error   : %lu\n"
                            "  lines pending : %u\n"
                            "  failed passes : %u\n",
                            path, static_cast<int>(openError),
                            static_cast<unsigned long>(openLastError),
                            static_cast<unsigned>(consumed),
                            static_cast<unsigned>(g_shared->logAppendFailures));
                    fflush(side);
                    fclose(side);
                }
            }
        }
        return;
    }
    if (skipped > 0) {
        fprintf(f, "---- log ring overflowed: %u line(s) lost ----\r\n", skipped);
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < consumed; ++i) {
        fprintf(f, "%s\r\n", lines[i]);
        g_readSeq = seqs[i];
    }
    // FLUSHED BEFORE CLOSE, AND THE FLUSH IS THE POINT.
    //
    // `fclose` flushes, so this changes nothing about the bytes that reach the
    // disk in a clean exit.  It changes everything about a process that is killed:
    // stdio buffers a few kilobytes, and when a crash killed the host the entire
    // log was lost -- every diagnostic line Phase 1 depended on, including the one
    // that would have said whether the JIT detour had ever been entered.  A log
    // that only survives a clean exit is not evidence, and this cost several
    // rounds of investigation before the cause was noticed.
    fflush(f);
    fclose(f);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The near-miss table.  See DrelayLog.h for why it is not in the shared block.

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kMaxObserved = 16;

struct ObservedHash {
    uint32_t targetIndex;
    uint8_t  hash[32];
};

ObservedHash     g_observed[kMaxObserved] = {};
volatile LONG    g_observedCount = 0;
volatile LONG    g_observedDirty = 0;
uint32_t         g_observedWritten = 0;

// The size histogram.  Open-addressed by `size % kMaxHistogramEntries`, linear
// probe, no allocation and no lock: the detour calls this on the JIT thread and the
// flusher reads it from another, so a torn read costs a slightly wrong count while a
// lock here would be a lock taken under the JIT's own.
//
// THE CAPACITY WAS WRONG BY A FACTOR OF TWO AND THE COMMENT SAID SO CONFIDENTLY.
// It read "512 distinct IL sizes is far more than a session produces (a few hundred
// at most)".  A measured session produces MORE than 512: the run that found three
// targets filled all 512 slots and reported `61 compilation(s) could not be
// recorded`.  The probe is no longer capped (see DrRecordCompileSize), so an entry
// is only lost when the table is genuinely full -- which it was.  4096 slots is
// 32 KB of the DLL's data section and makes "full" a state a session does not reach.
constexpr uint32_t kMaxHistogramEntries = 4096;

struct SizeCount {
    uint32_t size;
    uint32_t count;
};

SizeCount     g_sizeHistogram[kMaxHistogramEntries] = {};
volatile LONG g_sizeHistogramOverflow = 0;

// The exact per-target hit counters.  Indexed by the target's position in the
// shared block, incremented by a direct IL-size comparison and never by a table
// lookup, so these are the only numbers in this file that can be read as facts
// about whether a target was compiled.  See the note in DrRecordCompileSize.
uint32_t g_exactTargetHits[DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS] = {};

// Emits `hook.log.sizes`, the whole-run record of which IL sizes were compiled.
//
// REWRITTEN ON EVERY FLUSH PASS, WITH NO "NOTHING CHANGED" GUARD, AND THAT IS
// DELIBERATE.  A guard keyed on the near-miss table's count suppressed this file
// entirely on exactly the runs it exists for -- the ones where nothing matched.  A few
// hundred bytes, four times a second, on the thread whose whole job is file I/O, is
// not worth a guard that can be wrong.
//
// It is defined before `DrLogFlushObserved` rather than after, because the first
// attempt declared it and then defined it later, which the compiler rejects as
// "symbol involving type with internal linkage not defined" -- the declaration alone
// does not satisfy /W4 /WX when the definition has not been seen.
void WriteSizeHistogram() {
    wchar_t histPath[MAX_PATH] = {};
    _snwprintf_s(histPath, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s.sizes", g_logPath);
    FILE* h = nullptr;
    if (_wfopen_s(&h, histPath, L"wb") != 0 || h == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    fprintf(h, "# every distinct IL size compiled in this run, with its count.\n");
    fprintf(h, "# A target's IL size absent from this file was NEVER COMPILED -- that is a fact\n");
    fprintf(h, "# about the game's execution, not about the hook.  A size present without a match\n");
    fprintf(h, "# was compiled and its IL differs from the pinned build.\n");
    fprintf(h, "il_size,count,target\n");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxHistogramEntries; ++i) {
        const SizeCount& entry = g_sizeHistogram[i];
        if (entry.count == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        // Name the target whose size this is, if any, so the file reads without a
        // lookup table beside it.
        const char* which = "";
        if (g_shared != nullptr) {
            for (uint32_t t = 0; t < g_shared->targetCount && t < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS; ++t) {
                if (g_shared->targets[t].ilSizeLow == entry.size) {
                    which = g_shared->targets[t].name;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        fprintf(h, "%u,%u,%s\n", entry.size, entry.count, which);
    }
    if (g_sizeHistogramOverflow != 0) {
        fprintf(h, "# %ld compilation(s) could not be recorded: the table was full\n",
                static_cast<long>(g_sizeHistogramOverflow));
    }
    fflush(h);
    fclose(h);
}

// A one-line-per-target verdict: was a method of this target's IL size compiled at all?
//
// Printed through `DrLog` so it lands in `hook.log` and on the launcher's live console
// transcript, because it is the answer to the only question the last three runs left
// open and the operator should not have to open a CSV to get it.
void WriteTargetSizeSummary() {
    if (g_shared == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    for (uint32_t t = 0; t < g_shared->targetCount && t < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS; ++t) {
        const uint16_t want = g_shared->targets[t].ilSizeLow;
        // READ FROM THE EXACT COUNTER, NOT FROM THE HISTOGRAM.
        //
        // This loop used to scan g_sizeHistogram and report zero when no slot held
        // this size -- which is a correct answer only while every compilation of
        // that size found a slot.  It does not: the table is lossy, and a run that
        // dropped compilations would have printed "ZERO compiled -- this method
        // never reached the JIT" about a method that had in fact been compiled.  A
        // verdict that can be produced by an instrument fault is worse than no
        // verdict, because it is read as a fact about the game.
        const uint32_t count = static_cast<uint32_t>(g_exactTargetHits[t]);
        const bool found = (g_shared->targets[t].found != 0);
        char name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN] = {};
        memcpy(name, g_shared->targets[t].name, sizeof(name) - 1);
        if (count == 0) {
            DrLog(DRLOG_ERR, "target-size %-12s IL size %u: ZERO compiled -- this method never "
                             "reached the JIT in this run", name, static_cast<unsigned>(want));
        } else if (found) {
            // THE MATCHED CASE NEEDS ITS OWN WORDING.  It used to fall into the
            // branch below unconditionally, so the run that finally found a target
            // printed "compiled 1 time(s) but did not match" about a target that had
            // just been matched, patched and entered 297 times.  That line was
            // accurate only while no target had ever matched -- i.e. it was written
            // for the failure case and silently wrong the moment the fix landed.
            DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "target-size %-12s IL size %u: compiled %u time(s) AND MATCHED "
                              "-- the target is found", name, static_cast<unsigned>(want), count);
        } else {
            // THE MIDDLE GROUND, AND THE OLD WORDING ASSERTED THE WRONG HALF OF IT.  This
            // branch means "methods of this IL size were compiled and none of them was
            // this target"; it used to say "the pinned IL differs from this build's",
            // which is a claim about the BUILD.  The 2026-10-12 21:22 session is why that
            // is wrong: `escape` printed "compiled 6 time(s) but did not match" on a build
            // whose pinned IL is correct -- six other 335-byte methods were compiled and
            // `RequestEscape` was simply never reached.  A maintainer reading the old line
            // goes looking for a game patch that does not exist.  What tells the two cases
            // apart is `hook.log.observed`, which lists every same-size hash that was
            // seen, so the line now points at it instead of choosing for the reader.
            DrLog(DRLOG_INFO, "target-size %-12s IL size %u: %u same-size method(s) compiled, "
                              "none of them this target -- either the target never reached the "
                              "JIT in this run, or its IL differs from the pinned build; "
                              "hook.log.observed lists every same-size hash that was seen",
                  name, static_cast<unsigned>(want), count);
        }
    }
}

} // namespace

void DrLogTargetSizeSummary(void) {
    WriteTargetSizeSummary();
}

void DrRecordCompileSize(uint32_t ilSize) {
    // THE EXACT PER-TARGET COUNT, AND IT DOES NOT USE THE TABLE AT ALL.
    //
    // The table below is a *histogram*: it is lossy by construction, because the
    // probe is bounded to keep the JIT thread's work bounded.  A live run filled
    // 426 of its 512 slots and then dropped 101 compilations, and the reviewer's
    // question -- "were the missing targets among the dropped ones?" -- is exactly
    // the question the table cannot answer, because it records how many
    // compilations were lost and never which sizes they were.
    //
    // So the per-target verdict no longer comes from the table.  There are at most
    // DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS targets, so a direct comparison against each target's IL
    // size is a handful of instructions and is EXACT: no hashing, no probing, no
    // eviction, no overflow.  A target whose counter is zero here was not compiled,
    // full stop.  The histogram is kept as the whole-stream record it is good at
    // being (which sizes existed, and how many of each), and nothing that decides a
    // question reads it any more.
    if (g_shared != nullptr) {
        const uint32_t count = g_shared->targetCount;
        for (uint32_t t = 0; t < count && t < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS; ++t) {
            if (g_shared->targets[t].ilSizeLow == ilSize) {
                InterlockedIncrement(reinterpret_cast<volatile LONG*>(&g_exactTargetHits[t]));
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // 0 and 1 are not real IL sizes but a zero-sized body is possible for an empty
    // method; they are allowed through rather than special-cased, because filtering
    // here would make the histogram disagree with the compilation count.
    const uint32_t start = ilSize % kMaxHistogramEntries;
    for (uint32_t probe = 0; probe < kMaxHistogramEntries; ++probe) {
        const uint32_t slot = (start + probe) % kMaxHistogramEntries;
        SizeCount& entry = g_sizeHistogram[slot];
        if (entry.size == ilSize) {
            entry.count = entry.count + 1;
            return;
        }
        if (entry.count == 0) {
            // Claimed by this write.  `size` before `count`, because the reader uses
            // `count != 0` as "this slot is live" and a slot whose count is set before
            // its size would be read as a different size.
            entry.size = ilSize;
            entry.count = 1;
            return;
        }
    }
    // Reached only when the table is genuinely full -- the probe now covers every
    // slot, so it is a capacity, not a work bound.  The old bound of 64 probes made
    // this fire at 83% load, which is the regime a real session lands in: 426
    // distinct sizes in a 512-slot table, 16.8% of slots empty, and linear probing's
    // cluster-length variance is exactly what a 64-step cap truncates.  The cost of
    // a full scan is one pass over the table on a compilation whose size is new,
    // which is nothing next to hashing 32 bytes of IL -- and with 4096 slots the
    // scan is a state a session does not reach either.
    InterlockedIncrement(&g_sizeHistogramOverflow);
}

void DrRecordObservedHash(uint32_t targetIndex, const uint8_t hash[32]) {
    if (hash == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    // Bounded and lock-free, because this runs under the JIT's lock on whichever
    // thread is compiling.  A duplicate is the common case -- the same same-sized
    // method compiles once, but the size pre-filter fires for every compilation of it
    // -- so the scan is what keeps the table from filling with one hash.
    const LONG count = g_observedCount;
    for (LONG i = 0; i < count && i < static_cast<LONG>(kMaxObserved); ++i) {
        const ObservedHash& seen = g_observed[i];
        if (seen.targetIndex == targetIndex && memcmp(seen.hash, hash, 32) == 0) {
            return;
        }
    }
    const LONG slot = InterlockedIncrement(&g_observedCount) - 1;
    if (slot >= static_cast<LONG>(kMaxObserved)) {
        // Full.  The count still grows so the report can say how many distinct hashes
        // there were, but no new hash is stored -- overwriting one would lose the
        // earlier near-miss, which is the more interesting one.
        InterlockedExchange(&g_observedDirty, 1);
        return;
    }
    g_observed[slot].targetIndex = targetIndex;
    memcpy(g_observed[slot].hash, hash, 32);
    InterlockedExchange(&g_observedDirty, 1);
}

void DrLogFlushObserved(void) {
    if (g_logPath[0] == L'\0') {
        return;
    }

    // THE HISTOGRAM IS WRITTEN FIRST, AND THE ORDER IS A FIX.
    //
    // The first version wrote it after the near-miss table's "nothing changed" guard.
    // With no near-misses recorded, that guard is true on every call, and the
    // histogram -- the instrument that exists precisely for the run where nothing
    // matches -- was never written at all.  A diagnostic that appears only when it is
    // not needed is not a diagnostic.
    WriteSizeHistogram();

    const uint32_t count = static_cast<uint32_t>(g_observedCount < 0 ? 0 : g_observedCount);
    const uint32_t stored = (count < kMaxObserved) ? count : kMaxObserved;

    // The near-miss table is rewritten only when something changed: the flusher runs
    // four times a second and the file is tiny, so rewriting it unconditionally would
    // be 240 writes a minute for no new information.  The histogram above has the same
    // guard inside it, keyed on its own total.
    if (g_observedDirty == 0 && g_observedWritten == count) {
        return;
    }
    g_observedDirty = 0;
    g_observedWritten = count;

    wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
    _snwprintf_s(path, MAX_PATH, _TRUNCATE, L"%s.observed", g_logPath);
    FILE* f = nullptr;
    if (_wfopen_s(&f, path, L"wb") != 0 || f == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    fprintf(f, "# every distinct IL hash seen whose SIZE matched a target but whose hash did not.\n");
    fprintf(f, "# A target whose record is absent here never had a size match at all, which is a\n");
    fprintf(f, "# different finding from a near-miss: it means the method was not compiled.\n");
    fprintf(f, "target_index,target_name,il_size,observed_hash\n");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < stored; ++i) {
        char name[DRELAY_TARGET_NAME_LEN] = {};
        uint16_t ilSize = 0;
        const uint32_t ti = g_observed[i].targetIndex;
        if (ti < DRELAY_MAX_TARGETS && g_shared != nullptr) {
            memcpy(name, g_shared->targets[ti].name, sizeof(name) - 1);
            ilSize = g_shared->targets[ti].ilSizeLow;
        }
        fprintf(f, "%u,%s,%u,", ti, name, static_cast<unsigned>(ilSize));
        for (int b = 0; b < 32; ++b) {
            fprintf(f, "%02X", g_observed[i].hash[b]);
        }
        fprintf(f, "\n");
    }
    if (count > stored) {
        fprintf(f, "# (%u further distinct hashes were seen and not stored)\n", count - stored);
    }
    fflush(f);
    fclose(f);
}


```

`hook/native/DrelayLog.h`:

```h
// DrelayLog.h -- the hook's own log, and why it is a ring rather than a file.
//
// The native side writes log lines from three places that must not block and
// must not allocate: the JIT callback (which runs under the JIT's own lock, on
// whichever thread happened to compile something), the frame-tick detour (which
// runs inside the game's frame), and the watcher thread.  A file handle in any
// of those is a way to make the game stutter or deadlock.
//
// So the hook writes into the shared block's log ring, and a background flusher
// thread drains the ring to disk.  If the flusher never runs, the ring still
// holds the last 512 lines, so a crash still leaves evidence.  The reader
// detects overflow by watching the sequence numbers rather than by trusting the
// row count -- an overflowed log says so instead of looking complete.

#ifndef DRELAY_LOG_H
#define DRELAY_LOG_H

#include "DrelayHookShared.h"

enum {
    DRLOG_INFO = 0,
    DRLOG_WARN = 1,
    DRLOG_ERR  = 2
};

// Configure the run directory.  Called once from the watcher thread; if it is
// never called, logging stays in-ring only, which is the correct degradation.
void DrLogInit(DrelayShared* shared, const wchar_t* runDir);

// Start the flusher.  Separate from Init because Init must happen before the
// bootstrap is running but the flusher must not start until the run directory
// is known to exist.
void DrLogStartFlusher(void);
void DrLogStopFlusher(void);

void DrLog(int level, const char* fmt, ...);

// Emit a line only if `once` has not been set.  Used for the per-frame paths,
// where "this failed" would otherwise be 60 lines a second.
void DrLogOnce(unsigned int* once, int level, const char* fmt, ...);

// Drain the ring to `path` and close.  Called on shutdown and on unload.
void DrLogFlushTo(const wchar_t* path);

// Drain the ring to the configured run directory's log, synchronously.  Called at
// each decision point in the watcher rather than waiting for the flusher thread:
// the flusher runs every 250 ms, a decision point may be the last thing the
// process does, and a log that only exists if the process survives long enough is
// not evidence.  Cheap enough to call a dozen times per run -- it writes only what
// is new.
void DrLogFlushNow(void);

// Record that a method of a target's IL size was compiled and its hash did NOT
// match.  Called from inside the JIT detour, so it must not allocate, must not
// take a lock the JIT could already hold, and must not touch a file: it writes to a
// fixed table in this DLL's data section and returns.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL, GIVEN THE TRACE RING.
//
// The ring holds the last 1024 compilations, and a gameplay session produces
// thousands, so a target that compiled early is *evicted* -- after which "not in
// the trace" is indistinguishable from "never compiled".  That ambiguity has already
// cost one wrong conclusion in this phase: `0 of 4 targets found` was read as "the
// operator never reached gameplay" when the trace simply could not have shown a
// first-use compilation from thirty seconds earlier.
//
// This table keeps up to 16 *distinct* size-matching hashes for the whole run, so
// the memory of a near-miss survives the ring.  Sixteen is generous: the same size
// recurring across thousands of compilations is almost always one or two methods.
void DrRecordObservedHash(uint32_t targetIndex, const uint8_t hash[32]);

// Count every compilation by IL size, for the whole run, in a bounded table.
//
// THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS, AND WHY THE RING CANNOT.
//
// A ring of 1024 rows over a stream of ~3600 compilations retains about eight
// seconds, so "the target is not in the trace" says nothing about the other fifty.
// Counting sizes instead of retaining rows makes the *whole* stream observable in a
// few hundred bytes, and it is additive: two runs' histograms can be compared.  A
// target whose IL size appears with a count of zero was never compiled; one that
// appears without a match was compiled and did not match -- and those two readings
// have completely different causes, which is the distinction three live runs have
// failed to make from rows alone.
//
// `size` is `ILCodeSize`; entries are keyed by size and counted up to
// `kMaxHistogramEntries` distinct sizes, after which the count of unrecorded sizes is
// tracked as a single overflow number rather than silently dropped.
void DrRecordCompileSize(uint32_t ilSize);

// Write the observed table to `<runDir>\targets-observed.csv` if it has changed.
// Called from the flusher thread; never from the JIT thread.
void DrLogFlushObserved(void);

// Log one line per target saying whether a method of that target's IL size was compiled
```
