`hook/tools/Capture-DodgeTerms.ps1`:

```ps1
# ============================================================================
#  Capture-DodgeTerms.ps1 -- one recording replayed with `--frame N` for every
#  frame the dodge moved, so the score's own terms can be aggregated.
#
#  WHY A SCRIPT RATHER THAN ONE COMMAND. `--frame N` explains exactly one frame
#  and the decision is one frame at a time, so a term breakdown over a recording
#  is 1 600 invocations of the harness. Doing that by hand is not a thing anyone
#  does twice, and a measurement that will not be repeated is a measurement that
#  will not be re-run on the next change.
#
#  Usage:
#    .\hook\tools\Capture-DodgeTerms.ps1 -Recording 20261015-153805-p26156 -Out ..\work\terms-p26156
#
#  It reads the decision dump the harness already writes to find the frames that
#  moved, then asks for each of them in full.
# ============================================================================

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Recording,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Out,
    [string]$Harness,
    [string]$Tag,
    [string[]]$FrameArgs = @()
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
if (-not [System.IO.Path]::IsPathRooted($Out)) { $Out = Join-Path $root $Out }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Out | Out-Null
if (-not $Harness) { $Harness = Join-Path $root 'tools\SolverHarness\bin\Release\SolverHarness.exe' }
if (-not $Tag) { $Tag = ($Recording -split '-')[-1] }

$runDir = Join-Path (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook') $Recording
$trace = Join-Path $runDir 'trace.jsonl'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trace)) { Write-Error "no trace at $trace"; exit 2 }

# The list of frames to explain, from the decision dump. `Move` is the only action
# whose score terms describe a direction; `stand` and the intent early-out do not
# go through the candidate score at all.
$dec = Join-Path $Out "dec-$Tag.txt"
& $Harness --trace $trace --decisions $dec @FrameArgs *> (Join-Path $Out "rec-$Tag.txt")
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -and $LASTEXITCODE -ne 1) { Write-Error 'the decision pass failed'; exit 2 }

$frames = @()
foreach ($line in Get-Content -LiteralPath $dec) {
    if ($line.StartsWith('#') -or -not $line.Trim()) { continue }
    $parts = $line -split '\|'
    if ($parts.Count -lt 4) { continue }
    if ($parts[1].Trim() -ne 'Move') { continue }
    $frames += [int]$parts[0].Trim()
}
Write-Host "explaining $($frames.Count) moving frame(s) of $Tag" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$terms = Join-Path $Out "terms-$Tag.txt"
$list = Join-Path $Out "frames-$Tag.txt"
Set-Content -LiteralPath $list -Value ($frames -join "`r`n")
# ONE PASS, NOT ONE PROCESS PER FRAME. `--frames-from` exists for this: the alternative is 1 100 to
# 5 000 harness launches, each re-parsing the same trace, which is a measurement that never gets
# re-run on the next change.
& $Harness --trace $trace --frames-from $list @FrameArgs *> $terms

Write-Host "terms into $terms" -ForegroundColor Green
python (Join-Path $root 'tools\dodge_term_report.py') $runDir $terms

```

`hook/tools/Capture-LiveDodgeDecisions.ps1`:

```ps1
# ============================================================================
#  Capture-LiveDodgeDecisions.ps1 -- replay the three ACTING live sessions
#  through the current SolverHarness, with a decision dump.
#
#  WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE SCRIPT FROM Capture-DodgeDecisions.ps1. That one covers
#  the five *recordings*, which are the project's long-standing invariant and
#  direction-split corpus. This one covers the live acting sessions of
#  SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md section 15.9.3c, which are the only traces where
#  the operator was actually playing against the dodge -- and therefore the only
#  ones that can say anything about the halt defect, whose measurement is the
#  player's own `moving` column.
#
#  `p6412`'s trace is the one section 15.12 is about: its `H` record carries an
#  unescaped newline from before the writer was fixed. The repaired copy is used
#  here (tools\repair-trace.py), and the run is named in the output so a reader
#  knows which file the numbers came from.
#
#  Usage:
#    .\tools\Capture-LiveDodgeDecisions.ps1 -Out .\work\live-after
# ============================================================================
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Out,
    [string]$Harness,
    [string]$P6412Trace,
    [string]$P32752Trace
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
if (-not [System.IO.Path]::IsPathRooted($Out)) { $Out = Join-Path $root $Out }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Out | Out-Null
if (-not $Harness) {
    $Harness = Join-Path $root 'tools\SolverHarness\bin\Release\SolverHarness.exe'
}
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Harness)) { Write-Error "no harness at $Harness"; exit 2 }
$Harness = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Harness).Path
if (-not $P6412Trace) { $P6412Trace = Join-Path $root 'work\repair\trace-fixed.jsonl' }
# `p32752` IS THE SECOND SESSION WITH THE SAME WRITER DEFECT, and it failed the same way the first
# version of this script did: the raw trace throws `expected a number at offset 0` at line 2. The
# repaired copy is one byte larger than the original -- `repair-trace.py` writes a trailing newline
# the recorder did not -- and is otherwise the same recording.
if (-not $P32752Trace) { $P32752Trace = Join-Path $root 'work\repair2\run\trace.jsonl' }
# THE DEFAULT ABOVE NO LONGER EXISTS. `work/` is scratch and is not versioned, and the raw traces
# named `trace.jsonl` were pruned as stale -- so on a fresh checkout, and on this one, the p32752
# session has no default trace to read. Say that here rather than letting a JSON parser fail on a
# missing file, and point at the surviving repaired copies for this session and its sibling.
foreach ($pair in @(
    @{ Path = $P6412Trace;  What = 'the p6412 trace' },
    @{ Path = $P32752Trace; What = 'the p32752 trace' }
)) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pair.Path)) {
        Write-Error @"
$($pair.What) is not at $($pair.Path).
The raw traces named trace.jsonl were pruned from work/ as stale, so a repaired copy has to be
supplied: pass -P6412Trace <file> and -P32752Trace <file>. Surviving repaired traces in this tree:
  $(Join-Path $root 'work\repair\trace-fixed.jsonl')
  $(Join-Path $root 'work\repair\trace-repaired.jsonl')
  $(Join-Path $root 'work\repair2\check.jsonl')
Repair a raw trace with: python tools\repair-trace.py <in.jsonl> <out.jsonl>
"@
        exit 2
    }
}
$hookRuns = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'

$sessions = @(
    @{ Name = 'p34740'; Run = '20261015-212859-p34740'; Trace = $null;                               Note = 'acting, the axial build' },
    @{ Name = 'p6412';  Run = '20261015-214418-p6412';  Trace = $P6412Trace;                          Note = 'acting, trace repaired per 15.12' },
    @{ Name = 'p32752'; Run = '20261015-214927-p32752'; Trace = $P32752Trace;                         Note = 'acting, third session, trace repaired' },
    @{ Name = 'p440';   Run = '20261015-212602-p440';   Trace = $null;                               Note = 'DRY RUN, the field test' }
)

foreach ($s in $sessions) {
    $runDir = Join-Path $hookRuns $s.Run
    $trace = $s.Trace
    if (-not $trace) { $trace = Join-Path $runDir 'trace.jsonl' }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trace)) {
        Write-Warning "no trace at $trace -- skipped"
        continue
    }
    $collisions = Join-Path $runDir 'bootstrap.log'
    Write-Host ("{0}: {1} [{2}]" -f $s.Name, $trace, $s.Note)
    & $Harness --trace $trace --collisions $collisions `
               --decisions (Join-Path $Out "dec-$($s.Name).txt") *> (Join-Path $Out "rec-$($s.Name).txt")
    Write-Host ("    exit {0}" -f $LASTEXITCODE)
}
Write-Host "captured into $Out" -ForegroundColor Green
exit 0
```

`hook/tools/Dump-JitVtable.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Dumps the CILJit vtable and names each slot's own resolving module.
.DESCRIPTION
    `compileMethod` is documented as slot 0 of the vtable returned by
    `clrjit!getJit`, and HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md verifies the four-slot layout by
    disassembly.  What no tool here has done is ask Windows, at runtime, where
    each slot *points* and which module that address belongs to -- which is the
    question that matters when a detour on slot 0 is never entered.

    It resolves `getJit`, reads the vtable, and for each of the first eight slots
    reports the address, its module, and whether it lies outside clrjit (which
    slot would then be indirection rather than an implementation).

    Exit codes: 0 = dumped, 1 = could not resolve, 2 = the game directory is wrong.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param([string] $GamePath = "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion")

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Write-Host "JIT vtable dump from $GamePath"
Write-Host ''

$clrjit = Join-Path $GamePath 'clrjit.dll'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $clrjit)) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: $clrjit not found" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 2
}

if (-not ('JitDump' -as [type])) {
    Add-Type -TypeDefinition @'
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

public static class JitDump
{
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Unicode, SetLastError = true)]
    public static extern IntPtr LoadLibraryW(string path);

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Ansi, SetLastError = true)]
    public static extern IntPtr GetProcAddress(IntPtr module, string name);

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
    public static extern IntPtr GetModuleHandle(string name);

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Unicode, SetLastError = true)]
    public static extern int GetModuleFileNameW(IntPtr module, System.Text.StringBuilder name, int size);

    [UnmanagedFunctionPointer(CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
    public delegate IntPtr GetJitFn();

    public static IntPtr GetJitExport(IntPtr clrjit) { return GetProcAddress(clrjit, "getJit"); }

    public static IntPtr CallGetJit(IntPtr fn)
    {
        return Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer<GetJitFn>(fn)();
    }

    public static IntPtr VtableSlot(IntPtr jitObject, int index)
    {
        IntPtr vtable = Marshal.ReadIntPtr(jitObject, 0);
        return Marshal.ReadIntPtr(vtable, index * IntPtr.Size);
    }

    /// <summary>The module that contains an address, as a file name, or empty.</summary>
    public static string ModuleOf(IntPtr address)
    {
        var buffer = new System.Text.StringBuilder(1024);
        // GetModuleHandleEx with FROM_ADDRESS and UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT.
        IntPtr module;
        if (!GetModuleHandleExW(0x00000004 | 0x00000002, address, out module))
        {
            return "";
        }
        return GetModuleFileNameW(module, buffer, buffer.Capacity) > 0 ? buffer.ToString() : "";
    }

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
    private static extern bool GetModuleHandleExW(uint flags, IntPtr address, out IntPtr module);
}
'@ -ErrorAction Stop
}

$module = [JitDump]::LoadLibraryW($clrjit)
if ($module -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: LoadLibraryW($clrjit) failed" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
Write-Host ("clrjit.dll    : {0} (module 0x{1:X})" -f $clrjit, $module.ToInt64())

$getJit = [JitDump]::GetJitExport($module)
if ($getJit -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) {
    Write-Host 'FAIL: clrjit!getJit is not exported' -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
$jitObject = [JitDump]::CallGetJit($getJit)
Write-Host ("getJit        : 0x{0:X}" -f $getJit.ToInt64())
Write-Host ("CILJit object : 0x{0:X}" -f $jitObject.ToInt64())

$vtable = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ReadIntPtr($jitObject, 0)
Write-Host ("vtable        : 0x{0:X}" -f $vtable.ToInt64())
Write-Host ''
Write-Host 'slot  address              module'
Write-Host '----  -------------------  ------------------------------------------'
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 8; $i++) {
    $slot = [JitDump]::VtableSlot($jitObject, $i)
    $where = if ($slot -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { '<null>' } else { [JitDump]::ModuleOf($slot) }
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($where)) { $where = '<no module: not mapped>' }
    Write-Host ("{0,4}  0x{1:X16}  {2}" -f $i, $slot.ToInt64(), $where)
}
Write-Host ''
Write-Host 'Slot 0 is what the hook detours. If its module is not clrjit.dll, the'
Write-Host 'detour is being placed on indirection rather than on the JIT itself.'

```

`hook/tools/Fingerprint.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Phase 0 gate: prove the installed game is the build the hook was written for.

.DESCRIPTION
    Runs every static check the hook depends on and reports one line per component, then
    passes or fails as a whole. This is the script that turns "the hook crashed the game"
    into "the hook refused to install and said which component changed".

    It is deliberately read-only: it opens the game's files for reading and writes nothing
    except its own report.

    Checks, in the order they matter:
      1. the runtime's tiered-compilation setting   -- the assumption the whole design rests on
      2. the game assembly is pure IL, not ReadyToRun
      3. the assembly's size matches a known build  -- two apphosts ship DIFFERENT builds
      4. clrjit's ICorJitCompiler vtable layout     -- compileMethod slot and GUID slot
      5. the runtime DLL versions
      6. the target-method IL hashes                -- reported as a gap until Phase 0 generates them

.PARAMETER GamePath
    The game install directory, e.g. "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion".
    Defaults to the Steam library location recorded in known-build.json's "recordedFrom".

.PARAMETER Quiet
    Print only the verdict line.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Fingerprint.ps1
    .\Fingerprint.ps1 -GamePath "D:\Games\Darza's Dominion"

.NOTES
    Exit codes: 0 = all checks passed, 1 = at least one check failed, 2 = could not run
    (install not found, known-build.json unreadable).
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$GamePath,
    [switch]$Quiet
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$here = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
# known-build.json is the record the whole research directory is written against, so it lives
# beside the documents rather than inside tools/.
$recordPath = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $here) 'known-build.json'

if (-not (Test-Path $recordPath)) {
    Write-Error "known-build.json not found at $recordPath"
    exit 2
}
$known = Get-Content $recordPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json

if (-not $GamePath) {
    $GamePath = $known.recordedFrom
    if ($GamePath -and -not (Test-Path $GamePath)) {
        Write-Error "The recorded install path no longer exists: $GamePath`nPass -GamePath explicitly."
        exit 2
    }
}
if (-not $GamePath -or -not (Test-Path $GamePath)) {
    Write-Error "Game install not found. Pass -GamePath <dir>."
    exit 2
}

$assembly = Join-Path $GamePath $known.assembly.file
$coreclr  = Join-Path $GamePath 'coreclr.dll'
$clrjit   = Join-Path $GamePath 'clrjit.dll'
$runtimeconfig = Join-Path $GamePath 'DarzasDominion.runtimeconfig.json'

# Each check appends { Name; Expect; Actual; Ok } so the report and the verdict share one source.
$results = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
function Check([string]$name, $expect, $actual) {
    $ok = ("$expect" -eq "$actual")
    $results.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Name = $name; Expect = $expect; Actual = $actual; Ok = $ok })
    return $ok
}
function Note([string]$name, [string]$text) {
    $results.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Name = $name; Expect = $text; Actual = '<informational>'; Ok = $true })
}
# A "gap" is a check we cannot run yet; it must not be reported as a pass.
$gaps = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]

# --- minimal PE readers, so this script has no dependency on the probe scripts ------------
function Read-PE {
    param([string]$Path)
    $b = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
    $u16 = { param($o) [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b, $o) }
    $u32 = { param($o) [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $o) }
    $pe = [int](& $u32 0x3C)
    $coff = $pe + 4
    $opt = $coff + 20
    $magic = & $u16 $opt
    $dd = if ($magic -eq 0x20B) { $opt + 112 } else { $opt + 96 }
    $nsec = & $u16 ($coff + 2)
    $sizeOpt = & $u16 ($coff + 16)
    $sec0 = $opt + $sizeOpt
    $secs = @()
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $nsec; $i++) {
        $s = $sec0 + $i * 40
        $secs += [pscustomobject]@{
            Name = ([System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($b, $s, 8)).Trim([char]0)
            VA   = & $u32 ($s + 12)
            VS   = & $u32 ($s + 8)
            Raw  = & $u32 ($s + 20)
        }
    }
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Bytes = $b; Magic = $magic; DataDirs = $dd; Sections = $secs
        ImageBase = if ($magic -eq 0x20B) { [BitConverter]::ToUInt64($b, $opt + 24) } else { [uint64](& $u32 ($opt + 28)) }
    }
}
function RvaToOff($pe, [uint32]$rva) {
    foreach ($s in $pe.Sections) {
        if ($rva -ge $s.VA -and $rva -lt ($s.VA + $s.VS)) { return [int]($rva - $s.VA + $s.Raw) }
    }
    return -1
}

# --- 1. tiered compilation ----------------------------------------------------------------
if (Test-Path $runtimeconfig) {
    $rc = Get-Content $runtimeconfig -Raw
    $tcMatch = [regex]::Match($rc, '"System\.Runtime\.TieredCompilation"\s*:\s*(true|false)')
    if ($tcMatch.Success) {
        $actual = [bool]::Parse($tcMatch.Groups[1].Value)
        Check 'TieredCompilation off' $known.runtime.tieredCompilation $actual | Out-Null
    } else {
        Check 'TieredCompilation off' $known.runtime.tieredCompilation '<absent>' | Out-Null
    }
    $tfm = [regex]::Match($rc, '"tfm"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"').Groups[1].Value
    Check 'target framework' $known.runtime.tfm $tfm | Out-Null
} else {
    Check 'runtimeconfig.json present' 'yes' 'no' | Out-Null
}

# --- 2 & 3. the game assembly ------------------------------------------------------------
if (Test-Path $assembly) {
    $pe = Read-PE $assembly
    $cliOff = RvaToOff $pe ([uint32]([BitConverter]::ToUInt32($pe.Bytes, $pe.DataDirs + 14 * 8)))
    $flags = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($pe.Bytes, $cliOff + 16)
    $mnh = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($pe.Bytes, $cliOff + 0x40)

    Check 'assembly ILONLY set' $true ([bool]($flags -band 0x1)) | Out-Null
    Check 'assembly not ReadyToRun' $known.assembly.managedNativeHeaderRva $mnh | Out-Null

    $size = (Get-Item $assembly).Length
    $knownSize = if ($size -eq $known.assembly.sizeOpenGlVariant) {
        Note 'which apphost' 'OpenGL variant -- NOT the analysed build'
        $known.assembly.sizeOpenGlVariant
    } else { $known.assembly.size }
    Check 'assembly size' $knownSize $size | Out-Null

    # Size alone does not detect an edit that preserves length. A mutation test proved that:
    # flipping one byte of the assembly left every size-based check passing. The content hash
    # is what actually ties us to the build whose IL hashes the target table was made from.
    $sha = (Get-FileHash $assembly -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $knownSha = if ($size -eq $known.assembly.sizeOpenGlVariant) {
        $known.assembly.sha256OpenGlVariant
    } else { $known.assembly.sha256 }
    if ($knownSha) {
        Check 'assembly SHA-256' $knownSha $sha | Out-Null
    } else {
        $gaps.Add('assembly SHA-256: not recorded in known-build.json')
    }
} else {
    Check 'assembly present' 'yes' 'no' | Out-Null
}

# --- 4. the JIT vtable --------------------------------------------------------------------
if (Test-Path $clrjit) {
    $jit = Read-PE $clrjit
    # Resolve getJit from the export directory rather than hardcoding an RVA.
    # IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY layout: AddressOfFunctions at +28, AddressOfNames at +32,
    # AddressOfNameOrdinals at +36. The ordinal is an INDEX into AddressOfFunctions (after
    # subtracting OrdinalBase), and it is NOT the same as the loop counter unless the ordinals
    # happen to be contiguous from 0 -- which they are not in general.
    $expRva = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $jit.DataDirs)
    $expOff = RvaToOff $jit $expRva
    $found = $null
    if ($expOff -ge 0) {
        $nNames   = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $expOff + 24)
        $aFuncs   = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $expOff + 28)
        $aNames   = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $expOff + 32)
        $aOrds    = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $expOff + 36)
        $namesOff = RvaToOff $jit $aNames
        $funcsOff = RvaToOff $jit $aFuncs
        $ordsOff  = RvaToOff $jit $aOrds
        for ($i = 0; $i -lt $nNames; $i++) {
            $nameRva = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $namesOff + $i * 4)
            $nameOff = RvaToOff $jit $nameRva
            if ($nameOff -lt 0) { continue }
            $end = $nameOff; while ($jit.Bytes[$end] -ne 0) { $end++ }
            $nm = [System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($jit.Bytes, $nameOff, $end - $nameOff)
            if ($nm -eq 'getJit') {
                $ord = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($jit.Bytes, $ordsOff + $i * 2)
                $found = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($jit.Bytes, $funcsOff + $ord * 4)
                break
            }
        }
    }
    if ($null -ne $found) {
        # getJit body ends with `lea rcx,[g_CILJit]`; recover the absolute target from the
        # instruction stream by scanning for the RIP-relative LEA that feeds `and rax,rcx`.
        $bodyOff = RvaToOff $jit ([uint32]$found)
        $gCilJitRva = $null
        for ($i = 0; $i -lt 32; $i++) {
            # 48 8D 0D <rel32>  = lea rcx,[rip+rel32]
            if ($jit.Bytes[$bodyOff + $i] -eq 0x48 -and $jit.Bytes[$bodyOff + $i + 1] -eq 0x8D -and $jit.Bytes[$bodyOff + $i + 2] -eq 0x0D) {
                $rel = [BitConverter]::ToInt32($jit.Bytes, $bodyOff + $i + 3)
                $gCilJitRva = [uint32]($found + $i + 7 + $rel)
                break
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $gCilJitRva) {
            $objOff = RvaToOff $jit $gCilJitRva
            $vtVa = [BitConverter]::ToUInt64($jit.Bytes, $objOff)
            $vtRva = [uint32]($vtVa - $jit.ImageBase)
            $vtOff = RvaToOff $jit $vtRva
            # Count leading slots that point inside the image's executable section.
            $codeSlots = 0
            for ($k = 0; $k -lt 8; $k++) {
                $slotVa = [BitConverter]::ToUInt64($jit.Bytes, $vtOff + $k * 8)
                if ($slotVa -ge $jit.ImageBase -and $slotVa -lt ($jit.ImageBase + [uint64]$jit.Sections[0].VS + 0x1000)) {
                    $codeSlots++
                } else { break }
            }
            Check 'JIT vtable code slots' $known.jit.vtableCodeSlotCount $codeSlots | Out-Null
            Note 'compileMethod slot' "$($known.jit.compileMethodSlot) (unchanged on every .NET version)"
        } else {
            Check 'locate g_CILJit' 'a lea rcx,[rip+rel] in getJit' 'not found' | Out-Null
        }
    } else {
        Check 'clrjit exports getJit' 'yes' 'no' | Out-Null
    }
} else {
    Check 'clrjit.dll present' 'yes' 'no' | Out-Null
}

# --- 5. runtime versions ------------------------------------------------------------------
# FileVersion is "9,0,2026,41315 @Commit: <sha>", so normalise it: take the four numeric parts
# (comma-separated) and join them with dots. Comparing the raw string would fail on formatting
# rather than on a real version change, which is the wrong kind of failure for a gate.
foreach ($dll in @('coreclr.dll', 'clrjit.dll')) {
    $p = Join-Path $GamePath $dll
    if (Test-Path $p) {
        $raw = (Get-Item $p).VersionInfo.FileVersion
        $numeric = ([regex]::Match($raw, '^\s*(\d+)[,.](\d+)[,.](\d+)[,.](\d+)'))
        $norm = if ($numeric.Success) {
            '{0}.{1}.{2}.{3}' -f $numeric.Groups[1].Value, $numeric.Groups[2].Value,
                                $numeric.Groups[3].Value, $numeric.Groups[4].Value
        } else { $raw }
        Check "$dll version" $known.runtime.coreclrBuild $norm | Out-Null
    }
}

# --- 6. target method IL hashes -----------------------------------------------------------
# Two layers, and the difference matters.
#
#   (a) structural: for each target, the instruction stream at its recorded RVA must be
#       exactly `ilSize` bytes long, and hashing those bytes must reproduce `ilHash`.
#       This is the check that catches "a game patch changed one target's IL" -- the
#       failure the whole gate exists for -- and it needs no other tooling.
#
#   (b) executable: the hash must also be what tools/il_index.py regenerates from the
#       metadata, which is how the table is produced. Run it and compare.
#
# A same-length byte flip in a target's IL passes every file-level check (that is what the
# mutation test proved) but cannot pass (a).
$hashes = @($known.targetMethods.PSObject.Properties |
    Where-Object { $_.Name -notlike '_*' -and $null -ne $_.Value })

if ($hashes.Count -eq 0) {
    $gaps.Add('target-method IL hashes: not generated yet (Phase 0, tools/il_index.py)')
} elseif (-not (Test-Path $assembly)) {
    $gaps.Add('target-method IL hashes: cannot check, the assembly was not found')
} else {
    $pe = Read-PE $assembly
    foreach ($prop in $hashes) {
        $t = $prop.Value
        $name = "$($t.role)"
        if (-not $t.rva -or -not $t.ilHash -or -not $t.ilSize) {
            Check "target $name" 'rva, ilSize and ilHash recorded' 'incomplete entry' | Out-Null
            continue
        }
        # tiny header: high 6 bits are the size, code at +1. fat header: 12 bytes unless
        # MoreSects is set, in which case the +12 field carries the real header size.
        $bodyOff = RvaToOff $pe ([uint32]$t.rva)
        if ($bodyOff -lt 0) {
            Check "target $name IL" 'RVA inside a section' 'not mapped' | Out-Null
            continue
        }
        $first = $pe.Bytes[$bodyOff]
        if (($first -band 0x03) -eq 0x02) {
            $codeOff = $bodyOff + 1
            $codeSize = $first -shr 2
        } else {
            $flagsAndSize = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($pe.Bytes, $bodyOff)
            $codeSize = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($pe.Bytes, $bodyOff + 4)
            if ($flagsAndSize -band 0x0008) {
                # MoreSects. The documented rule is to take the +12 field, but this build
                # disagrees with it for DarzaWindow::Update (the FlagsAndSize field says 12,
                # the +12 field says 60, and the code is at +12). il_index.py resolves it by
                # decoding both candidates; the tie-breaker here is the recorded ilSize,
                # which is legitimate because ilSize was itself confirmed against the
                # disassembly and the two candidates are 48 bytes apart.
                $declared = ($flagsAndSize -shr 12) * 4
                $alt = ([BitConverter]::ToUInt16($pe.Bytes, $bodyOff + 12) -shr 12) * 4
                $codeOff = $bodyOff + $declared
                if ($alt -ne $declared -and $alt -ge 12 -and $alt -le 64) {
                    $altSize = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($pe.Bytes, $bodyOff + 4)
                    # The recorded ilSize is the same either way (it is CodeSize), so pick
                    # the candidate whose *own* header reads consistently: the one that puts
                    # the code where the comment says it is. Prefer the declared header
                    # unless it would place the code inside the +12 size field itself.
                    if ($declared -lt 12) { $codeOff = $bodyOff + $alt }
                }
            } else {
                $codeOff = $bodyOff + (($flagsAndSize -shr 12) * 4)
            }
        }
        if ($codeSize -ne $t.ilSize) {
            Check "target $name ilSize" $t.ilSize $codeSize | Out-Null
            continue
        }
        $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
        try {
            $digest = $sha.ComputeHash($pe.Bytes, $codeOff, $codeSize)
        } finally {
            $sha.Dispose()
        }
        $actual = -join ($digest | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString('X2') })
        Check "target $name IL hash" $t.ilHash $actual | Out-Null
    }

    # (b) the executable half: regenerate and compare.
    $ilIndex = Join-Path $here 'il_index.py'
    $python = Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ((Test-Path $ilIndex) -and $python) {
        $json = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("drelay_il_index_{0}.json" -f $PID)
        try {
            & $python.Source $ilIndex --check --json $json 2>&1 | Out-Null
            $regen = $null
            if (Test-Path $json) { $regen = Get-Content $json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json }
            $diff = @()
            if ($regen) {
                foreach ($prop in $hashes) {
                    $fresh = $regen.targets.($prop.Name)
                    if (-not $fresh) {
                        $diff += "$($prop.Name): absent from the regenerated table"
                    } elseif ($fresh.ilHash -ne $prop.Value.ilHash) {
                        $diff += ("$($prop.Name): recorded {0}, regenerated {1}" -f `
                                  $prop.Value.ilHash, $fresh.ilHash)
                    }
                }
            }
            if (-not $regen) {
                $gaps.Add('target IL hashes: il_index.py produced no JSON to compare against')
            } elseif ($diff.Count -gt 0) {
                foreach ($d in $diff) {
                    Check 'target IL hash (regenerated)' 'same as recorded' $d | Out-Null
                }
            } else {
                Note 'target IL hashes' ("{0} targets re-derived by il_index.py, all matching" -f $hashes.Count)
            }
        } finally {
            if (Test-Path $json) { Remove-Item $json -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
        }
    } else {
        $gaps.Add('target IL hashes: python or il_index.py unavailable, so the recorded hashes were checked physically but not re-derived')
    }
}
$gaps.Add('effective runtime environment: cannot be read from a script (check DOTNET_TieredCompilation is unset in the launcher)')
$gaps.Add('the loaded assembly MVID: must be re-checked in-process at attach')

# --- report ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not $Quiet) {
    Write-Output ''
    Write-Output "Fingerprint of $GamePath"
    Write-Output ("  recorded from : {0} ({1})" -f $known.recordedFrom, $known.recorded)
    Write-Output ''
    Write-Output ("  {0,-28} {1,-22} {2,-22} {3}" -f 'CHECK', 'EXPECTED', 'ACTUAL', 'RESULT')
    Write-Output ("  {0,-28} {1,-22} {2,-22} {3}" -f ('-' * 28), ('-' * 22), ('-' * 22), ('-' * 6))
    foreach ($r in $results) {
        $verdict = if ($r.Actual -eq '<informational>') { 'info' } elseif ($r.Ok) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }
        Write-Output ("  {0,-28} {1,-22} {2,-22} {3}" -f $r.Name, $r.Expect, $r.Actual, $verdict)
    }
    if ($gaps.Count -gt 0) {
        Write-Output ''
        Write-Output '  Known gaps (not failures, but not passes either):'
        foreach ($g in $gaps) { Write-Output "    - $g" }
    }
}

$failed = @($results | Where-Object { -not $_.Ok })
if ($failed.Count -eq 0) {
    if (-not $Quiet) { Write-Output '' }
    Write-Output ("FINGERPRINT OK -- {0} checks passed, {1} known gap(s)" -f $results.Count, $gaps.Count)
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output ''
    Write-Output ("FINGERPRINT FAILED -- {0} of {1} checks failed:" -f $failed.Count, $results.Count)
    foreach ($f in $failed) { Write-Output ("  {0}: expected {1}, got {2}" -f $f.Name, $f.Expect, $f.Actual) }
    Write-Output ''
    Write-Output 'The hook must NOT be installed against this build. Regenerate known-build.json'
    Write-Output 'after establishing what changed, and re-verify the target IL hashes.'
    exit 1
}

```

`hook/tools/Get-PeExports.ps1`:

```ps1
param([Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$Path)
$b = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
function U16($o){ [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b,$o) }
function U32($o){ [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b,$o) }
$e=[int](U32 0x3C); $coff=$e+4; $nsec=U16 ($coff+2); $so=U16 ($coff+16); $opt=$coff+20
$magic=U16 $opt
$dd = if ($magic -eq 0x20B) { $opt+112 } else { $opt+96 }
$sec0=$opt+$so
$secs=@(); for($i=0;$i -lt $nsec;$i++){$s=$sec0+$i*40; $secs+=[pscustomobject]@{Name=([System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($b,$s,8)).Trim([char]0);VA=U32 ($s+12);VS=U32 ($s+8);Raw=U32 ($s+20)}}
function R2O([uint32]$r){foreach($s in $secs){if($r -ge $s.VA -and $r -lt ($s.VA+$s.VS)){return [int]($r-$s.VA+$s.Raw)}};return -1}
$exp = U32 $dd
if ($exp -eq 0) { Write-Output "$([System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path)): no exports"; return }
$eo=R2O $exp
$nn=U32 ($eo+24); $af=U32 ($eo+28); $an=U32 ($eo+32); $ao=U32 ($eo+36)
Write-Output "== $([System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($Path))  ($nn exported names)"
$names=@()
for($i=0;$i -lt $nn;$i++){
  $nr=U32 ((R2O $an)+$i*4); $no=R2O $nr; $n=''; $k=$no
  while($b[$k] -ne 0){$n+=[char]$b[$k];$k++}
  $ord=U16 ((R2O $ao)+$i*2); $rva=U32 ((R2O $af)+$ord*4)
  $names += [pscustomobject]@{N=$n;RVA=$rva}
}
$want = @('getCLRRuntimeHost','coreclr_initialize','coreclr_create_delegate','coreclr_execute_assembly','CLRDataCreateInstance','CLRDataCreateInstance2','MiniDumpWriteDump','getJit','jitStartup','hostfxr_initialize_for_runtime_config','hostfxr_get_runtime_delegate','DllGetClassObject','CoreCLRCreateCppCliType','coreclr_shutdown')
foreach($w in $want){ $m = $names | Where-Object { $_.N -eq $w }; if($m){ foreach($mm in $m){ Write-Output ("   {0,-40} RVA=0x{1:X}" -f $mm.N,$mm.RVA) } } }
if ($names.Count -gt 0) { Write-Output ("   (first 12 exports: " + (($names | Select-Object -First 12 | ForEach-Object { $_.N }) -join ', ') + ")") }

```

`hook/tools/LauncherHarness/LauncherHarness.csproj`:

```csproj
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <!--
    LauncherHarness: the launcher's configuration, without a game, a registry or a console.

    WHY IT COMPILES THE LAUNCHER'S SOURCES RATHER THAN REFERENCING ITS DLL.

    Same argument as SolverHarness, and the same mechanism.  The launcher's assembly is an
    executable whose entry point starts a game, so a test process cannot reference it without
    inheriting that; and a second implementation of the merge in the harness would agree with the
    shipped one until it did not, which is the failure HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md section 13 is
    written to prevent.  `Compile Include` puts the SAME source into both places, so a change to
    the precedence rules breaks this build immediately.

    WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT COMPILED HERE:

      * Program.cs: it owns `Main`, the console and the P/Invokes; the checks that are about it
        (C5's pause rule) read it as source instead, which is stated where it happens;
      * DiscoveryWindows.cs: the registry and the filesystem.  Everything *decided* about
        discovery is in Discovery.cs, which is compiled here and driven through a fake
        environment, so the Steam library walk is tested with no Steam installed.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <AssemblyName>LauncherHarness</AssemblyName>
    <RootNamespace>Drelay.LauncherHarness</RootNamespace>
    <UseAppHost>true</UseAppHost>
    <AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>false</AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>
    <Nullable>disable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>disable</ImplicitUsings>
    <LangVersion>12.0</LangVersion>
    <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>
    <Deterministic>true</Deterministic>
    <!--
      CS0649 is `Options.RunDirectory` never being assigned, in THIS compilation.  The only code
      that assigns it is `Program.Run`, which this project deliberately does not compile; the field
      is real, used, and warned about in neither place that ships.  Suppressing it here keeps the
      warning list meaningful for the sources that do compile.
    -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);CS0649</NoWarn>
    <!--
      WarningLevel is deliberately not inherited from managed/Directory.Build.props: this project
      lives under hook/tools, which that props file does not reach, and the harness is not shipped
      into the game.
    -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\Settings.cs" Link="Launcher\Settings.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\CommandLine.cs" Link="Launcher\CommandLine.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\ConfigFile.cs" Link="Launcher\ConfigFile.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\Discovery.cs" Link="Launcher\Discovery.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\EnvironmentBlock.cs" Link="Launcher\EnvironmentBlock.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\Configuration.cs" Link="Launcher\Configuration.cs" />
    <Compile Include="..\..\managed\Drelay.Launcher\FirstRun.cs" Link="Launcher\FirstRun.cs" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

```

`hook/tools/LauncherHarness/Program.cs`:

```cs
// Program.cs -- the launcher's offline harness.
//
// WHAT THIS PROGRAM IS FOR, IN ONE SENTENCE: it proves the launcher's configuration behaviour --
// the four sources, their precedence, the file, the discovery walk and the environment it builds
// -- without a game, a Steam install, a registry or a console.
//
// THE INVARIANTS IT CHECKS ARE HANDOFF-LAUNCH-CONFIG.md SECTION 13'S TABLE, BY NAME:
//
//   C1  a config field never overrides a value typed on the command line
//   C2  an unset field is absent from the child's environment, not set to the default
//   C3  a typo in AutoAim refuses and names the field
//   C4  discovery never returns a directory containing the OpenGL assembly
//   C5  a zero-argument run with redirected input never pauses
//   C6  the written template contains no test-harness key
//   C7  every config field has a flag, and every user-facing flag a field
//
// plus the boundary cases section 11 asks for by step.  Each check prints one line; a failure
// prints what it expected and what it found, and the process exits 1.
//
// THE CODE UNDER TEST IS THE SHIPPED CODE.  Every source file compiled here is the launcher's own
// (`Compile Include` in the csproj), so this program cannot agree with a copy of the rules while
// disagreeing with the rules.  Two things are read as *source* rather than executed, and both say
// so where they do it: `Program.Main`'s pause rule (C5) and, when given
// `--known-build`, the pinned record the generated table comes from.
//
// Usage:
//   LauncherHarness                       run every check
//   LauncherHarness --check c4            run one
//   LauncherHarness --source PATH         also check Program.cs's pause rule (C5)
//   LauncherHarness --known-build PATH    also check the pinned record has what discovery needs
//
// Exit codes: 0 = every check passed, 1 = a check failed, 2 = usage or an internal error.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;
using Drelay.Launcher;

namespace Drelay.LauncherHarness
{
    internal sealed class CheckException : Exception
    {
        public CheckException(string message) : base(message) { }
    }

    internal static class Program
    {
        private static readonly List<string> Failures = new List<string>();
        private static readonly List<string> Ran = new List<string>();
        private static string _tmp;
        private static string _programSource;
        private static string _knownBuild;

        private static int Main(string[] args)
        {
            string only = null;
            for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
            {
                switch (args[i])
                {
                    case "--check":
                        if (i + 1 >= args.Length) { Usage(); return 2; }
                        only = args[++i];
                        break;
                    case "--source":
                        if (i + 1 >= args.Length) { Usage(); return 2; }
                        _programSource = args[++i];
                        break;
                    case "--known-build":
                        if (i + 1 >= args.Length) { Usage(); return 2; }
                        _knownBuild = args[++i];
                        break;
                    case "--print-template":
                        // WHAT A FIRST RUN WILL ACTUALLY WRITE, without starting a game.  The
                        // template is the release's default behaviour (§16.2), so being able to read
                        // it from the build is worth one option.
                        Console.Write(ConfigFile.Template());
                        return 0;
                    case "--help":
                    case "-h":
                        Usage();
                        return 0;
                    default:
                        Console.Error.WriteLine("unknown option: " + args[i]);
                        Usage();
                        return 2;
                }
            }

            try
            {
                _tmp = MakeTemp();
            }
            catch (CheckException ex)
            {
                Console.Error.WriteLine("FAILED: " + ex.Message);
                return 2;
            }

            var checks = new List<KeyValuePair<string, Action>>
            {
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c1 per-field precedence", C1),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c2 the child's environment", C2),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c3 a typo names its field", C3),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c4 discovery and the OpenGL gate", C4),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c5 the pause rule", C5),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c6 the first-run template", C6),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c7 config fields and flags, both directions", C7),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("c8 the pinned record discovery needs", C8),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("r1 the config reader's boundaries", R1),
                new KeyValuePair<string, Action>("r2 the command line's boundaries", R2),
            };

            foreach (var check in checks)
            {
                if (only != null && !check.Key.StartsWith(only, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { continue; }
                Ran.Add(check.Key);
                try
                {
                    check.Value();
                    Console.WriteLine("ok   " + check.Key);
                }
                catch (CheckException ex)
                {
                    Failures.Add(check.Key);
                    Console.WriteLine("FAIL " + check.Key);
                    Console.WriteLine("       " + ex.Message);
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    Failures.Add(check.Key);
                    Console.WriteLine("FAIL " + check.Key);
                    Console.WriteLine("       " + ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message);
                }
            }

            try { Directory.Delete(_tmp, true); } catch (Exception) { }

            Console.WriteLine();
            if (Ran.Count == 0)
            {
                Console.Error.WriteLine("no check matched '" + only + "'");
                return 2;
            }
            if (Failures.Count > 0)
            {
                Console.Error.WriteLine("LAUNCHER CHECKS FAILED: " + string.Join(", ", Failures.ToArray()));
                return 1;
            }
            Console.WriteLine("LAUNCHER CHECKS OK -- " + Ran.Count + " check(s)");
            return 0;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// A directory this process may write in.
        ///
        /// TWO CANDIDATES, BECAUSE %TEMP% IS NOT ALWAYS WRITABLE.  A process started from the DSH
        /// agent harness is confined to the repository, so `Path.GetTempPath()` -- which is under
        /// `%LOCALAPPDATA%` -- fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED before a single check has run.  That
        /// is a property of where this program is started from rather than of the launcher, and it
        /// is the same quirk the README records for `--runroot`.  The fallback keeps the checks
        /// runnable from either place.
        /// </summary>
        private static string MakeTemp()
        {
            string name = "drelay-launcher-harness-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
            var candidates = new List<string>
            {
                Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), name),
                Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "harness-tmp", name),
            };
            foreach (string candidate in candidates)
            {
                try
                {
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(candidate);
                    return candidate;
                }
                catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException || ex is UnauthorizedAccessException)
                {
                }
            }
            throw new CheckException("no writable directory for the harness's temporary files");
        }

        private static void Usage()
        {            Console.WriteLine(@"LauncherHarness -- the launcher's configuration, offline.

  --check NAME     run only the checks whose name starts with NAME (c1..c8, r1, r2)
  --source PATH    Program.cs, so C5 can assert Main's single pause is behind FirstRun.ShouldPause
  --known-build PATH  hook/known-build.json, so C8 can assert the record carries the app id and
                      the OpenGL assembly size that discovery names the variant with
  --print-template print the configuration file a first run writes, and exit
  --help           this text");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // helpers
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void Expect(bool condition, string what)
        {
            if (!condition) { throw new CheckException(what); }
        }

        private static void ExpectEqual(string expected, string actual, string what)
        {
            if (!string.Equals(expected, actual, StringComparison.Ordinal))
            {
                throw new CheckException(what + ": expected '" + expected + "', got '" + actual + "'");
            }
        }

        private static void ExpectEqual(int expected, int actual, string what)
        {
            if (expected != actual)
            {
                throw new CheckException(what + ": expected " + expected + ", got " + actual);
            }
        }

        private static void ExpectEqual(double expected, double actual, string what)
        {
            if (Math.Abs(expected - actual) > 1e-9)
            {
                throw new CheckException(what + ": expected " + expected + ", got " + actual);
            }
        }

        private static Settings Empty()
        {
            return new Settings();
        }

        /// <summary>The command line as a `Settings`, refusing to continue if it will not parse.</summary>
        private static Settings Cli(params string[] args)
        {
            List<string> gameArguments;
            return Cli(args, out gameArguments);
        }

        private static Settings Cli(string[] args, out List<string> gameArguments)
        {
            Settings settings;
            bool help;
            string error;
            if (!CommandLine.TryParse(args, out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error))
            {
                throw new CheckException("the command line [" + string.Join(" ", args) + "] was refused: " + error);
            }
            return settings;
        }

        /// <summary>Write a config file and read it back through the shipped reader.</summary>
        private static Settings Config(string json, out string path, out List<string> recognised)
        {
            path = Path.Combine(_tmp, "config-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".json");
            File.WriteAllText(path, json, new UTF8Encoding(false));
            Settings settings;
            string error;
            if (!ConfigFile.TryRead(path, out settings, out recognised, out error))
            {
                throw new CheckException("the config was refused: " + error);
            }
            return settings;
        }

        private static Settings Config(string json)
        {
            string path;
            List<string> recognised;
            return Config(json, out path, out recognised);
        }

        /// <summary>Read a config file and return the refusal, or null when it was accepted.</summary>
        private static string ConfigError(string json, out string path)
        {
            path = Path.Combine(_tmp, "config-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".json");
            File.WriteAllText(path, json, new UTF8Encoding(false));
            Settings settings;
            List<string> recognised;
            string error;
            if (ConfigFile.TryRead(path, out settings, out recognised, out error)) { return null; }
            return error;
        }

        private static Options Resolve(Settings config, Settings cli, IDiscoveryEnv env)
        {
            ResolveResult result = Configuration.Resolve(
                config, cli, new List<string>(), env ?? new FakeEnv(), Pinned(), @"C:\app");
            if (result.Outcome != ResolveOutcome.Ready)
            {
                throw new CheckException("expected a usable configuration, got " + result.Outcome
                                         + (result.Error != null ? ": " + result.Error : string.Empty));
            }
            return result.Options;
        }

        private static ResolveResult ResolveRaw(Settings config, Settings cli, IDiscoveryEnv env)
        {
            return Configuration.Resolve(
                config, cli, new List<string>(), env ?? new FakeEnv(), Pinned(), @"C:\app");
        }

        /// <summary>The pinned build the harness tests against -- deliberately not the real one.</summary>
        private static PinnedBuild Pinned()
        {
            return new PinnedBuild
            {
                RecordedFrom = @"E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion",
                ExecutableFileName = "DarzasDominion.exe",
                AssemblyFileName = "DarzasDominion.dll",
                AssemblySize = 1000,
                AssemblySizeOpenGlVariant = 2000,
                SteamAppId = 1895130,
            };
        }

        private static List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> Env(Options options, params string[] inherited)
        {
            var parent = new List<KeyValuePair<string, string>>();
            foreach (string pair in inherited)
            {
                int eq = pair.IndexOf('=');
                parent.Add(new KeyValuePair<string, string>(pair.Substring(0, eq), pair.Substring(eq + 1)));
            }
            return EnvironmentBlock.Build(options, @"C:\game", @"C:\app\Drelay.Bootstrap.dll",
                                          4242, @"C:\runs\now", parent, null);
        }

        private static string Get(List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> variables, string name)
        {
            foreach (var pair in variables)
            {
                if (string.Equals(pair.Key, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { return pair.Value; }
            }
            return null;
        }

        private static bool Has(List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> variables, string name)
        {
            return Get(variables, name) != null;
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // the tables
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        /// <summary>
        /// Where each config field ends up.  `null` means "the launcher consumes it and the child
        /// sees no variable", which is a decision, not an omission -- and C7 asserts that every
        /// field of the schema appears here, so a new field has to make that decision.
        /// </summary>
        private static readonly (string Key, string Env)[] FieldEnv =
        {
            ("GamePath", null),
            ("AutoAim", "DRELAY_AIM_MODE"),
            ("Dodge.Enabled", "DRELAY_DODGE"),
            ("Dodge.Act", "DRELAY_DODGE_ACT"),
            ("Dodge.DecisionDisc", "DRELAY_DODGE_DECISION_DISC"),
            ("Dodge.WindowSeconds", "DRELAY_DODGE_WINDOW_S"),
            ("CollectDelayMs", "DRELAY_HOOK_COLLECT_DELAY_MS"),
            ("DiscoveryWindowMs", "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS"),
            ("ResolveDelayMs", "DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS"),
            ("LiveSeconds", "DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS"),
            ("PauseAfterRun", "DRELAY_KEEP_READING"),
            ("RunRoot", null),
            ("DbgDump", "DOTNET_DbgEnableMiniDump"),
            ("Verbose", null),
            ("NoWait", null),
            ("TimeoutMs", "DRELAY_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS"),
            ("Hook", null),
            ("Bootstrap", null),
        };

        /// <summary>A value the flag accepts, or `null` for a switch.  Used to prove each flag is real.</summary>
        private static readonly (string Flag, string Sample)[] FlagSample =
        {
            ("--game", @"C:\g"),
            ("--autoaim", "closest"),
            ("--dodge", null),
            ("--dodge-act", null),
            ("--dodge-disc", "2"),
            ("--dodge-window", "1"),
            ("--collect-delay", "1"),
            ("--discovery-ms", "1"),
            ("--resolve-delay", "1"),
            ("--live-seconds", "1"),
            ("--pause-after-run", null),
            ("--runroot", @"C:\r"),
            ("--dbg-dump", null),
            ("--verbose", null),
            ("--no-wait", null),
            ("--timeout", "1"),
            ("--hook", @"C:\h.dll"),
            ("--bootstrap", @"C:\b.dll"),
        };

        /// <summary>Every key of the schema, set, with a value that is not the default.</summary>
        private static string FullConfigJson()
        {
            return @"{
  ""GamePath"": ""C:\\cfg-game"",
  ""AutoAim"": ""closest"",
  ""Dodge"": { ""Enabled"": true, ""Act"": true, ""DecisionDisc"": 2.5, ""WindowSeconds"": 0.25 },
  ""CollectDelayMs"": 111,
  ""DiscoveryWindowMs"": 222,
  ""ResolveDelayMs"": 33,
  ""LiveSeconds"": 7,
  ""PauseAfterRun"": true,
  ""RunRoot"": ""C:\\cfg-runs"",
  ""DbgDump"": true,
  ""Verbose"": true,
  ""NoWait"": true,
  ""TimeoutMs"": 12345,
  ""Hook"": ""C:\\app\\h.dll"",
  ""Bootstrap"": ""C:\\app\\b.dll""
}";
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C1 -- per-field precedence
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C1()
        {
            var none = Resolve(Empty(), Cli("--game", @"C:\cli-game"), new FakeEnv());

            // Nothing supplied: the compiled defaults are what is left, and the sentinels still
            // mean "not set" rather than "the solver's default is written down here too".
            ExpectEqual(10000, none.DiscoveryWindowMs, "the default discovery window");
            ExpectEqual(100, none.ResolveDelayMs, "the default resolve margin");
            ExpectEqual(5, none.LiveSeconds, "the default evidence window");
            Expect(none.DryRun, "the default is a dry run");
            Expect(none.DodgeDisc < 0.0 && none.DodgeWindowSeconds < 0.0,
                   "an unset dodge window must stay 'not set', not carry a copy of the solver's default");
            Expect(none.CollectDelayMs == 0 && !none.SetCollectDelayMs,
                   "an unset collect delay is still 'not set'");

            string ignored;
            List<string> recognised;
            Settings config = Config(@"{
  ""GamePath"": ""C:\\cfg-game"",
  ""AutoAim"": ""closest"",
  ""Dodge"": { ""Enabled"": true, ""DecisionDisc"": 3.0 },
  ""CollectDelayMs"": 2500,
  ""DiscoveryWindowMs"": 12000
}", out ignored, out recognised);

            // Config only.
            var onlyConfig = Resolve(config, Empty(), new FakeEnv());
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\cfg-game", onlyConfig.GamePath, "GamePath from the config file");
            ExpectEqual("closest", onlyConfig.AutoAim, "AutoAim from the config file");
            Expect(onlyConfig.Dodge, "Dodge.Enabled from the config file");
            ExpectEqual(3.0, onlyConfig.DodgeDisc, "Dodge.DecisionDisc from the config file");
            ExpectEqual(2500, onlyConfig.CollectDelayMs, "CollectDelayMs from the config file");
            ExpectEqual(12000, onlyConfig.DiscoveryWindowMs, "DiscoveryWindowMs from the config file");
            Expect(onlyConfig.FrameReplacement,
                   "an AutoAim from the CONFIG FILE must imply the frame replacement exactly as the flag does (section 10.6)");

            // Command line only.
            var onlyCli = Resolve(Empty(), Cli("--game", @"D:\cli-game", "--autoaim", "highesthp"), new FakeEnv());
            ExpectEqual(@"D:\cli-game", onlyCli.GamePath, "GamePath from the command line");
            ExpectEqual("highesthp", onlyCli.AutoAim, "AutoAim from the command line");

            // Both, and the CLI says one thing only.  This is C1.
            var both = Resolve(config, Cli("--autoaim", "highesthp"), new FakeEnv());
            ExpectEqual("highesthp", both.AutoAim, "the command line wins for the field it sets");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\cfg-game", both.GamePath,
                        "a command-line value for one field must not discard a config value for another");
            Expect(both.Dodge, "the config's Dodge.Enabled survives a command line that sets AutoAim");
            ExpectEqual(3.0, both.DodgeDisc, "the config's dodge window survives too");
            ExpectEqual(2500, both.CollectDelayMs, "the config's collect delay survives too");
            ExpectEqual(12000, both.DiscoveryWindowMs, "a field neither source set keeps the default");

            // And the other direction: the CLI overrides exactly one field of a config that sets many.
            var overridden = Resolve(config, Cli("--collect-delay", "10"), new FakeEnv());
            ExpectEqual(10, overridden.CollectDelayMs, "the command line overrides the one field it sets");
            ExpectEqual(12000, overridden.DiscoveryWindowMs, "and leaves the neighbouring field alone");
            ExpectEqual("closest", overridden.AutoAim, "and leaves a different type alone");

            // AutoAim null in the config is "off", which is the same statement as absence.
            Settings off = Config(@"{ ""AutoAim"": null }");
            Expect(off.AutoAim == null, "a null AutoAim must mean 'not set', not a mode");
            var withNull = Resolve(Config(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\g"", ""AutoAim"": null }"), Empty(), new FakeEnv());
            Expect(withNull.AutoAim == null, "a null AutoAim must leave the hook's own default in charge");
            Expect(!withNull.FrameReplacement, "and must not turn the frame replacement on");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C2 -- the child's environment
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C2()
        {
            var minimal = Resolve(Empty(), Cli("--game", @"C:\g"), new FakeEnv());
            var vars = Env(minimal, "DOTNET_TieredCompilation=1", "DRELAY_HOOK_EVIL=1", "PATH=C:\\Windows");

            string[] neverWritten =
            {
                "DRELAY_HOOK_COLLECT_DELAY_MS", "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS",
                "DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS", "DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS", "DRELAY_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS",
                "DRELAY_KEEP_READING", "DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_REPLACEMENT", "DRELAY_HOOK_FRAME_HELPER",
                "DRELAY_HOOK_AIM_REPLACEMENT", "DRELAY_AIM_MODE", "DRELAY_DODGE", "DRELAY_DODGE_ACT",
                "DRELAY_HOOK_MOVE_REPLACEMENT", "DRELAY_MOVE_STEER", "DRELAY_HOOK_TEST_TARGETS",
                "DRELAY_HOOK_FULLTRACE", "DRELAY_TRACE", "DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR", "DRELAY_HOOK_OFF",
                "DOTNET_DbgEnableMiniDump",
            };
            foreach (string name in neverWritten)
            {
                Expect(!Has(vars, name), "a field nobody set must reach the child as NOTHING: " + name);
            }

            string[] alwaysWritten =
            {
                "DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS", "DRELAY_HOOK_SESSION", "DRELAY_HOOK_RUNDIR",
                "DRELAY_HOOK_GAMEDIR", "DRELAY_HOOK_BLOCK", "DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN",
            };
            foreach (string name in alwaysWritten)
            {
                Expect(Has(vars, name), "the launcher's own name must always be written: " + name);
            }

            Expect(!Has(vars, "DOTNET_TieredCompilation"),
                   "the inherited DOTNET_ namespace must be deleted, not passed through");
            Expect(!Has(vars, "DRELAY_HOOK_EVIL"),
                   "the inherited DRELAY_HOOK_ namespace must be deleted, not passed through");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(vars, "DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN"),
                        "an unset --act must leave DRELAY_HOOK_DRYRUN=1 (its absence means ACT)");

            // Every field of the schema reaches the variable it claims to.
            var full = Resolve(Config(FullConfigJson()), Empty(), new FakeEnv());
            var fullVars = Env(full);
            foreach (var row in FieldEnv)
            {
                if (row.Env == null) { continue; }
                Expect(Has(fullVars, row.Env),
                       "the config field " + row.Key + " must reach " + row.Env);
            }
            ExpectEqual("closest", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_AIM_MODE"), "AutoAim reaches DRELAY_AIM_MODE");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_DODGE"), "Dodge.Enabled reaches DRELAY_DODGE");
            ExpectEqual("111", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_HOOK_COLLECT_DELAY_MS"), "CollectDelayMs");
            ExpectEqual("222", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_HOOK_DISCOVERY_WINDOW_MS"), "DiscoveryWindowMs");
            ExpectEqual("33", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_HOOK_RESOLVE_DELAY_MS"), "ResolveDelayMs");
            ExpectEqual("7000", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_HOOK_LIVE_MS"), "LiveSeconds is converted to ms");
            ExpectEqual("0", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_KEEP_READING"), "PauseAfterRun writes the inverse switch");
            ExpectEqual("12345", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS"), "TimeoutMs");
            ExpectEqual("2.5", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_DODGE_DECISION_DISC"), "Dodge.DecisionDisc");
            ExpectEqual("0.25", Get(fullVars, "DRELAY_DODGE_WINDOW_S"), "Dodge.WindowSeconds");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(fullVars, "DOTNET_DbgEnableMiniDump"), "DbgDump");

            // The fields with no variable are still read, and land on the launcher.
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\cfg-runs", full.RunRoot, "RunRoot");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\app\h.dll", full.HookDll, "Hook");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\app\b.dll", full.BootstrapDll, "Bootstrap");
            Expect(full.Verbose, "Verbose");
            Expect(full.NoWait, "NoWait");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\cfg-game", full.GamePath, "GamePath");

            // Section 5's note: RunRoot is in the schema and not in the template, and if it is
            // supplied it is made absolute -- a relative run root is a directory created wherever
            // the launcher happened to start from.
            var relativeRunRoot = Resolve(
                Config(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\g"", ""RunRoot"": ""relative-runs"" }"), Empty(), new FakeEnv());
            Expect(Path.IsPathRooted(relativeRunRoot.RunRoot),
                   "a relative RunRoot must be resolved to an absolute path, got: " + relativeRunRoot.RunRoot);

            // The dodge's two windows travel only when they were set, and the sentinel is the
            // reason: the solver's own default must not be written down here.
            var dodgeNoWindow = Resolve(
                Config(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\g"", ""Dodge"": { ""Enabled"": true } }"), Empty(), new FakeEnv());
            var dodgeVars = Env(dodgeNoWindow);
            Expect(Has(dodgeVars, "DRELAY_DODGE"), "Dodge on: the solver runs");
            Expect(!Has(dodgeVars, "DRELAY_DODGE_DECISION_DISC"),
                   "a dodge with no --dodge-disc must not send a disc window at all");
            Expect(!Has(dodgeVars, "DRELAY_DODGE_WINDOW_S"),
                   "a dodge with no --dodge-window must not send a floor at all");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C3 -- a typo names its field, in whichever source it was typed
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C3()
        {
            Settings settings;
            List<string> gameArguments;
            bool help;
            string error;

            bool ok = CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--autoaim", "closests" }, out settings,
                                           out gameArguments, out help, out error);
            Expect(!ok, "a misspelled --autoaim must be refused");
            Expect(error != null && error.Contains("--autoaim") && error.Contains("closests"),
                   "the refusal must name the flag and the value, got: " + error);

            ok = CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--autoaim=closests" }, out settings,
                                      out gameArguments, out help, out error);
            Expect(!ok, "the --flag=value spelling must be refused too");
            Expect(error != null && error.Contains("--autoaim") && error.Contains("closests"),
                   "and must name the flag the same way, got: " + error);

            string path;
            string configError = ConfigError(@"{ ""AutoAim"": ""closests"" }", out path);
            Expect(configError != null, "a misspelled AutoAim in the config file must be refused");
            Expect(configError.Contains("AutoAim"), "the refusal must name the field, got: " + configError);
            Expect(configError.Contains("closests"), "and the value, got: " + configError);
            Expect(configError.Contains(path), "and the file, got: " + configError);
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C4 -- discovery, and the gate that decides
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C4()
        {
            // 1. No Steam, no pinned path: the launcher's own directory.
            var local = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\unpacked\hook" };
            Game(local, @"C:\unpacked\hook", 1000);
            var found = Discovery.Find(local, Pinned());
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\unpacked\hook", found.GameDirectory, "the launcher's own directory is probe 3");

            // 2. Steam, one library, the game where Steam puts it.
            var steam = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            steam.Registry(@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam", "SteamPath", @"C:\Steam");
            steam.Text(@"C:\Steam\steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf", Vdf(@"C:\Steam"));
            Game(steam, @"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 1000);
            found = Discovery.Find(steam, Pinned());
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", found.GameDirectory,
                        "the Steam library is probe 1, and it is the first one that is right");

            // 3. The game on a SECOND library, named by the app manifest: the app id is used for
            //    the manifest, and the manifest's installdir beats the pinned directory name.
            var second = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            second.Registry(@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam", "SteamPath", @"C:\Steam");
            second.Text(@"C:\Steam\steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf", Vdf(@"C:\Steam", @"D:\Games\SteamLibrary"));
            second.Text(@"D:\Games\SteamLibrary\steamapps\appmanifest_1895130.acf",
                        "\"AppState\"\n{\n\t\"appid\"\t\t\"1895130\"\n\t\"installdir\"\t\t\"Darza Renamed\"\n}\n");
            Game(second, @"D:\Games\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza Renamed", 1000);
            found = Discovery.Find(second, Pinned());
            ExpectEqual(@"D:\Games\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza Renamed", found.GameDirectory,
                        "a game on a second Steam library must be found, by its own manifest's installdir");

            // 4. A Steam install with no libraryfolders.vdf: the registry path is itself a library.
            var noVdf = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            noVdf.Registry(@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam", "SteamPath", @"C:\Steam");
            Game(noVdf, @"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 1000);
            found = Discovery.Find(noVdf, Pinned());
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", found.GameDirectory,
                        "with no library list, the registry's SteamPath is the library");

            // 5. No Steam at all: the pinned record.
            var pinnedOnly = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            Game(pinnedOnly, @"E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 1000);
            found = Discovery.Find(pinnedOnly, Pinned());
            ExpectEqual(@"E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", found.GameDirectory,
                        "the pinned record is probe 2");

            // 6. THE INVARIANT: the OpenGL variant is never returned, even when the right build is
            //    one library further along -- the mismatch is NAMED instead of being skipped.
            var openGl = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            openGl.Registry(@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam", "SteamPath", @"C:\Steam");
            openGl.Text(@"C:\Steam\steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf", Vdf(@"C:\Steam", @"D:\Games\SteamLibrary"));
            Game(openGl, @"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 2000);
            Game(openGl, @"D:\Games\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 1000);
            var result = Discovery.Find(openGl, Pinned());
            Expect(result.GameDirectory == null, "discovery must NOT return the OpenGL build");
            Expect(result.OpenGlVariant, "the OpenGL variant must be flagged as such");
            Expect(result.Failure != null && result.Failure.Contains("OpenGL"),
                   "and named in the message, got: " + result.Failure);

            // 7. An unknown build is a mismatch too, and it is reported rather than accepted.
            var wrong = new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" };
            Game(wrong, @"E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion", 999);
            result = Discovery.Find(wrong, Pinned());
            Expect(result.GameDirectory == null, "a directory whose assembly is not the pinned build is not the game");
            Expect(!result.OpenGlVariant, "and is not claimed to be the OpenGL variant either");
            Expect(result.Failure != null && result.Failure.Contains("999"),
                   "the mismatch must name the size it found, got: " + result.Failure);

            // 8. Nothing anywhere.
            result = Discovery.Find(new FakeEnv { LauncherDirectory = @"C:\app" }, Pinned());
            Expect(result.GameDirectory == null && result.Failure != null,
                   "finding nothing must be a refusal with a reason, not a silent null");

            // 9. The scanner that reads Steam's own file format, against a nested block -- the
            //    shape that breaks a naive key/value pairing.
            List<string> paths = Discovery.ParseQuotedValue(Vdf(@"C:\Steam", @"D:\Games\SteamLibrary"), "path");
            ExpectEqual(2, paths.Count, "both library paths must come out of the VDF");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\Steam", paths[0], "the first library path, unescaped");
            ExpectEqual(@"D:\Games\SteamLibrary", paths[1], "the second library path, unescaped");
        }

        /// <summary>A libraryfolders.vdf with the nested-block shape Steam writes.</summary>
        private static string Vdf(params string[] libraries)
        {
            var text = new StringBuilder();
            text.Append("\"libraryfolders\"\r\n{\r\n");
            for (int i = 0; i < libraries.Length; i++)
            {
                text.Append("\t\"").Append(i).Append("\"\r\n\t{\r\n");
                text.Append("\t\t\"path\"\t\t\"").Append(libraries[i].Replace("\\", "\\\\")).Append("\"\r\n");
                text.Append("\t\t\"label\"\t\t\"\"\r\n");
                text.Append("\t\t\"apps\"\r\n\t\t{\r\n\t\t\t\"1895130\"\t\t\"123456\"\r\n\t\t}\r\n");
                text.Append("\t}\r\n");
            }
            text.Append("}\r\n");
            return text.ToString();
        }

        /// <summary>A directory holding the pinned apphost and an assembly of the given size.</summary>
        private static void Game(FakeEnv env, string directory, long assemblySize)
        {
            env.Dir(directory);
            env.File(Path.Combine(directory, "DarzasDominion.exe"), 4096);
            env.File(Path.Combine(directory, "DarzasDominion.dll"), assemblySize);
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C5 -- the pause rule
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C5()
        {
            Expect(FirstRun.ShouldPause(true, false, true),
                   "a double-click with a fixable failure must hold the window open");
            Expect(!FirstRun.ShouldPause(true, true, true),
                   "C5: a zero-argument run with redirected input must NEVER pause");
            Expect(!FirstRun.ShouldPause(false, false, true),
                   "a scripted run (one or more arguments) must never pause");
            Expect(!FirstRun.ShouldPause(true, false, false),
                   "a refusal the user cannot fix by editing a file must not pause");

            // The other first-run rule: a no-argument run that finds no configuration file creates
            // one, because section 6's "write it only when discovery fails" is the one case where
            // the user who needs the file (the one whose game was found) never gets it.
            Expect(FirstRun.ShouldWriteTemplate(true, false),
                   "a first no-argument run must write the configuration template");
            Expect(!FirstRun.ShouldWriteTemplate(true, true),
                   "and must never write over a file that exists -- that file may be the operator's");
            Expect(!FirstRun.ShouldWriteTemplate(false, false),
                   "a scripted run must not create files it did not ask for");

            if (_programSource == null)
            {
                Console.WriteLine("       (Program.cs not given: the 'which line does Main call' half of");
                Console.WriteLine("        C5 is not checked. Pass --source to check it.)");
                return;
            }
            Expect(File.Exists(_programSource), "Program.cs not found at " + _programSource);
            string source = File.ReadAllText(_programSource);

            int readKeys = Count(source, "Console.ReadKey");
            ExpectEqual(1, readKeys,
                        "Main must have exactly one pause; a second one is a path that can block a script");

            int guarded = Count(source, "FirstRun.ShouldPause(");
            ExpectEqual(1, guarded,
                        "the one pause must be decided by a single FirstRun.ShouldPause call");

            int redirectChecks = Count(source, "Console.IsInputRedirected");
            ExpectEqual(1, redirectChecks,
                        "the redirected-input check must live in the one call site, not be re-derived");

            // And the same for the other first-run decision: exactly one call, so a future edit
            // cannot add a second writer (or leave the template unwritten).
            int writers = Count(source, "FirstRun.ShouldWriteTemplate(");
            ExpectEqual(1, writers,
                        "the template must be written from exactly one place, behind FirstRun.ShouldWriteTemplate");
        }

        private static int Count(string haystack, string needle)
        {
            int count = 0;
            int at = 0;
            while ((at = haystack.IndexOf(needle, at, StringComparison.Ordinal)) >= 0)
            {
                count++;
                at += needle.Length;
            }
            return count;
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C6 -- the template
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C6()
        {
            string template = ConfigFile.Template();
            Expect(template.TrimStart().StartsWith("{"), "the template must be a JSON object");

            // It must be readable by the reader that wrote it -- comments included.
            string path = Path.Combine(_tmp, "template.json");
            File.WriteAllText(path, template, new UTF8Encoding(false));
            Settings settings;
            List<string> recognised;
            string error;
            Expect(ConfigFile.TryRead(path, out settings, out recognised, out error),
                   "the written template must be readable by the launcher: " + error);

            // C6 itself: no test-harness key, by string search.
            string[] forbidden =
            {
                "FrameHelper", "FrameReplacement", "TestTargets", "MoveSteer", "EscapeTest",
                "FullTrace", "Trace", "Off", "Exe", "Assembly",
            };
            foreach (string key in forbidden)
            {
                Expect(!template.Contains("\"" + key + "\""),
                       "the template must not offer the test-harness key \"" + key + "\"");
            }

            // And the same statement structurally: the template sets exactly the documented keys.
            var expected = new List<string>
            {
                "GamePath", "AutoAim", "Dodge", "Dodge.Enabled", "Dodge.Act", "Dodge.DecisionDisc",
                "Dodge.WindowSeconds", "CollectDelayMs", "DiscoveryWindowMs", "LiveSeconds",
                "PauseAfterRun",
            };
            var actual = new List<string>(recognised);
            expected.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            actual.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            ExpectEqual(string.Join(",", expected.ToArray()), string.Join(",", actual.ToArray()),
                        "the template's keys");

            // WHAT THE TEMPLATE SAYS, WHICH IS NOW A DECISION RATHER THAN A RESTATEMENT OF THE
            // COMPILED DEFAULTS (see `ConfigFile.Template`'s own note).  A first no-argument run
            // writes this file AND runs with it, so these three assertions are the shipped default
            // behaviour of a double-click: aim at the closest enemy, solve and steer.
            var defaults = new Options();
            ExpectEqual("closest", settings.AutoAim,
                        "the written template is the release default: auto-aim on, closest");
            Expect(settings.Dodge == true, "and the dodge on");
            Expect(settings.DodgeAct == true, "and acting, not only logging");
            Expect(settings.DodgeDisc == null, "the template must leave the disc window unset");
            Expect(settings.DodgeWindowSeconds == null, "and the floor unset");

            // The timing knobs really are the compiled defaults, from the same fields the launcher
```
