```cs
            // uses -- a default changed in Options without changing the template fails here.
            ExpectEqual(defaults.CollectDelayMs, settings.CollectDelayMs ?? -999, "CollectDelayMs");
            ExpectEqual(defaults.DiscoveryWindowMs, settings.DiscoveryWindowMs ?? -999, "DiscoveryWindowMs");
            ExpectEqual(defaults.LiveSeconds, settings.LiveSeconds ?? -999, "LiveSeconds");
            Expect(settings.PauseAfterRun == false, "PauseAfterRun must be false in the template");
            Expect(settings.GamePath == null, "GamePath must be empty, so the first run has something to fill in");
            Expect(settings.TimeoutMs == null, "the template must not pin the timeout");

            // AND THE WHOLE POINT OF THE FILE: resolved through the shipped merge, it produces a run
            // that asks the hook for both modules, rather than the all-off run of 2026-10-16.
            Options resolved = Resolve(settings, Cli("--game", @"C:\g"), new FakeEnv());
            Expect(resolved.FrameReplacement,
                   "the written template must install the managed frame replacement -- it is the entry "
                   + "point both the dodge and auto-aim are driven from");
            var vars = Env(resolved);
            ExpectEqual("closest", Get(vars, "DRELAY_AIM_MODE"), "the template must reach DRELAY_AIM_MODE");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(vars, "DRELAY_DODGE"), "and DRELAY_DODGE");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(vars, "DRELAY_DODGE_ACT"), "and DRELAY_DODGE_ACT");
            ExpectEqual("dodge", Get(vars, "DRELAY_MOVE_STEER"), "and the pilot's dodge mode");
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(vars, "DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR"), "and the sensor the dodge reads");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C7 -- the table, in both directions
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C7()
        {
            // Direction 1: every field of the config has a flag, and the flag is real.
            foreach (ConfigField field in ConfigFile.Schema)
            {
                bool known = false;
                foreach (var row in FlagSample)
                {
                    if (row.Flag == field.Flag) { known = true; break; }
                }
                Expect(known, "the schema claims " + field.Key + " maps to " + field.Flag
                              + ", which is not a flag this harness knows how to exercise");
            }
            foreach (var row in FlagSample)
            {
                Settings parsed;
                List<string> gameArguments;
                bool help;
                string error;
                string[] args = row.Sample == null
                    ? new[] { row.Flag, "--game", @"C:\g" }
                    : new[] { row.Flag, row.Sample, "--game", @"C:\g" };
                Expect(CommandLine.TryParse(args, out parsed, out gameArguments, out help, out error),
                       "the flag " + row.Flag + " must be accepted by the command line: " + error);
            }

            // Direction 2: every field the config reader recognises is in the table.
            string path;
            List<string> recognised;
            Config(FullConfigJson(), out path, out recognised);
            var expected = new List<string>();
            foreach (ConfigField field in ConfigFile.Schema)
            {
                expected.Add(field.Key);
                if (field.Key.StartsWith("Dodge.", StringComparison.Ordinal) && !expected.Contains("Dodge"))
                {
                    // `Dodge` itself is recognised too, and it is one key however many children it
                    // has: the reader records the parent once, when it opens the object.
                    expected.Add("Dodge");
                }
            }
            var actual = new List<string>(recognised);
            expected.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            actual.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            ExpectEqual(string.Join(",", expected.ToArray()), string.Join(",", actual.ToArray()),
                        "the keys the reader recognised on a document that sets every field");

            // And every field's destination is a decision somebody made.
            foreach (ConfigField field in ConfigFile.Schema)
            {
                bool decided = false;
                foreach (var row in FieldEnv)
                {
                    if (row.Key == field.Key) { decided = true; break; }
                }
                Expect(decided, "the config field " + field.Key
                                + " has no entry in the harness's environment table, so where it goes is undocumented");
            }
            foreach (var row in FieldEnv)
            {
                bool inSchema = false;
                foreach (ConfigField field in ConfigFile.Schema)
                {
                    if (field.Key == row.Key) { inSchema = true; break; }
                }
                Expect(inSchema, "the harness documents " + row.Key + ", which is not in the config schema");
            }
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // C8 -- the pinned record carries what discovery needs
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void C8()
        {
            if (_knownBuild == null || !File.Exists(_knownBuild))
            {
                Console.WriteLine("       (known-build.json not given: skipped. Pass --known-build to check it.)");
                return;
            }
            using (JsonDocument document = JsonDocument.Parse(File.ReadAllText(_knownBuild)))
            {
                JsonElement root = document.RootElement;
                JsonElement assembly = root.GetProperty("assembly");
                long size = assembly.GetProperty("size").GetInt64();
                Expect(assembly.TryGetProperty("sizeOpenGlVariant", out JsonElement openGl),
                       "known-build.json must record sizeOpenGlVariant: discovery NAMES the OpenGL "
                       + "install with it, and without it the refusal degrades to 'not the pinned build'");
                long openGlSize = openGl.GetInt64();
                Expect(openGlSize > 0, "sizeOpenGlVariant must be a real size, not 0");
                Expect(openGlSize != size,
                       "sizeOpenGlVariant must differ from size, or the gate cannot tell them apart");

                JsonElement game = root.GetProperty("game");
                Expect(game.TryGetProperty("steamAppId", out JsonElement appId),
                       "known-build.json must record game.steamAppId: discovery reads the app manifest with it");
                Expect(appId.GetInt32() > 0, "steamAppId must be a real app id, not 0");
            }
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // R1 -- the config reader's boundaries (section 11 step 2)
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void R1()
        {
            Settings settings;
            List<string> recognised;
            string error;

            // A missing file is "defaults", not an error.
            string missing = Path.Combine(_tmp, "not-there.json");
            Expect(ConfigFile.TryRead(missing, out settings, out recognised, out error),
                   "a missing file must not be an error: " + error);
            Expect(settings.IsEmpty, "a missing file must leave every field unset");

            // An empty file is the same statement.
            string emptyPath = Path.Combine(_tmp, "empty.json");
            File.WriteAllText(emptyPath, "   \r\n");
            Expect(ConfigFile.TryRead(emptyPath, out settings, out recognised, out error),
                   "an empty file must not be an error: " + error);
            Expect(settings.IsEmpty, "an empty file must leave every field unset");

            // An unknown key is ignored, not refused: a config from a later version must still start.
            Settings withUnknown = Config(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\g"", ""FrameHelper"": true, ""NotAKey"": 1 }");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\g", withUnknown.GamePath, "a known key beside an unknown one is still read");
            Expect(withUnknown.FrameHelper == null,
                   "a test-harness key must be UNKNOWN to the reader, not a hidden switch");

            // Malformed JSON names the file.
            string path;
            string malformed = ConfigError(@"{ ""GamePath"": }", out path);
            Expect(malformed != null && malformed.Contains(path),
                   "malformed JSON must name the file, got: " + malformed);

            // A wrong type names the field.
            string wrongType = ConfigError(@"{ ""LiveSeconds"": ""5"" }", out path);
            Expect(wrongType != null && wrongType.Contains("LiveSeconds"),
                   "a wrong type must name the field, got: " + wrongType);

            string negative = ConfigError(@"{ ""CollectDelayMs"": -1 }", out path);
            Expect(negative != null && negative.Contains("CollectDelayMs"),
                   "a negative number must name the field, got: " + negative);

            string badDodge = ConfigError(@"{ ""Dodge"": 3 }", out path);
            Expect(badDodge != null && badDodge.Contains("Dodge"),
                   "a Dodge that is not an object must name the field, got: " + badDodge);

            string notAnObject = ConfigError(@"[]", out path);
            Expect(notAnObject != null && notAnObject.Contains(path),
                   "a top-level array must be refused with the file named, got: " + notAnObject);

            // Trailing commas and comments are accepted, because the template has both.
            Settings commented = Config("{\n  // a comment\n  \"GamePath\": \"C:\\\\g\",\n}");
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\g", commented.GamePath, "a comment and a trailing comma must not be a startup failure");

            // The default location is where the documents say, under the given profile.
            string expectedDir = Path.Combine(@"D:\profile", "drelay", "hook");
            ExpectEqual(expectedDir, ConfigFile.Directory(@"D:\profile"), "the config directory");
            ExpectEqual(Path.Combine(expectedDir, "drelay.config.json"),
                        ConfigFile.DefaultPath(@"D:\profile"), "the config file path");

            // Writing the template, then reading it back, is the first-run round trip.
            string written = Path.Combine(_tmp, "written", "drelay.config.json");
            Expect(ConfigFile.WriteTemplate(written, out error), "the template must be writable: " + error);
            Expect(File.Exists(written), "and must exist afterwards");
            Expect(ConfigFile.WriteTemplate(written, out error), "writing it twice must be a no-op");
            File.WriteAllText(written, @"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\mine"" }");
            ConfigFile.WriteTemplate(written, out error);
            ExpectEqual(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\mine"" }", File.ReadAllText(written),
                        "writing the template must NEVER overwrite a file the user has");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // R2 -- the command line's boundaries
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        private static void R2()
        {
            Settings settings;
            List<string> gameArguments;
            bool help;
            string error;

            // An unknown option is refused; a bare word is the game's.
            Expect(!CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--nonsense" }, out settings, out gameArguments,
                                         out help, out error),
                   "an unknown option must be refused");
            Expect(CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--game", @"C:\g", "-screen-width", "1920" },
                                        out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error),
                   "an argument the launcher does not own must be passed through: " + error);
            ExpectEqual(2, gameArguments.Count, "both game arguments must be passed through");
            ExpectEqual("-screen-width", gameArguments[0], "in order");

            // The equals spelling, for the flags a script is most likely to build.
            Expect(CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { @"--game=C:\g", "--autoaim=highesthp" },
                                        out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error),
                   "--flag=value must parse: " + error);
            ExpectEqual(@"C:\g", settings.GamePath, "--game=PATH");
            ExpectEqual("highesthp", settings.AutoAim, "--autoaim=MODE");

            // A number a user can get wrong is refused with its own name, not by an exception.
            Expect(!CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--game", @"C:\g", "--timeout", "abc" },
                                         out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error),
                   "--timeout abc must be refused");
            Expect(error != null && error.Contains("--timeout"),
                   "and must name the flag, got: " + error);
            Expect(!CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--game", @"C:\g", "--live-seconds", "-1" },
                                         out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error),
                   "a negative knob must be refused");

            // A flag with no value is a message, not an unhandled exception -- the harness calls the
            // parser the way `Main` does, and `Main` catches `ArgumentException` for exactly this.
            bool threw = false;
            try
            {
                CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--game" }, out settings, out gameArguments, out help, out error);
            }
            catch (ArgumentException)
            {
                threw = true;
            }
            Expect(threw, "a flag with no value must be reported as a failure (Main turns it into a message)");

            // The one contradiction that is refused rather than resolved.
            ResolveResult contradiction = ResolveRaw(
                new Settings(),
                Cli(new[] { "--game", @"C:\g", "--dodge-act", "--move-steer", "hold:90:8000" }, out gameArguments),
                new FakeEnv());
            Expect(contradiction.Outcome == ResolveOutcome.Invalid,
                   "--dodge-act with an explicit --move-steer must be refused, not resolved");
            Expect(contradiction.Error != null && contradiction.Error.Contains("--dodge-act"),
                   "and the refusal must name the flag, got: " + contradiction.Error);

            // BUT THE SAME PAIR IS A RUN WHEN THE `Act` CAME FROM THE CONFIGURATION FILE, because
            // the file cannot be told "not this time" and the command line is the more specific
            // statement.  This is the case the shipped template creates: it ships `"Act": true`,
            // and `Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Sweep|Hold` passes `--move-steer`.
            ResolveResult fromFile = ResolveRaw(
                Config(@"{ ""GamePath"": ""C:\\g"", ""Dodge"": { ""Enabled"": true, ""Act"": true } }"),
                Cli(new[] { "--move-steer", "hold:90:8000" }, out gameArguments),
                new FakeEnv());
            Expect(fromFile.Outcome == ResolveOutcome.Ready,
                   "a command-line --move-steer must override the FILE's Dodge.Act rather than be refused: "
                   + fromFile.Error);
            Expect(!fromFile.Options.DodgeAct, "the command line's actuator choice wins");
            ExpectEqual("hold:90:8000", fromFile.Options.MoveSteer, "and the pilot runs the experiment asked for");
            Expect(fromFile.Options.Dodge,
                   "the file's Dodge.Enabled is NOT discarded: solving and logging do not contradict "
                   + "somebody else steering");
            Expect(fromFile.Notices.Count == 1,
                   "and the override must be reported, not silent");
            Expect(fromFile.Notices[0].Contains("--move-steer") && fromFile.Notices[0].Contains("Act"),
                   "with a notice naming both, got: " + fromFile.Notices[0]);
            // The adapter reads `DRELAY_DODGE_ACT == "1"`, so NOT writing the name is the statement
            // "do not act" -- which is also C2's rule for a field the operator did not ask for.
            Expect(!Has(Env(fromFile.Options), "DRELAY_DODGE_ACT"),
                   "the child must not be told to act, by name or by value");
            ExpectEqual("hold:90:8000", Get(Env(fromFile.Options), "DRELAY_MOVE_STEER"), "the pilot's own value");

            // --dodge-act on its own puts the pilot in dodge mode, which is the implication the
            // config file has to get too (section 10.6).
            Options acting = Resolve(Empty(), Cli("--game", @"C:\g", "--dodge-act"), new FakeEnv());
            Expect(acting.DodgeAct && acting.Dodge, "--dodge-act implies --dodge");
            ExpectEqual("dodge", acting.MoveSteer, "--dodge-act puts the pilot in dodge mode");
            var actingVars = Env(acting);
            ExpectEqual("1", Get(actingVars, "DRELAY_DODGE_ACT"), "--dodge-act reaches the adapter");
            ExpectEqual("dodge", Get(actingVars, "DRELAY_MOVE_STEER"), "and the pilot");

            // --escape-test implies the frame replacement, which is where the call is made from.
            Options escape = Resolve(Empty(), Cli("--game", @"C:\g", "--escape-test", "25"), new FakeEnv());
            Expect(escape.FrameReplacement, "--escape-test implies --frame-replacement");
            ExpectEqual("25", Get(Env(escape), "DRELAY_ESCAPE_TEST_SEC"), "--escape-test reaches the hook");

            // --help is not an error.
            Expect(CommandLine.TryParse(new[] { "--help" }, out settings, out gameArguments, out help,
                                        out error) && help,
                   "--help must parse as a help request");
        }

        // ------------------------------------------------------------------
        // the fake environment discovery is driven through
        // ------------------------------------------------------------------

        /// <summary>
        /// A machine with no registry, no files and no directories until one is added.
        ///
        /// PATHS ARE NORMALISED THE SAME WAY ON BOTH SIDES, so a test cannot pass because the fake
        /// happened to store a path with the separator the probe used.
        /// </summary>
        private sealed class FakeEnv : IDiscoveryEnv
        {
            private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _registry = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _texts = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            private readonly HashSet<string> _directories = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            private readonly Dictionary<string, long> _files = new Dictionary<string, long>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

            public string LauncherDirectory { get; set; }

            private static string Norm(string path)
            {
                if (path == null) { return string.Empty; }
                return path.Replace('/', '\\').TrimEnd('\\');
            }

            public FakeEnv Registry(string keyPath, string valueName, string value)
            {
                _registry[Norm(keyPath) + "|" + valueName] = value;
                return this;
            }

            public FakeEnv Dir(string path)
            {
                _directories.Add(Norm(path));
                return this;
            }

            public FakeEnv File(string path, long size)
            {
                _files[Norm(path)] = size;
                return this;
            }

            public FakeEnv Text(string path, string text)
            {
                _texts[Norm(path)] = text;
                return this;
            }

            public bool TryReadRegistryString(string keyPath, string valueName, out string value)
            {
                return _registry.TryGetValue(Norm(keyPath) + "|" + valueName, out value);
            }

            public string ReadTextOrNull(string path)
            {
                return _texts.TryGetValue(Norm(path), out string text) ? text : null;
            }

            public bool DirectoryExists(string path)
            {
                return _directories.Contains(Norm(path));
            }

            public bool FileExists(string path)
            {
                return _files.ContainsKey(Norm(path));
            }

            public long FileSize(string path)
            {
                return _files.TryGetValue(Norm(path), out long size) ? size : -1;
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/tools/Probe-DodgeDryRun.ps1`:

```ps1
# Probe-DodgeDryRun.ps1 -- does the dodge adapter actually run on a live frame path?
#
# THIS IS THE ONE THING NO OFFLINE HARNESS COULD CHECK. `SolverHarness` never runs
# `DodgeAdapter.OnFrame`; it re-derives a snapshot from a recorded trace with its own reader. So
# "the adapter resolves, arms, decides on real frames and writes its report" is a claim about the
# HOOK, and the only instrument that can test it without the game is the synthetic host -- which
# has a World, a Player and a frame tick, and none of the fields the adapter treats as optional.
#
# It is deliberately narrow. It does not test the dodge's quality (that is the synthetic scenarios
# and, eventually, recorded play) and it does not test the actuator (that is Run-Phase3Session).
# What it tests is the wiring: the switch, the resolve, the frame path, the log line.
#
# Usage: powershell -File .\Probe-DodgeDryRun.ps1

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

$hookRoot  = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$repoRoot  = Split-Path -Parent $hookRoot
$outDir    = Join-Path $hookRoot 'out'
$testRoot  = Join-Path $hookRoot 'tests\SyntheticHost\bin\Release'
$launcher  = Join-Path $outDir 'Drelay.Launcher.exe'
$hostDll   = Join-Path $testRoot 'SyntheticHost.dll'
$hashTool  = Join-Path $repoRoot 'hook\tools\il_method_hash.py'

$failures = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
function Check([string] $name, [bool] $ok, [string] $detail) {
    $state = if ($ok) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }
    $colour = if ($ok) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-4} {1,-56} {2}" -f $state, $name, $detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
    if (-not $ok) { $failures.Add($name) | Out-Null }
}

Write-Host '=== dodge dry-run probe (synthetic host) ===' -ForegroundColor Cyan

foreach ($required in @($launcher, $hostDll)) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $required)) {
        Write-Host "missing: $required -- run hook\build.ps1 and build SyntheticHost first" -ForegroundColor Red
        exit 2
    }
}

# The frame tick has to be published as a test target, because the synthetic host is not the game
# and the pinned table holds the game's four methods. Same recipe as Test-Injection.ps1.
$hashText = (& python $hashTool --assembly $hostDll `
        --type 'SyntheticHostFixture.Cadence' --name 'FrameTick' --arity 1 2>&1 | Out-String)
$ilSize = $null
$ilHash = $null
if ($hashText -match 'ilSize=(\d+)') { $ilSize = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($hashText -match 'ilHash=([0-9A-Fa-f]{64})') { $ilHash = $Matches[1].ToUpperInvariant() }
if (-not $ilSize -or -not $ilHash) {
    Write-Host "could not hash the host's frame tick: $hashText" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 2
}
$testSpec = "frameTick|SyntheticHostFixture.Cadence|FrameTick|$ilSize|$ilHash"

$runRoot = Join-Path $hookRoot 'obj\cases\dodge-dryrun'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $runRoot | Out-Null

# The host's own lifetime and the delay before it calls its frame tick. The delay matters for the
# reason Test-Injection.ps1 records: a method compiled before the watching window opens is
# unwatched and can never be patched.
$env:DRELAY_TEST_HOLD_MS = '30000'
$env:DRELAY_TEST_CADENCE_DELAY_MS = '5000'

$before = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $runRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)

$argv = @('--game', $testRoot,
          '--exe', (Join-Path $testRoot 'SyntheticHost.exe'),
          '--assembly', $hostDll,
          '--runroot', $runRoot,
          '--collect-delay', '500',
          '--live-seconds', '15',
          '--test-target', $testSpec,
          '--dodge')
Write-Host "  launch: Drelay.Launcher.exe $($argv -join ' ')" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

$text = (& $launcher @argv 2>&1 | Out-String)
$exit = $LASTEXITCODE

$after = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $runRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
           Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)
$new = @($after | Where-Object { $_ -notin $before } | Sort-Object -Descending)
$runDir = if ($new.Count -ge 1) { Join-Path $runRoot $new[0] } else { $null }

Check 'the launcher exited cleanly' ($exit -eq 0) "exit=$exit"
if (-not $runDir) {
    Write-Host 'no run directory was produced; the launcher output follows' -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host $text
    exit 1
}
Write-Host "  run dir: $runDir" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

$boot = Join-Path $runDir 'bootstrap.log'
$bootText = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $boot) { Get-Content -LiteralPath $boot -Raw } else { '' }
$hook = Join-Path $runDir 'hook.log'
$hookText = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $hook) { Get-Content -LiteralPath $hook -Raw } else { '' }

Check 'the adapter armed' ($bootText -match 'dodge ARMED') `
    'the resolve line names the mode, the grid, the intent and the health source'

Check 'the sensor resolved against this host' ($bootText -match 'sensor read path resolved') `
    'the adapter runs on the sensor''s frame path, so this is its prerequisite'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DID THE PROBE'S SUBJECT RUN AT ALL?  This is assertion F's question, asked
# before any statement about the adapter is believed.
#
# The adapter is called from the managed frame replacement, so it needs the host's frame tick to be
# MATCHED AND PATCHED.  If that did not happen, no frame reaches `DodgeAdapter.OnFrame` and every
# downstream check below reports the absence of something that was never given a chance -- which is
# exactly the failure shape this project keeps writing down, and it must not be reported as a dodge
# defect.  `hook.log` says which it was: a match logs a patch, a near miss logs the hash warning.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$frameTickPatched = ($hookText -match "PATCHED 'frameTick'")
$hashNearMiss = ($hookText -match "matches target 'frameTick' but the hash does not")
$warmupEntered = ($bootText -match 'MANAGED REPLACEMENT entered \(call 1\)')

Check 'the host frame tick was matched and patched' $frameTickPatched `
    $(if ($frameTickPatched) {
        'the managed frame replacement is in the game''s own call path'
      } elseif ($hashNearMiss) {
        'NO -- a size-23 method was hashed and did not match, so this host''s frame tick was never' +
        ' patched and NOTHING below is a statement about the adapter. This is a test-target problem' +
        ' (Test-Injection.ps1 run 7/8), not a dodge problem.'
      } else {
        'NO -- no frameTick match and no hash warning in hook.log'
      })

if (-not $frameTickPatched) {
    Write-Host ''
    Write-Host '  The probe could not run its subject. Everything past this point is unmeasurable,' -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host '  so it is reported as one finding rather than as a row of adapter failures.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
    if ($warmupEntered) {
        Write-Host '  The only entry the adapter ever got was the resolve-time warm-up call, which' -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        Write-Host '  runs before the host has a world -- so it correctly counted one frame with no world.' -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    }
    Write-Host ''
    Write-Host 'PROBE VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE -- the subject never ran (see above).' -ForegroundColor Yellow
    exit 3
}

$numbers = [regex]::Match($bootText, 'PHASE 3 DODGE NUMBERS \| mode ([A-Z ]+) \| frames (\d+)')
Check 'the dodge reported its own numbers' $numbers.Success `
    $(if ($numbers.Success) { "mode '$($numbers.Groups[1].Value.Trim())' over $($numbers.Groups[2].Value) frame(s)" } else { 'no PHASE 3 DODGE NUMBERS line in bootstrap.log' })

# THE EMPTY-TRACE CHECK, IN THIS PROBE'S OWN TERMS. `frames 0` satisfies every other statement on
# the report line vacuously -- defect 3.8, and the reason `SolverHarness` grew assertion F.
$frames = if ($numbers.Success) { [int]$numbers.Groups[2].Value } else { -1 }
Check 'it decided on more than zero frames' ($frames -gt 0) "frames=$frames"

Check 'it reported in DRY RUN' ($bootText -match 'PHASE 3 DODGE NUMBERS \| mode DRY RUN') `
    '--dodge without --dodge-act must never act'

Check 'the detail line was written' ($bootText -match 'PHASE 3 DODGE DETAIL') `
    'candidates, threats, speed and precedence'

# The host has no byte[,] on World and no Player.Totems, so these two are the DEGRADED paths
# being exercised rather than a defect -- and each has to SAY so rather than pass as resolved.
Check 'the missing grid was named, not assumed' ($bootText -match 'collision grid did NOT resolve') `
    'the synthetic host has no byte[,]; the adapter must say walls are ignored'

Check 'the missing totem collection was named' ($bootText -match 'precedence UNRESOLVED') `
    'the host has no Player.Totems, so the precedence rule reports itself unresolved'

# The report line is the one the runner parses, so a silent truncation would break the check above
# in a way that looks like a missing run. 256 is the native buffer.
$lineLengths = @()
foreach ($line in ($bootText -split "`r?`n")) {
    if ($line -match 'dodge ARMED|dodge config|PHASE 3 DODGE|dodge WOULD|steer dodge') { $lineLengths += $line.Length }
}
$longest = if ($lineLengths.Count -gt 0) { ($lineLengths | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum } else { 0 }
Check 'no dodge line exceeds the native 256-byte log buffer' ($longest -le 256) `
    "longest dodge line: $longest character(s), including the [level] prefix"

Write-Host ''
if ($failures.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host 'PROBE VERDICT: the dodge adapter resolves, arms, decides and reports on a live frame path.' -ForegroundColor Green
    exit 0
}
Write-Host "PROBE VERDICT: $($failures.Count) check(s) failed: $($failures -join '; ')" -ForegroundColor Red
exit 1
```

`hook/tools/Resolve-HookRva.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Resolve a `Module+RVA` from a drelay crash report to the nearest symbol in
    the hook's linker map.

.DESCRIPTION
    A crash report from Drelay.Hook.dll names addresses as `Drelay.Hook.dll+0xRVA`
    and there is no debugger on this machine to type them into.  The linker map
    that `build.ps1` now emits is the substitute: it lists every public symbol
    with the address it was placed at, so the nearest symbol at or below an RVA
    names the function that faulted.

    This is a strictly weaker answer than a debugger's -- Release code is built
    with `/OPT:REF /OPT:ICF`, so a static function may have been folded into
    another or dropped entirely, and a static function has no public symbol at
    all.  What it does give is the enclosing function for the RVAs that matter,
    which is what turns "coreclr.dll+0xD828D" into "the reverse-P/Invoke
    transition, called from DrelayInvokeResolveCallback".

    RVAs are read either from the command line or, with -CrashFile, straight out
    of a `crash.txt`.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Resolve-HookRva.ps1 -Rva 0x1A45, 0x3987, 0x2C40

.EXAMPLE
    .\Resolve-HookRva.ps1 -CrashFile "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\drelay\hook\...\crash.txt"
#>
[CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'Rva')]
param(
    [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'Rva', Mandatory = $true, Position = 0)]
    [uint32[]] $Rva,

    [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'Crash', Mandatory = $true)]
    [string] $CrashFile,

    # Which module's RVAs to resolve.  Defaults to the hook's own map, because
    # that is the only module whose symbols exist locally.
    [string] $Map = (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)) 'obj\Drelay.Hook.map'),
    [string] $ModuleName = 'Drelay.Hook.dll'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Map)) {
    Write-Error "no map file at $Map -- run build.ps1, which emits it (link /MAP)."
    exit 1
}

if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'Crash') {
    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $CrashFile -Raw
    $pattern = [regex]::Escape($ModuleName) + '\+0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)'
    $Rva = [regex]::Matches($text, $pattern) |
        ForEach-Object { [uint32]::Parse($_.Groups[1].Value, 'HexNumber') } |
        Sort-Object -Unique
    if (-not $Rva -or $Rva.Count -eq 0) {
        Write-Error "no $ModuleName+0x... addresses in $CrashFile"
        exit 1
    }
}

# The map lists each symbol twice -- once as `section:offset` and once as the
# absolute address it would have at the preferred load address.  The absolute
# form is the one that becomes an RVA, and it is identified by being exactly 16
# hex digits.
$symbols = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
# Parsed from a string rather than written as a hex literal: Windows PowerShell
# reads a hex literal that does not fit in Int32 as a *negative* Int32, so
# `0x180000000` arrives as -6442450944 and the subtraction below overflows.
$preferredBase = [uint64]::Parse('180000000', [System.Globalization.NumberStyles]::HexNumber)
foreach ($line in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $Map)) {
    $m = [regex]::Match($line, '^\s+([0-9A-Fa-f]{4}):([0-9A-Fa-f]{8})\s+(\S+)\s+([0-9A-Fa-f]{16})\s')
    if (-not $m.Success) { continue }
    $absolute = [uint64]::Parse($m.Groups[4].Value, [System.Globalization.NumberStyles]::HexNumber)
    # The map also carries an `<absolute>` group whose addresses are zero, so the
    # subtraction below would underflow and the cast to UInt32 would throw.  They
    # are absolute symbols with no place in the image, so they are skipped.
    if ($absolute -lt $preferredBase) { continue }
    # The preferred base is 0x180000000 for a DLL; the RVA is what is left.
    $symbols.Add([pscustomobject]@{
        Name = $m.Groups[3].Value
        Rva  = [uint32]($absolute - $preferredBase)
    })
}
$symbols.Sort([System.Comparison[object]] { param($a, $b) $a.Rva.CompareTo($b.Rva) })

Write-Host ("{0} symbols from {1}" -f $symbols.Count, (Split-Path -Leaf $Map)) -ForegroundColor DarkGray
Write-Host ''

foreach ($r in $Rva) {
    # The nearest symbol at or below the RVA.  Binary search rather than a scan
    # because the map has thousands of rows and this is run in a loop.
    $lo = 0; $hi = $symbols.Count - 1; $best = $null
    while ($lo -le $hi) {
        $mid = [int](($lo + $hi) / 2)
        if ($symbols[$mid].Rva -le $r) { $best = $symbols[$mid]; $lo = $mid + 1 } else { $hi = $mid - 1 }
    }
    if ($null -eq $best) {
        Write-Host ("{0}+0x{1:X}  <below the first symbol in the map>" -f $ModuleName, $r)
        continue
    }
    $delta = $r - $best.Rva
    # Undecorated is how a C++ name reads; the decorated form is kept alongside
    # because it is what the map and the PDB actually contain, and a name that
    # has been folded by /OPT:ICF only appears decorated.
    $clean = $best.Name
    if ($clean.StartsWith('?')) {
        $clean = ($clean -replace '^[?]', '') -replace '@@.*$', ''
    }
    Write-Host ("{0}+0x{1:X}  =  {2} + 0x{3:X}   [{4}]" -f $ModuleName, $r, $clean, $delta, $best.Name)
}

```

`hook/tools/Run-Endurance.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    The Phase 1 endurance run: N minutes of play with the hook reading live state,
    then the assertions that decide whether it counts.

.DESCRIPTION
    IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md's Exit 1 and PHASE1-VERIFICATION.md section 8 item 7.  The
    hook's recording window is `--live-seconds`, and the evidence files are written when
    it closes, so this script passes `-Minutes` through as that window and then checks:

      launcher exit code 0, no Application Error / .NET Runtime event for the window,
      `phase 1 complete`, frame calls consistent with the whole session, live reads
      present and plausible, the frame read reported PAUSED (the window control fired),
      the hook's own worst frame call inside the 300 us ceiling, and -- from the game's
      own log, which is ground truth (PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 11) -- the zone
      transitions, GCs and slow frames that actually happened while the hook was in.

    WHAT IT CANNOT PROVE.  "No frame regression" is asserted for the hook's own
    measured cost only (`worst call`, measured inside the detour).  The game's own
    `[StallProbe] slow frame` lines are reported as context and never as a pass: the
    game hitches on its own, and there is no hour-long un-hooked baseline to compare
    against, so a claim either way would be invented.

.PARAMETER Minutes
    How long the hook records, in minutes.  The criterion asks for 30-60.
    `--live-seconds` is `Minutes * 60`.

.PARAMETER KeepReading
    Do not pause the frame read when the window closes.  Off by default: the pause is
    the wired control this run is meant to exercise.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Run-Endurance.ps1 -Minutes 60

.EXAMPLE
    # A first, cheaper pass at 30 minutes.
    .\Run-Endurance.ps1 -Minutes 30
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $GamePath = "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion",
    [string] $RunRoot = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'),
    [int]    $Minutes = 60,
    [int]    $CollectDelay = 20000,
    [string] $CaseDir,
    [switch] $KeepReading
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if ($Minutes -lt 1 -or $Minutes -gt 360) { throw "-Minutes must be between 1 and 360" }

$repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)
$out = Join-Path $repo 'hook\out'
$launcher = Join-Path $out 'Drelay.Launcher.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcher)) { throw "no launcher at $launcher -- run build.ps1 first" }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $GamePath)) { throw "no game at $GamePath" }
if (-not $CaseDir) { $CaseDir = Join-Path $repo ("hook\obj\cases\endurance-{0}m" -f $Minutes) }

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $CaseDir | Out-Null
Get-ChildItem $CaseDir -File | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

$checks = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
function Add-Check([string] $name, [string] $state, [string] $detail) {
    $checks.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Check = $name; State = $state; Detail = $detail })
    $colour = switch ($state) { 'PASS' { 'Green' } 'FAIL' { 'Red' } default { 'Yellow' } }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-4} {1,-38} {2}" -f $state, $name, $detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
}

Write-Host "=== Phase 1 endurance run: $Minutes minute(s) ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "case dir      : $CaseDir"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "WHAT TO DO WHILE IT RUNS" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  1. cap the frame rate at 60 in the game's own settings (the design point)"
Write-Host "  2. get into gameplay and stay there for the whole window"
Write-Host "  3. change zones at least once, so a map transition is inside the window"
Write-Host "  4. alt-tab away and back once"
Write-Host "  5. do not close the game until the launcher prints 'phase 1 complete'"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "THE WINDOW IS $Minutes MINUTE(S); the evidence is written when it closes." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host ""

$identity = foreach ($f in 'Drelay.Hook.dll', 'Drelay.Bootstrap.dll', 'Drelay.Launcher.exe') {
    $p = Join-Path $out $f
    "$f  $((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $p -Algorithm SHA256).Hash)"
}
$identity | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'build-identity.txt')
$identity | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  build: $_" -ForegroundColor DarkGray }

Get-Process -Name DarzasDominion, 'Drelay.Launcher' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    ForEach-Object { Write-Host "killing stale $($_.ProcessName) $($_.Id)"; $_.Kill() }
Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500

# The game's own log is ground truth for what actually happened.  Its length is
# recorded now so the run is read from its own offset and not from an older session.
$gameLog = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'RippleStudio\Darza\logs\darza.log'
$logOffsetBefore = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $gameLog) { (Get-Item -LiteralPath $gameLog).Length } else { 0 }

$runDirsBefore = @(Get-ChildItem $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)
$startedLocal = Get-Date
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()


$argv = @(
    '--game', "`"$GamePath`"",
    '--runroot', "`"$RunRoot`"",
    '--collect-delay', $CollectDelay,
	'--live-seconds', ($Minutes * 60),
    '--verbose'
)
$stdout = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stdout.txt'
$stderr = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stderr.txt'

# `DRELAY_KEEP_READING` is a plain `DRELAY_` name precisely so it survives the
# launcher's environment filter and reaches the hook; the child inherits it from here.
#
# THE SWITCH IS WRITTEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS NOW, AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE.  The
# hook's default changed: it keeps reading after the evidence window (that read is the
# sensor the dodge runs on), and `0` is what asks for the pause this run asserts about.
# Leaving the variable unset therefore no longer means "pause", so an absent `-KeepReading`
# has to say so explicitly or the check below would report FAIL on a correct run.
if ($KeepReading) { $env:DRELAY_KEEP_READING = '1' } else { $env:DRELAY_KEEP_READING = '0' }

$child = Start-Process -FilePath $launcher -ArgumentList $argv -PassThru -NoNewWindow `
    -RedirectStandardOutput $stdout -RedirectStandardError $stderr

# TOUCH `.Handle` BEFORE WAITING.  Windows PowerShell 5.1's Start-Process returns a
# Process whose exit code is unreachable (`$child.ExitCode` is $null, and `Refresh()`
# does not help) unless the process handle has been materialised first; PowerShell 7
# is unaffected.  This cost both acceptance runs of 2026-10-12 a false FAIL on
# "launcher exit code 0" while the launcher had in fact exited 0.  Measured on this
# machine: PS 5.1.19041.6328 with -PassThru -NoNewWindow and redirection gives $null
# without this line and the real code with it.
$null = $child.Handle

$timeoutMs = ($Minutes * 60 + 300) * 1000
if (-not $child.WaitForExit($timeoutMs)) {
    Write-Warning "the launcher did not exit within $([int]($timeoutMs / 1000)) s; killing it"
    $child.Kill()
    $child.WaitForExit(10000) | Out-Null
}
$sw.Stop()
$exitCode = $child.ExitCode

$runDir = Get-ChildItem $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $runDirsBefore -notcontains $_.Name } |
    Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $runDir) { throw "the launcher never created a run directory under $RunRoot" }
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "run directory : $($runDir.FullName)"
Write-Host "launcher exit : $exitCode after $([int]$sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds) s"
"exit=$exitCode`nelapsed_s=$([int]$sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)`nminutes=$Minutes`nrundir=$($runDir.FullName)" |
    Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'run.txt')

Get-ChildItem $runDir.FullName -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Copy-Item -Destination $CaseDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# --- the game's own log, from the offset this run started at ----------------------
$newGameLines = @()
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $gameLog) {
    $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($gameLog, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open,
                                 [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read,
                                 [System.IO.FileShare]::ReadWrite)
    try {
        $length = $fs.Length
        # A rotated or truncated log would make the offset meaningless; read it all
        # rather than seek past the end and report an empty window.
        $from = if ($length -ge $logOffsetBefore) { $logOffsetBefore } else { 0 }
        $fs.Seek($from, [System.IO.SeekOrigin]::Begin) | Out-Null
        $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($fs)
        $newGameLines = @($reader.ReadToEnd() -split "`r?`n")
    } finally { $fs.Dispose() }
}
$newGameLines | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'darza.log.window.txt')

# --- event log --------------------------------------------------------------------
$since = $startedLocal.AddSeconds(-5)
$events = Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Application'; StartTime = $since } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.ProviderName -in @('.NET Runtime', 'Application Error', 'Windows Error Reporting') }
$events | ForEach-Object {
    "----- $($_.TimeCreated.ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'))  $($_.ProviderName)  id=$($_.Id)"
    $_.Message
    ''
} | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'eventlog.txt')

# --- assertions --------------------------------------------------------------------
$summaryLines = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $CaseDir 'summary.txt')) { Get-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'summary.txt') } else { @() }
$hookLines = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log')) { Get-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log') } else { @() }
function Get-Summary([string] $pattern) {
    $m = $summaryLines | Select-String -Pattern $pattern | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($m) { $m.Line.Trim() } else { '' }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the run survived ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Add-Check 'launcher exit code 0' `
    $(if ($null -eq $exitCode) { 'GAP' } elseif ($exitCode -eq 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($null -eq $exitCode) { 'the host did not expose the launcher exit code; this is not a pass' } else { "exit=$exitCode" })
$faults = @($events | Where-Object { $_.ProviderName -in @('.NET Runtime', 'Application Error') })
Add-Check 'no fault recorded for the window' $(if ($faults.Count -eq 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($faults.Count -eq 0) { "$Minutes minute(s) with no Application Error / .NET Runtime event" } else { "$($faults.Count) event(s); see eventlog.txt" })
$complete = $hookLines | Select-String -Pattern 'phase 1 complete' | Select-Object -First 1
Add-Check 'the run reached phase 1 complete' $(if ($complete) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($complete) { $complete.Line.Trim() } else { 'no such line in hook.log' })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the window covered the session ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$calls = $null
if ((Get-Summary 'calls\s*:') -match 'calls\s*:\s*(\d+)') { $calls = [int]$Matches[1] }
$expectedMin = $Minutes * 60 * 30      # a 30 Hz average floor
Add-Check 'frame calls cover the window' `
    $(if ($null -ne $calls -and $calls -ge $expectedMin) { 'PASS' } elseif ($null -eq $calls) { 'FAIL' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($null -ne $calls) { "$calls frame(s) over $([int]$sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds) s = $([math]::Round($calls / $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 1)) Hz average; floor for $Minutes min is $expectedMin" } else { 'no calls line in summary.txt' })
$frameRowLine = Get-Summary 'frame rows'
Add-Check 'the frame ring is reported' 'GAP' "$frameRowLine -- an hour cannot fit the ring; the counters above are the endurance evidence, not frames.csv"

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the read ran, and then stopped ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$reads = Get-Summary 'frame reads'
$okCount = $null
if ($reads -match ':\s*(\d+)\s+ok') { $okCount = [int]$Matches[1] }
Add-Check 'live reads happened' $(if ($null -ne $okCount -and $okCount -gt 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) $reads
$valueLine = Get-Summary 'read value'
$value = $null
if ($valueLine -match ':\s*(-?[\d.]+)') { $value = [double]$Matches[1] }
Add-Check 'the value read is plausible' $(if ($null -ne $value -and [math]::Abs($value) -lt 100000) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) $valueLine
$readState = Get-Summary 'frame read\s+:'
Add-Check 'the read was paused at the window close' `
    $(if ($KeepReading) { 'GAP' } elseif ($readState -match 'PAUSED') { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($KeepReading) { '-KeepReading was passed, so the pause is deliberately off' } else { $readState })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the hook's own cost ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$worstLine = Get-Summary 'worst call'
$worst = $null
if ($worstLine -match ':\s*(\d+)\s*us') { $worst = [int]$Matches[1] }
Add-Check 'worst frame call within the 300 us ceiling' `
    $(if ($null -eq $worst) { 'FAIL' } elseif ($worst -le 300) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    "$worstLine -- the first call is the slow one (274 us measured at 60 Hz); the ceiling is HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 7"

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- what the game's own log says ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$maps = @($newGameLines | Select-String -Pattern 'Now playing: ([^,]+), From Map Info: True' |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value.Trim() } | Sort-Object -Unique)
Add-Check 'a map transition is in the window' $(if ($maps.Count -ge 2) { 'PASS' } else { 'GAP' }) `
    "$($maps.Count) distinct map-info track(s): $($maps -join ', ') -- a proxy, because the log names the track and not the map"
$gcCount = @($newGameLines | Select-String -Pattern 'GC').Count
Add-Check 'a collection happened while the hook was in' $(if ($gcCount -ge 1) { 'PASS' } else { 'GAP' }) `
    "$gcCount line(s) mentioning GC in the game's log for this window"
$stalls = @($newGameLines | Select-String -Pattern '\[StallProbe\] slow frame (\d+) ms')
$stallMax = 0
foreach ($s in $stalls) { if ($s.Line -match 'slow frame (\d+) ms') { $m = [int]$Matches[1]; if ($m -gt $stallMax) { $stallMax = $m } } }
Add-Check 'the game hitched on its own, for context only' 'GAP' `
    "$($stalls.Count) slow-frame report(s), worst $stallMax ms -- the game's own watchdog, not the hook's cost; there is no un-hooked hour to compare with"

# --- verdict -----------------------------------------------------------------------
$failed = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'FAIL' })
$gaps = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'GAP' })
$verdict = if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { "ENDURANCE PASS ($Minutes min)" } else { "ENDURANCE FAIL ($Minutes min)" }
Write-Host ""
Write-Host ("{0} -- {1} passed, {2} failed, {3} gap(s)" -f $verdict, ($checks.Count - $failed.Count - $gaps.Count), $failed.Count, $gaps.Count) `
    -ForegroundColor $(if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })
"$verdict`n$($checks | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String)" | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'verdict.txt')
Write-Host "artifacts in $CaseDir"

if ($failed.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }

```

`hook/tools/Run-Exit2a-LogDenial.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Exit 2a: deny the hook its log file while it runs, and assert the four properties.

.DESCRIPTION
    IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md Phase 1 Exit 2a, as a runnable test.

    While the hook is attached and the frame tick is patched, this script holds
    `<run dir>\hook.log` open with sharing disabled -- the mechanism every observed
    append failure has had, a second process holding the file -- releases it, lets the
    run finish, and asserts:

      1. the game is unaffected      the launcher exits 0, the run reaches
                                     `phase 1 complete`, and the Windows event log
                                     records no fault for the window;
      2. the frame cost is unchanged frames.csv's elapsed_us against a baseline run's;
                                     the first call is expected to be the one slow
                                     frame and nothing else should be;
      3. the kill was felt           `hook.log.append-failed` exists, and summary.txt
                                     carries `log appends : N failed pass(es)`;
      4. a transient kill lost nothing  `log lines: N written, 0 overflowed` with at
                                     least N lines in hook.log -- the retry caught up.

    THE LOCK IS TAKEN DURING THE COLLECTION DELAY, so it is held before the evidence
    files are written.  That is the ordering assertion 3 needs for the `summary.txt`
    line to appear at all, and it is why the default `-CollectDelay` is not zero.

    The script also proves that the lock denies a write to itself (see "control"): a
    run that reports no append failure must not be a run whose control never engaged
    -- PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 8, third question.

.PARAMETER BaselineRunDir
    An uninterrupted run of the same build, for assertion 2's comparison.  Defaults to
    the operator's ARMED run of 2026-10-11 when it is still present.

.PARAMETER KeepReading
    Let the frame read stay open when the evidence window closes (DRELAY_KEEP_READING=1).
    Without it this script writes DRELAY_KEEP_READING=0, which pauses the read -- the
    hook's behaviour before the release default changed.  This test does not need the
    read to stay open, and asking for the pause keeps its runs comparable with the ones
    recorded earlier.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Run-Exit2a-LogDenial.ps1 -Verbose

.EXAMPLE
    # A different collection delay, for an operator who needs longer in the menu.
    .\Run-Exit2a-LogDenial.ps1 -CollectDelay 30000
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $GamePath = "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion",
    [string] $RunRoot = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'),
    [int]    $CollectDelay = 20000,
    [int]    $LiveSeconds = 20,
    [int]    $HoldSeconds = 25,
    [string] $CaseDir,
    [string] $BaselineRunDir = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook\20261011-221035-p4364'),
    [switch] $KeepReading
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)
$out = Join-Path $repo 'hook\out'
$launcher = Join-Path $out 'Drelay.Launcher.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcher)) { throw "no launcher at $launcher -- run build.ps1 first" }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $GamePath)) { throw "no game at $GamePath" }
if (-not $CaseDir) { $CaseDir = Join-Path $repo 'hook\obj\cases\exit2a-logdenial' }

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $CaseDir | Out-Null
Get-ChildItem $CaseDir -File | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

$checks = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
function Add-Check([string] $name, [string] $state, [string] $detail) {
    $checks.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Check = $name; State = $state; Detail = $detail })
    $colour = switch ($state) { 'PASS' { 'Green' } 'FAIL' { 'Red' } default { 'Yellow' } }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-4} {1,-34} {2}" -f $state, $name, $detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
}

Write-Host "=== Exit 2a: the log target is denied to the hook ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "case dir      : $CaseDir"
Write-Host "baseline      : $BaselineRunDir"

# --- the build this run is pinned to ------------------------------------------
$identity = foreach ($f in 'Drelay.Hook.dll', 'Drelay.Bootstrap.dll', 'Drelay.Launcher.exe') {
    $p = Join-Path $out $f
    $h = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $p -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    "$f  $h"
}
$identity | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'build-identity.txt')
$identity | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  build: $_" -ForegroundColor DarkGray }

# --- a stale game holds the hook DLL and poisons the next run ------------------
Get-Process -Name DarzasDominion, 'Drelay.Launcher' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    ForEach-Object { Write-Host "killing stale $($_.ProcessName) $($_.Id)"; $_.Kill() }
Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500

$runDirsBefore = @(Get-ChildItem $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)
$startedLocal = Get-Date
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

# --- launch ---------------------------------------------------------------------
$argv = @(
    '--game', "`"$GamePath`"",
    '--runroot', "`"$RunRoot`"",
    '--collect-delay', $CollectDelay,
    '--live-seconds', $LiveSeconds,
    '--verbose'
)
$stdout = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stdout.txt'
$stderr = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stderr.txt'

# `DRELAY_KEEP_READING` is a plain `DRELAY_` name precisely so it survives the
# launcher's environment filter and reaches the hook.
#
# BOTH BRANCHES WRITE IT NOW, because the hook's default changed: it keeps reading after
# the evidence window (that read is the sensor the dodge runs on) and `0` is what asks
# for a pause.  An unset variable therefore no longer means "stop", so `-KeepReading`
# being absent has to say so for this script's runs to stay comparable with the ones
# recorded before the default moved.
if ($KeepReading) { $env:DRELAY_KEEP_READING = '1' } else { $env:DRELAY_KEEP_READING = '0' }

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Launching. Get past the menu and into gameplay when the hook says collection" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "has started; the lock is taken within the first second of the run either way." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host ""

$child = Start-Process -FilePath $launcher -ArgumentList $argv -PassThru -NoNewWindow `
    -RedirectStandardOutput $stdout -RedirectStandardError $stderr

# TOUCH `.Handle` BEFORE WAITING.  Windows PowerShell 5.1's Start-Process returns a
# Process whose exit code is unreachable (`$child.ExitCode` is $null, and `Refresh()`
# does not help) unless the process handle has been materialised first; PowerShell 7
# is unaffected.  This cost both acceptance runs of 2026-10-12 a false FAIL on
# "launcher exit code 0" while the launcher had in fact exited 0.  Measured on this
# machine: PS 5.1.19041.6328 with -PassThru -NoNewWindow and redirection gives $null
# without this line and the real code with it.
$null = $child.Handle

# --- wait for the run directory, then deny its log -------------------------------
$runDir = $null
$deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(60)
while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline -and -not $runDir) {
    $runDir = Get-ChildItem $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $runDirsBefore -notcontains $_.Name } |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $runDir) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 100 }
}
if (-not $runDir) { throw "the launcher never created a run directory under $RunRoot" }
$hookLog = Join-Path $runDir.FullName 'hook.log'

# --- take the log away from the hook ---------------------------------------------
#
# THE MECHANISM IS A SECOND PROCESS HOLDING THE FILE, NOT A DELETE.  Windows keeps a
# deleted file alive while a handle is open, and the hook recreates the path on its
# next flush pass, so a rename or a delete tests nothing.  What every observed failure
# has actually had is another handle on that path -- a scanner, or the launcher's own
# tail -- so the denial here is `FileShare::None`, which refuses the native flusher's
# `_wfopen_s(..., "ab")` for as long as this handle lives.
#
# IT IS TAKEN DURING THE COLLECTION DELAY, BEFORE THE EVIDENCE FILES ARE WRITTEN.
# `summary.txt` prints the failed-append counter when the live window closes, so a lock
# taken after that would leave a `.append-failed` side file and a summary that says
# nothing about it.  Assertion 3 asks for both, and this ordering is what produces both.
$lockDeadline = $startedLocal.AddSeconds($CollectDelay / 1000 + 15)
$lock = $null
while ((Get-Date) -lt $lockDeadline -and -not $lock) {
    try {
        $lock = [System.IO.File]::Open($hookLog, [System.IO.FileMode]::OpenOrCreate,
                                       [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read,
                                       [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
    } catch [System.IO.IOException] {
        # The launcher's live tail opens this same path for microseconds every two
        # seconds; a refusal here is that, and it is worth another try, not a failure.
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 25
    }
}
if (-not $lock) { throw "could not deny $hookLog within the collection delay: another handle never let go" }
$lockTakenAt = Get-Date
Write-Host "log denied    : $hookLog (exclusive since t+$([int]($lockTakenAt - $startedLocal).TotalSeconds) s)" -ForegroundColor Yellow

# --- control: the lock really does deny a write ------------------------------------
#
# ASSERTION 3 IS ONLY EVIDENCE IF THE CONTROL ENGAGED.  A run that reports no append
# failure is a failure of assertion 3 and a pass of assertion 4, and the two are the
# same run unless this proves the denial was real -- PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 8, third
# question.  So a second open of the same path, for writing, is attempted and must fail.
$controlOk = $false
$controlMsg = ''
$probe = $null
try {
    $probe = [System.IO.File]::Open($hookLog, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open,
                                    [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write,
                                    [System.IO.FileShare]::ReadWrite)
} catch [System.IO.IOException] {
    $controlOk = $true
    $controlMsg = $_.Exception.Message
} finally {
    if ($probe) { $probe.Dispose() }
}
"lock taken at : $($lockTakenAt.ToString('o'))`nshare mode    : None (read handle held by this script)`nwrite probe   : $(if ($controlOk) { 'refused' } else { 'SUCCEEDED -- the lock denies nothing' })`nprobe error   : $controlMsg" |
    Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'lock.txt')
Write-Host "lock control  : $(if ($controlOk) { 'a write to the log was refused' } else { 'A WRITE SUCCEEDED; the denial is not real' })" `
    -ForegroundColor $(if ($controlOk) { 'DarkGray' } else { 'Red' })

# --- hold it, then let go ----------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "The log is denied for $HoldSeconds s, across the end of the collection delay and" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "the start of the recording window. Stay in gameplay; do not close the game yet." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host ""
Start-Sleep -Seconds $HoldSeconds
$lock.Dispose()
$lock = $null
Write-Host "lock released : t+$([int]((Get-Date) - $startedLocal).TotalSeconds) s; the hook's retry should recover every line"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Now close the game once the launcher prints 'phase 1 complete'." -ForegroundColor Cyan

# --- wait for the run to finish ----------------------------------------------------
$timeoutMs = [int](($CollectDelay / 1000 + $LiveSeconds + 300) * 1000)
if (-not $child.WaitForExit($timeoutMs)) {
    Write-Warning "the launcher did not exit within $([int]($timeoutMs / 1000)) s; killing it"
    $child.Kill()
    $child.WaitForExit(10000) | Out-Null
}
$sw.Stop()
$exitCode = $child.ExitCode
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "run directory : $($runDir.FullName)"
Write-Host "launcher exit : $exitCode after $([int]$sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds) s"

Get-ChildItem $runDir.FullName -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Copy-Item -Destination $CaseDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

"exit=$exitCode`nelapsed_s=$([int]$sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)`nrundir=$($runDir.FullName)`nlock_taken_local=$($lockTakenAt.ToString('o'))`nwrite_probe_refused=$controlOk" |
    Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'run.txt')

# --- event log ----------------------------------------------------------------------
$since = $startedLocal.AddSeconds(-5)
$events = Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Application'; StartTime = $since } -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.ProviderName -in @('.NET Runtime', 'Application Error', 'Windows Error Reporting') }
$events | ForEach-Object {
    "----- $($_.TimeCreated.ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'))  $($_.ProviderName)  id=$($_.Id)"
    $_.Message
    ''
} | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'eventlog.txt')

# --- assertions --------------------------------------------------------------------
$summaryLines = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $CaseDir 'summary.txt')) { Get-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'summary.txt') } else { @() }
$hookLines = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log')) { Get-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log') } else { @() }
function Get-Summary([string] $pattern) {
    $m = $summaryLines | Select-String -Pattern $pattern | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($m) { $m.Line.Trim() } else { '' }
}

# `elapsed_us` is the last column of frames.csv.  The first call is the JIT-warm one --
# 274 us at 60 Hz in the measured runs and the only slow one -- so it is reported and
# never compared: assertion 2 is about every call after it.
function Get-FrameCost([string] $dir) {
    $path = Join-Path $dir 'frames.csv'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path)) { return $null }
    $all = @(Import-Csv -LiteralPath $path |
        Where-Object { $_.elapsed_us -match '^\d+$' } |
        ForEach-Object { [int]$_.elapsed_us })
    if ($all.Count -eq 0) { return $null }
    $after = if ($all.Count -gt 1) { @($all[1..($all.Count - 1)]) } else { @() }
    $sorted = @($all | Sort-Object)
    $half = [int]($sorted.Count / 2)
    $median = if ($sorted.Count % 2 -eq 1) { $sorted[$half] } else { [int](($sorted[$half - 1] + $sorted[$half]) / 2) }
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Path            = $path
        Count           = $all.Count
        First           = $all[0]
        Worst           = ($all | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum
        WorstAfterFirst = $(if ($after.Count -gt 0) { ($after | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum } else { 0 })
        Median          = $median
    }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- 1. the game is unaffected ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Add-Check 'launcher exit code 0' `
    $(if ($null -eq $exitCode) { 'GAP' } elseif ($exitCode -eq 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($null -eq $exitCode) { 'the host did not expose the launcher exit code; this is not a pass' } else { "exit=$exitCode" })
$faults = @($events | Where-Object { $_.ProviderName -in @('.NET Runtime', 'Application Error') })
Add-Check 'no fault recorded for the window' $(if ($faults.Count -eq 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($faults.Count -eq 0) { 'no Application Error / .NET Runtime event since the launch' } else { "$($faults.Count) event(s); see eventlog.txt" })
$complete = $hookLines | Select-String -Pattern 'phase 1 complete' | Select-Object -First 1
Add-Check 'the run reached phase 1 complete' $(if ($complete) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($complete) { $complete.Line.Trim() } else { 'no such line in hook.log' })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- 2. the frame cost is unchanged ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$runCost = Get-FrameCost $runDir.FullName
$baseCost = Get-FrameCost $BaselineRunDir
Add-Check 'frames.csv carries the run''s frame calls' $(if ($runCost) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($runCost) { "$($runCost.Count) call(s): first $($runCost.First) us, median $($runCost.Median) us, worst $($runCost.Worst) us" } else { "no frames.csv under $($runDir.FullName)" })
Add-Check 'the worst call after the first is inside the 300 us ceiling' `
    $(if ($null -eq $runCost) { 'FAIL' } elseif ($runCost.WorstAfterFirst -le 300) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    "$(if ($runCost) { "$($runCost.WorstAfterFirst) us" } else { 'no frames.csv' }) -- the ceiling is HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 7"
Add-Check 'the cost matches the untouched baseline' `
    $(if ($null -eq $baseCost) { 'GAP' } elseif ($null -eq $runCost) { 'FAIL' } elseif ($runCost.WorstAfterFirst -le [math]::Max($baseCost.WorstAfterFirst * 2, 50)) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($null -eq $baseCost) { "no frames.csv under $BaselineRunDir -- the comparison was not made" } elseif ($null -eq $runCost) { 'this run has no frames.csv' } else { "worst after the first $($runCost.WorstAfterFirst) us vs the baseline's $($baseCost.WorstAfterFirst) us (baseline median $($baseCost.Median) us, worst $($baseCost.Worst) us)" })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- 3. the kill was felt ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Add-Check 'the lock denied a write to itself' $(if ($controlOk) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) $controlMsg
$sidecar = Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log.append-failed'
$hasSidecar = Test-Path -LiteralPath $sidecar
$sideText = if ($hasSidecar) { Get-Content -LiteralPath $sidecar -Raw } else { '' }
Add-Check 'hook.log.append-failed exists' $(if ($hasSidecar) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($hasSidecar) { (@($sideText -split "`r?`n" | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\s*(path|errno|win32 error)\s*:' }) -join ' | ') } else { "no $sidecar -- the hook never reported a failed append" })
$appendLine = Get-Summary 'log appends\s*:'
$failedPasses = $null
if ($appendLine -match ':\s*(\d+)\s+failed') { $failedPasses = [int]$Matches[1] }
Add-Check 'summary.txt counts the failed passes' `
    $(if ($null -ne $failedPasses -and $failedPasses -ge 1) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($appendLine) { "$appendLine -- the lock preceded the evidence write by design" } else { 'no log appends line in summary.txt: the lock did not precede the write, or the denial never reached the hook' })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- 4. a transient kill lost no line ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$linesLine = Get-Summary 'log lines\s*:'
$written = $null
$overflowed = $null
if ($linesLine -match ':\s*(\d+)\s+written,\s*(\d+)\s+overflowed') {
    $written = [int]$Matches[1]
    $overflowed = [int]$Matches[2]
}
Add-Check 'the ring discarded nothing' `
    $(if ($null -ne $overflowed -and $overflowed -eq 0 -and $written -gt 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $linesLine
Add-Check 'every written line reached hook.log' `
    $(if ($null -eq $written) { 'FAIL' } elseif ($hookLines.Count -ge $written) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    "$($hookLines.Count) line(s) in hook.log against $written written -- the read cursor advances only on a successful write, so the retry is the mechanism this asserts"

# --- verdict -----------------------------------------------------------------------
$failed = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'FAIL' })
$gaps = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'GAP' })
$verdict = if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { 'EXIT 2A PASS' } else { 'EXIT 2A FAIL' }
Write-Host ""
Write-Host ("{0} -- {1} passed, {2} failed, {3} gap(s)" -f $verdict, ($checks.Count - $failed.Count - $gaps.Count), $failed.Count, $gaps.Count) `
    -ForegroundColor $(if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })
"$verdict`n$($checks | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String)" | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'verdict.txt')
Write-Host "artifacts in $CaseDir"

if ($failed.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }
```

`hook/tools/Run-Phase2Session.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    A Phase 2 session: play the game with the sensor attached, then publish the four
    decision numbers.

.DESCRIPTION
    IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md's Phase 2 exit criteria, as a runnable session.  The phase is
    read-only -- it changes nothing about the game -- and what it produces is four numbers
    that decide whether a dodge is worth building at all:

      * the WARNING DISTRIBUTION over every collision the client resolved,
      * the FALSE NEGATIVES   (hits the sensor never predicted),
      * the FALSE POSITIVES   (predictions for bullets that never hit), and
      * the PER-FRAME COST    p50 and p99, from bucket histograms rather than a maximum.

    WHY A SCRIPT AND NOT A COMMAND LINE.  The hook writes its evidence into the shared
    block and its logs into the run directory, and the numbers only become the phase's
    numbers once someone has read them out and said which run they came from.  Phase 1
    learned this twice: `Run-Endurance.ps1` and `Run-Exit2a-LogDenial.ps1` exist because a
    run whose assertions live in prose is a run nobody re-checks.  This is the same shape,
    for the same reason.

    IT LAUNCHES THE GAME AND WAITS FOR A PERSON.  Unlike the Phase 1 runners this one
    cannot drive itself: the sensor needs a character in a zone, and the client's menus
    are not automated here.  So it starts the game, prints what to do, waits the requested
    time, kills the game, and analyses.

.PARAMETER Minutes
    How long to play.  Thirty minutes is enough to see collisions; the plan asks for
    several hours before the numbers are treated as final.

.PARAMETER AnalyseOnly
    Skip the launch and analyse a run directory that already exists.  This is how the
    analysis is verified without a game, and how a session that has already been played is
    re-read.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Run-Phase2Session.ps1 -Minutes 60

.EXAMPLE
    # Re-read a session that has already been played.
    .\Run-Phase2Session.ps1 -AnalyseOnly "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\drelay\hook\20261012-065927-p21968"
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $GamePath = "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion",
    [string] $RunRoot = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'),
    [int]    $Minutes = 30,
    [int]    $CollectDelayMs = 25000,
    [string] $CaseDir,
    [string] $AnalyseOnly
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)
$out = Join-Path $repo 'hook\out'
$launcher = Join-Path $out 'Drelay.Launcher.exe'
if (-not $CaseDir) { $CaseDir = Join-Path $repo 'hook\obj\cases\phase2-session' }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $CaseDir | Out-Null

$checks = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
function Add-Check([string] $name, [string] $state, [string] $detail) {
    $checks.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Check = $name; State = $state; Detail = $detail })
    $colour = switch ($state) { 'PASS' { 'Green' } 'FAIL' { 'Red' } default { 'Yellow' } }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-4} {1,-46} {2}" -f $state, $name, $detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
}

Write-Host "=== Phase 2 session ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Launch, or analyse
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$runDir = $null

if ($AnalyseOnly) {
    $runDir = Get-Item -LiteralPath $AnalyseOnly -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $runDir) { throw "no run directory at $AnalyseOnly" }
    Write-Host "analysing     : $($runDir.FullName)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
} else {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcher)) { throw "no launcher at $launcher -- run build.ps1 first" }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $GamePath)) { throw "no game at $GamePath" }

    # The game must not already be running: a stale process holds the hook DLL and the
    # next launch's injection fails in a way that looks like the hook refusing to install.
    Get-Process -Name DarzasDominion, 'Drelay.Launcher' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        ForEach-Object { Write-Host "killing stale $($_.ProcessName) $($_.Id)"; $_.Kill() }
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500

    $runRootPath = $RunRoot
    # A run started from an agent harness cannot create its directory under
    # %LOCALAPPDATA% -- the harness confines its children to the workspace -- so the
    # runroot moves inside the repository when the default is not writable.  From an
    # operator's own shell the default is fine.
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $runRootPath)) {
        try { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $runRootPath | Out-Null }
        catch {
            $runRootPath = Join-Path $repo 'hook\obj\live-runs'
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $runRootPath | Out-Null
            Write-Host "runroot moved : $runRootPath" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        }
    }

    $dirsBefore = @(Get-ChildItem $runRootPath -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)
    $startedLocal = Get-Date

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "WHAT TO DO WHILE IT RUNS" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "  1. get past the menu and into a zone with a character"
    Write-Host "  2. play normally -- the sensor is read-only and changes nothing"
    Write-Host "  3. let bullets come at you; that is the whole point of the session"
    Write-Host "  4. do not close the game until this script kills it"
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "THE WINDOW IS $Minutes MINUTE(S)." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host ""

    $argv = @(
        '--game', "`"$GamePath`"",
        '--runroot', "`"$runRootPath`"",
        '--collect-delay', $CollectDelayMs,
        '--live-seconds', ($Minutes * 60),
        '--frame-replacement',          # the sensor is a managed replacement, not a native detour
        '--verbose'
    )

    # `DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR` is a plain `DRELAY_` name, which is what lets it survive the
    # launcher's environment filter -- PHASE1-HANDOFF.md section 4 trap 1.
    $savedSensor = $env:DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR
    $env:DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR = '1'

    $stdout = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stdout.txt'
    $stderr = Join-Path $CaseDir 'launcher.stderr.txt'
    $child = Start-Process -FilePath $launcher -ArgumentList $argv -PassThru -NoNewWindow `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $stdout -RedirectStandardError $stderr
    # Touch `.Handle` before waiting: Windows PowerShell 5.1 returns a Process whose exit
    # code is unreachable otherwise, which cost Phase 1's acceptance runs a false FAIL.
    $null = $child.Handle

    # Wait for the run directory, then for the session.
    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(120)
    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline -and -not $runDir) {
        $runDir = Get-ChildItem $runRootPath -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $dirsBefore -notcontains $_.Name } |
            Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $runDir) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250 }
    }
    if (-not $runDir) { throw "the launcher never created a run directory under $runRootPath" }
    Write-Host "run directory : $($runDir.FullName)" -ForegroundColor Yellow

    # The session's clock starts when the evidence starts, not when the process did: the
    # collection delay and the discovery window are the hook's, not the player's.
    $sessionSeconds = ($Minutes * 60) + 90
    Write-Host "playing for   : $sessionSeconds s" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $sessionSeconds

    Get-Process -Name DarzasDominion -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        ForEach-Object { Write-Host "closing the game ($($_.Id))"; $_.Kill() }
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
    if (-not $child.HasExited) { $child.Kill(); $child.WaitForExit(10000) | Out-Null }
    if (-not $AnalyseOnly) { $env:DRELAY_FRAME_SENSOR = $savedSensor }

    Write-Host "session ended : $([int]((Get-Date) - $startedLocal).TotalSeconds) s" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Evidence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$boot = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $runDir.FullName 'bootstrap.log')) {
    Get-Content (Join-Path $runDir.FullName 'bootstrap.log') -Raw
} else { '' }
$hook = if (Test-Path (Join-Path $runDir.FullName 'hook.log')) {
    Get-Content (Join-Path $runDir.FullName 'hook.log') -Raw
} else { '' }
$boot | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'bootstrap.log')
$hook | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'hook.log')

$bootLines = $boot -split "`r?`n"
function Find-Line([string] $pattern) {
    $m = $bootLines | Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -Last 1
    if ($m) { $m.Trim() } else { '' }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the sensor came up ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$readLine = Find-Line 'sensor read path resolved'
$samplerLine = Find-Line 'trajectory sampler resolved'
$collisionLine = Find-Line 'collision observation resolved'
Add-Check 'the read path resolved against this assembly' $(if ($readLine) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($readLine) { ($readLine -replace '^\[INFO\] boot: ', '') } else { 'no "sensor read path resolved" line' })
Add-Check 'the trajectory sampler resolved' $(if ($samplerLine) { 'PASS' } else { 'GAP' }) `
    $(if ($samplerLine) { ($samplerLine -replace '^\[INFO\] boot: ', '') } else { 'no "trajectory sampler resolved" line' })
Add-Check 'the collision observation resolved' $(if ($collisionLine) { 'PASS' } else { 'GAP' }) `
    $(if ($collisionLine) { ($collisionLine -replace '^\[INFO\] boot: ', '') } else { 'no "collision observation resolved" line' })
```
