```ps1
$entered = @($bootLines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'MANAGED REPLACEMENT entered \(call 1\): total=\d{4,}' })
Add-Check 'the managed replacement was entered by the game' $(if ($entered.Count -gt 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($entered.Count -gt 0) { $entered[0].Trim() } else { 'the replacement was never entered -- the patch did not take effect' })

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "--- the phase's four numbers ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$report = Find-Line 'PHASE 2 NUMBERS'
if ($report) {
    Write-Host ("  {0}" -f ($report -replace '^\[INFO\] boot: ', '')) -ForegroundColor White
} else {
    Add-Check 'the four numbers were published' 'FAIL' 'no "PHASE 2 NUMBERS" line -- the sensor did not run'
}

$warnings = @()
foreach ($line in ($bootLines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'collision: key=' })) {
    if ($line -match 'warning=([\d.]+)ms') { $warnings += [double]$Matches[1] }
}
$predictedHits = 0
$unpredictedHits = 0
foreach ($line in ($bootLines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'collision: key=' })) {
    if ($line -match 'predicted=yes') { $predictedHits++ } else { $unpredictedHits++ }
}

$warningP50 = $null
$warningP90 = $null
if ($warnings.Count -gt 0) {
    $sorted = @($warnings | Sort-Object)
    $warningP50 = $sorted[[int][math]::Floor(($sorted.Count - 1) * 0.50)]
    $warningP90 = $sorted[[int][math]::Floor(($sorted.Count - 1) * 0.90)]
}

Add-Check 'collisions were resolved by the client during the session' `
    $(if ($warnings.Count -ge 1) { 'PASS' } elseif ($report) { 'FAIL' } else { 'GAP' }) `
    "$($warnings.Count) collision decision(s) observed"

# --- WAS THE SESSION EVEN IN THE GAME? -------------------------------------
#
# THE ONE DIAGNOSIS THIS ANALYSIS WAS MISSING, and the first live sessions produced it.
# "0 collisions observed" is the correct verdict both for a session that fought for an hour
# and never got hit and for one that sat at the menu, and those need different responses
# from whoever reads it.  The sensor distinguishes them itself: `frames_read=0` with
# `unreconciled` equal to the frame count means every frame found no world, which is the
# menu -- `World.Shared` is null until a zone loads.  A session that was in the game and
# merely saw no collisions has `frames_read` in the thousands.
$lastSensor = $bootLines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'sensor: frame \d+:' } | Select-Object -Last 1
$framesRead = $null
$unreconciled = $null
$bulletsRead = $null
$bulletsFromLayer = $null
$bulletsFromObjects = $null
$layerNodesWalked = $null
if ($lastSensor -match 'unreconciled=(\d+)') { $unreconciled = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($lastSensor -match 'frames_read=(\d+)') { $framesRead = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($lastSensor -match 'live=(\d+) other=') { $bulletsRead = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($lastSensor -match 'layer_live=(\d+)') { $bulletsFromLayer = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($lastSensor -match 'objects_live=(\d+)') { $bulletsFromObjects = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($lastSensor -match 'layer_nodes=(\d+)') { $layerNodesWalked = [int]$Matches[1] }
if ($null -ne $framesRead) {
    Add-Check 'the client produced a world during the session' `
        $(if ($framesRead -gt 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        $(if ($framesRead -gt 0) {
            "$framesRead frame(s) read the world; $unreconciled had no world"
        } else {
            "EVERY frame found no world ($unreconciled of them): the client never left the menu, so this session produced no numbers. The game needs a character in a zone -- the client's own window cannot be captured (BitBlt and PrintWindow both return black), so this cannot be driven from outside; it needs a person."
        })
}

# --- WAS THERE ANYTHING TO READ? -------------------------------------------
#
# THE SECOND DIAGNOSIS THIS ANALYSIS WAS MISSING, AND IT COST A SESSION.  The world check
# above passes on a Nexus, on a menu with a scene loaded, and on any frame where
# `World.Shared` is non-null -- and the evening session of 2026-10-12 passed it with
# 54 599 frames read, hours of gameplay in the game's own log, and not one bullet in the
# sensor, because the sensor was reading `World.Objects` and the client keeps its
# projectiles in `World.GameObjectLayer.Children`.  "In a world" and "reading the thing
# this phase is about" are different facts and they need different verdict lines.
Add-Check 'the sensor read projectiles from the world' `
    $(if ($null -ne $bulletsRead -and $bulletsRead -gt 0) { 'PASS' }
      elseif ($null -ne $framesRead -and $framesRead -gt 0) { 'FAIL' }
      else { 'GAP' }) `
    $(if ($null -ne $bulletsRead -and $bulletsRead -gt 0) {
        "$bulletsRead live projectile(s) on the last sensor frame: $bulletsFromLayer from the layer's $layerNodesWalked node(s), $bulletsFromObjects from World.Objects"
    } elseif ($null -ne $framesRead -and $framesRead -gt 0) {
        "0 projectile(s) on the last sensor frame after $framesRead frame(s) with a world. A session that fought and never got shot is possible, but a session that never SAW a bullet cannot produce a warning distribution, a false-negative rate or a false-positive rate -- check `objects_live`/`layer_live` above, and the game's own log at %LOCALAPPDATA%\RippleStudio\Darza\logs\darza.log for whether bullets were on screen."
    } else {
        "no sensor line carried a projectile count -- the read path did not resolve"
    })

if ($warnings.Count -gt 0) {
    Add-Check 'the warning distribution' 'PASS' `
        ("min {0:N1} ms / p50 {1:N1} / p90 {2:N1} / max {3:N1} over {4} hit(s)" -f `
            ($warnings | Measure-Object -Minimum).Minimum, $warningP50, $warningP90, `
            ($warnings | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum, $warnings.Count)
    Add-Check 'the false negatives' 'PASS' "$unpredictedHits hit(s) the sensor had not predicted"
}

# The cost, from the report line's own percentiles.  The phase's criterion is that the
# sensor fits the frame with room for the solver, and HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 gives
# the frame tick 150 us of a 16.7 ms frame.
if ($report -match 'read n=(\d+) p50<=(\d+)us p99<=(\d+)us') {
    $readN = [int]$Matches[1]; $readP50 = [int]$Matches[2]; $readP99 = [int]$Matches[3]
    # The histogram's edges include the 150 us slice and the 300 us ceiling, so this is a
    # decision and not an interval: a run whose p99 lands above 150 has said so.
    Add-Check 'the read cost is inside the frame-tick slice' `
        $(if ($readP99 -le 150) { 'PASS' } elseif ($readP99 -le 300) { 'FAIL' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        "read p50 <= $readP50 us, p99 <= $readP99 us over $readN frame(s); the slice is 150 us and the ceiling 300"
} else {
    Add-Check 'the read cost is inside the frame-tick slice' 'GAP' 'no cost percentiles in the report line'
}
if ($report -match 'sampler n=(\d+) p50<=(\d+)us p99<=(\d+)us') {
    $sampN = [int]$Matches[1]; $sampP50 = [int]$Matches[2]; $sampP99 = [int]$Matches[3]
    Add-Check 'the sampler cost is inside the frame-tick slice' `
        $(if ($sampP99 -le 150) { 'PASS' } elseif ($sampP99 -le 300) { 'FAIL' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        "sampler p50 <= $sampP50 us, p99 <= $sampP99 us over $sampN frame(s)"
} else {
    Add-Check 'the sampler cost is inside the frame-tick slice' 'GAP' 'no sampler percentiles in the report line'
}

# THE FIFTH NUMBER, AND THE PROVENANCE OF THE OTHER FOUR.  PHASE2-SCOPE.md section 2 names
# the straight fraction separately from the four, and the source split is what makes the
# four believable: `warnings: 0` is a very different statement when the sensor read no
# bullets at all, and the 2026-10-12 evening run is exactly that case.
if ($report -match 'projectiles: (\d+) observation\(s\) from the layer.s (\d+) node\(s\), (\d+) from World\.Objects') {
    Add-Check 'the report names the projectile source' 'PASS' `
        "$($Matches[1]) from the layer's $($Matches[2]) node(s), $($Matches[3]) from World.Objects"
} else {
    Add-Check 'the report names the projectile source' 'GAP' 'no "projectiles:" field in the report line'
}
if ($report -match 'linearity: (\d+) linear, (\d+) not, straight fraction (\d+[.,]\d+)') {
    Add-Check 'the straight fraction is published' 'PASS' `
        "$($Matches[1]) linear, $($Matches[2]) not, straight fraction $($Matches[3]) -- the fifth measurement the plan names"
} else {
    Add-Check 'the straight fraction is published' 'GAP' 'no "linearity:" field in the report line'
}

if ($report -match 'false positives: (\d+)') {
    Add-Check 'the false positives' 'PASS' "$($Matches[1]) prediction(s) for bullets that never hit"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verdict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$failed = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'FAIL' })
$gaps = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'GAP' })
$verdict = if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { "PHASE 2 SESSION OK" } else { "PHASE 2 SESSION INCOMPLETE" }
Write-Host ""
Write-Host ("{0} -- {1} passed, {2} failed, {3} gap(s)" -f $verdict, `
    ($checks.Count - $failed.Count - $gaps.Count), $failed.Count, $gaps.Count) `
    -ForegroundColor $(if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })

$header = @(
    $verdict,
    "run       : $($runDir.FullName)",
    "analysed  : $(Get-Date -Format o)",
    "warnings  : $($warnings.Count) hit(s), min $([math]::Round(($warnings | Measure-Object -Minimum).Minimum,1)) ms, p50 $warningP50 ms, p90 $warningP90 ms, max $([math]::Round(($warnings | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum,1)) ms",
    "predicted : $predictedHits hit(s) predicted, $unpredictedHits not (false negatives)",
    "",
    "the four numbers, as the hook published them:",
    ($report -replace '^\[INFO\] boot: ', ''),
    "",
    "checks:"
)
$header + ($checks | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String) | Set-Content (Join-Path $CaseDir 'verdict.txt')
Write-Host "artifacts in $CaseDir"

if ($failed.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }

```

`hook/tools/Run-Phase3Session.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    A Phase 3 session: run one of the phase's experiments and publish a verdict.

.DESCRIPTION
    IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md's Phase 3 criteria, as runnable sessions.  Phase 3 asks one question
    with three ways of failing it, so this runner offers the three experiments that answer it:

      * `Sweep`  -- `--move-steer sweep:240`.  Walks eight evenly spaced INPUT angles, 240 frames
                    each, and logs the commanded value beside the value read back and the heading
                    the player actually travelled.  This is the calibration run: it measures the
                    `MoveAngle + (-WorldRotation + aimOffset)` transform instead of assuming it,
                    and it is the run whose displacement log is the per-frame half of the move
                    budget (PHASE3-SCOPE.md section 5.2 measured the other half offline).
      * `Hold`   -- `--move-steer hold:DEG:FRAMES`.  One world heading, the shape the solver's
                    output takes.  A run of this is what "the dodge can steer" will look like.
      * `Escape` -- `--escape-test SEC`.  Calls `World.RequestEscape()` once, from inside the
                    game, SEC seconds after the world exists.  This is the FLOOR -- the thing
                    reached when no admissible move avoids lethal damage -- and it is tested
                    alone, before the solver exists to need it, because `escape` was reported
                    MISSING in the live run of 2026-10-13 for the one reason a target can be
                    missing with nothing wrong: nothing had ever called it.
      * `Dodge`  -- `--dodge-act`.  DELIVERABLE 3.3, AND THE RUN THAT IS NOT A CALIBRATION.
                    The solver decides at the frame tick and the pilot writes its answer at the
                    movement integrator's entry; on every frame the adapter publishes no command
                    the pilot writes nothing and the player's own input stands.  This is the first
                    session in which the decision and the game share a frame.

    `-Dodge` IS A SEPARATE SWITCH, NOT AN EXPERIMENT.  It adds the DRY RUN (`--dodge`) to whatever
    else the run is doing -- the solver decides on every frame and logs what it would have done,
    and nothing moves on its word.  That is the mode to run first, it is the paired-trial evidence
    IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md asks for, and it is the only shape in which the decision can be lined up
    against a session's health trace before anything acts on it.

    It can also run all three end to end (`-Experiment All`), which is the cheapest way for an
    operator to answer the whole spike in one sitting.

    WHY A SCRIPT AND NOT A COMMAND LINE.  Same reason as `Run-Phase2Session.ps1`: the evidence
    only becomes a result once someone has read it out and said which run it came from, and a
    run whose assertions live in prose is a run nobody re-checks.

    IT LAUNCHES THE GAME AND WAITS FOR A PERSON.  The client's menus are not automated from
    outside -- the window renders black to every capture path tried (PHASE2-SCOPE.md section
    4.13) -- so this starts the game, says what to do, waits, closes it, and analyses.  **The
    character will walk on its own during Sweep and Hold.**  Run it somewhere it does not matter.

    THE GAME CRASHING WHEN YOU CLOSE IT IS EXPECTED AND IS NOT THIS RUN'S RESULT.  Every Phase 3
    run so far has left a `crash.txt` and an event-log `0x80131506` at the moment the operator
    closed the game; a control run with steering switched off and the movement target unpatched
    reproduced it, so it belongs to the hook's long-standing close behaviour and not to this
    phase (PHASE3-SCOPE.md section 5.1). Read the verdict, not the crash file.

.PARAMETER Experiment
    Sweep, Hold, Escape, or All.  Default Sweep.

.PARAMETER Seconds
    How long to keep the game open.  **This has to outlast the phases or the run proves nothing**:
    `sweep:240` needs about 35 s of gameplay for its eight phases and `hold` 600 frames is about
    10 s, so the default is generous and a run closed early reports "no phase summary" -- which is
    what the first two live attempts show.  It does NOT include the game's own startup: the hook's
    collection delay plus the time to reach a zone is on top.

.PARAMETER Character
    The character slot for the `Hold` experiment's preview.  Recorded in the verdict so the run
    can be attributed; it is not sent to the game.

.PARAMETER RelayLog
    The relay's session log, if the relay was run alongside.  Needed for the two checks that only
    the wire can answer: whether the server sent `GmKicked` (movement validation) and whether the
    escape actually left the machine (`GmEscape` / `EscapeAck`).  Without it those checks report
    "no relay log given" rather than a pass.

.PARAMETER AnalyseOnly
    Skip the launch and analyse a run directory that already exists.  This is how the analysis is
    verified without a game, and how a session that has already been played is re-read.

.PARAMETER Trace
    SPIKE 3.2: record `trace.jsonl` in the run directory -- one line per frame with the player, the
    collision grid and every threat's sampled path.  It is OFF BY DEFAULT because it is expensive:
    about a kilobyte per bullet per frame, so a busy thirty-second session is tens of megabytes.
    The recorder turns the Phase 2 sensor on for itself, because the trace's input is that sensor's
    output.

    The file is what `tools\SolverHarness` reads.  Without a recorded trace, T7 -- "predicted and
    actual collision agree" -- cannot be evaluated at all: it is the one invariant that needs a
    session somebody actually played.

.EXAMPLE
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Sweep -Seconds 240

.EXAMPLE
    # A recording session, then the offline solver over it.  The character will walk.
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Hold -Seconds 300 -Trace
    tools\SolverHarness\bin\Release\SolverHarness.exe --trace <run>\trace.jsonl --collisions <run>\bootstrap.log

.EXAMPLE
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Sweep -Seconds 240

.EXAMPLE
    # All three, one after another -- the operator stays in the world between them.
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment All -Seconds 240 -RelayLog .\logs\relay-....log

.EXAMPLE
    # THE DRY RUN.  The solver decides on every frame and logs every move it would have made;
    # nothing is written to the input.  Beat on by some bullets and read the DODGE NUMBERS line.
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Hold -Seconds 180 -Dodge

.EXAMPLE
    # THE LIVE DODGE.  The solver steers.  Somewhere it does not matter.
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Dodge -Seconds 180 -RelayLog .\logs\relay-....log

.EXAMPLE
    # Re-read a run that has already been played.
    .\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -AnalyseOnly "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\drelay\hook\20261014-023248-p5392"
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('Sweep', 'Hold', 'Escape', 'Dodge', 'All')]
    [string] $Experiment = 'Sweep',
    [string] $GamePath = "E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Darza's Dominion",
    [string] $RunRoot = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'),
    [int]    $Seconds = 240,
    [int]    $HoldDegrees = 90,
    [int]    $HoldFrames = 600,
    [int]    $EscapeAfterSeconds = 25,
    [string] $RelayLog,
    [string] $CaseDir,
    [string] $AnalyseOnly,
    [string] $DrelayRoot,
    [switch] $Trace,
    # DELIVERABLE 3.3'S DRY RUN, ON ANY EXPERIMENT. `-Dodge` adds `--dodge` to the launch
    # whatever else the run is doing, so a `Hold` run can carry the decision stream beside the
    # steering evidence -- which is exactly the shape SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md's section 6
    # keeps asking for and the only way the dry run gets a real session.
    [switch] $Dodge,
    # NOT A FEATURE: A NAMED REFUSAL. `-Dodge` is the dry run and `-Experiment Dodge` is the
    # acting one, and that pair was confused by a caller who reached for `-DodgeAct` -- which
    # PowerShell refused with "A parameter cannot be found", a message that names what is
    # missing and not what to type. The switch exists so the mistake binds and gets an answer.
    [switch] $DodgeAct
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THIS SCRIPT MUST SURVIVE A FAILURE, WHICH IT DID NOT.
#
# The first version ran with `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` and wrapped the launch in
# `& $launcher @argv`. The launcher writes its own errors and returns non-zero, and a
# *native* non-zero exit under `Stop` is raised as a terminating error -- so the script
# died on the launch line, printed nothing about why, and stopped before it analysed
# anything. That is exactly what the operator saw: "prints stuff but exits very quickly".
# A diagnostic tool that quits at the first failure cannot diagnose one, so failures are
# collected and reported here instead.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE TWO NAMES THAT DO NOT EXIST, NAMED SO THE CALLER LEARNS THE REAL ONES.
#
# `-Dodge` is the DRY RUN (`--dodge`): the solver decides and logs and MOVES NOBODY.
# `--dodge-act` -- the solver actually steering -- is the `Dodge` EXPERIMENT
# (`-Experiment Dodge`). Two things named "dodge" that do opposite things is a trap,
# and it was walked into: a session was launched with `-DodgeAct`, PowerShell had no
# parameter of that name, and the command died before the game started. The message
# then was "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'DodgeAct'",
# which says what is missing and not what to type.
#
# A near-miss is REFUSED rather than ignored, because `-DodgeAct` is close enough to a
# real switch that accepting it silently would be worse than stopping: a run that
# looks like it acted and only decided is exactly the shape of mistake section 6 of
# HANDOFF-DIRECTED-DODGE.md keeps recording.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
foreach ($key in $MyInvocation.BoundParameters.Keys) {
    if ($key -eq 'DodgeAct') {
        Write-Host "there is no -$key switch, and this is the pair that gets confused:" -ForegroundColor Red
        Write-Host "  -Dodge                  the DRY RUN: the solver decides, logs, and moves NOBODY" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "  -Experiment Dodge       the ACTING run: the solver steers the character" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "for a live acting session, recorded so it can be measured afterwards:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Write-Host "  .\hook\tools\Run-Phase3Session.ps1 -Experiment Dodge -Seconds 300 -Trace" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        exit 2
    }
}

# AND THE OTHER HALF OF THAT MISTAKE, WHICH COSTS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN A RUN: an ACTING session
# with no `-Trace` decides correctly and leaves nothing behind to measure. `20261015-212859-p34740`
# is that run -- `mode=LIVE`, `dryRun=False`, the right build, and `trace.jsonl` at 0 bytes.
if ($Experiment -eq 'Dodge' -and -not $Trace -and -not $AnalyseOnly) {
    Write-Host "this is the ACTING experiment with no -Trace: the dodge will steer, and the run" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "will leave no trace.jsonl to measure it against afterwards." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "  add -Trace to record it, or press on if you only want to feel it." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host ""
}

# A LAUNCHER CANNOT CREATE A RUN DIRECTORY IN A CONFINED SHELL, AND THE FAILURE LOOKS LIKE
# NOTHING AT ALL. When this script is run from the agent harness, `Directory.CreateDirectory`
# for the run directory throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` inside the launcher, which
# prints one `FAILED:` line and exits 1 -- before the game starts. The check below is the
# difference between that and a verdict that says so.
function Test-RunRoot {
    param([string] $Path)
    try {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Path -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
        }
        $probe = Join-Path $Path ('.phase3-write-probe-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $probe -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $probe -Force -ErrorAction Stop
        return $null
    } catch {
        return $_.Exception.Message
    }
}

$repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)
$out = Join-Path $repo 'hook\out'
$launcher = Join-Path $out 'Drelay.Launcher.exe'
$report = Join-Path $repo 'hook\tools\steering_report.py'
if (-not $CaseDir) { $CaseDir = Join-Path $repo 'hook\obj\cases\phase3-session' }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $CaseDir | Out-Null

$checks = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
function Add-Check([string] $name, [string] $state, [string] $detail) {
    $checks.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Check = $name; State = $state; Detail = $detail })
    $colour = switch ($state) { 'PASS' { 'Green' } 'FAIL' { 'Red' } default { 'Yellow' } }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-4} {1,-52} {2}" -f $state, $name, $detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
}

Write-Host "=== Phase 3 session ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The experiment commands
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function Get-SteerArgument([string] $which) {
    switch ($which) {
        'Sweep'  { return @('--move-steer', "sweep:240") }
        'Hold'   { return @('--move-steer', "hold:${HoldDegrees}:${HoldFrames}") }
        'Escape' { return @('--escape-test', "$EscapeAfterSeconds") }
        # THE ONE EXPERIMENT THAT IS NOT A CALIBRATION. `--dodge-act` puts the pilot in dodge mode
        # and lets the solver write the heading; every frame it publishes nothing, the player's own
        # input stands. It carries its own actuator flags, so no `--move-steer` is added beside it.
        'Dodge'  { return @('--dodge-act') }
        default  { throw "no steer argument for '$which'" }
    }
}

function Get-ExperimentNote([string] $which) {
    switch ($which) {
        'Sweep'  { return "the character will WALK, turning a quarter-turn every 240 frames (~4 s). Let it." }
        'Hold'   { return "the character will WALK at $HoldDegrees deg for about $([math]::Round($HoldFrames / 60.0, 1)) s, then stop." }
        'Escape' { return "nothing moves; the hook will press the nexus ONCE, about $EscapeAfterSeconds s after the world loads." }
        'Dodge'  { return "THE SOLVER STEERS. The character moves only where the decision sends it, and stands still where the player's own input is left alone. Run it somewhere it does not matter." }
        default  { return "" }
    }
}

$toRun = if ($Experiment -eq 'All') { @('Sweep', 'Hold', 'Escape') } else { @($Experiment) }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Launch, or analyse
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$launchedRuns = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]

if ($AnalyseOnly) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $AnalyseOnly)) {
        Write-Host "no run directory at $AnalyseOnly" -ForegroundColor Red
        exit 2
    }
    $launchedRuns.Add((Get-Item -LiteralPath $AnalyseOnly).FullName) | Out-Null
    Write-Host "analysing     : $AnalyseOnly" -ForegroundColor Yellow
} else {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcher)) {
        Write-Host "no launcher at $launcher -- run hook\build.ps1 first" -ForegroundColor Red
        exit 2
    }

    # PRE-FLIGHT, AND IT IS THE CHECK THAT WAS MISSING. A run root this process cannot write
    # to makes the launcher fail before the game starts, and the only symptom is one line the
    # caller may not read. Catching it here names the problem instead.
    $rootProblem = Test-RunRoot $RunRoot
    if ($rootProblem) {
        Write-Host "the run root is not writable: $RunRoot" -ForegroundColor Red
        Write-Host "  $rootProblem" -ForegroundColor Red
        Write-Host "  Pass -RunRoot <a directory this shell can create in>, e.g." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "  -RunRoot (Join-Path `$env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook')" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        exit 2
    }

    foreach ($which in $toRun) {
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "--- $which ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
        Write-Host "  launch      : $launcher" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        Write-Host "  experiment  : $which" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        Write-Host ("  NOTE        : {0}" -f (Get-ExperimentNote $which)) -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "  Get into a world and stay there. Closing the game early is the one way to" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "  waste the run: the phases need the seconds they ask for." -ForegroundColor Yellow

        # THE RUN ROOT IS PASSED, NOT INHERITED. A confined shell cannot let the launcher create
        # its own directory under %LOCALAPPDATA%, and the launcher already has the switch.
        $argv = @('--game', $GamePath, '--live-seconds', "$Seconds", '--runroot', $RunRoot)
        $argv += Get-SteerArgument $which
        # SPIKE 3.2's RECORDING, AND IT RIDES ON THE RUN RATHER THAN REPLACING IT.
        #
        # ONE FLAG, BECAUSE THE THREE DEPENDENCIES BELONG TO THE LAUNCHER. A trace needs the
        # recorder, the recorder is called from the MANAGED frame replacement, and its input is the
        # Phase 2 sensor's threat set. Miss any one of the three and the run writes a valid, empty
        # trace -- indistinguishable from a session in which no bullet came near. That is what the
        # run of `20261014-164314-p12060` produced, so `--trace` now sets all three, and this runner
        # passes the switch rather than setting an environment variable and hoping.
        if ($Trace) {
            $argv += '--trace'
            Write-Host "  trace       : the run will write trace.jsonl into its run directory" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        }
        # THE DRY RUN RIDES ON WHATEVER EXPERIMENT WAS ASKED FOR. `-Experiment Dodge` already asked
        # for the acting form, so it is not doubled here.
        if ($Dodge -and $which -ne 'Dodge') {
            $argv += '--dodge'
            Write-Host "  dodge       : the solver will DECIDE on every frame and log what it would" -ForegroundColor Yellow
            Write-Host "                have done. It will not write the input." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        }
        Write-Host "  command     : Drelay.Launcher.exe $($argv -join ' ')" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        Write-Host "  The launcher stays attached and streams the hook's log. Close the game when" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        Write-Host "  the character has finished walking." -ForegroundColor DarkGray

        $before = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                    Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)

        # THE LAUNCHER IS ALLOWED TO FAIL WITHOUT TAKING THIS SCRIPT WITH IT. It returns
        # non-zero on a refusal (a fingerprint mismatch, a denied run root), and that refusal is
        # the most useful thing in the transcript.
        & $launcher @argv 2>&1 | Tee-Object -Variable launcherOutput | Out-Null
        $launcherExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        foreach ($line in $launcherOutput) { Write-Host "  | $line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray }
        if ($launcherExit -ne 0) {
            Add-Check "$which launched" 'FAIL' "the launcher exited $launcherExit (see its own lines above)"
        } else {
            Add-Check "$which launched and the game was closed" 'PASS' "launcher exit 0"
        }

        $after = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $RunRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                   Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name)
        $new = @($after | Where-Object { $_ -notin $before })
        if ($new.Count -ge 1) {
            $newest = $new | Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
            $launchedRuns.Add((Join-Path $RunRoot $newest)) | Out-Null
            Write-Host "  run dir     : $(Join-Path $RunRoot $newest)" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        } else {
            Add-Check "$which produced a run directory" 'FAIL' "no new directory under $RunRoot"
        }
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The report, once per run
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$allText = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
foreach ($dir in $launchedRuns) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "--- report: $dir ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $argv = @($report, $dir)
    if ($RelayLog) { $argv += $RelayLog }
    $text = & python @argv 2>&1 | Out-String
    Write-Host $text
    $allText.Add($text) | Out-Null
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verdict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "=== verdict ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$joined = ($allText -join "`n")

# The three things the experiment is for, in the order the plan states them.  Each is read from
# the report's own PASS/FAIL lines rather than recomputed here, so there is one place that
# decides what a run means and this script only states it.
$steered = $joined -match 'PASS A the input landed'
$moved = $joined -match 'PASS B the integrator acted'
$direction = $joined -match "PASS C the direction was obeyed" -or $joined -match "PASS C'"
$patched = $joined -match 'PASS the movement target was PATCHED'
$noKick = $joined -match 'PASS D the server did not object'
$escapeCalled = $joined -match 'PASS F the escape call was MADE and RETURNED'
$escapeWire = $joined -match "PASS F'' the escape reached the wire"
# NOT-ASKED IS ONLY A FINDING WHEN THERE WAS A RUN TO ASK OF. This read
# `$joined -notmatch '...not requested...'`, so an EMPTY report -- a launch that failed, or no run
# directory at all -- matched nothing and was therefore taken as "the escape was requested", and
# the verdict grew two escape checks that could only fail. A negative test against an empty set is
# not a negative result; it is no result.
$escapeAsked = ($launchedRuns.Count -gt 0) -and
               ($joined -notmatch 'PASS F the escape floor \(not requested this run\)')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DELIVERABLE 3.3'S OWN CHECK, AND IT IS ASSERTION F ALL OVER AGAIN.
#
# The adapter's report line is read from `bootstrap.log` directly rather than through the Python
# report, because the report is the ACTUATOR's instrument and this is the solver's. And it is read
# for the same reason `SolverHarness` grew assertion F after defect 3.8: a dodge that never ran, a
# dodge whose sensor never resolved and a dodge that ran and found nothing are three different
# findings, and only the frame count separates them. `frames 0` is a failure even though every
# other number on the line is a perfectly valid zero.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$dodgeAsked = $Dodge -or ($Experiment -eq 'Dodge')
$dodgeFrames = -1
$dodgeMode = 'none'
$dodgeLine = $null
foreach ($dir in $launchedRuns) {
    $boot = Join-Path $dir 'bootstrap.log'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $boot)) { continue }
    $hit = Select-String -LiteralPath $boot -Pattern 'PHASE 3 DODGE NUMBERS \| mode ([A-Z ]+) \| frames (\d+)' |
           Select-Object -Last 1
    if ($hit) {
        $dodgeMode = $hit.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value.Trim()
        $dodgeFrames = [int]$hit.Matches[0].Groups[2].Value
        $dodgeLine = $hit.Line
    }
}

if ($launchedRuns.Count -eq 0) {
    Add-Check 'at least one run was produced and analysed' 'FAIL' `
        'nothing was launched or nothing was found to analyse -- the checks below cannot be read'
    Add-Check 'the launcher ran the game' 'FAIL' 'see the launcher output above'
}

Add-Check 'the movement replacement was patched' $(if ($patched) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    'the hook wrote GameScene.GameInput from the game''s own call'

# THE PHASE-BASED CHECKS BELONG TO A PLANNED WALK, AND A DODGE RUN HAS NO PLAN. `-Experiment Dodge`
# runs no phases -- the heading comes from the solver frame by frame -- so `PASS A` has nothing to
# read its `steer frame` lines from unless the solver happened to move, and `PASS B`/`C` need phase
# summaries that will never exist. Asking for them would fail a successful run for being the wrong
# experiment, which is the "negative test against an empty set" this script's own comment warns
# about. `-Dodge` BESIDE another experiment keeps them, because that run really is a planned walk.
if ($Experiment -ne 'Dodge') {
    Add-Check 'the input write landed' $(if ($steered) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'the value read back from MoveAngle equals the value written'

    Add-Check 'the client acted on it' $(if ($moved) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'the player moved on a majority of the phase''s frames'

    Add-Check 'it moved in the commanded direction' $(if ($direction) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'the per-phase observed headings follow the commanded ones'
} else {
    Add-Check 'the movement replacement was exercised in dodge mode' `
        $(if ($dodgeAsked -and $dodgeFrames -ge 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'the pilot writes only what DodgeAdapter publishes'
}

if ($dodgeAsked) {
    Add-Check 'the dodge decided on live frames' $(if ($dodgeFrames -gt 0) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        $(if ($dodgeLine) {
            "the adapter's own line says mode '$dodgeMode' over $dodgeFrames frame(s)"
        } else {
            'no PHASE 3 DODGE NUMBERS line in bootstrap.log -- the adapter never ran (see hook.log for why)'
        })
}

Add-Check 'the server did not object' $(if ($noKick) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
    $(if ($RelayLog) { 'no GmKicked in the relay log' } else { 'no relay log given -- cannot be witnessed in-process' })

if ($escapeAsked) {
    Add-Check 'the escape call was reached and returned' $(if ($escapeCalled) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'World.RequestEscape() ran the client''s own gates'
    Add-Check 'the escape left the machine' $(if ($escapeWire) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }) `
        'GmEscape or the escape-cast-state pair on the wire, with EscapeAck back'
}

$failed = @($checks | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'FAIL' }).Count
Write-Host ""
if ($failed -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "VERDICT: the movement question is answered YES for this run." -ForegroundColor Green
    if ($escapeAsked) { Write-Host "         and the escape floor was reached and acknowledged." -ForegroundColor Green }
} else {
    Write-Host "VERDICT: $failed check(s) did not pass. Read them in order -- the first failure is" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "         almost always the cause of the rest." -ForegroundColor Red
}

# The two things a reader needs and neither the report nor the checks carry.
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "  NOT a result of this run:" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
Write-Host "    a crash.txt and an event-log 0x80131506 at the moment you close the game are" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
Write-Host "    expected here. A control run with steering off reproduced them, so they belong to" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
Write-Host "    the hook's close behaviour (PHASE3-SCOPE.md section 5.1), not to Phase 3." -ForegroundColor DarkGray

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Write it down
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$verdictPath = Join-Path $CaseDir 'verdict.txt'
$lines = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$lines.Add("drelay hook -- Phase 3 session verdict")
$lines.Add("=====================================")
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("written       : $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')")
$lines.Add("experiment    : $Experiment")
$lines.Add("seconds asked : $Seconds")
$lines.Add("relay log     : $(if ($RelayLog) { $RelayLog } else { '(none given)' })")
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("runs analysed :")
foreach ($dir in $launchedRuns) { $lines.Add("  $dir") }
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("checks")
foreach ($c in $checks) { $lines.Add(("  {0,-4} {1,-52} {2}" -f $c.State, $c.Check, $c.Detail)) }
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("WHAT THIS RUN ESTABLISHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT")
$lines.Add("  Establishes : " + $(if ($failed -eq 0) {
        "the hook steered the player through the client's own input path and the client obeyed" }
        else { "nothing on its own -- $failed check(s) did not pass; see above" }))
$lines.Add("  Does not    : that the dodge is safe or tuned. This is Spike 3.1: the actuator and the")
$lines.Add("                escape floor, with no solver behind them (DODGE-ALGORITHM.md sections 5-7).")
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("  A crash.txt in a run directory is NOT a result about that run: the reporter cannot see")
$lines.Add("  COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE (0x80131506), and the close-time fault reproduces with steering")
$lines.Add("  off and the movement target unpatched. See PHASE3-SCOPE.md section 5.1.")
$lines.Add("")
$lines.Add("raw reports")
$lines.Add("-----------")
foreach ($t in $allText) {
    foreach ($l in ($t -split "`r?`n")) { $lines.Add("  " + $l) }
}
Set-Content -LiteralPath $verdictPath -Value $lines -Encoding utf8
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "verdict written to $verdictPath" -ForegroundColor Yellow

exit $(if ($failed -eq 0) { 0 } else { 1 })
```

`hook/tools/SolverHarness/MiniJson.cs`:

```cs
// MiniJson.cs -- enough JSON to read what the trace recorder writes, and no more.
//
// WHY NOT `System.Text.Json`. The trace is written by hand as JSON lines by the hook, and the
// hook may not take a dependency it does not already have. Reading it back with a full parser
// would work -- but this project's rule is that a fixture is only evidence if it can be checked
// by eye, and a parser whose behaviour depends on a package version is one more thing between
// the operator's run and the number in the report.
//
// WHY NOT REGULAR EXPRESSIONS. Because the shape is recursive (an array of objects with arrays
// inside) and a regex that "works" on the sample stops working on the frame where a bullet's
// path is one sample long. This is a small recursive-descent parser: about two hundred lines,
// one behaviour, no surprises. It has no error recovery and throws on bad input, which is right:
// a malformed trace should stop the analysis, not be skipped.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Text;

namespace Drelay.SolverHarness
{
    /// <summary>A parsed JSON value, or a fluent accessor for one.</summary>
    public sealed class Json
    {
        private readonly object _value;

        private Json(object value)
        {
            _value = value;
        }

        public static readonly Json Null = new Json(null);

        public bool IsNull => _value == null;
        public bool IsObject => _value is Dictionary<string, Json>;
        public bool IsArray => _value is List<Json>;
        public bool IsNumber => _value is double;

        public double AsDouble(double fallback = 0.0)
        {
            if (_value is double d)
            {
                return d;
            }
            if (_value is string s && double.TryParse(s, NumberStyles.Float,
                                                      CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out double parsed))
            {
                return parsed;
            }
            return fallback;
        }

        public float AsFloat(float fallback = 0.0f) => (float)AsDouble(fallback);

        public int AsInt(int fallback = 0)
        {
            double d = AsDouble(fallback);
            return (int)d;
        }

        public long AsLong(long fallback = 0)
        {
            double d = AsDouble(fallback);
            return (long)d;
        }

        public bool AsBool(bool fallback = false)
        {
            if (_value is bool b)
            {
                return b;
            }
            if (_value is double d)
            {
                return d != 0.0;
            }
            return fallback;
        }

        public string AsString(string fallback = "")
        {
            if (_value is string s)
            {
                return s;
            }
            return fallback;
        }

        /// <summary>The array's elements, or an empty list. Never null, so callers need no branch.</summary>
        public List<Json> Items => _value as List<Json> ?? new List<Json>();

        public int Count => Items.Count;

        /// <summary>A member of an object, or Null. Chained lookups therefore never throw.</summary>
        public Json this[string name]
        {
            get
            {
                if (_value is Dictionary<string, Json> map && map.TryGetValue(name, out Json found))
                {
                    return found;
                }
                return Null;
            }
        }

        public bool Has(string name) => _value is Dictionary<string, Json> map && map.ContainsKey(name);

        /// <summary>Parses one line. The trace is JSON Lines, so this is called once per line.</summary>
        public static Json Parse(string text)
        {
            int index = 0;
            Json value = ParseValue(text, ref index);
            SkipWhitespace(text, ref index);
            if (index != text.Length)
            {
                throw new FormatException("trailing content at offset " + index);
            }
            return value;
        }

        private static void SkipWhitespace(string s, ref int i)
        {
            while (i < s.Length && (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\t' || s[i] == '\r' || s[i] == '\n'))
            {
                i++;
            }
        }

        private static Json ParseValue(string s, ref int i)
        {
            SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
            if (i >= s.Length)
            {
                throw new FormatException("unexpected end of input");
            }
            char c = s[i];
            switch (c)
            {
                case '{': return ParseObject(s, ref i);
                case '[': return ParseArray(s, ref i);
                case '"': return new Json(ParseString(s, ref i));
                case 't': Expect(s, ref i, "true"); return new Json(true);
                case 'f': Expect(s, ref i, "false"); return new Json(false);
                case 'n': Expect(s, ref i, "null"); return Null;
                default: return new Json(ParseNumber(s, ref i));
            }
        }

        private static void Expect(string s, ref int i, string word)
        {
            if (i + word.Length > s.Length || string.CompareOrdinal(s, i, word, 0, word.Length) != 0)
            {
                throw new FormatException("expected '" + word + "' at offset " + i);
            }
            i += word.Length;
        }

        private static Json ParseObject(string s, ref int i)
        {
            var map = new Dictionary<string, Json>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            i++;   // {
            SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
            if (i < s.Length && s[i] == '}')
            {
                i++;
                return new Json(map);
            }
            while (true)
            {
                SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
                string key = ParseString(s, ref i);
                SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
                if (s[i] != ':')
                {
                    throw new FormatException("expected ':' at offset " + i);
                }
                i++;
                map[key] = ParseValue(s, ref i);
                SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
                if (i < s.Length && s[i] == ',')
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                if (i < s.Length && s[i] == '}')
                {
                    i++;
                    return new Json(map);
                }
                throw new FormatException("expected ',' or '}' at offset " + i);
            }
        }

        private static Json ParseArray(string s, ref int i)
        {
            var list = new List<Json>();
            i++;   // [
            SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
            if (i < s.Length && s[i] == ']')
            {
                i++;
                return new Json(list);
            }
            while (true)
            {
                list.Add(ParseValue(s, ref i));
                SkipWhitespace(s, ref i);
                if (i < s.Length && s[i] == ',')
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                if (i < s.Length && s[i] == ']')
                {
                    i++;
                    return new Json(list);
                }
                throw new FormatException("expected ',' or ']' at offset " + i);
            }
        }

        private static string ParseString(string s, ref int i)
        {
            if (i >= s.Length || s[i] != '"')
            {
                throw new FormatException("expected a string at offset " + i);
            }
            i++;
            var sb = new StringBuilder();
            while (i < s.Length)
            {
                char c = s[i++];
                if (c == '"')
                {
                    return sb.ToString();
                }
                if (c != '\\')
                {
                    sb.Append(c);
                    continue;
                }
                if (i >= s.Length)
                {
                    break;
                }
                char esc = s[i++];
                switch (esc)
                {
                    case '"': sb.Append('"'); break;
                    case '\\': sb.Append('\\'); break;
                    case '/': sb.Append('/'); break;
                    case 'b': sb.Append('\b'); break;
                    case 'f': sb.Append('\f'); break;
                    case 'n': sb.Append('\n'); break;
                    case 'r': sb.Append('\r'); break;
                    case 't': sb.Append('\t'); break;
                    case 'u':
                        if (i + 4 <= s.Length
                            && int.TryParse(s.Substring(i, 4), NumberStyles.HexNumber,
                                            CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out int code))
                        {
                            sb.Append((char)code);
                            i += 4;
                        }
                        break;
                    default: sb.Append(esc); break;
                }
            }
            throw new FormatException("unterminated string");
        }

        private static double ParseNumber(string s, ref int i)
        {
            int start = i;
            while (i < s.Length)
            {
                char c = s[i];
                if ((c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '+' || c == '.'
                    || c == 'e' || c == 'E')
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                break;
            }
            if (i == start)
            {
                throw new FormatException("expected a number at offset " + start);
            }
            return double.Parse(s.Substring(start, i - start), NumberStyles.Float,
                                CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/tools/SolverHarness/Program.cs`:

```cs
// Program.cs -- Spike 3.2's offline harness.
//
// WHAT THIS PROGRAM IS FOR, IN ONE SENTENCE: it runs the shipped solver against recorded or
// synthetic frames and tries to prove it wrong.
//
// The four things it asserts are DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 10's invariants 1, 2, 3 and 4 --
// T5, T6, T10 and T7 in IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md's table -- because those are the four the plan
// says belong here and nowhere else:
//
//   T5    `stand` is never rejected while durably safe        "the dodge moving for no reason"
//   T6    no emitted move is inside a bullet's disc at arrival  "the core safety invariant"
//   T10   hysteresis cannot lock a heading that became unsafe   "anti-jitter turning into a death"
//   T7    predicted and actual collision agree                  "the model being wrong"
//
// T7 IS THE ONE THAT NEEDED A LIVE RUN, AND IT IS WHY TraceRecorder EXISTS. The other three are
// properties of the solver's own geometry and are asserted against synthetic frames; T7 is a
// statement about the world and can only be checked against frames somebody actually played.
//
// WHAT THIS PROGRAM DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. It does not re-implement the solver, it does not
// approximate the temporal test, and it does not "fix up" a frame it does not understand. Every
// number it prints comes from `DodgeSolver.Decide` and from the trace; a harness with its own
// idea of what the answer should be is a second solver, and the project has one.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Globalization;
using System.IO;
using Drelay.Bootstrap;

namespace Drelay.SolverHarness
{
    internal static class Program
    {
        private static int Main(string[] args)
        {
            try
            {
                return Run(args);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // THE ONE INPUT ERROR THAT DESERVES AN INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN A STACK TRACE. A trace
                // whose game is still running is open for writing, and `File.ReadLines` -- which the
                // reader uses for the reasons its own comment gives -- cannot open it. The first time
                // this happened it was a session the operator was still playing, and the message was
                // a raw `IOException` about another process, which reads as a harness defect. See
                // `TraceFile.Load`'s own guard for why the check there is not enough.
                if (ex is System.IO.IOException
                    && ex.Message.IndexOf("being used by another process", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0)
                {
                    Console.Error.WriteLine("FAILED: this trace is STILL BEING WRITTEN -- close the game"
                                            + " first.");
                    Console.Error.WriteLine("        the recorder holds trace.jsonl open for the whole"
                                            + " session, so a run that is in progress cannot be"
                                            + " replayed: half of it is not on disk yet, and the"
                                            + " numbers would describe part of a session.");
                    Console.Error.WriteLine("        " + ex.Message);
                    return 2;
                }
                Console.Error.WriteLine("FAILED: " + ex.GetType().Name + ": " + ex.Message);
                Console.Error.WriteLine(ex.StackTrace);
                return 2;
            }
        }

        private static int Run(string[] args)
        {
            if (args.Length == 0)
            {
                Usage();
                return 2;
            }

            string tracePath = null;
            string collisionLog = null;
            string scenarioName = null;
            string exportPath = null;
            string decisionsPath = null;
            string playerSpeedText = null;
            int seed = 1;
            int frames = 600;
            bool quiet = false;
            string configArgs = null;
            string presetName = null;
            int traceFrame = -1;
            int repeat = 1;
            bool strict = false;
            int debugThreatId = -1;
            System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<int> framesToExplain = null;

            for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
            {
                string a = args[i];
                switch (a)
                {
                    case "--trace": tracePath = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--collisions": collisionLog = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--scenario": scenarioName = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--seed": seed = int.Parse(Next(args, ref i), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); break;
                    case "--frames": frames = int.Parse(Next(args, ref i), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); break;
                    case "--export": exportPath = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--decisions": decisionsPath = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--player-speed": playerSpeedText = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--config": configArgs = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--preset": presetName = Next(args, ref i); break;
                    case "--frame": traceFrame = int.Parse(Next(args, ref i), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); break;
                    case "--frames-from":
                    {
                        // One frame number per line, `#` comments and blanks skipped. See
                        // `FramesToExplain` for why a set of frames needs a switch of its own.
                        string listPath = Next(args, ref i);
                        framesToExplain = new System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<int>();
                        foreach (string raw in System.IO.File.ReadAllLines(listPath))
                        {
                            string trimmed = raw.Trim();
                            if (trimmed.Length == 0 || trimmed[0] == '#')
                            {
                                continue;
                            }
                            int parsed;
                            if (int.TryParse(trimmed, NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                                             out parsed))
                            {
                                framesToExplain.Add(parsed);
                            }
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    case "--repeat": repeat = int.Parse(Next(args, ref i), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); break;
                    case "--strict": strict = true; break;
                    case "--debug-threat": debugThreatId = int.Parse(Next(args, ref i), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); break;
                    case "--quiet": quiet = true; break;
                    case "-h":
                    case "--help":
                        Usage();
                        return 0;
                    default:
                        if (a.StartsWith("--scenario=", StringComparison.Ordinal))
                        {
                            scenarioName = a.Substring("--scenario=".Length);
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            Console.Error.WriteLine("unknown argument '" + a + "'");
                            Usage();
                            return 2;
                        }
                        break;
                }
            }

            // The preset first, then `--config`, for the same reason the hook applies them in that
            // order: a `--config` line is meant to move ONE number from a named starting point.
            DodgeConfig config = DodgeConfig.Preset(presetName);
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(configArgs))
            {
                ApplyConfig(configArgs, ref config);
            }

            DodgeTrace trace;
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(tracePath))
            {
                trace = DodgeTrace.Load(tracePath, collisionLog);
                if (!quiet)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine("trace    : " + tracePath
                                      + " (" + trace.Frames.Count + " frame(s), "
                                      + trace.Grids.Count + " grid window(s))");
                    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(trace.DodgeConfig))
                    {
                        Console.WriteLine("recorded : the hook's dodge settings were " + trace.DodgeConfig);
                    }
                }
            }
            else if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(scenarioName))
            {
                Scenario kind = ParseScenario(scenarioName);
                var synthetic = new SyntheticTrace(kind, seed)
                {
                    Frames = frames,
                    // The scenarios whose point is that the solver must react to a bullet keep the
                    // player still; the ones whose point is that it must NOT react let them walk.
                    PlayerWalking = kind != Scenario.HeadOn && kind != Scenario.Dodge
                                    && kind != Scenario.Volley && kind != Scenario.Corridor,
                };
                trace = synthetic.Build();
                if (!quiet)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine("scenario : " + kind + " (seed " + seed + ", "
                                      + trace.Frames.Count + " frame(s))");
                }
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(exportPath))
                {
                    synthetic.WriteJsonLines(trace, exportPath);
                    if (!quiet)
                    {
                        Console.WriteLine("exported : " + exportPath);
                    }
                }
            }
            else
            {
                Console.Error.WriteLine("either --trace or --scenario is required");
                Usage();
                return 2;
            }

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(playerSpeedText))
            {
                float speed = float.Parse(playerSpeedText, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                foreach (RecordedFrame f in trace.Frames)
                {
                    f.SpeedOverride = speed;
                }
            }

            var harness = new Harness(trace, config);
            harness.FrameToExplain = traceFrame;
            harness.FramesToExplain = framesToExplain;
            harness.ExpectMove = string.Equals(scenarioName, "dodge", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            harness.ExpectFrames = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(tracePath);
            harness.Repeat = repeat;
            harness.Strict = strict;
            harness.DebugThreatId = debugThreatId;
            harness.DecisionsPath = decisionsPath;
            harness.Run(!quiet);
            return harness.Failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
        }

        private static string Next(string[] args, ref int i)
        {
            i++;
            if (i >= args.Length)
            {
                throw new ArgumentException("missing value after " + args[i - 1]);
            }
            return args[i];
        }

        private static Scenario ParseScenario(string name)
        {
            switch (name.ToLowerInvariant())
            {
                case "peaceful": return Scenario.Peaceful;
                case "headon":
                case "head-on": return Scenario.HeadOn;
                case "dodge": return Scenario.Dodge;
                case "volley": return Scenario.Volley;
                case "corridor": return Scenario.Corridor;
                case "passingby":
                case "passing-by": return Scenario.PassingBy;
                default:
                    throw new ArgumentException("unknown scenario '" + name + "'");
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// `name=value,name=value` over the tuning weights, so a weight can be swept from the
        /// command line without editing the source -- which is what "tune in the harness" has to
        /// mean concretely.
        /// </summary>
        /// <summary>
        /// Applies `--config` on top of the preset.
        ///
        /// `ref`, AND THE `ref` IS THE WHOLE OF A DEFECT THAT SURVIVED FROM THE DAY THIS METHOD WAS
        /// WRITTEN. `DodgeConfig` is a struct, so the parameter without `ref` was a COPY: every
        /// assignment below landed in a temporary that was discarded on return, `--config` silently
        /// did nothing, and the harness printed the preset's numbers as though they were the ones it
        /// had just been asked for. It was found by trying to measure whether one new term mattered:
        /// two runs of `--config goal=0,fan=0` produced byte-identical decision histograms, which is
        /// what a switch that does not throw and does not work looks like. It is the same defect as
        /// SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md section 3.2 -- a struct passed by value whose writes are lost --
        /// in the instrument rather than in the solver, and it is the reason that section's lesson
        /// is about calling conventions and not about arithmetic.
        /// </summary>
        private static void ApplyConfig(string text, ref DodgeConfig config)
        {
            foreach (string pair in text.Split(','))
            {
                if (pair.Length == 0)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                string[] kv = pair.Split('=');
                if (kv.Length != 2)
                {
                    throw new ArgumentException("--config wants name=value pairs; got '" + pair + "'");
                }
                float v = float.Parse(kv[1], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                switch (kv[0].ToLowerInvariant())
                {
                    case "clear": config.WeightClearance = v; break;
                    case "resolve": config.WeightResolve = v; break;
                    case "standstops": config.StandStops = v != 0.0f; break;
                    case "durable": config.WeightDurability = v; break;
                    case "intent": config.WeightIntent = v; break;
                    case "goal": config.WeightGoal = v; break;
                    case "plan": config.PlanLookaheadSeconds = v; break;
                    case "front": config.GoalLookaheadSeconds = v; break;
                    case "fan": config.GoalFanSteps = (int)v; break;
                    // THE DECISION WINDOW, IN THE TWO FORMS `DodgeConfig` CARRIES. `disc` is the
                    // multiplier on this projectile's own disc-crossing time and is the knob that
                    // matters; `window` is the absolute floor under it. `disc=0` is legal and means
                    // "no speed scaling", which is how the change is A/B'd against the recording --
                    // `--config disc=0,window=0.05` is exactly the old fixed window.
                    case "disc": config.DecisionDiscMultiplier = v; break;
                    case "window": config.MoveTemporalWindowSeconds = v; break;
                    case "heading": config.WeightHeading = v; break;
                    case "lateral": config.WeightLateral = v; break;
                    case "move": config.WeightMove = v; break;
                    case "stand": config.WeightStandBias = v; break;
                    case "margin": config.HysteresisMargin = v; break;
                    case "dwell": config.HysteresisDwellSeconds = v; break;
                    // THE PATHFINDER, AND `path=0` IS THE A/B THE WHOLE CHANGE RESTS ON. With it off
                    // the score is the pre-path one and the goal term has to be put back by hand
                    // (`--config path=0,goal=0.9`), because `DodgeConfig.Default` cuts `goal` when the
                    // path is on and a comparison against the old behaviour has to restore both
                    // halves of the same change.
                    case "path": config.PathEnable = v != 0.0f; break;
                    case "wpath": config.WeightPath = v; break;
                    case "pathdel": config.PathStepCostWeight = v; break;
                    case "pathcap": config.PathNodeCap = (int)v; break;
                    case "pathpad": config.PathDangerPadUnits = v; break;
                    case "pathtarget": config.PathTargetSeconds = v; break;
                    case "pathdwell": config.PathHysteresisDwellSeconds = v; break;
                    case "pathwp": config.PathWaypointUnits = v; break;
                    // THE PROJECTED-DANGER TERM. `projected=0` is the off-switch and restores the
                    // section 15 behaviour exactly, which is the A/B the next measurement needs.
                    case "projected": config.WeightProjectedDanger = v; break;
                    // THE AXIAL PENALTY -- the term this task is about. `axial=0` is the off-switch.
                    case "axial": config.WeightAxial = v; break;
                    case "projseconds": config.ProjectedSeconds = v; break;
                    case "projsamples": config.ProjectedSamples = (int)v; break;
                    case "wpfraction": config.PathWaypointFraction = v; break;
                    case "horizon": config.HorizonMs = v; break;
                    case "trust": config.TrustSeconds = v; break;
                    case "legalern": config.LethalFraction = v; break;
                    default:
                        throw new ArgumentException("unknown config key '" + kv[0] + "'");
                }
            }
        }

        private static void Usage()
        {
            Console.Error.WriteLine(@"SolverHarness -- Spike 3.2: run the dodge solver over recorded frames.

  --trace PATH        a trace.jsonl written by DRELAY_TRACE=1
  --collisions PATH   the run's bootstrap.log, for the predicted-vs-actual half of T7
  --scenario NAME     synthetic frames instead: peaceful | headon | volley | corridor | passingby
  --seed N            synthetic scenario seed (default 1)
  --frames N          synthetic frame count (default 600)
  --export PATH       write the synthetic trace in the recorder's format, for the reader's sake
  --player-speed V    world units/s, overriding the measured and derived estimates
  --preset NAME       a named, coherent tuning. Three, and they are meant to be compared:
                        balanced  the specification's weights and the specification's `stand`
                        assist    never stops the player; steers toward where they were going
                        evasive   safety first, willing to fight the player for it
                      Applied BEFORE --config, so `--preset evasive --config move=0.4` moves one
                      number from the preset rather than starting again from the default.
  --config K=V,...    override tuning weights and the plan geometry:
                      resolve,clear,durable,intent,goal,heading,lateral,move,stand,margin,dwell,
                      horizon,trust,lethalfraction,standstops,plan,front,fan,disc,window
                      disc   the rule 6 decision window as a multiple of the projectile's own
                             collision-disc crossing time (default 2.0). disc=0 turns the speed
                             scaling off and runs the rule on `window` alone.
                      window an absolute floor in seconds under that window (default 0).
  --quiet             suppress the per-part headings
  --repeat N          run the decision N times per frame and keep the FASTEST, for the cost
                      number. Single-shot `decide()` measures the collector as much as the
                      solver; use --repeat 50 before believing a p99.
  --decisions PATH    write one line per frame: the frame, the decision, the player's held
                      direction, the goal, and where the goal came from. This is the instrument
                      HANDOFF-DIRECTED-DODGE.md section 6.10 asks for -- without it the only view
                      of a per-frame decision is the adapter's 400-line `WOULD MOVE` log, which is
                      capped at 400 lines a session, so every experiment is a mean over a sample
                      rather than a diff of two files. See tools/decisions_report.py.
  --strict            treat the trace reader's warnings (a half-written last line, an unknown
                      record type) as a failure instead of a report line.
  --debug-threat ID   dump every recorded observation of the bullet with this GameId, with the
                      distance from its samples to the player on each frame. For T7 disagreements.

Exit codes: 0 = every invariant held, 1 = an invariant failed, 2 = usage or input problem.");
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The replay. One solver instance across the whole trace, because the hysteresis and the
    /// previous heading are state the solver is *supposed* to carry between frames -- running a
    /// fresh solver per frame would test T5/T6 and quietly not test T10.
    /// </summary>
    internal sealed class Harness
    {
        private readonly DodgeTrace _trace;
        private readonly DodgeConfig _config;
        private readonly DodgeSolver _solver;

        public int Failures;

        /// <summary>
        /// When set, the report asserts that the solver moved, and fails if it did not.
        ///
        /// WHY THIS IS A FLAG AND NOT A PROPERTY OF EVERY RUN. Three of the four invariants are
        /// satisfied by a solver that never moves, so a suite made only of them cannot tell a
        /// working dodge from a disabled one -- and "it passed" would then mean "it did nothing".
        /// The flag is set for the one scenario whose geometry guarantees that not moving is the
        /// wrong answer, and the failing message says so.
        /// </summary>
        public bool ExpectMove;

        /// <summary>
        /// When set, the report fails if the trace contained no frames at all.
        ///
        /// THIS IS THE ASSERTION THAT WOULD HAVE SAVED A RUN, AND ITS ABSENCE IS WHY A BROKEN
        /// RECORDING LOOKED LIKE A CLEAN ONE. Every invariant is a statement of the form "for every
        /// frame, ...", and a report over zero frames satisfies all of them vacuously -- so the
        /// harness printed "every asserted invariant held" over a trace whose only content was its
        /// header. The run of `20261014-164314-p12060` did exactly that: the recorder was armed but
        /// the game's frame path took the native detour instead of the managed replacement, so the
        /// recorder was never called.
        ///
        /// **A test suite that passes on no data is worse than one that fails**, because it is
        /// believed. This flag makes an empty recording a failure with a named cause.
        /// </summary>
        public bool ExpectFrames;

        /// <summary>
        /// When set, one frame's whole candidate evaluation is printed.
        ///
        /// THIS EXISTS BECAUSE A SOLVER THAT REFUSES EVERYTHING LOOKS LIKE A SOLVER THAT FOUND NO
        /// THREAT. The aggregate report says "0 admissible" and nothing about which of the seven
        /// rules did the refusing, and the difference between "the geometry is wrong" and "the
        /// geometry is right and the world is genuinely closed" is not visible from a count. One
        /// frame printed in full is worth an hour of reading the code.
        /// </summary>
        public int FrameToExplain = -1;

        /// <summary>
        /// A SET of frames to explain, from `--frames-from`, for the term breakdown.
        ///
        /// `--frame N` EXPLAINS ONE FRAME AND A MEASUREMENT NEEDS THOUSANDS. `tools/dodge_term_report.py`
        /// aggregates the chosen move's score terms by the direction it chose, and the dodge moves on
        /// 1 100 to 5 000 frames of each recording -- so the alternative to this is one process per
        /// frame, each one re-parsing a 7 MB trace, which is a measurement nobody runs twice.
        /// </summary>
        public System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<int> FramesToExplain;

        /// <summary>
        /// Where to write one line per frame -- the whole decision, joined to the player's input.
        ///
        /// THIS IS THE INSTRUMENT, AND ITS ABSENCE WAS THE REASON EVERY EXPERIMENT IN THIS TASK
        /// WAS A MEAN RATHER THAN A DIFF. The per-frame decision (heading, scale, reason, goal, and
        /// where the goal came from) exists on a live run only in `DodgeAdapter`'s `dodge WOULD
        /// MOVE` log, which is **capped at 400 lines a session**; the replay that reads the whole
        /// recording reports only histograms. So "did the goal move to the player's direction, and
        /// did the deflection decay" could be answered as "the mean fell from 47.4 deg to X" and
        /// not as "here are the 1665 frames, before and after, side by side" -- and a mean over a
        /// 400-line sample of 1665 moves is the weakest form of the evidence this project accepts.
        ///
        /// The fields are chosen so that the two questions the handoff asks are answerable from the
        /// file alone: `held`/`hintent` are the player's own request (so the deflection is
        /// `signed(heading - hintent)` and needs nothing else), and `goalsrc` says where the goal
        /// came from on that frame -- which is the one fact that makes "the goal is the course" and
        /// "the goal is the player" distinguishable after the change.
        /// </summary>
        public string DecisionsPath;

        /// <summary>
        /// How many times `Decide` is run per frame for the cost measurement. 1 is the honest
        /// single-shot number, and it is not the number to tune against.
        ///
        /// WHY REPEATING A PURE FUNCTION IS THE ONLY WAY TO MEASURE IT HERE. The harness builds a
        /// fresh `DodgeSnapshot` for every frame -- correctly, because the game hands the solver
        /// one plain-data view per frame and the solver must not depend on object identity -- and
        /// that is hundreds of small allocations a frame. A single `Stopwatch` around one `Decide`
        /// therefore measures the solver *plus whichever garbage collection happens to land in
        /// that window*, and the measurement shows it: the reported p99 moved from 890 us to 746 to
        /// 737 as work was REMOVED from the solver, and forcing server GC moved it to 516 on its
        /// own. A number that responds to the collector and not to the algorithm is not a
        /// measurement of the algorithm.
        ///
        /// With `--repeat N` the decision is run N times on the same snapshot and the MINIMUM is
        /// kept: the solver is a pure function of the snapshot except for its own hysteresis, which
        /// is bounded state, so the fastest of N runs is the one with the least interference and
        /// the best available estimate of the true cost. Nothing downstream changes -- the
        /// decision reported, the invariants and the T7 tracking all still use the first run.
        /// </summary>
        public int Repeat = 1;

        /// <summary>
        /// Makes the reader's warnings fatal. Off by default, and the default is a judgement: a
        /// half-written last line is what closing the game by hand produces, not a defect in the
        /// recording, and refusing to analyse 2173 good frames over 40 lost bytes would be the
        /// wrong trade. On for a CI-shaped run, where "the file is not quite what was promised"
        /// should stop the line rather than print a paragraph nobody reads.
        /// </summary>
        public bool Strict;

        /// <summary>
        /// A bullet key (`GameId`) to dump in full: for every frame the trace records it, the
        /// sampler's own radius, the samples' distances to the player's recorded position on that
        /// frame, and whether any sample was ever inside. Added to settle why
        /// `TrackPredictions` records no prediction for a bullet the game resolved as a hit.
        /// </summary>
        public int DebugThreatId = -1;

        private readonly List<string> _debugThreatLines = new List<string>();
        private float _debugThreatBest = float.MaxValue;
        private int _debugThreatBestFrame = -1;
        private bool _debugThreatEverInside;
        private float _debugThreatRadius = float.NaN;

        // --- Accumulators ---------------------------------------------------------------

        private readonly Dictionary<DodgeAction, int> _actions = new Dictionary<DodgeAction, int>();
        private readonly Dictionary<DodgeReason, int> _reasons = new Dictionary<DodgeReason, int>();
        private long _frames;
        private long _evaluatedTotal;
        private long _admissibleTotal;
        private long _framesWithCandidates;
        private long _hysteresisHolds;
        /// <summary>
        /// The dodge's OWN heading history -- the stutter measure. Contrast `_overridesIntent`.
        /// </summary>
        private long _adjacentMoves;
        private long _adjacentHeadingChanges;
        private double _turnDegrees;
        private float _lastChosenHeading = float.NaN;
        private int _lastChosenFrame = int.MinValue;

        /// <summary>Moving frames whose heading disagreed with the player's input by more than 90 deg.</summary>
        private long _overridesIntent;

        /// <summary>Moving frames whose heading pointed within 90 deg of the forward goal.</summary>
        private long _goalAligned;
        private long _goalConsidered;

        /// <summary>
        /// Every candidate refusal the run made, over every evaluated frame. The denominator for
        /// `_solver.WindowRefusals`, which counts only the ones rule 6's unconditional clause caused.
        /// </summary>
        private long _refusalsTotal;

        /// <summary>
        /// Moving frames whose heading pointed within 90 deg of the direction the player's hands
        /// were holding.
        ///
        /// THE MEASUREMENT THE OPERATOR'S SENTENCE ASKS FOR. `keeps its course` was the right
```
