`hook/tools/SolverHarness/Synthetic.cs`:

```cs
// Synthetic.cs -- traces that can be asserted against when no live run exists.
//
// WHY THIS IS NOT "JUST A UNIT TEST FIXTURE".
//
// The invariants in DODGE-ALGORITHM.md section 10 are statements about *decisions over time*:
// "stand is never rejected while durably safe", "an admissible candidate is never inside a
// bullet's disc at arrival", "the chosen heading never changes while it stays admissible".
// None of them can be checked on a single call. They need a sequence of frames whose geometry
// the author knows exactly, so that a failure says which term is wrong rather than that
// something moved.
//
// A synthetic trace is also the only way to give the harness teeth TODAY. The live trace that
// the recorder writes is the ground truth for the trajectory model (invariant T7), and that one
// genuinely needs a played session. The other three do not: they are properties of the solver's
// own geometry, and a bullet that flies straight at a stationary player is a strictly harder
// case than anything the model has to get right in a live run.
//
// THE SCENARIOS BELOW ARE CHOSEN TO BE FALSIFIABLE, NOT TO BE REALISTIC. Each one has a known
// correct answer, so a solver that regresses on it fails loudly:
//
//   peaceful       nothing on a collision course. The solver must do nothing, every frame.
//   headon         one bullet straight at a stationary player. The solver must move, and the
//                  move must be perpendicular rather than along the bullet's line.
//   volley         four bullets from four directions with a gap in one of them. Anything that
//                  only reacts to the nearest bullet fails here.
//   corridor       a walled lane with one bullet coming down it. The dodge may not solve this
//                  by walking through a wall, and with no wall-aware admission it would.
//   passing-by     bullets that cross the player's line but never come within a disc. The
//                  solver must not flinch -- false positives are the failure the operator sees.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.IO;
using System.Text;
using Drelay.Bootstrap;

namespace Drelay.SolverHarness
{
    /// <summary>The scenarios this generator knows, and what each one is for.</summary>
    public enum Scenario
    {
        Peaceful,
        HeadOn,
        Volley,
        Corridor,
        PassingBy,

        /// <summary>
        /// The one scenario whose assertion is that the solver MOVES: a bullet on a line that comes
        /// close enough to matter and far enough that a single frame's step clears it.
        ///
        /// THE WINDOW IS NARROW AND THAT IS THE POINT OF HAVING IT. A player at 8.2 units/s covers
        /// 0.137 units in a frame, so a bullet whose closest approach is `m` is escapable this frame
        /// only when `m + 0.137` exceeds the 0.45 collision radius -- `m` above about 0.31. Below
        /// that no candidate can be admitted and the solver reports `NoAdmissible`, which is the
        /// honest answer and not a dodge. `Dodge` sits at 0.34, inside the window by a hair, so it
        /// fails loudly if any of the admission or durability rules becomes one notch too strict.
        /// </summary>
        Dodge,
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Builds a synthetic trace. Deterministic for a given seed, so a failure can be re-run and a
    /// weight can be re-tuned against exactly the same frames.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class SyntheticTrace
    {
        public Scenario Kind;
        public int Seed = 1;
        public int Frames = 600;
        public float Dt = 1.0f / 60.0f;
        public float PlayerSpeed = 8.2f;       // world units/s, the resolved law at a middling SPD
        public float PlayerRadius = 0.25f;
        public float BulletRadius = 0.2f;
        public float BulletSpeed = 24.0f;      // world units/s: fast enough that a dodge matters
        public float StartX = 100.0f;
        public float StartY = 100.0f;
        public int GridSize = 64;
        public int GridOrigin = 68;            // 100 - 32, so the player starts mid-window

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether the player is supposed to be walking under their own input.
        ///
        /// THE SCENARIOS THAT EXIST TO MAKE THE SOLVER MOVE HAVE THE PLAYER STILL, AND THAT IS NOT
        /// A CONVENIENCE. A recorded trajectory is anchored on the bullet's live position at the
        /// moment it was sampled, so it describes where the bullet will be if the world -- the
        /// *player* included -- does not change. A synthetic trace whose player walks while the
        /// scripted bullets fly at the position it started from is not a trace of anything; the
        /// bullets and the player are moving in different coordinate systems, and the naive reading
        /// ("no threat") is correct.
        ///
        /// The walking scenarios are the ones whose point is that the solver should NOT move, and
        /// for those the walk is harmless because the bullets never come close anyway.
        /// </summary>
        public bool PlayerWalking = true;

        /// <summary>Walls, as a predicate over grid cells in the window's own indices.</summary>
        private readonly List<int[]> _walls = new List<int[]>();

        private readonly Random _random;

        public SyntheticTrace(Scenario kind, int seed)
        {
            Kind = kind;
            Seed = seed;
            _random = new Random(seed);
        }

        /// <summary>Fills a trace object with the scenario's frames.</summary>
        public DodgeTrace Build()
        {
            var trace = new DodgeTrace();
            trace.Source = "synthetic:" + Kind + ":" + Seed;
            trace.Synthetic = true;
            trace.DodgeConfig = "synthetic";
            trace.GridSource = "synthetic";

            var grid = new GridWindow();
            grid.Generation = 1;
            grid.OriginX = GridOrigin;
            grid.OriginY = GridOrigin;
            grid.Width = GridSize;
            grid.Height = GridSize;
            grid.Cells = new byte[GridSize * GridSize];
            trace.Grids.Add(grid);

            PlanWalls();
            foreach (int[] wall in _walls)
            {
                int cx = wall[0] - grid.OriginX;
                int cy = wall[1] - grid.OriginY;
                if (cx >= 0 && cy >= 0 && cx < grid.Width && cy < grid.Height)
                {
                    grid.Cells[(cy * grid.Width) + cx] = 1;
                }
            }

            // The bullets, as spawn descriptions. Each is a straight line at a constant speed,
            // sampled on the same 30 ms grid the hook samples on, so the solver sees exactly the
            // shape it sees live.
            List<Spawn> spawns = PlanSpawns();

            float x = StartX;
            float y = StartY;
            float heading = 0.0f;
            float clock = 0.0f;
            for (int f = 0; f < Frames; f++)
            {
                var frame = new RecordedFrame();
                frame.Frame = f;
                frame.Dt = Dt;
                frame.ClockMs = clock;
                frame.PlayerX = x;
                frame.PlayerY = y;
                frame.PlayerRadius = PlayerRadius;
                frame.Health = 100.0f;
                frame.Moving = true;
                frame.Intent = heading;
                frame.Rotation = 0.0f;
                frame.Grid = grid;

                foreach (Spawn spawn in spawns)
                {
                    float spawnTime = spawn.StartFrame * Dt;
                    float now = f * Dt;
                    if (now < spawnTime)
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    float ageMs = (now - spawnTime) * 1000.0f;
                    if (ageMs > spawn.LifetimeMs)
                    {
                        continue;
                    }

                    var threat = new RecordedThreat();
                    threat.GameId = spawn.GameId;
                    threat.StartTime = (int)(spawnTime * 1000.0f);
                    threat.Radius = BulletRadius;
                    threat.Damage = spawn.Damage;
                    threat.Projectable = true;
                    threat.Count = Trajectory.MaxSamples;
                    threat.Xs = new float[threat.Count];
                    threat.Ys = new float[threat.Count];
                    threat.Alive = new bool[threat.Count];

                    for (int s = 0; s < threat.Count; s++)
                    {
                        float ahead = ageMs + (s * 30.0f);
                        threat.Xs[s] = spawn.X + (spawn.Vx * ahead / 1000.0f);
                        threat.Ys[s] = spawn.Y + (spawn.Vy * ahead / 1000.0f);
                        threat.Alive[s] = ahead <= spawn.LifetimeMs;
                    }
                    threat.X = threat.Xs[0];
                    threat.Y = threat.Ys[0];
                    frame.Threats.Add(threat);
                }

                // The player walks along the intent heading, which for every scenario here is a
                // steady circle except `corridor`, where it is a straight line. See `PlayerWalking`
                // for why the scenarios that need the solver to react keep the player still.
                if (!PlayerWalking)
                {
                    heading = 0.0f;
                }
                else if (Kind == Scenario.Corridor)
                {
                    heading = (float)(Math.PI / 2.0);   // due +y, straight down the lane
                }
                else
                {
                    heading += 0.004f;
                }
                if (PlayerWalking)
                {
                    x += (float)Math.Cos(heading) * PlayerSpeed * Dt;
                    y += (float)Math.Sin(heading) * PlayerSpeed * Dt;
                }

                trace.Frames.Add(frame);
                clock += Dt * 1000.0f;
            }

            return trace;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Writes the trace out in the recorder's own format, so that the reader, the writer and
        /// the solver are all exercised on the same bytes. A synthetic trace that is never
        /// serialised would leave the reader untested until the operator's first live run.
        /// </summary>
        public void WriteJsonLines(DodgeTrace trace, string path)
        {
            using (var writer = new StreamWriter(new FileStream(path, FileMode.Create, FileAccess.Write),
                                                 new UTF8Encoding(false)))
            {
                var line = new StringBuilder(8192);
                line.Append("{\"t\":\"H\",\"v\":1,\"dodge\":\"synthetic\",\"player\":\"Player\",")
                    .Append("\"projectile\":\"Projectile\",\"samples\":21,\"gridSource\":\"synthetic\",")
                    .Append("\"synthetic\":true}");
                writer.WriteLine(line.ToString());

                foreach (GridWindow g in trace.Grids)
                {
                    line.Length = 0;
                    line.Append("{\"t\":\"G\",\"g\":").Append(g.Generation)
                        .Append(",\"ox\":").Append(g.OriginX)
                        .Append(",\"oy\":").Append(g.OriginY)
                        .Append(",\"w\":").Append(g.Width)
                        .Append(",\"h\":").Append(g.Height)
                        .Append(",\"rle\":[");
                    int i = 0;
                    bool first = true;
                    while (i < g.Cells.Length)
                    {
                        byte value = g.Cells[i];
                        int run = 1;
                        while (i + run < g.Cells.Length && g.Cells[i + run] == value)
                        {
                            run++;
                        }
                        if (!first)
                        {
                            line.Append(',');
                        }
                        first = false;
                        line.Append(value).Append(',').Append(run);
                        i += run;
                    }
                    line.Append("]}");
                    writer.WriteLine(line.ToString());
                }

                foreach (RecordedFrame f in trace.Frames)
                {
                    line.Length = 0;
                    line.Append("{\"t\":\"F\",\"f\":").Append(f.Frame)
                        .Append(",\"dt\":").Append(Num(f.Dt))
                        .Append(",\"clock\":").Append(Num(f.ClockMs))
                        .Append(",\"px\":").Append(Num(f.PlayerX))
                        .Append(",\"py\":").Append(Num(f.PlayerY))
                        .Append(",\"r\":").Append(Num(f.PlayerRadius))
                        .Append(",\"hp\":").Append(Num(f.Health))
                        .Append(",\"moving\":").Append(f.Moving ? "true" : "false")
                        .Append(",\"intent\":").Append(Num(f.Intent))
                        .Append(",\"dead\":false,\"safe\":false,\"rot\":0")
                        .Append(",\"grid\":").Append(f.Grid != null ? f.Grid.Generation : 0)
                        .Append(",\"threats\":[");
                    for (int t = 0; t < f.Threats.Count; t++)
                    {
                        if (t > 0)
                        {
                            line.Append(',');
                        }
                        RecordedThreat th = f.Threats[t];
                        line.Append("{\"id\":").Append(th.GameId)
                            .Append(",\"st\":").Append(th.StartTime)
                            .Append(",\"x\":").Append(Num(th.X))
                            .Append(",\"y\":").Append(Num(th.Y))
                            .Append(",\"rad\":").Append(Num(th.Radius))
                            .Append(",\"lin\":1")
                            .Append(",\"dmg\":").Append(Num(th.Damage))
                            .Append(",\"dmgp\":0,\"mdmg\":0")
                            .Append(",\"n\":").Append(th.Count)
                            .Append(",\"xs\":[");
                        for (int s = 0; s < th.Count; s++)
                        {
                            if (s > 0) { line.Append(','); }
                            line.Append(Num(th.Xs[s]));
                        }
                        line.Append("],\"ys\":[");
                        for (int s = 0; s < th.Count; s++)
                        {
                            if (s > 0) { line.Append(','); }
                            line.Append(Num(th.Ys[s]));
                        }
                        line.Append("],\"alive\":[");
                        for (int s = 0; s < th.Count; s++)
                        {
                            if (s > 0) { line.Append(','); }
                            line.Append(th.Alive[s] ? '1' : '0');
                        }
                        line.Append("]}");
                    }
                    line.Append("],\"skipped\":0}");
                    writer.WriteLine(line.ToString());
                }
            }
        }

        // --- Scenarios -------------------------------------------------------------------

        private struct Spawn
        {
            public int GameId;
            public int StartFrame;
            public float X;
            public float Y;
            public float Vx;
            public float Vy;
            public float LifetimeMs;
            public float Damage;
        }

        private void PlanWalls()
        {
            if (Kind != Scenario.Corridor)
            {
                return;
            }
            // Two solid rows either side of the start position, leaving a two-tile lane running
            // along +y. A dodge that ignores walkability will happily step into the wall.
            int laneX = (int)StartX;
            for (int dy = -8; dy <= 24; dy++)
            {
                for (int dx = -3; dx <= 3; dx++)
                {
                    if (dx == 0 || dx == 1)
                    {
                        continue;   // the lane itself
                    }
                    _walls.Add(new[] { laneX + dx, (int)StartY + dy });
                }
            }
        }

        private List<Spawn> PlanSpawns()
        {
            var spawns = new List<Spawn>();
            switch (Kind)
            {
                case Scenario.Peaceful:
                    // Two bullets crossing far away, so the trace is not simply empty.
                    spawns.Add(Far(1, 60, -12.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
                    spawns.Add(Far(2, 120, 0.0f, 12.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
                    break;

                case Scenario.HeadOn:
                    // A bullet that crosses the player's line 0.5 units to one side and reaches
                    // that point inside the horizon, so there is something to dodge and somewhere
                    // to dodge to.
                    //
                    // THE GEOMETRY OF "A BULLET THAT MATTERS" IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS, AND THE
                    // FIRST TWO VERSIONS OF THIS SCENARIO GOT IT WRONG. The decision only sees
                    // bullets whose predicted path enters the hit disc *inside the horizon* --
                    // 0.45 s of a 24 unit/s bullet is 10.8 units -- so a bullet aimed at where the
                    // player is standing, arriving in two seconds, is not a threat the model is
                    // looking for and the correct answer is to do nothing. A scenario that is
                    // meant to produce motion has to put its bullet in the window:
                    //
                    //     fired from (89, 100.5) at 24 units/s along +x
                    //     crosses x = 100 at t = 0.458, and by the horizon it is at x = 99.8:
                    //     closest approach 0.5 in y, against a 0.45 hit radius.
                    //
                    // 0.5 against 0.45 is deliberate: it is close enough to threat, and far
                    // enough that a 0.137-unit sidestep clears it. `stand` is refused (0.5 > 0.45,
                    // so standing is *not* safe forever, but it is safe inside the horizon -- the
                    // distinction the durability test is about).
                    spawns.Add(Offset(1, 30, StartX - 11.0f, StartY + 0.30f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    spawns.Add(Offset(2, 210, StartX - 11.0f, StartY + 0.30f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    break;

                case Scenario.Dodge:
                    spawns.Add(Offset(1, 30, StartX - 11.0f, StartY + 0.43f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    spawns.Add(Offset(2, 210, StartX - 11.0f, StartY + 0.43f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    break;

                case Scenario.Volley:
                    // Four bullets closing on the start position from four diagonals, each passing
                    // 0.5 units off it and each starting 10 units out -- outside the disc, so the
                    // player has an immediate choice to make. It is a dense test of the candidate
                    // set: the gap is real but narrow, and a solver that only reacts to the
                    // nearest bullet fails here.
                    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++)
                    {
                        double angle = Math.PI / 4.0 + (k * Math.PI / 2.0);
                        float ox = (float)(-Math.Sin(angle) * 0.45);
                        float oy = (float)(Math.Cos(angle) * 0.45);
                        spawns.Add(Aimed(10 + k, 40, 10.0f, (float)angle,
                                         StartX + ox, StartY + oy));
                    }
                    break;

                case Scenario.Corridor:
                    // Down the lane, from ahead, passing 0.5 units to one side. The lane's walls are
                    // what make this a terrain test: a dodge that steps sideways into the wall is
                    // a dodge that has stopped.
                    spawns.Add(Aimed(1, 40, 10.0f, (float)(Math.PI / 2.0),
                                     StartX + 0.45f, StartY + 10.0f));
                    spawns.Add(Aimed(2, 240, 10.0f, (float)(Math.PI / 2.0),
                                     StartX + 0.45f, StartY + 10.0f));
                    break;

                case Scenario.PassingBy:
                    // Through the neighbourhood, never within a disc: perpendicular passes that
                    // miss by 1.5 units, well outside the 0.45 unit hit radius.
                    spawns.Add(Offset(1, 30, StartX - 14.0f, StartY + 1.5f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    spawns.Add(Offset(2, 150, StartX + 14.0f, StartY - 1.5f, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0f, 0f));
                    break;
            }
            return spawns;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// A bullet fired from `from` along `(dirX, dirY)`.
        ///
        /// THE DIRECTION IS ALWAYS PASSED EXPLICITLY. An earlier version inferred it from a
        /// "through" point and the inference silently produced a stationary direction for the
        /// scenarios that passed a zero vector -- a bullet that never arrives looks exactly like a
        /// bullet that was successfully dodged, which is the worst possible way for a fixture to be
        /// wrong.
        /// </summary>
        private Spawn Offset(int id, int startFrame, float fromX, float fromY,
                             float dirX, float dirY, float unusedX, float unusedY)
        {
            float vx = dirX;
            float vy = dirY;
            float len = (float)Math.Sqrt((vx * vx) + (vy * vy));
            if (len < 1e-6f)
            {
                throw new ArgumentException("a synthetic bullet needs a direction");
            }
            return new Spawn
            {
                GameId = id,
                StartFrame = startFrame,
                X = fromX,
                Y = fromY,
                Vx = (vx / len) * BulletSpeed,
                Vy = (vy / len) * BulletSpeed,
                LifetimeMs = 2000.0f,
                Damage = 30.0f,
            };
        }

        /// <summary>A bullet at `from` whose line passes through the player's start position.</summary>
        private Spawn Aimed(int id, int startFrame, float distance, float angle,
                            float passX, float passY)
        {
            float fromX = passX - ((float)Math.Cos(angle) * distance);
            float fromY = passY - ((float)Math.Sin(angle) * distance);
            return new Spawn
            {
                GameId = id,
                StartFrame = startFrame,
                X = fromX,
                Y = fromY,
                Vx = (float)Math.Cos(angle) * BulletSpeed,
                Vy = (float)Math.Sin(angle) * BulletSpeed,
                LifetimeMs = 1400.0f,
                Damage = 30.0f,
            };
        }

        private Spawn Far(int id, int startFrame, float vx, float vy, float ox, float oy)
        {
            return new Spawn
            {
                GameId = id,
                StartFrame = startFrame,
                X = StartX - 14.0f + ox,
                Y = StartY - 14.0f + oy,
                Vx = vx,
                Vy = vy,
                LifetimeMs = 1400.0f,
                Damage = 10.0f,
            };
        }

        private static string Num(float value)
        {
            return value.ToString("0.####", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        }
    }
}

```

`hook/tools/SolverHarness/TraceFile.cs`:

```cs
// TraceFile.cs -- read a recorded trace, and the ground truth that goes beside it.
//
// THE TWO HALVES OF INVARIANT T7 COME FROM TWO FILES, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
//
//   `trace.jsonl`      what the model said: one line per frame, with the player, the collision
//                      grid and every culled threat's sampled path.
//   `bootstrap.log`    what actually happened: `CollisionObservation` writes one `collision:`
//                      line per `HitCharacter` that returned **true**, with the bullet's key.
//
// Neither file is written by this program, and neither is derived from the other. A predicted-
// versus-actual comparison is only worth something if the prediction was recorded before the
// collision was observed, and the fact that they are separate artefacts written by separate code
// paths is what makes that true rather than merely asserted.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Globalization;
using System.IO;
using Drelay.Bootstrap;

namespace Drelay.SolverHarness
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The packed `(GameId, startTime)` identity, in the same form the hook's `ThreatKey` packs it.
    ///
    /// DUPLICATED RATHER THAN IMPORTED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE COST. `ThreatKey` lives in
    /// `ThreatSet.cs`, which the harness does not compile: that file is the sensor's bookkeeping and
    /// carries the retirement policy, which has nothing to do with reading a trace. Two lines of
    /// packing are a cheaper price than dragging the sensor into the offline build -- and the
    /// identity itself is not a detail to be re-invented, which is why the hook's version is the
    /// one quoted here and the harness never keys on an address.
    /// </summary>
    internal static class Keys
    {
        public static long Packed(int gameId, int startTime)
        {
            return ((long)gameId << 32) ^ (uint)startTime;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>One bullet's recorded path for one frame.</summary>
    public sealed class RecordedThreat
    {
        public int GameId;
        public int StartTime;
        public float X;
        public float Y;
        public float Radius;
        public float Damage;
        public float DamagePercent;
        public int ManaDamage;
        public bool Projectable;
        public int Count;
        public float[] Xs;
        public float[] Ys;
        public bool[] Alive;

        /// <summary>The identity, in the packed form the harness keys its dictionaries by.</summary>
        public long Key => Keys.Packed(GameId, StartTime);
    }

    /// <summary>One recorded frame.</summary>
    public sealed class RecordedFrame
    {
        public int Frame;
        public float Dt;
        public float ClockMs;
        public float PlayerX;
        public float PlayerY;
        public float PlayerRadius;
        public float Health;
        public bool Moving;
        public float Intent;
        public bool Dead;
        public bool SafeWorld;
        public float Rotation;

        /// <summary>The grid window this frame references, or null.</summary>
        public GridWindow Grid;

        /// <summary>
        /// World units per second, when the caller overrode the measurement.
        ///
        /// THE SPEED IS NOT IN THE TRACE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The trace records the player's
        /// position every frame, and the speed is the difference between two of those divided by
        /// the frame delta -- a measurement, not a field to be trusted. The override exists for the
        /// one case the measurement cannot cover: a frame where the player did not move, where the
        /// harness wants to assert admission against a *larger* budget than the player used.
        /// </summary>
        public float SpeedOverride;

        public readonly List<RecordedThreat> Threats = new List<RecordedThreat>();
        public int Skipped;

        /// <summary>
        /// Projectiles the sampler declined this frame because the client says they can never hit a
        /// player -- the local player's own shots and allies', by `Projectile.HitsPlayer` and
        /// `Projectile.LocalSeedDerived`. Absent from a recording made before those fields were
        /// resolved, which is why it defaults to zero and why the harness reports it rather than
        /// asserting on it.
        /// </summary>
        public int NoHit;

        /// <summary>
        /// True when the frame line carried `nohit` at all. A recording made before
        /// `TrajectorySampler` grew the exclusion has no such key, and "the field is absent" and
        /// "the filter declined nothing" are different findings -- the first is a trace that cannot
        /// speak to the question, the second is a run with no own shots (or a filter that is not in
        /// force, which `bootstrap.log`'s resolution line settles).
        /// </summary>
        public bool NoHitRecorded;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The client's collision grid, as it was recorded: a window of `byte[x, y]` cells plus the
    /// world-coordinate index of its first cell.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class GridWindow
    {
        public long Generation;
        public int OriginX;
        public int OriginY;
        public int Width;
        public int Height;

        /// <summary>Row-major over `[x, y]`, exactly as the recorder wrote it.</summary>
        public byte[] Cells;

        /// <summary>
        /// The solver's own window type, rebuilt from the record.
        ///
        /// THE TRUNCATION IS THE GAME'S. `World` turns a float position into a grid index with a C
        /// cast (`conv.i4`), and so does `CollisionWindow`. If this conversion were wrong the
        /// offline walkability answer would differ from the live one and every terrain test in the
        /// harness would be measuring the harness.
        /// </summary>
        public CollisionWindow ToSolverWindow()
        {
            CollisionWindow window = default(CollisionWindow);
            window.Present = Width > 0 && Height > 0 && Cells != null;
            window.OriginX = OriginX;
            window.OriginY = OriginY;
            window.Width = Width;
            window.Height = Height;
            window.Cells = Cells;
            return window;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>One resolved collision, from the bootstrap log.</summary>
    public sealed class ObservedHit
    {
        public int GameId;
        public int StartTime;
        public bool Tracked;
        public bool Predicted;

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether the log line carried a `predicted=` field at all.
        ///
        /// WITHOUT THIS, A LOG THAT PREDATES THE FIELD LOOKS LIKE A LOG WHOSE OBSERVER PREDICTED
        /// NOTHING. `Predicted` defaults to false, so the parity check below would compare fifteen
        /// real agreements against a field that was never written and report every collision as a
        /// disagreement. The absence of a measurement is not a measurement -- the same distinction
        /// the empty-trace check makes at the top of the invariant list.
        /// </summary>
        public bool HasPredictedFlag;

        public float WarningMs;
        public float BulletX;
        public float BulletY;
        public float Radius;
        public int LineNumber;

        /// <summary>The identity, packed. `(GameId, startTime)` and never the object's address:
        /// `Projectile` is pooled, and state keyed on an address inherits a dead bullet's history
        /// (HOOK-ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4).</summary>
        public long Key => Keys.Packed(GameId, StartTime);
        public override string ToString() => "(" + GameId + "," + StartTime + ")";
    }

    /// <summary>A whole trace: the header, the grid windows and the frames.</summary>
    public sealed class DodgeTrace
    {
        public string Source;
        public int Version;
        public string DodgeConfig = "";
        public string GridSource = "";
        public int SampleCount = 21;

        /// <summary>
        /// True when these frames did not come off a live client.
        ///
        /// IT CHANGES EXACTLY ONE ASSERTION, AND THE REASON IS A PROPERTY OF THE GENERATOR RATHER
        /// THAN A LICENCE. A synthetic bullet's sampled path is laid on the 30 ms grid from a
        /// position that no frame boundary necessarily visits; a live bullet's path is derived from
        /// the same object the game's own per-frame collision test reads. So a synthetic trace can
        /// contain a bullet whose *sampled* path grazes the player while its *frame-boundary* path
        /// never does, and the strict false-positive test -- "the model claimed a hit the game never
        /// resolved" -- then reports the generator's quantisation as a model error.
        ///
        /// For synthetic frames T7 therefore asserts only the gross property: no prediction for a
        /// bullet that never came near. For recorded frames it asserts the real one, which is the
        /// test the plan says needs a live run.
        /// </summary>
        public bool Synthetic;

        public readonly List<RecordedFrame> Frames = new List<RecordedFrame>();
        public readonly List<GridWindow> Grids = new List<GridWindow>();
        public readonly List<ObservedHit> Hits = new List<ObservedHit>();

        public readonly List<string> Warnings = new List<string>();

        public RecordedFrame FrameAt(int index) => Frames[index];

        /// <summary>
        /// Reads a trace file, and the collision log beside it when one is given.
        ///
        /// THE COLLISION LOG IS OPTIONAL AND ITS ABSENCE IS RECORDED. A trace with no hits is a
        /// perfectly good file -- it is the control case -- but a trace whose run had hits and
        /// whose log was not passed in would silently look like one that had none, and that is
        /// the failure mode that turns "the model predicted nothing" into a passing test.
        /// </summary>
        public static DodgeTrace Load(string tracePath, string collisionLogPath)
        {
            var trace = new DodgeTrace();
            trace.Source = tracePath;

            // A TRACE THAT IS STILL BEING WRITTEN IS A NAMED FAILURE, AND THE GUARD IS REFUSING RATHER
            // THAN PROBING. The recorder holds the file open for the whole session, and the two ways
            // a replay of a live run can go are BOTH wrong: opened read-only it fails with "being
            // used by another process", and opened shared it reads HALF A SESSION and reports the
            // line it is halfway through as `a second malformed line: the recording is corrupt, not
            // truncated` -- which is a worse lie than the first, because it accuses a healthy
            // recording.
            //
            // So the file is opened with the sharing the recorder GRANTS (`FileShare.Read`, its own
            // creation mode) and nothing else: if another process holds it for writing, this fails
            // and says why. `20261015-214418-p6412` is that case -- an acting session with `-Trace`,
            // measured while the operator was still playing it.
            try
            {
                using (var probe = new FileStream(tracePath, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read,
                                                  FileShare.Read))
                {
                    probe.ReadByte();
                }
            }
            catch (IOException ex)
            {
                throw new IOException("the trace at " + tracePath + " is STILL BEING WRITTEN -- close"
                    + " the game first. The recorder holds it open for the whole session, so a run"
                    + " that is in progress cannot be replayed: half of it is not on disk yet and the"
                    + " numbers would describe part of a session. (" + ex.Message + ")", ex);
            }

            // THE LAST RECORD OF A RECORDED RUN CAN BE HALF-WRITTEN, AND THAT IS NOT A CORRUPT FILE.
            //
            // The recorder appends a line per frame and flushes every 30 frames, and the operator
            // ends the session by closing the game by hand -- which can kill the process in the
            // middle of `StreamWriter.Write`, leaving a prefix of one line on disk. A COMPLETE file
            // therefore always ends in a newline, and a file that does not is one the process did
            // not finish writing. Measured: the run of 20261014-192048-p15744 ends
            // `...,1211.228,1211.079,1210.923,1210.76,1210` -- cut inside a coordinate in the
            // middle of the last threat's `xs` array, after 2473 complete lines.
            //
            // The first version of this reader threw, and the whole 2173-frame session became
            // unanalysable because of its last 40 bytes. Treating it as a warning instead is the
            // same judgement Assertion F makes about an empty file, in the other direction: report
            // what is missing, and analyse what is there. It is deliberately narrow -- only the
            // final line, only when the file is unterminated -- because a malformed line in the
            // MIDDLE of a recording means the writer is broken, and that must still fail loudly.
            bool endsCleanly = EndsWithNewline(tracePath);

            var byGeneration = new Dictionary<long, GridWindow>();
            int lineNumber = 0;
            int malformedLine = 0;
            string malformedMessage = null;
            foreach (string line in File.ReadLines(tracePath))
            {
                lineNumber++;
                if (line.Length == 0)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                Json record;
                try
                {
                    record = Json.Parse(line);
                }
                catch (FormatException ex)
                {
                    // A malformed line is a hard failure UNLESS it is the last line of an
                    // unterminated file. `ReadLines` is lazy, so "is this the last line" is only
                    // knowable once the enumeration ends: the line is tagged here and judged after
                    // the loop. At most one line can be tagged, because the next iteration either
                    // parses or throws with the tags already set.
                    if (malformedLine != 0)
                    {
                        throw new FormatException(tracePath + ":" + lineNumber + ": " + ex.Message
                                                  + " (a second malformed line: the recording is"
                                                  + " corrupt, not truncated)");
                    }
                    malformedLine = lineNumber;
                    malformedMessage = ex.Message;
                    continue;
                }

                string kind = record["t"].AsString();
                switch (kind)
                {
                    case "H":
                        trace.Version = record["v"].AsInt();
                        trace.DodgeConfig = record["dodge"].AsString();
                        trace.GridSource = record["gridSource"].AsString();
                        trace.SampleCount = record["samples"].AsInt(21);
                        // The header may declare the trace synthetic. Real recordings never do, so
                        // the reader's default is "recorded" and the flag can only ever relax the
                        // one assertion that a generated trace cannot answer.
                        trace.Synthetic = record["synthetic"].AsBool(false);
                        break;

                    case "G":
                    {
                        GridWindow g = ReadGrid(record);
                        byGeneration[g.Generation] = g;
                        trace.Grids.Add(g);
                        break;
                    }

                    case "F":
                    {
                        RecordedFrame frame = ReadFrame(record, byGeneration, trace.Warnings);
                        trace.Frames.Add(frame);
                        break;
                    }

                    default:
                        trace.Warnings.Add("line " + lineNumber + ": unknown record type '" + kind + "'");
                        break;
                }
            }

            if (malformedLine != 0 && (endsCleanly || malformedLine != lineNumber))
            {
                // A malformed line that is not the last line of an unterminated file: the writer is
                // broken. Fail, naming which of the two conditions failed.
                throw new FormatException(tracePath + ":" + malformedLine + ": " + malformedMessage
                                          + (endsCleanly
                                             ? " (the file ends in a newline, so this is not a"
                                               + " truncated final write)"
                                             : " (a later line parsed, so this is not the last"
                                               + " line)"));
            }
            if (malformedLine != 0)
            {
                trace.Warnings.Add("the last line (" + malformedLine + ") is half-written and was"
                                   + " skipped: the file does not end in a newline, so the process"
                                   + " died inside a write. " + (lineNumber - 1)
                                   + " complete line(s) read.");
            }

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(collisionLogPath) && File.Exists(collisionLogPath))
            {
                LoadHits(collisionLogPath, trace.Hits);
            }

            return trace;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Whether the file's last byte is a newline. An empty file counts as clean (there is
        /// nothing half-written in it); a file with no trailing newline does not.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool EndsWithNewline(string path)
        {
            using (var stream = new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.ReadWrite))
            {
                if (stream.Length == 0)
                {
                    return true;
                }
                stream.Seek(-1, SeekOrigin.End);
                return stream.ReadByte() == '\n';
            }
        }

        private static GridWindow ReadGrid(Json record)
        {
            var g = new GridWindow();
            g.Generation = record["g"].AsLong();
            g.OriginX = record["ox"].AsInt();
            g.OriginY = record["oy"].AsInt();
            g.Width = record["w"].AsInt();
            g.Height = record["h"].AsInt();
            g.Cells = new byte[Math.Max(0, g.Width * g.Height)];

            List<Json> rle = record["rle"].Items;
            int cell = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i + 1 < rle.Count; i += 2)
            {
                byte value = (byte)rle[i].AsInt();
                int run = rle[i + 1].AsInt();
                for (int k = 0; k < run && cell < g.Cells.Length; k++)
                {
                    g.Cells[cell++] = value;
                }
            }
            return g;
        }

        private static RecordedFrame ReadFrame(Json record, Dictionary<long, GridWindow> grids,
                                               List<string> warnings)
        {
            var frame = new RecordedFrame();
            frame.Frame = record["f"].AsInt();
            frame.Dt = record["dt"].AsFloat(1.0f / 60.0f);
            frame.ClockMs = record["clock"].AsFloat();
            frame.PlayerX = record["px"].AsFloat();
            frame.PlayerY = record["py"].AsFloat();
            frame.PlayerRadius = record["r"].AsFloat(0.25f);
            frame.Health = record["hp"].AsFloat();
            frame.Moving = record["moving"].AsBool();
            frame.Intent = record["intent"].AsFloat();
            frame.Dead = record["dead"].AsBool();
            frame.SafeWorld = record["safe"].AsBool();
            frame.Rotation = record["rot"].AsFloat();
            frame.Skipped = record["skipped"].AsInt();
            frame.NoHitRecorded = !record["nohit"].IsNull;
            frame.NoHit = record["nohit"].AsInt();

            long gridId = record["grid"].AsLong();
            if (gridId != 0 && grids.TryGetValue(gridId, out GridWindow g))
            {
                frame.Grid = g;
            }

            foreach (Json t in record["threats"].Items)
            {
                var threat = new RecordedThreat();
                threat.GameId = t["id"].AsInt();
                threat.StartTime = t["st"].AsInt();
                threat.X = t["x"].AsFloat();
                threat.Y = t["y"].AsFloat();
                threat.Radius = t["rad"].AsFloat();
                threat.Damage = t["dmg"].AsFloat();
                threat.DamagePercent = t["dmgp"].AsFloat();
                threat.ManaDamage = t["mdmg"].AsInt();
                threat.Projectable = t["lin"].AsInt() != 0;
                List<Json> xs = t["xs"].Items;
                List<Json> ys = t["ys"].Items;
                List<Json> alive = t["alive"].Items;
                threat.Count = t["n"].AsInt(xs.Count);

                // THE COUNT IS CLAMPED TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT, because a truncated trace (a
                // process killed mid-write) must read as a short path rather than as a
                // zero-filled bullet sitting at the origin -- which is inside the player's disc
                // and would look exactly like a model that predicts everything as a hit.
                int n = Math.Min(threat.Count, Math.Min(xs.Count, ys.Count));
                if (n != threat.Count)
                {
                    warnings.Add("frame " + frame.Frame + ": threat " + threat.GameId
                                 + " declared " + threat.Count + " samples but carries " + n);
                }
                threat.Count = n;
                threat.Xs = new float[n];
                threat.Ys = new float[n];
                threat.Alive = new bool[n];
                for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
                {
                    threat.Xs[i] = xs[i].AsFloat();
                    threat.Ys[i] = ys[i].AsFloat();
                    threat.Alive[i] = i < alive.Count ? alive[i].AsInt() != 0 : true;
                }
                frame.Threats.Add(threat);
            }
            return frame;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Reads `collision:` lines out of a bootstrap log.
        ///
        /// THE SHAPE IS PINNED BY `CollisionObservation.ObserveHit` AND IS ASSERTED HERE, not
        /// assumed: a line that does not match is counted and reported rather than skipped
        /// silently. A parser that quietly finds nothing is how a run with forty hits reports
        /// forty false positives and looks like a broken model.
        /// </summary>
        public static void LoadHits(string path, List<ObservedHit> into)
        {
            int lineNumber = 0;
            foreach (string line in File.ReadLines(path))
            {
                lineNumber++;
                int marker = line.IndexOf("collision: key=(", StringComparison.Ordinal);
                if (marker < 0)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                // collision: key=(375634,57919) tracked=yes predicted=yes warning=103.7ms
                //            bullet=(383.7,1102.7) r=0.2 | run: ...
                string rest = line.Substring(marker + "collision: key=(".Length);
                int close = rest.IndexOf(')');
                if (close < 0)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                string[] key = rest.Substring(0, close).Split(',');
                if (key.Length != 2)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                var hit = new ObservedHit();
                hit.GameId = int.Parse(key[0], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                hit.StartTime = int.Parse(key[1], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
                hit.Tracked = rest.Contains("tracked=yes");
                hit.HasPredictedFlag = rest.Contains("predicted=");
                hit.Predicted = rest.Contains("predicted=yes");
                hit.WarningMs = ExtractFloat(rest, "warning=");
                hit.BulletX = ExtractPair(rest, "bullet=", 0);
                hit.BulletY = ExtractPair(rest, "bullet=", 1);
                hit.Radius = ExtractFloat(rest, "r=");
                hit.LineNumber = lineNumber;
                into.Add(hit);
            }
        }

        private static float ExtractFloat(string text, string key)
        {
            int at = text.IndexOf(key, StringComparison.Ordinal);
            if (at < 0)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            at += key.Length;
            int end = at;
            while (end < text.Length && (char.IsDigit(text[end]) || text[end] == '.'
                                         || text[end] == '-' || text[end] == '+'))
            {
                end++;
            }
            return float.TryParse(text.Substring(at, end - at), NumberStyles.Float,
                                  CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out float value) ? value : 0.0f;
        }

        private static float ExtractPair(string text, string key, int which)
        {
            int at = text.IndexOf(key, StringComparison.Ordinal);
            if (at < 0)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            at += key.Length;
            int open = text.IndexOf('(', at);
            if (open < 0)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            int close = text.IndexOf(')', open);
            if (close < 0)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            string[] parts = text.Substring(open + 1, close - open - 1).Split(',');
            if (which >= parts.Length)
            {
                return 0.0f;
            }
            return float.TryParse(parts[which], NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                                  out float value) ? value : 0.0f;
        }
    }
}
```

`hook/tools/Test-DodgeObjective.ps1`:

```ps1
# ============================================================================
#  Test-DodgeObjective.ps1 -- does the dodge still satisfy the objective?
#
#  WHY THIS EXISTS. HANDOFF-DIRECTED-DODGE.md section 1 states one objective and
#  five ways to know it; SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md section 15 is the evidence that
#  it was met. Checking it by hand is six commands and a table read by eye, which is
#  how a regression gets missed -- and this project has already paid twice for a
#  number nobody re-ran (sections 10.4 and 14.4).
#
#  EVERY CHECK HERE IS ONE THE OBJECTIVE NAMES, and each prints the number it used:
#
#    1. SIDESTEP exceeds OUTRUN on all five recordings          (section 1.1)
#    2. every recording carries the path's own decision columns (section 1.2)
#    3. F, T5, T6, T10 and PATH pass on all five recordings     (section 1.3)
#    4. the same five pass on all six scenarios, and `dodge` moves
#    5. decide() p99 is inside the budget                       (section 1.3)
#
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  CHECK 1 IS EXPECTED TO FAIL ON `p20152` SINCE THE HALT FIX, AND WHY.
#
#  The halt fix (SPIKE3.2-OFFLINE-SOLVER.md section 15.14) stops `stand` from halting a
#  player who is holding a direction when an admissible move exists. That is the operator's
#  own verdict, and it is worth 0 % halts against 18.0/23.5/31.4 % on the live sessions.
#
#  The recordings' direction split was the objective of the PREVIOUS task, and it measures
#  the frames the dodge chose a heading on. The halt fix deliberately chooses a heading on
#  more frames, and those frames were not part of the population the old split was ranking:
#  they were `stand`. The halt ends on 6936 walking frames of the five recordings (12.1 % of
#  them on `p20152`, 16.7 % on `p5824`, 19.8 % on `p26684`, 13.4 % on `p5424`, 28.0 % on
#  `p26156`), and on 4823 more across the four live sessions. On the added frames the split
#  is nearly even, so it moves the aggregate. SIDESTEP still exceeds OUTRUN on three of the
#  five, and `p20152` lands at OUTRUN 45.5 % against SIDESTEP 44.4 % (1.1 points apart), on a
#  check the operator's instruction ("keep the code as is right now") and this fix now pull
#  in opposite directions.
#
#  THE CHECK IS LEFT ALONE AND LEFT FAILING, DELIBERATELY, BY THE OPERATOR'S DECISION. It is
#  not re-scoped and not deleted: a check that is edited whenever it disagrees with the code
#  is a check that certifies nothing, and re-scoping it here would hide exactly the trade-off
#  a reader needs to see. `OBJECTIVE: 17 of 18` is therefore the expected output of this
#  script on this build, and the one FAILED line is this one.
#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
#  Usage:
#    .\tools\Test-DodgeObjective.ps1                 # the five recordings
#    .\tools\Test-DodgeObjective.ps1 -Out work\check # keep the dumps it captured
#
#  Exit codes: 0 = every check passed, 1 = at least one failed.
# ============================================================================

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$Out,
    [string]$Harness,
    [string[]]$Recordings = @(
        '20261015-021911-p20152',
        '20261015-024717-p5824',
        '20261015-032549-p26684',
        '20261015-151232-p5424',
        '20261015-153805-p26156'
    ),
    [int]$BudgetUs = 300
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
if (-not $Out) { $Out = Join-Path $root 'work\objective' }
if (-not [System.IO.Path]::IsPathRooted($Out)) { $Out = Join-Path $root $Out }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Out | Out-Null
if (-not $Harness) { $Harness = Join-Path $root 'tools\SolverHarness\bin\Release\SolverHarness.exe' }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Harness)) { Write-Error "no harness at $Harness"; exit 1 }
$Harness = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Harness).Path

$hookRuns = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'drelay\hook'
$checks = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList

function Add-Check([string]$name, [bool]$ok, [string]$detail) {
    [void]$checks.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Name = $name; Ok = $ok; Detail = $detail })
    $tag = if ($ok) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }
    Write-Host ("  [{0}] {1}" -f $tag, $name) -ForegroundColor $(if ($ok) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })
    Write-Host ("         {0}" -f $detail)
}

# --- 1-3: the five recordings --------------------------------------------------
$dirOut = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
foreach ($d in $Recordings) {
    $runDir = Join-Path $hookRuns $d
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $runDir 'trace.jsonl'))) {
        Add-Check "recording $d is present" $false "no trace.jsonl in $runDir"
        continue
    }
    $tag = ($d -split '-')[-1]
    $dec = Join-Path $Out "dec-$tag.txt"
    $rec = Join-Path $Out "rec-$tag.txt"
    & $Harness --trace (Join-Path $runDir 'trace.jsonl') `
               --collisions (Join-Path $runDir 'bootstrap.log') `
               --decisions $dec *> $rec

    # 1 and 2: the direction split, and that the dump carries the path's columns.
    $dir = Join-Path $Out $tag
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $dec -Destination (Join-Path $dir "dec-$tag.txt") -Force
    [void]$dirOut.Add($dir)

    # THE HEADER SPANS LINES, WHICH THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS CHECK GOT WRONG: it read four lines
    # and required `pathwhy` to be on one of them, and the path columns are on the third of a
    # three-line header.
    #
    # THE COLUMN HEADER CONTINUES ONTO A SECOND `#` LINE, AND IT STARTS WITH `|`. That leading bar is
    # the whole of a misalignment this check got wrong three times: splitting each comment line
    # separately gives `stSetup` one index too early, because the continuation supplies the separator
    # the previous line did not. The header and the data are read the SAME way -- concatenate, then
    # split on `|` -- which is the only form that cannot disagree with itself.
    $allComment = Get-Content -LiteralPath $dec | Where-Object { $_ -like '#*' }
    $start = -1
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $allComment.Count; $i++) {
        if ($allComment[$i] -like '# frame |*') { $start = $i; break }
    }
    $colNames = @()
    if ($start -ge 0) {
        $joined = (($allComment[$start..($allComment.Count - 1)]) -join ' ') -replace '^#\s*', ''
        $colNames = $joined -split '\|' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() }
    }
    $colIndex = @{}
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $colNames.Count; $i++) { $colIndex[$colNames[$i]] = $i }
    $needed = @('wp', 'wpdist', 'pathn', 'pathlen', 'pathcost', 'pathwhy',
                'stAdmit', 'stScore', 'stPath', 'stEscape')
    $missingCols = @($needed | Where-Object { -not $colIndex.ContainsKey($_) })
    Add-Check "$tag the decision dump carries the path's own columns" ($missingCols.Count -eq 0) `
        $(if ($missingCols.Count -eq 0) { "$($colNames.Count) column(s); the path's ten are present" }
          else { 'missing: ' + ($missingCols -join ', ') })

    # 3: the invariants, read from the harness's own verdict lines.
    $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $rec -Raw
    $required = @('F   the recording contains frames',
                  'T5  a move is never less durable than the safe stand it replaced',
                  'T6  no emitted move is inside a disc at arrival',
                  'T10 hysteresis cannot hold an unsafe heading',
                  'PATH no planned route cuts a corner through a wall')
    $missing = @()
    foreach ($r in $required) {
        $pattern = '\[PASS\] ' + [regex]::Escape($r)
        if ($text -notmatch $pattern) { $missing += $r }
    }
    Add-Check "$tag F, T5, T6, T10 and PATH all pass" ($missing.Count -eq 0) `
        $(if ($missing.Count -eq 0) { 'all five asserted invariants report PASS' }
          else { 'not PASS: ' + ($missing -join '; ') })

    # 5: the cost.
    #
    # MEASURED FROM THE DUMP AND NOT FROM `decide() evaluating p99`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF
    # SECTION 15.11. The harness's cost line is a BEST-OF-N p99, and its tail is its own garbage
    # collector: it printed 819 us on `p20152` for a solver whose mean decision is a few tens of
    # microseconds. The per-frame `costUs` column is the same estimator and carries the same tail,
    # so neither is held against a budget here. What IS held against it is the stage clock's
    # per-frame total, which is the solver's own measurement of every decision it took -- and the
    # check that it is PRESENT is as important as the number, because a missing clock reads as 0.
    $frameRows = Get-Content -LiteralPath $dec | Where-Object { $_ -notlike '#*' -and $_.Trim() }
    $stageCols = @('stSetup', 'stPath', 'stGates', 'stAdmit', 'stScore', 'stEscape') |
        ForEach-Object { $colIndex[$_] } | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }
    $decided = 0
    $stageTotal = 0L
    $worst = 0L
    foreach ($row in $frameRows) {
        $f = $row -split '\|'
        if ($f.Count -ne $colNames.Count) { continue }
        $t = 0L
        foreach ($k in $stageCols) {
            $raw = $f[$k].Trim()
            $v = 0L
            if ([long]::TryParse($raw, [ref]$v)) { $t += $v }
        }
        if ($t -le 0) { continue }
        $decided++
        $stageTotal += $t
        if ($t -gt $worst) { $worst = $t }
    }
    if ($decided -eq 0) {
        Add-Check "$tag the decision's stage clock is present and inside the budget" $false `
            'no frame carried a non-zero stage total -- the stage clock is missing or was zeroed'
    }
    else {
        $mean = [math]::Round($stageTotal / $decided, 1)
        # THE CHECK IS THE MEAN, AND THE NUMBER IS THE STAGE TOTAL RATHER THAN THE HARNESS'S PER-FRAME
        # `costUs`. Both are deliberate and both are the lesson of SPIKE3.2 section 15.11: the harness
        # allocates a snapshot and a candidate list per frame, so its `costUs` carries its own garbage
        # collector and printed a 169 us mean on `p20152` for a solver whose mean decision is a few
        # tens of microseconds. The stage clock is the solver's own measurement of the work it did.
        # The WORST frame is reported because it is the interesting number and it is NOT the check --
        # a single 4 ms frame is a collection, and section 15.11 records exactly that mistake.
        Add-Check "$tag the mean decision is inside the budget" ($mean -lt $BudgetUs) `
            ("mean {0} us/frame over {1} decided frame(s), worst {2} us, against a {3} us budget" -f `
             $mean, $decided, $worst, $BudgetUs) +
            " -- ONE PASS, SO THE MEAN INCLUDES WHATEVER THE HARNESS'S OWN COLLECTOR PUT INSIDE" +
            " `Decide`: section 15.11 measures 55.5 us/frame at --repeat 20 on the most demanding" +
            " trace, and the live run's own log reads p50<=50us p99<=300us"
    }
}

# --- 1 (the ratio itself): one report over every dump --------------------------
if ($dirOut.Count -gt 0) {
    $report = & python (Join-Path $root 'tools\dodge_direction_report.py') $Out 2>&1 | Out-String
    Write-Host ''
    Write-Host $report.Trim()
    $blocks = [regex]::Matches($report, '(?s)== ([^:]+):.*?OUTRUN\s+(\d+) \(\s*([\d.]+)%\).*?SIDESTEP\s+(\d+) \(\s*([\d.]+)%\)')
    $inverted = 0
    $total = 0
    foreach ($b in $blocks) {
        $total++
        if ([double]$b.Groups[5].Value -gt [double]$b.Groups[3].Value) { $inverted++ }
    }
    Add-Check "SIDESTEP exceeds OUTRUN on every recording" ($total -eq $Recordings.Count -and $inverted -eq $total) `
        "$inverted of $total recording(s) inverted, against $($Recordings.Count) expected"
}

# --- 4: the six scenarios ------------------------------------------------------
$scenPass = 0
$scenMoved = @{}
foreach ($s in 'peaceful','headon','dodge','volley','corridor','passingby') {
    $out = & $Harness --scenario $s --frames 900 2>&1 | Out-String
    $fails = ([regex]::Matches($out,'\[FAIL\]')).Count
    $passes = ([regex]::Matches($out,'\[PASS\]')).Count
    $scenMoved[$s] = [int]([regex]::Match($out,'frames that moved\s+: (\d+)').Groups[1].Value)
    # SIX ASSERTIONS PER SCENARIO, AND THE SIXTH IS THE SETTINGS-STRING SHAPE. It was five until the
    # trace-writer defect (SPIKE3.2 section 15.12) turned a fourth line in `DodgeConfig.Describe` into an
    # unescaped newline inside a JSON string -- so the check that the string is three log lines and ONE
    # json line now runs on every invocation, and this threshold moves with it.
    if ($fails -eq 0 -and $passes -ge 6) { $scenPass++ }
    else { Write-Host "  scenario $s FAILED: $fails failure(s), $passes pass(es)" -ForegroundColor Red }
}
Add-Check "all six scenarios pass every asserted invariant" ($scenPass -eq 6) "$scenPass of 6 green"
Add-Check "the dodge still moves when a bullet is clearly dodgeable" ($scenMoved['dodge'] -gt 0) `
    "the dodge scenario moved on $($scenMoved['dodge']) frame(s)"

# --- the verdict ---------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host ''
$failed = @($checks | Where-Object { -not $_.Ok })
Write-Host ("OBJECTIVE: {0} of {1} check(s) hold." -f ($checks.Count - $failed.Count), $checks.Count) `
    -ForegroundColor $(if ($failed.Count -eq 0) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' })
if ($failed.Count -gt 0) {
    foreach ($f in $failed) { Write-Host ("  FAILED: {0} -- {1}" -f $f.Name, $f.Detail) -ForegroundColor Red }
    exit 1
}
Write-Host "dumps kept in $Out" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
exit 0
```

`hook/tools/Test-FingerprintGate.ps1`:

```ps1
# Prove the Phase 0 gate can fail at the METHOD level, not just the file level.
#
# The first version of Fingerprint.ps1 checked the assembly's *size*, and a mutation test
# found the hole: flipping one byte left every check passing. The SHA-256 closed that. This
# test closes the next one down: a single-byte edit inside a target's IL, with the file
# length unchanged, must make the gate name that target's IL hash and exit non-zero.
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$here = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$root = Split-Path -Parent $here
$recordPath = Join-Path $root 'known-build.json'
$known = Get-Content $recordPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json

$gamePath = $known.recordedFrom
$assembly = Join-Path $gamePath $known.assembly.file
$sandbox = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("drelay_gate_test_{0}" -f $PID)

Write-Output "Gate mutation test"
Write-Output "  source   : $assembly"
Write-Output "  sandbox  : $sandbox"
Write-Output ''

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $sandbox | Out-Null
try {
    # The gate needs the assembly, its runtimeconfig and the two runtime DLLs beside it.
    foreach ($f in @($known.assembly.file, 'DarzasDominion.runtimeconfig.json',
                     'coreclr.dll', 'clrjit.dll')) {
        $src = Join-Path $gamePath $f
        if (Test-Path $src) { Copy-Item $src (Join-Path $sandbox $f) -Force }
    }
    $mutated = Join-Path $sandbox $known.assembly.file

    $target = $known.targetMethods.collision
    $rva = [uint32]$target.rva

    # Map the RVA to a file offset the same way the gate does.
    $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($mutated)
    $pe = [int][BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, 0x3C)
    $coff = $pe + 4
    $opt = $coff + 20
    $sizeOpt = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($bytes, $coff + 16)
    $nsec = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($bytes, $coff + 2)
    $sec0 = $opt + $sizeOpt
    $fileOff = -1
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $nsec; $i++) {
        $s = $sec0 + $i * 40
        $va = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, $s + 12)
        $vs = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, $s + 8)
        $raw = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, $s + 20)
        if ($rva -ge $va -and $rva -lt ($va + $vs)) { $fileOff = $rva - $va + $raw; break }
    }
    if ($fileOff -lt 0) { throw "RVA 0x$($rva.ToString('X')) is not mapped" }

    $headerSize = ([BitConverter]::ToUInt16($bytes, $fileOff) -shr 12) * 4
    $flipAt = $fileOff + $headerSize + [int]($target.ilSize / 2)
    $original = $bytes[$flipAt]
    $bytes[$flipAt] = $original -bxor 0x01
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($mutated, $bytes)

    Write-Output ("  flipped byte {0:X2} -> {1:X2} at file offset 0x{2:X}, inside {3}::{4} IL" -f `
                  $original, ($original -bxor 1), $flipAt,
                  $target.declaringType, $target.name)
    Write-Output ("  file size unchanged: {0}" -f `
                  ((Get-Item $mutated).Length -eq $known.assembly.size))
    Write-Output ''

    $output = & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass `
        -File (Join-Path $here 'Fingerprint.ps1') -GamePath $sandbox 2>&1
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    $output | Where-Object { $_ -match 'target ' -or $_ -match 'FINGERPRINT' -or $_ -match 'SHA-256' } |
        ForEach-Object { Write-Output ("    " + $_) }
    Write-Output ''
    if ($code -ne 0) {
        Write-Output "GATE MUTATION TEST PASSED -- the gate refused the mutated build (exit $code)"
        exit 0
    }
    Write-Output 'GATE MUTATION TEST FAILED -- the gate accepted a build with mutated target IL'
    exit 1
} finally {
    Remove-Item $sandbox -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
```

`hook/tools/Test-HookAbi.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Checks Drelay.Hook.dll's ABI in a throwaway process, without touching the game.

.DESCRIPTION
    The hook is injected into a suspended game process, which makes it awkward to
    test in isolation: a broken export, or a DllMain that does work, would show up
    as a game that fails to start -- a bad way to find out.

    So this loads the DLL into *this* PowerShell process and checks what can be
    checked without the .NET runtime being present:

      1. the DLL loads at all, so DllMain completed without doing anything fatal.
         DllMain was written to do nothing but DisableThreadLibraryCalls; if that
         ever changes, this is where it will be noticed.
      2. the three exported entry points resolve, found the way the launcher finds
         them (GetProcAddress on the loaded module).
      3. DrelayHook_AbiVersion returns the version the launcher was built against.
         This is the check that stops a stale DLL being injected by a new launcher,
         or the reverse.
      4. DrelayHook_Init *without* the launcher's session returns 0 rather than
         crashing. "Fail closed" is the hook's contract when it cannot find its
         shared block, and this is the only negative test that is safe in-process.

    Exit codes: 0 = all checks passed, 1 = a check failed, 2 = the DLL is missing.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $HookDll,
    [uint32] $ExpectedAbi = 1
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# The default is derived from the script's own location rather than from
# $PSScriptRoot: this script lives in a subdirectory, and when it is invoked in a
# way that does not populate that automatic variable the parameter default is
# evaluated against an empty string and throws before a single check runs --
# which is a confusing failure for a self-test to have.
if (-not $HookDll) {
    $scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
    if (-not $scriptDir) { $scriptDir = $PWD.Path }
    $HookDll = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $scriptDir) 'out\Drelay.Hook.dll'
}
$hookDll = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($HookDll)

function Write-Check {
    param([string] $Name, [bool] $Ok, [string] $Detail = '')
    $word = if ($Ok) { 'PASS' } else { 'FAIL' }
    $colour = if ($Ok) { 'Green' } else { 'Red' }
    Write-Host ("  {0,-40} {1}  {2}" -f $Name, $word, $Detail) -ForegroundColor $colour
}

Write-Host "ABI self-test of $hookDll"
Write-Host ''

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $hookDll)) {
    Write-Host 'FAIL: the DLL does not exist. Build it with .\build.ps1 -Native' -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 2
}

# The P/Invoke surface, compiled once into this session.  Add-Type is used rather
# than a prebuilt assembly so this script stays a single file with no build step.
if (-not ('DrelayAbiProbe' -as [type])) {
    Add-Type -TypeDefinition @'
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

public static class DrelayAbiProbe
{
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Unicode, SetLastError = true)]
    private static extern IntPtr LoadLibraryW(string path);

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Ansi, SetLastError = true)]
    private static extern IntPtr GetProcAddress(IntPtr module, string name);

    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
    private static extern bool FreeLibrary(IntPtr module);

    public static IntPtr Load(string path) { return LoadLibraryW(path); }

    public static IntPtr Resolve(IntPtr module, string name) { return GetProcAddress(module, name); }

    public static void Unload(IntPtr module) { if (module != IntPtr.Zero) FreeLibrary(module); }

    [UnmanagedFunctionPointer(CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
    private delegate uint AbiVersionFn();
    public static uint CallAbiVersion(IntPtr fn)
    {
        return Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer<AbiVersionFn>(fn)();
    }

    [UnmanagedFunctionPointer(CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
    private delegate int InitFn();
    public static int CallInit(IntPtr fn)
    {
        return Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer<InitFn>(fn)();
    }
}
'@ -ErrorAction Stop
}

$failed = 0

# 1. Load.  LoadLibraryW directly rather than Add-Type -Path: Add-Type would also
#    work, but it inspects the assembly for managed types first and this is not a
#    managed assembly, so the error it produces when something is wrong is about
#    reflection rather than about loading.
$module = [DrelayAbiProbe]::Load($hookDll)
if ($module -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) {
    $code = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetLastWin32Error()
    Write-Check 'DLL loads (DllMain is inert)' $false "LoadLibraryW failed, win32 error $code"
    Write-Host ''
    Write-Host 'ABI SELF-TEST FAILED' -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
Write-Check 'DLL loads (DllMain is inert)' $true ("module 0x{0:X}" -f $module.ToInt64())

try {
    # 2. Exports.
    $addresses = @{}
    foreach ($name in @('DrelayHook_AbiVersion', 'DrelayHook_Init', 'DrelayHook_Shutdown')) {
        $addr = [DrelayAbiProbe]::Resolve($module, $name)
        $addresses[$name] = $addr
        $ok = $addr -ne [IntPtr]::Zero
        if (-not $ok) { $failed++ }
        Write-Check "export $name" $ok ("0x{0:X}" -f $addr.ToInt64())
    }

    # 3. The ABI version, by calling the export for real.
    if ($addresses['DrelayHook_AbiVersion'] -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) {
        $version = [DrelayAbiProbe]::CallAbiVersion($addresses['DrelayHook_AbiVersion'])
        $ok = $version -eq $ExpectedAbi
        if (-not $ok) { $failed++ }
        Write-Check 'DrelayHook_AbiVersion' $ok "returned $version, expected $ExpectedAbi"
    }

    # 4. Init with no session must fail closed, not crash.
    if ($addresses['DrelayHook_Init'] -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) {
        $init = [DrelayAbiProbe]::CallInit($addresses['DrelayHook_Init'])
        $ok = $init -eq 0
        if (-not $ok) { $failed++ }
        Write-Check 'DrelayHook_Init without a session returns 0' $ok "returned $init"
    }
}
finally {
    [DrelayAbiProbe]::Unload($module)
}

Write-Host ''
if ($failed -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "ABI SELF-TEST FAILED ($failed check(s))" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
Write-Host 'ABI SELF-TEST OK' -ForegroundColor Green
exit 0

```

`hook/tools/Test-HookOffline.ps1`:

```ps1
# ============================================================================
#  Test-HookOffline.ps1 -- every hook check that does not need the game installed.
#
#  WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#  --------------------
#  Most of this component's verification is *pinned to one installed build of one game*, and that is
#  the point of it: Fingerprint.ps1 compares the installed assembly against the values in
#  known-build.json, il_index.py --check re-derives each target's IL hash out of that assembly, and
#  Test-Injection.ps1 stages the game's own runtime files beside a synthetic host. None of those can
#  run on a build machine that has no copy of Darza's Dominion, so none of them run in CI.
#
#  What is left is this list: the checks whose answer depends only on the sources in this directory.
#  They are worth running in CI because they are exactly the ones a refactor breaks -- the DLL's
#  exported ABI, the two generated files against the record they are generated from, the two report
#  tools against their fixtures, and the launcher's configuration invariants (the four sources, their
#  per-field precedence, the discovery walk and the environment the child is given; its discovery
#  runs against a fake Steam tree, so it needs no game and no registry either).
#
#  THE METADATA READER'S SELF-TEST IS NOT ON THAT LIST, AND IT USED TO BE.  It reads the game's own
#  PE -- `il_index.py --self-test` builds a `PE(assembly)` and checks the reader against the method,
#  type and parameter counts the documents state for *this* build -- so on a machine without the game
#  it cannot run at all. It was listed here because its docstring says it reads neither the record nor
#  the IL dump, which is true of the function and beside the point: it needs the assembly. The first
#  hook run in CI is how that was found, and it is now conditional on the install being present, and
#  named when it is not.
#
#  The game-pinned checks are NOT silently skipped. They are named at the end of every run, so a
#  green CI result is never read as "the hook was verified against the game".
#
#  Usage:
#    .\Test-HookOffline.ps1                     # run everything, exit 1 on a failure
#    .\Test-HookOffline.ps1 -Quiet              # suppress the per-check output
#    .\Test-HookOffline.ps1 -GamePath <dir>     # an install that is not where the record says
#
#  Exit codes: 0 = every check passed, 1 = a check failed, 2 = a toolchain is missing.
# ============================================================================

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Quiet,
    # The install to point the metadata reader's self-test at, when it has moved.  Default: the
    # `recordedFrom` path in known-build.json, which is where the build the record describes was.
    [string]$GamePath
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$tools = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$hookRoot = Split-Path -Parent $tools
$outDir = Join-Path $hookRoot 'out'

function Write-Step { param([string]$t) if (-not $Quiet) { Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Cyan } }
function Write-Ok   { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Green }
function Write-Bad  { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor Red }
function Write-Note { param([string]$t) Write-Host $t -ForegroundColor DarkGray }

# A FAILING CHECK HAS TO BE READABLE FROM THE OUTSIDE.
#
# These checks gate a release, and the first time they ran in CI the step reported nothing but
# "Process completed with exit code 1": a run's step log needs a signed-in browser, the check-run
# API carries only the annotations, and `gh` is not installed everywhere. So a failure is emitted
# as a runner ANNOTATION as well as a line of output -- `::error::` is the runner's own protocol,
# and it is what the API can read back. GITHUB_ACTIONS is set by the runner, so a local run prints
# nothing extra.
function Write-Annotation {
    param([string]$Text)
    if ($env:GITHUB_ACTIONS -eq 'true') { Write-Host "::error title=offline checks::$Text" }
}

# WHICH CHECK WAS RUNNING, KEPT WHERE AN UNPLANNED STOP CAN REACH IT.  A terminating error -- an
# exception rather than a non-zero exit code -- used to abort the script with nothing said about
# where it happened, which is the other half of the same blind spot.
$script:currentCheck = 'startup'

trap {
    $where = "the offline suite stopped in '$script:currentCheck': " + $_.Exception.Message
    Write-Bad $where
    Write-Note "  the check's own output is above, under '--- $script:currentCheck'"
    Write-Annotation $where
    exit 1
}

if (-not (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Bad 'python is not on PATH; the generators and the metadata reader need it.'
    Write-Annotation 'python is not on PATH; the generators and the metadata reader need it.'
    exit 2
}
foreach ($required in 'Drelay.Hook.dll', 'Drelay.Bootstrap.dll', 'Drelay.Launcher.exe') {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $outDir $required))) {
        $missing = "missing $outDir\$required -- run build.ps1 first."
        Write-Bad $missing
        Write-Annotation $missing
        exit 2
    }
}

$failures = @()
$ran = @()

function Invoke-Check {
    param([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Body)
    $script:currentCheck = $Name
    Write-Step "--- $Name"
    & $Body
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Write-Bad "FAIL: $Name"
        Write-Annotation "FAIL: $Name (exit $LASTEXITCODE)"
        $script:failures += $Name
    } else {
        if (-not $Quiet) { Write-Ok "ok: $Name" }
    }
    $script:ran += $Name
}

# The DLL's exported ABI: the three exports exist, the version constant is the one this source
# declares, and Init refuses without a session. No game, no elevation, no host process.
Invoke-Check 'ABI self-test' {
    & (Join-Path $tools 'Test-HookAbi.ps1')
}

# The PE/CLI metadata reader against the signatures the documents state for THIS BUILD.
#
# IT READS THE INSTALLED ASSEMBLY, SO IT IS GAME-PINNED -- see the header. The assembly is resolved
# the way `il_index.py` resolves it (the `recordedFrom` path plus the assembly's file name in
# known-build.json) unless -GamePath says the install has moved, and when it is not there the check
# is NAMED as not run rather than failed: a machine without the game has not discovered a defect.
$selfTestAssembly = $null
try {
    $record = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $hookRoot 'known-build.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
    $selfTestDir = if ($GamePath) { $GamePath } else { $record.recordedFrom }
```
